findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-004: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion…
findings.finding_value: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion on whom I have compassion"), covenantally grounded (chesed as the bond-loyalty that grounds the characteristic), and situationally responsive (splanchnizō — triggered by the specific sight of suffering). These three bases are not in tension but in integration: divine compassion is free, covenanted, and responsive simultaneously. The scope finding is among the most analytically significant in the registry: compassion explicitly and repeatedly crosses covenantal boundaries (Nineveh, the Samaritan/Jew axis, the power-asymmetric relationship). Scope is defined by perceived need, not moral standing or covenantal membership — this is formally confirmed in the data and distinguishes compassion from many other relational characteristics. The chesed/splanchnizō distinction maps onto distinct relational registers: chesed sustains within established bonds; splanchnizō extends across distance and difference. T4.4 (receiver's inner-being experience) is the most significant gap — four P-rated prompts, entirely absent from the data. T4.6 (spiritual beings interface) is entirely silent across all four prompts.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-010: T1's scope finding (compassion requires a suffering other; scope is determined by perceived need, not moral standing) is precisely confirmed in T4's relational analysis. The explicit crossing of coven…
findings.finding_value: T1's scope finding (compassion requires a suffering other; scope is determined by perceived need, not moral standing) is precisely confirmed in T4's relational analysis. The explicit crossing of covenantal boundaries (Nineveh, Samaritan/Jew) evidenced in T4 is the relational expression of T1's boundary-definition: compassion ends where the condition (pitiable need) is absent, not where covenantal membership ends. T1's four modes of operation (T1.4) — intra-covenantal, cross-boundary, anticipatory, Christological — map onto T4's chesed/splanchnizō distinction (within-bond sustaining vs across-distance extending) and the scope analysis (covenantal and transcovenantal registers). Definition and relational scope are structurally co-determining.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-015: T2's constitutional origin analysis (somatic-relational-covenantal triple ground) and T4's relational direction analysis are structurally aligned. The somatic origin (womb, gut) grounds the cross-boun…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional origin analysis (somatic-relational-covenantal triple ground) and T4's relational direction analysis are structurally aligned. The somatic origin (womb, gut) grounds the cross-boundary relational direction in T4: splanchnizō's somatic immediacy is precisely what enables it to cross covenantal boundaries — the gut-movement toward the suffering other precedes any covenantal assessment of the relationship. The covenantal origin (chesed) grounds the within-bond sustaining direction in T4. The constitutional origin therefore predicts the relational direction: somatic = cross-boundary; covenantal = within-bond. T2's soul-body interface classification explains T4's scope-by-need finding: because compassion originates at the soul-body interface (before covenantal-rational assessment), its scope is determined by the pre-rational recognition of need rather than the post-rational assessment of covenantal standing.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-019: T3's perceptive-trigger finding (compassion is activated by sight — splanchnizō is perceptively dependent) and T4's scope-by-need finding (scope is determined by perceived need, not covenantal standin…
findings.finding_value: T3's perceptive-trigger finding (compassion is activated by sight — splanchnizō is perceptively dependent) and T4's scope-by-need finding (scope is determined by perceived need, not covenantal standing) are the same finding from two analytical perspectives. T3 names the faculty (perception) and its function (triggering compassion by seeing the pitiable condition); T4 names the relational consequence (scope defined by what is seen). The cross-boundary extension in T4 (Nineveh, Samaritan/Jew) is the relational expression of T3's merit-independence: compassion is perceptively dependent (it must see the need) but merit-independent (it does not assess the moral standing of the one seen). The three relational modes in T3.11 (building/sustaining, restoring/repairing, extending across difference) correspond precisely to T4's chesed/splanchnizō/cross-boundary structure.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-023: T4's finding that divine compassion operates on three simultaneous bases (sovereignly free, covenantally grounded, situationally responsive) and T5's three mechanisms of change (encounter/sudden, cove…
findings.finding_value: T4's finding that divine compassion operates on three simultaneous bases (sovereignly free, covenantally grounded, situationally responsive) and T5's three mechanisms of change (encounter/sudden, covenantal-sustaining/gradual, participatory-ontological) are structurally isomorphic. The sovereignly-free basis corresponds to the encounter/sudden mechanism: divine compassion operating freely produces the sudden compassion-event (splanchnizō). The covenantally-grounded basis corresponds to the covenantal-sustaining mechanism: chesed as the sustaining relational ground operates gradually and consistently. The situationally-responsive basis opens toward the participatory-ontological mechanism: formation at the deepest constitutional level produces a person who is dispositionally responsive to every situation of need. T4's relational architecture and T5's formation mechanisms are the same structural reality described from relational and developmental perspectives respectively.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-024: T4's scope-by-need finding (compassion crosses covenantal boundaries) and T6's co-occurrence landscape (the human-response cluster — peace, faith, will, surrender — co-occurring with compassion) revea…
findings.finding_value: T4's scope-by-need finding (compassion crosses covenantal boundaries) and T6's co-occurrence landscape (the human-response cluster — peace, faith, will, surrender — co-occurring with compassion) reveal a structural pattern: divine compassion reaching across boundaries generates a characteristic cluster of human inner-being responses regardless of the covenantal position of the recipient. The Nineveh response (repentance and turning) and the pattern of peace/faith/will/surrender co-occurring with compassion both confirm this: compassion-received generates a recognisable inner-being response cluster that is structurally consistent across relational positions. T6's mapping of the human-response cluster is the co-occurrence evidence for T4's structural finding about scope and response.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-025: T4's three bases of divine compassion (sovereignly free, covenantally grounded, situationally responsive) are each grounded in specific textual evidence from T7. The sovereignly-free basis is evidence…
findings.finding_value: T4's three bases of divine compassion (sovereignly free, covenantally grounded, situationally responsive) are each grounded in specific textual evidence from T7. The sovereignly-free basis is evidenced in Rom 9:15 (T7's argument structure analysis — divine compassion as sovereign determination). The covenantally-grounded basis is evidenced in Exod 34:6 (T7's most multiply-anchored verse — the divine self-declaration in the covenant context). The situationally-responsive basis is evidenced in the Synoptic splanchnizō pattern (T7.2 — the sight-event structure of the Gospels). T7's framework divergences (sovereignty vs automaticity) map directly onto T4's relational analysis: the framework correctly identifies that divine compassion's sovereign freedom (T4.1) is what exceeds the natural empathic automaticity that human science frameworks describe.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-004: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — a…
findings.finding_value: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — all God-as-subject). The basis of divine extension is the giver's character and prior knowing (Exo 33:17 — "I know you by name"), not the receiver's merit — neither merit-based nor arbitrary. The human-to-God direction is specifically supplication: tachanum (H8469) is the receiving side's corresponding vocabulary built into the same root family as the giving side (chen/chanan) — the vocabulary embeds the two-directional circuit in a single root. The human-giving direction extends grace horizontally through three modes: forgiving (charizō — Eph 4:32), gracious conduct (chen as character quality — 889-003), and gracious speech (SD022). The receiving direction is the most underexamined (T4.4 — P-rated throughout); the scope analysis (T4.5) reveals grace crossing covenantal and social boundaries (Ruth narrative — grace in the context of foreign status and vulnerability). T4.6 (spiritual beings) is evidenced at one point: Luk 1:28 (kecharitōmenē — the angel's announcement), which implies angelic ministry as a vehicle of grace rather than grace operating independently in the spiritual-beings register. T4 synthesis: the relational architecture of grace is unique in the programme — it is the only characteristic where the giving-side vocabulary and the receiving-side vocabulary are built from the same root (chen/tachanum), encoding the grace-circuit's two-sidedness at the lexical level.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-010: T1's four modes of operation map onto T4's four relational directions. The sovereign-bestowal mode corresponds to the God-to-human direction (T4.1 — primary and dominant). The covenantal-relational-su…
findings.finding_value: T1's four modes of operation map onto T4's four relational directions. The sovereign-bestowal mode corresponds to the God-to-human direction (T4.1 — primary and dominant). The covenantal-relational-sustaining mode corresponds to the relational scope (T4.5 — grace operating within and across covenantal boundaries). The capacity-conferring mode corresponds to the human-to-God direction in its supplication register (T4.2 — SD026: grace giving even the capacity to appeal). The character-forming mode corresponds to the human-giving direction (T4.3 — gracious conduct and speech as the horizontal expression of received grace-character). The vocabulary's structural insight (T4 synthesis: giving-side and receiving-side built from the same root, chen/tachanum) explains T1's finding that grace requires the receptor's inner engagement to complete its operation — the vocabulary encodes the two-sidedness because grace is constitutively a two-sided circuit.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-015: T2's origin analysis (grace does not originate in the human constitutional system — it arrives from God) and T4's directional analysis (God-to-human is primary and dominant) are the same finding from …
findings.finding_value: T2's origin analysis (grace does not originate in the human constitutional system — it arrives from God) and T4's directional analysis (God-to-human is primary and dominant) are the same finding from constitutional and relational perspectives respectively. The spirit level as reception point (T2.1) and the God-to-human direction as primary (T4.1) are mutually explanatory: because grace originates with God and is received at the spirit level, the primary relational direction is necessarily God-initiated toward the human spirit. The human-to-God direction (T4.2 — supplication) corresponds to T2.10's constitutional movement in reverse: the soul's recognition of need translates into the somatic enactment of supplication (prostration, fasting, sackcloth), which is T2.7's bidirectional body-soul finding. Constitutional location and relational direction are co-determining.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-023: T4's relational directions correspond to T5's formation mechanisms. The God-to-human direction (T4.1 — sovereign bestowal) corresponds to the encounter and spirit-outpouring mechanisms (T5.3 — sudden …
findings.finding_value: T4's relational directions correspond to T5's formation mechanisms. The God-to-human direction (T4.1 — sovereign bestowal) corresponds to the encounter and spirit-outpouring mechanisms (T5.3 — sudden specific relational event; Zec 12:10). The human-to-God direction (T4.2 — supplication) corresponds to the sustained-formation arc of T5.5: the person who habitually supplicates is being formed into the character that supplicates, which is itself the character-quality kind identified in T1. The human-giving direction (T4.3 — gracious forgiving, speech-grace) corresponds to T5.3's mediated-transformation mechanism (grace → tenderheartedness → forgiving → gracious speech — SD030, Eph 4:32). T4 describes the relational shape of each mechanism; T5 describes the inner formation process each mechanism produces.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-024: T4's relational architecture and T6's co-occurrence network express the same structural reality from relational and cross-registry perspectives. The seeking co-occurrence dominance (T6 — R140, 40 vers…
findings.finding_value: T4's relational architecture and T6's co-occurrence network express the same structural reality from relational and cross-registry perspectives. The seeking co-occurrence dominance (T6 — R140, 40 verses) is the co-occurrence expression of T4.2 (the human-to-God supplication direction): seeking is the relational posture, and R140 is the registry that names it. The sequential relationship confirmed in T6.2 (grace precedes and enables faith, repentance, supplication, mourning — SD003, SD006, SD026, SD038) is the causal expression of T4's architectural finding: grace is the enabling condition for every positive human-to-God relational posture. The boundary questions in T6.5 (grace-love, grace-mercy, grace-chesed) correspond to T4.5's scope analysis: the characteristics that share grace's scope (particularly love and mercy) are the same characteristics whose relational scope overlaps with grace's at T4.5.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-025: T4's most analytically distinctive finding (the vocabulary encodes the two-sided grace-circuit in a single root: chen/chanan for giving; tachanum/techinah for seeking) is T7's most significant root-le…
findings.finding_value: T4's most analytically distinctive finding (the vocabulary encodes the two-sided grace-circuit in a single root: chen/chanan for giving; tachanum/techinah for seeking) is T7's most significant root-level finding. T7.1 confirms: the chen root family embeds both the giving side (chen — favour, chanan — to be gracious) and the receiving-seeking side (tachanum, techinah — supplication) in a single etymological family. This is unique in the programme's vocabulary data: no other characteristic has the giving-side and receiving-side vocabulary built from the same root. T4's relational architecture and T7's lexical analysis are the relational and lexical descriptions of the same structural reality — that grace is constitutively a two-sided circuit whose two sides are inseparable at the root level.

findings.session_b_note: The evidence shows a spectrum of conditionality across the covenant traditions, not a single answer. (1) Unconditional: the Noahic covenant (765-001 — OBS-034-038): God commits without human precondition; the covenant is made with all living creatures. The patriarchal covenant (Abraham) is similarly initiated without precondition beyond faith (Act 3:25; Neh 9:8). (2) Bilateral-conditional: the Sinai covenant (765-002 — OBS-034-039): Deu 7:9 — "with those who love him and keep his commandments." God's covenant-faithfulness is stated as responsive to human covenant-keeping. Exo 19:5: "if you will indeed obey my voice and keep my covenant." (3) Covenantal-unconditional in the new covenant: Heb 8:8-10 — God establishes the new covenant unilaterally as a declaration, not a condition. "I will make" — not "if you will make." The new covenant shifts back toward unconditional establishment while retaining the bilateral response structure at the level of reception and growth. (4) The DIM-34-SD001 hypothesis — God's faithfulness to covenant transcends human covenant-keeping (Gen 9:15; Lk 1:72 — "to remember his holy covenant" even for an unfaithful people) — is confirmed across the OT traditions: God's covenant-basis is ultimately his own character, not human performance.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-034-004: T4 as a whole reveals that covenant's relational interface structure is asymmetric but genuinely bilateral. The God-to-human direction (T4.1) is the founding and sustaining axis — God initiates, commi…
findings.finding_value: T4 as a whole reveals that covenant's relational interface structure is asymmetric but genuinely bilateral. The God-to-human direction (T4.1) is the founding and sustaining axis — God initiates, commits, inscribes, and mediates. The human-to-God direction (T4.2) is the responsive axis — the whole person moves toward God through commitment, love, and faithfulness. The horizontal directions (T4.3 giving; T4.4 receiving) are genuine but secondary, and the evidence shows they are grounded in and enabled by the vertical. The relational scope expands progressively across the covenant trajectory — from particular (Abraham) to expanding (Israel) to universal (new covenant in Christ). The spiritual-beings interface (T4.6) is largely absent from the data — the only relevant material is the pagan deity named "lord of covenant" (H1286) and the inferred adversarial spiritual claim. T4 as a whole shows that covenant's relational architecture is constituted by God's prior initiative and realised through the whole person's responsive engagement.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-010: T1 establishes that covenant has directional, relational, and constitutional implications that orient the entire enquiry (Q&A-015). T4 shows how these directional implications are realised: the God-to…
findings.finding_value: T1 establishes that covenant has directional, relational, and constitutional implications that orient the entire enquiry (Q&A-015). T4 shows how these directional implications are realised: the God-to-human direction is the primary axis (T4.1), the human-to-God direction is the responsive axis (T4.2), and the horizontal direction (T4.3/4.4) is grounded in the vertical. The T1 × T4 synthesis: the directional implication identified at the definitional level (T1) is fully realised in the relational interface structure (T4). The asymmetry of the definition (God initiates, human responds — Q&A-015) is the same asymmetry that governs all four relational directions in T4. Definition and relational interface are structurally consistent — covenant is asymmetric at every level of analysis.

findings.session_b_note: Most extensively evidenced direction in the registry. H2617A group 536-001 (180 relevant verses, dominant subject GOD [XREG: H2617A, OBS-099-083]) documents the full range. Conditionality is in manifestation; attribute itself is unconditional. (c) What it reveals: God whose primary inner disposition toward the creature is committed faithful generous good will — chesed before, through, and after judgment.

findings.session_b_note: The data establishes covenant as the primary basis. God's peace is extended: (1) Through covenant: Num 25:12 ("my covenant of peace"), Isa 54:10 (covenant of peace that shall not be removed), Eze 34:25, 37:26 (covenants of peace in the new covenant context); (2) Through covenant faithfulness: Psa 85:8 — God speaks peace to his saints "but let them not turn back to folly" — the condition is covenant fidelity, not merit; (3) Through the cross: Col 1:20 ("making peace by the blood of his cross") — the basis shifts in the NT from the Sinai covenant to the new covenant accomplished in Christ's sacrifice; (4) Through grace not merit: Joh 14:27 ("not as the world gives do I give to you") — the basis of Christ's peace-gift is explicitly distinguished from transactional exchange; the gift is given freely. The ground shifts from covenant-as-obligation to covenant-as-grace across the canon.

findings.session_b_note: The data reveals four distinct bases operating across the groups: (1) Covenantal (872-001): God gives because the covenant is in force — the giving enacts prior covenantal commitment, regardless of immediate merit. Gen 15:18 — the covenant ratification is the basis; the giving follows from it. Mal 2:5 — "my covenant with him was one of life and peace, and I gave them to him" — the giving is covenantal through and through. (2) Responsive (872-002): God gives in response to presented inner need — Leah's condition triggers divine hearing and giving (Gen 29:33). The basis is the creature's condition, perceived by divine attentiveness. (3) Formative (872-003): God gives Spirit/wisdom as constitutive endowment — the basis appears to be divine formative purpose for the person, not contingent on their current state. (4) Moral-consequential (872-004): God gives-over as moral response to faithlessness — the basis is moral consistency: the covenant is executed in both directions. (5) Eschatological-grace (872-007): God gives to the mourning without stated precondition — grace and eschatological initiative are the basis. No single basis covers all modes; the characteristic operates across a spectrum from pure grace to moral consequence.
findings.finding_value: The data reveals four distinct bases operating across the groups: (1) Covenantal (872-001): God gives because the covenant is in force — the giving enacts prior covenantal commitment, regardless of immediate merit. Gen 15:18 — the covenant ratification is the basis; the giving follows from it. Mal 2:5 — "my covenant with him was one of life and peace, and I gave them to him" — the giving is covenantal through and through. (2) Responsive (872-002): God gives in response to presented inner need — Leah's condition triggers divine hearing and giving (Gen 29:33). The basis is the creature's condition, perceived by divine attentiveness. (3) Formative (872-003): God gives Spirit/wisdom as constitutive endowment — the basis appears to be divine formative purpose for the person, not contingent on their current state. (4) Moral-consequential (872-004): God gives-over as moral response to faithlessness — the basis is moral consistency: the covenant is executed in both directions. (5) Eschatological-grace (872-007): God gives to the mourning without stated precondition — grace and eschatological initiative are the basis. No single basis covers all modes; the characteristic operates across a spectrum from pure grace to moral consequence.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-060-004: T4 as a whole reveals that the relational architecture of this characteristic is directionally structured and asymmetrical. The dominant direction is God-to-human (6 of 7 groups, confirmed across T4.1…
findings.finding_value: T4 as a whole reveals that the relational architecture of this characteristic is directionally structured and asymmetrical. The dominant direction is God-to-human (6 of 7 groups, confirmed across T4.1); the human direction is responsive (T4.2: human gives back what was first given). The basis of divine giving is plural — covenantal, responsive, formative, moral-consequential, eschatological-grace (Q&A-102) — revealing that faithfulness is not a single relational mode but a relational orientation that differentiates itself across relational conditions while remaining unified in character. The human-to-God direction reveals responsive correspondence as the relational structure (Q&A-107): the proper relational form is one in which the human gives back to God what is his (glory, praise, self), having first received. The human-to-human direction is thinner in the data (Q&A-109) — reflecting the registry's God-subject dominance. T4.6 is substantially silent on spiritual beings. What T4 reveals as a whole: faithfulness-as-giving is constitutively a divine-initiative relational reality that the human enters through responsive participation. The human's giving is always downstream of divine giving; the correspondence is the proper form of the relationship.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-003: The five operational modes of giving (T1.4) map onto the four relational interfaces (T4) in a specific structural way. Performative and covenantal giving (modes 1) operate through the God-to-human int…
findings.finding_value: The five operational modes of giving (T1.4) map onto the four relational interfaces (T4) in a specific structural way. Performative and covenantal giving (modes 1) operate through the God-to-human interface (T4.1) with a covenantal basis. Responsive giving (mode 2) operates through the God-to-human interface with a responsive basis. Endowing giving (mode 3) operates through God-to-human with a formative basis. Judicial giving (mode 4) operates through God-to-human with a moral-consequential basis. Relinquishing self-giving (human mode) operates through the human-to-God interface. Glory-giving operates through the human-to-God interface. The relational interface is not external to the definition — it is a structural element of each operational mode. What this pair reveals: the characteristic cannot be defined without specifying its relational direction. The same act-concept (giving) becomes a different operational mode depending on which interface it operates through.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-016: The relational interfaces (T4 — divine-initiative, human-responsive, covenantal scope) and the formation arc (T5 — constitutive endowment, sustained narrative, eschatological orientation) reveal that …
findings.finding_value: The relational interfaces (T4 — divine-initiative, human-responsive, covenantal scope) and the formation arc (T5 — constitutive endowment, sustained narrative, eschatological orientation) reveal that formation happens through relational interfaces. The God-to-human interface is the channel through which constitutive formation occurs (Spirit given, wisdom deposited — T5.5). The human-to-God interface is both the goal of formation (glory-giving as the proper orientation of the formed person) and a constituent of the formation process (practising glory-giving forms the person who gives glory). What this pair reveals: formation is not an individual inner process — it is a relational event. The person is not formed in isolation from God and others; they are formed through the giving and receiving that constitutes the relational interfaces. The formation arc (T5) is the temporal dimension of the relational structure (T4): what the interfaces do over time is formation.

findings.finding_value: The relational interfaces (T4 — God-to-human primary, human-to-God responsive, covenantal scope) and the structural landscape (T6 — hub position, causal sequences, shared anchors) reveal that R060's hub position is constituted by its position at the centre of the divine-human relational network. The sequential patterns (T6.2 — giving→worship, suffering→giving, faithlessness→giving-over) are relational sequences: each involves God and the human in the roles described by T4. The shared anchors (T6.6) are high-density precisely because they are relational nodes — Hos 11:8 anchors five registries because it holds the divine inner-being and the human relational situation simultaneously. What this pair reveals: the structural hub position of R060 in the inner-being landscape is a direct consequence of its occupation of the divine-human relational centre. It is a hub because it is where the primary divine-human dynamic (God gives, human receives and responds) is most directly expressed and most extensively connected.

findings.finding_value: Across all sub-groups, God's engagement with M06 characteristics is consistently: (1) responsive to human moral choices, never arbitrary; (2) covenantally grounded; (3) aimed at justice, deliverance, or restoration. God does not extend M06 characteristics as character expressions toward innocent or righteous persons — his movement is always in response to what the human has become or done, or in advocacy for those who suffer under others' M06 characteristics.

Covenantal and unconditional in its deepest form — "with everlasting love I have loved you" (Jer 31:3 — Group 1542). Responsive to covenant-love: "to a thousand generations of those who love me" (Exo 20:6 — Group 1583-a).

Compassion (ra.chum) in Exo 34:6 (Group 1594) is stated as divine constitutive character rather than conditional on Israel's merit. Triggered by their groaning (Judg 2:18 — Group 1742) — responsive to need.
Sovereignly — "not because of works but because of him who calls" (Rom 9:11-12 — Group 1628 context). Mercy's basis is divine sovereign will, not human merit.
Grace — "immeasurable riches of his grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus" (Eph 2:7 — Group 1111). Unconditional in character, directed toward repentance in purpose.
Constitutive character — God's gentleness is not conditional but is what he is toward the creature. The warrior-king who comes meekly (Mat 21:5 — Group 1261) images the unconditional divine mode.
Covenantal faithfulness and responsive compassion — "let your steadfast love comfort me according to your promise to your servant" (Psa 119:76 — Group 1741). Both promised and responsive.

Faithfulness and grace — "God is faithful, by whom you were called into the fellowship of his Son" (1Cor 1:9 — Group 1055). "Not counting their trespasses against them" (2Cor 5:19 — Group 2069) — the basis is non-accounting of trespasses, i.e., grace.

**[A2 — Human Righteousness / C — Justification]** Primarily grace received through faith. "Being justified by his grace" (Tit 3:7); "faith was counted to Abraham as righteousness" (Rom 4:9, VSG 3410-001). The basis is not human moral performance but divine grace received by faith. The OT material shows that righteousness is also extended on the basis of covenant faithfulness: God keeps his covenant with the righteous across generations (Psa 103:17, VSG M26-A1-003) — the covenantal basis.

**[D — Avenging Justice]** Responsive — God's avenging justice is responsive to injustice done: it is triggered by the cry of the wronged (Luk 18:3–8) and by the accumulated injustice done to his servants (Rev 19:2). The basis is just response to wrong.

**[E — Condemnation]** On the basis of assessed guilt — God's condemnation is the just verdict pronounced on those whose standing before his righteousness is one of guilt. The basis is not arbitrary — it is the just response of the righteous judge to wickedness.

**[CLUSTER]** The basis varies by sub-group: grace through faith (C, A2), covenant (A1-003, A2-014), just response (D, E). The common thread is that God's righteousness operates from his character — he acts in accordance with who he is in every mode.

findings.finding_value: M01-A shows a primarily **covenantal** basis: the fear God implants (Jer 32:40) is a covenant promise; the fear God commands is grounded in the covenant relationship (Deu 6:13-14; Mal 2:5). The Psa 25:14 material (covenant intimacy offered to those who fear) suggests a **responsive** dimension — God's covenant friendship responds to the human person's reverential posture.

M01-C and D show a **conditional-responsive** basis: God deploys terror against Israel's enemies in response to their opposition to his covenantal purposes (Exo 23:27; Deu 11:25); he dismays rebels in response to their defiance (Psa 2:5; Jer 49:37). The basis is conditional on the enemies' opposition.

M01-C and D show a **conditional-responsive** basis: God deploys terror against Israel's enemies in response to their opposition to his covenantal purposes (Exo 23:27; Deu 11:25); he dismays rebels in response to their defiance (Psa 2:5; Jer 49:37). The basis is conditional on the enemies' opposition.
M01-F-VCG-03 (covenantal curse-dread) is explicitly **conditional** on covenant violation: Deu 28:66-67 is the direct consequence of failing to obey the terms of the covenant.

The basis of God's operation across M01 is primarily **covenantal and responsive**: God extends reverential fear-formation to covenant members (M01-A), deploys terror against covenant enemies (M01-C), and imposes dread as covenant-curse on the unfaithful (M01-F). The characteristic's operation from God toward the human person is consistently embedded in the covenant structure.

The basis is consistently moral and relational: idolatry, covenant violation, faithlessness, and deliberate provocation are the conditions that trigger divine anger. Jer 11:17 (M02-D-VCG-01): Baal worship specifically names the basis. 2Ki 22:17 (M02-D-VCG-01): "the intent behind the idolatry was explicitly to provoke God to anger" — the willfulness of the offense matters to the basis. The basis is conditional on moral failure and responsive — it is not arbitrary or unconditional.

The basis is consistently moral and relational: idolatry, covenant violation, faithlessness, and deliberate provocation are the conditions that trigger divine anger. Jer 11:17 (M02-D-VCG-01): Baal worship specifically names the basis. 2Ki 22:17 (M02-D-VCG-01): "the intent behind the idolatry was explicitly to provoke God to anger" — the willfulness of the offense matters to the basis. The basis is conditional on moral failure and responsive — it is not arbitrary or unconditional.

Psa 7:11 (M02-C-VCG-01) reveals a continuous moral basis: divine indignation is a daily disposition against wickedness as such — not episodic response to specific acts but an enduring stance. The basis is God's moral nature (his holiness) rather than Israel's specific acts alone.

The bases are varied. Disciplinary: God's use of distress and grief to press the inner will back toward him (M03-D-VCG-03). Judgmental: grief imposed as direct consequence of sin and covenant violation (Deu 28:65; Lam 2:5 — M03-B-VCG-02). Redemptive: God puts the servant to grief for salvific purpose (Isa 53:10 — BOUNDARY). Compassion-responsive: God hears the groaning of the oppressed and responds with covenantal faithfulness (Exo 2:24 — M03-E-VCG-01). The basis therefore includes both punitive and redemptive-compassionate modes — God extends grief-experiences toward the human person not uniformly but in ways conditioned by the person's covenantal situation, sin, and need.

**[CHAR-1]** E — God's exultation toward his people is consistently **covenantal and responsive**: (1) **Covenantal** — Jer 32:41's context is the new covenant; Deu 30:9's is the restoration covenant after return; Isa 62:5's is the eschatological marriage of YHWH and Zion; (2) **Responsive** — God's exultation is directed at a restored people (Deu 30:9 — "as he took delight in your fathers"; Zep 3:17 — he who will save, in your midst); (3) **Conditional by the people's covenant posture** — Deu 28:63 shows the same su.s applied to God's delight in ruin when Israel is unfaithful, confirming the covenantal conditionality. God's exultation over his people is not unconditional but arises from the fulfilment of covenant relationship.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Multiple bases evidenced: (1) **Covenantal faithfulness** — the feast-commandment joy (Deu 16:11–15) is joy given in the context of covenant obedience and God's blessing; Deu 28:47 makes its withdrawal contingent on covenant failure; (2) **Repentance** — Luk 15:7, 10 (God's joy over the repentant sinner — Joy given in response to turning); Psa 51:12 (restoration of joy requested after confession); (3) **Pleasing God** — Ecc 2:26 (God gives joy "to the one who pleases him"); (4) **Grace in Christ** — the NT Spirit-mediated joy (Gal 5:22; 1Th 1:6; Rom 14:17) is given through the Spirit as a gift, not earned; Joh 15:11 (Christ's joy given as part of abiding relationship with him); (5) **Eschatological promise** — M04-E (sa.s.von) shows God promising joy as the eschatological reversal of sorrow, grounded in his covenant commitment to restore.

**[CHAR-7]** E — (1) **Gospel relationship** — Act 16:34 (the jailer's Suffering-Joy arises immediately upon coming to faith in God — the basis is the new faith-relationship); (2) **Participation in Christ's suffering** — 1Pe 4:13 ("insofar as you share Christ's sufferings") — the basis is active participation in Christ's mission-suffering, not merely suffering in general; (3) **Covenant faithfulness and call** — Mat 5:12's context (persecution for righteousness' sake) and Luk 6:23's context (rejection for the Son of Man's sake) — the basis is faithful alignment with Christ under persecution; (4) **Faith in the unseen** — 1Pe 1:8 ("you believe in him and rejoice") — faith is both the basis and the enabling condition.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Multiple bases: (1) **Unconditional character-goodness** — God's intrinsic goodness (M04-L-VCG-01) is not conditioned on human response; it is the permanent quality of his nature ("his steadfast love endures forever" — ki-tov formulas); (2) **Covenantal faithfulness** — M04-O-VCG-04: God's good promises are fulfilled to the covenant community (Jos 21:45); his good hand enables those who are faithful to his call (Ezr 7:9; Neh 2:8); (3) **Moral responsiveness** — Psa 73:1 ("God is good to Israel, to those who are pure in heart") — moral purity is the precondition for experiencing God's goodness as directed toward oneself; Psa 112:5 ("it is well with the man who deals generously") — justice and generosity are conditions for the wellbeing Gladness; (4) **Grace in redemption** — Gen 2:18 (God identifies the not-good and provides the remedy — grace without merit); Deu 9:6 ("not because of your righteousness" — the good land given by grace).

**[CHAR-4]** E — Multiple bases, none purely meritocratic: (1) **Grace in election** — Deu 30:9 ("as he took delight in your fathers") — the delight in the fathers is prior to any merit; Jer 31:20's Ephraim-cherishing persists through rebuke — grace, not merit; (2) **Moral faithfulness** — Psa 37:23 ("when he delights in his way") — the person's way is what God delights in, making faithfulness a condition of received divine pleasure; Psa 51:6 ("you delight in truth in the inward being") — inward truthfulness as the condition; (3) **Covenantal relationship** — Isa 62:4 (God's Delight in Zion as the covenantal reversal of desolation); (4) **Christ's perfect pleasing** — Mat 3:17; 12:18 — the basis of God's ultimate eudokeo toward the Son is the Son's perfect correspondence to the Father; this becomes the basis for God's delight in all who are in Christ; (5) **Repentance** — Eze 18:23 ("I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from his way and live") — God's Delight toward the sinner is specifically conditioned on turn-and-live; his Delight toward life is the basis of the command to repent.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Multiple bases: (1) **Covenantal faithfulness** — the ni.cho.ach corpus: God's receptive Pleasure at worship depends on covenant-obedient offering (Lev 26:31 — withheld from unfaithful); the basis is obedient worship; (2) **Seeking his presence** — Psa 27:4 (one who asks and seeks after God receives the Pleasure of his beauty); (3) **Grace and character** — Psa 36:8 (the river of delights is lavishly given to those in God's house — gracious supply); Psa 90:17 (divine pleasantness asked to rest upon the community — grace); (4) **Restoration** — Eze 20:41 (God will accept the restored Israel as a pleasing aroma after scattering — restoration as the basis of resumed Pleasure).

**[CHAR-6]** E — Multiple bases: (1) **Covenantal faithfulness** — Exo 34:10 ("before all your people I will do marvels… it is an awesome thing that I will do with you") — covenantal relationship as the basis; (2) **Steadfast love** — Psa 31:21 ("wondrously shown his steadfast love") — hesed as the inner motivation of God's wonder-acts; Psa 107:8, 15, 21, 31 (wondrous works to the children of man, grounds for thanking steadfast love) — steadfast love and wondrous works are paired; (3) **Purpose and sovereign plan** — Isa 25:1 ("plans formed of old, faithful and sure") — God's wonder-acts executed according to long-planned purpose; (4) **Restoration** — Eze 20:41 (God acting wondrously at the regathering — adjacent); Mic 7:15; Joel 2:26 — restoration as the basis of renewed wonder-acts.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Three bases emerge from the comparative evidence: (1) **Covenantal faithfulness** is the primary stated basis for most characteristics: God's wonder-acts are covenantally grounded (Exo 34:10); God's Delight toward persons is covenantally motivated (Deu 30:9 — "as he took delight in your fathers"; Jer 31:20 — Ephraim as darling child through rebuke); God's Joy over his people is the joy of covenant restoration; (2) **Grace prior to merit** — the most theologically significant basis across Chars 3–4: Deu 9:6 (God's goodness toward Israel is not because of their righteousness); Jer 31:20's sha.a.shu.im persisting through rebuke; Pro 8:30–31's Wisdom-Delight in the children of man is grounded in creation, not covenant performance. **[CHAR-2]** E — God's response to constitutional inner evil is responsive and principled. The wrath (Rom 1:18 — VCG-05) is responsive to the constitutional unrighteousness — the suppression of truth draws the divine response. The grace-for-transformation (Act 3:26 — VCG-05: "God, having raised up his servant, sent him to you first, to bless you by turning every one of you from your wickedness") is covenantal-mission: the divine initiative to address the constitutional evil is grounded in the Abrahamic-covenant mission ("to you first"). Heb 10:22 (VCG-06): the cleanising of the evil conscience is covenantal — grounded in the new covenant mercy that "remembers sins no more" (Heb 8:12 — VCG-06). The basis is both principled-responsive (wrath to unrighteousness) and covenantal-gracious (mission and mercy to the constitutionally evil).

**[CHAR-3]** E — God's revulsion-verdict is responsive and principled. It is responsive to specific inner moral conditions: Pro 11:20 (vc=1677 — VCG-01): crooked heart triggers the verdict; Pro 16:5 (vc=1689 — VCG-02): arrogant heart triggers the verdict. The verdict is not unconditional (it is tied to specific inner conditions) but it is also not arbitrarily conditional — it is principled: every abominable inner condition named in the corpus triggers the same divine response of revulsion. The covenantal dimension appears in Mal 2:11 (vc=66004 — VCG-04): faithless covenant-betrayal as abomination — the covenantal relationship defines the space within which certain acts are specifically abominable. The verdict is thus: principled-responsive (God's holiness responds consistently to specific inner moral conditions) with a heightened covenantal register where covenant defines what specifically is a betrayal that constitutes abomination.

**[CHAR-4]** E — God's response to idolatrous abomination is covenantally responsive: responsive to specific acts of idolatrous betrayal within a covenantal relationship that defines what constitutes betrayal. Deu 32:16 (vc=65938 — VCG-02): "stirred him to jealousy" — jealousy is a covenantal response (the covenant defines the exclusivity within which jealousy is appropriate). Eze 5:11 (vc=65969 — VCG-05): "because you have defiled my sanctuary… I will withdraw" — the divine response is explicitly conditioned on the prior idolatrous act. Jer 44:22 (vc=65967 — VCG-04): "the Lord could no longer bear your evil deeds and the abominations that you committed" — a threshold was crossed; the divine response is proportional and escalating. The basis is covenantal-responsive: the covenant defines the relationship within which idolatrous abomination is a specific form of betrayal requiring response.

**[CHAR-5]** E — God's response to iniquity as active scheming is responsive and principled: responsive to the specific inner conduct of scheming and harm-generation, and principled in that the response is consistent with the moral order. Deu 28:20 (vc=38439 — VCG-05): "because of the evil of your deeds, because you have forsaken me" — the basis is explicitly the evil deeds and the forsaking of covenant relationship. Psa 94:23 (VCG-03): "bring back on them their iniquity" — the response is proportional: the iniquity returns as the measure of judgment. Job 21:19 (vc=38209 — VCG-04): "God stores up their iniquity for their children" — the deferred-but-certain response shows the principled nature: the divine response is certain even if delayed. The basis is covenantal-responsive: the covenant defines the relationship within which iniquity is a betrayal, and the response is to that betrayal.

**[CHAR-6]** E — God's judgment in the Rev 16 context (VCG-01) is responsive and proportional: the plagues are responses to accumulated sin and defiance. Rev 16:9 (vc=14352 — VCG-01): "they cursed the name of God who had power over these plagues" — the judgment precedes the blasphemy (the scorching provokes the cursing), showing that the divine judgment is responsive to prior condition and that the blasphemous response to it is an escalation. The basis is covenantal-responsive: God responds to the defiance of his created order and the rejection of his authority (Jude 8 — VCG-01) with escalating judgment that discloses the depth of the hardened will. 1Pe 2:12 (vc=14377 — VCG-03): the day of visitation — God's evaluation of conduct — is consistent and principled.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster reveals a consistent basis for God's response across all six characteristics: responsive and principled. The response is responsive — conditioned on specific inner-being conditions and acts (Char 3: specific inner conditions triggering divine revulsion; Char 4: specific idolatrous acts triggering withdrawal; Char 6: specific blasphemous speech triggering divine judgment). The response is principled — consistent, proportional, and morally grounded (Char 5: Psa 94:23 — bringing back iniquity as retributive proportionality; Char 6: Rom 3:8 — "their condemnation is just"). The covenantal dimension adds a heightened context: Chars 4 and 6 specifically show covenantal betrayal as intensifying the divine response within the covenant relationship (Char 4: Deu 32:16 — jealousy provoked within covenant; Char 6: God's glory withheld within covenantal relationship). The cluster's unanimous basis: God's response to M10b characteristics is not arbitrary but principled-responsive — triggered by specific conditions, proportional in measure, and covenantally contextualised.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Covenantal. The clean/unclean categorical system is delivered within the Sinai covenant (Lev 11:44-45, M10c-A-VCG-04: "I am the Lord your God... I am holy"). The system is not universal to all peoples (Deu 12:15/22/15:22, M10c-A-VCG-08 — the unclean and clean may eat ordinary game alike, showing the system does not create absolute exclusion from life but from sacred domains); it is specifically covenantal, addressing Israel as the covenant people. The basis is covenantal holiness: God's character as holy establishes the boundary; the human person's defilement-state is the condition that must be managed to maintain covenant access to the divine presence.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Responsive and judicial. Rom 1:24 (VCG-02) frames the divine giving-over as a response to a prior human act — the rejection of God, the suppression of truth (Rom 1:18-23 — context). God's withdrawal of restraint is responsive to human moral defection. The basis is not unconditional or arbitrary; it is a judicial response proportioned to the human act of rejecting divine truth. The divine calling at 1Th 4:7 (VCG-02) — "God has not called us for impurity, but in holiness" — frames the opposite direction: God's calling is inherently toward holiness, and the judicial giving-over is the consequence of refusing that calling.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The divine judicial response is covenantal and responsive. Eze 5:11 (VCG-03): "because you have defiled my sanctuary... therefore I will withdraw" — the basis is responsive: God's withdrawal is proportionate and consequential to the community's specific act of defiling what he had made holy. The judicial deepening at Eze 20:26 is also responsive: God uses the community's own defiant idolatrous offering as the instrument of further judgment — the response is precisely calibrated to the nature of the sin. The cleansing promise is covenantal and gracious: Eze 37:23 — "they shall be my people, and I will be their God" — the covenant formula restored grounds the divine cleansing in covenant faithfulness rather than in the community's merit.

**[CHAR-4]** E — God's reversal of the characteristic is sovereign, compassionate, and responsive. Luk 6:18 (VCG-02): "those troubled with unclean spirits were cured" — the healing is offered to all who come; no condition is named for eligibility. Mar 7:25 (VCG-01): the Syrophoenician woman's daughter is healed — the mother comes; the child receives healing. The basis is responsive to need and seeking: the persons or their proxies come, and God's authority acts without evidence of a covenantal or merit-based condition.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The four bases reveal a cluster-level pattern: the basis of God's action matches the character of each defilement register. Characteristic 1: covenantal — the clean/unclean system is delivered within the Sinai covenant and governed by the call to holiness ("I am the Lord your God... I am holy" — Lev 11:44-45); God's action is structurally covenantal and formative. Characteristic 2: responsive-judicial — God's giving-over (Rom 1:24) is a response to prior human rejection of divine truth; the basis is not arbitrary but proportioned to human moral defection. Characteristic 3: covenantal and responsive — divine withdrawal is proportionate to specific covenantal betrayal (Eze 5:11 — "because you have defiled my sanctuary... therefore I will withdraw"); the eschatological cleansing is covenantal-gracious (Eze 37:23 — covenant formula restored). Characteristic 4: sovereign-compassionate and responsive to need — "those troubled with unclean spirits were cured" (Luk 6:18 VCG-02) — no merit-based or covenantal condition named; healing is responsive to the presence of need and seeking. The cluster's governance of divine action: covenantal formation (Char 1) → responsive judicial judgment (Char 2) → covenantal judgment and grace (Char 3) → sovereign compassion responsive to need (Char 4).

questions.question_text: What does God's extension of the characteristic show about his disposition toward the human person?

findings.session_b_note:
The corpus reveals God's disposition toward the human person through the forgiveness vocabulary with unusual clarity:

**God's disposition is fundamentally oriented toward release, not retention.** The sal.lach attribute (Psa 86:5) names forgiveness as belonging to God's essential goodness — it is not a reluctant concession but an expression of his character. He is *forgiving* as a settled disposition.

**The scope of God's forgiveness-disposition is maximally inclusive.** Mar 3:28 — "all sins will be forgiven the children of man, and whatever blasphemies they utter" — the comprehensive inclusivity of divine forgiveness is stated before the one exception (Mar 3:29). God's disposition is to forgive broadly; the limit is the single exception, not the rule.

**God's forgiveness is costly, not cheap.** Eph 1:7 — "redemption through his blood." The extension of forgiveness required the atoning act of Christ. The disposition to forgive is genuine and costly — not indifference to the wrong done but the absorption of its cost. OBS-064-033 (Q033 answer) notes: "forgiveness at the highest level is costly to the one who forgives."

**God's forgiveness disposition generates relational openness.** Jer 31:34 — the new covenant forgiveness enables direct knowing of God. The disposition that forgives is the same disposition that opens itself to be known. The forgiveness-character and the relational-availability-character are linked.

findings.session_b_note:
The data reveals three dimensions of divine disposition:

**Constitutive orientation toward the human:** God's compassion is not a decision made in response to human need — it is the character of his inner being that precedes and underlies all encounter with the human person. The Exod 34:6 self-declaration names this as the constitutive truth about who God is. God's disposition toward the human person is compassionate before the human person does anything or becomes anything.

**Deliberative retention of compassion over judgment:** Hos 11:8 — the divine inner contest in which compassion wins over judgment — reveals a disposition that actively maintains compassion against the claims of righteousness and justice. God does not merely feel compassion; he chooses it against competing inner orientations. The deliberate character of the divine compassion-commitment means it is not a sentiment but a sustained volitional orientation.

**Maternal intimacy:** The womb-language (ra.cham, re.chem; Isa 46:3) reveals that God's disposition toward the human person is not that of a distant benevolent authority but of the one who carries life from within. The most intimate possible relational stance — bearing another inside one's own body — is the image Scripture uses for God's compassionate disposition. This is the deepest available statement about divine inner orientation toward the human person: God is disposed toward the person as a mother toward the child she is carrying.

findings.session_b_note:
God's response to contrition reveals a consistent divine disposition: **particular attentiveness to and care for the lowly and broken**. Psa 34:18 — "the Lord is near to the brokenhearted and saves the crushed in spirit." Isa 57:15 — God dwells with the contrite to revive them. Isa 66:2 — God looks specifically to the humble, contrite, and trembling. Psa 51:17 — God will not despise the broken and contrite heart.

The pattern is unambiguous and consistent: God is drawn toward the contrite inner being. This reveals a divine disposition of care for creaturely vulnerability — specifically the vulnerability that arises from honest self-disclosure before God. The God of this data is not indifferent to inner states but specifically responsive to the posture of lowliness.

findings.session_b_note:
Finding 062-DIVINE-001 addresses this directly: "God's disposition is toward inclusion in divine fellowship rather than exclusion." The evidence supports three qualities of divine disposition:

**Inclusion-oriented:** God grants promises for divine nature participation — he moves *toward* the human person, opening access to his own nature.

**Unifying:** God joins the divided (Eze 37:19) — his disposition is to restore what is separated, not to maintain separation.

**Faithful witness:** God witnesses covenantal companionship bonds (Mal 2:14) — his disposition is to hold and honour the relational bonds humans form with each other.

findings.session_b_note: God's extension of goodness reveals a disposition of initiatory, generous, and sustaining goodwill toward the human person. Three dimensions: (1) Initiatory — God acts first in goodness (Gen 1:31; Eph 2:7 — "so that in the coming ages he might show the immeasurable riches of his grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus"). The initiative is always divine. (2) Generous — chrēstotēs names not merely adequate goodness but generous goodwill (886-001): God's disposition is one of overflowing benevolence. (3) Sustaining — the covenantal promise (884-005, Jos 23:14: "not one word has failed") names a goodness that holds through time and maintains its commitment. The disposition is not reactive but proactive, generous, and reliable. Lam 3:25 ("the Lord is good to those who wait for him") names waiting as the human posture corresponding to this divine sustaining goodness — the relationship is not passive but involves a human receptive posture. (OBS-067-OBS-006, OBS-067-OBS-033, OBS-067-OBS-034, SBF-067-Q006)

findings.session_b_note: The receiver is constituted as agapētos (beloved) — an identity state, not merely a felt experience (OBS-103-040, OBS-103-122). The immediate inner-being state upon receiving divine love: rest/quieting (Zep 3:17, OBS-103-094); fullness and pleasure (Psa 16:11, OBS-103-112); soul-satisfaction (Jer 31:14, OBS-103-081). The sustained inner-being state: security ('I will never leave you' — Heb 13:5), known-ness ('Lord, you know everything — Joh 21:17, OBS-103-153), and free-from-striving (Psa 127:2, OBS-103-084). The person who receives divine love becomes the person who rests in it. The identity-state (beloved) and the experiential state (rest, fullness) are both dimensions of the receiver's inner condition.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-103-004: Love's relational architecture is structured by three directional axes — GOD → HUMAN, HUMAN → GOD, HUMAN → HUMAN — with divine love structurally prior and causally generative of all subsequent love. 1…
findings.finding_value: Love's relational architecture is structured by three directional axes — GOD → HUMAN, HUMAN → GOD, HUMAN → HUMAN — with divine love structurally prior and causally generative of all subsequent love. 1Jo 4:19 ('we love because he first loved us') is the axis-precedence statement: the first axis is not responsive to but constitutive of the second and third. The GOD → HUMAN direction moves through four mechanisms: covenantal declaration (naming the beloved — Jer 12:7, Mat 3:17), Spirit-infusion (Rom 5:5), redemptive acts (Joh 3:16), and covenantal covering (Eze 16:8). The HUMAN → GOD direction requires total inner mobilisation (Mat 22:37 — all heart, soul, mind) and the clearing of rival loves as its condition (1Jo 4:19, 1Ti 6:10). The HUMAN → HUMAN direction spans five structural types (neighbour, enemy, community, friendship, family) and creates the social architecture described in Q&A-088 (restructured kinship, public legibility, competitive generosity). The most significant finding in T4: the human-to-God direction is conditioned by prior reception of divine love — the capacity for human love toward God is itself a gift. The one structural gap: T4.6 (spiritual beings) is absent from the evidence.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-008: The constitutional location data and the relational interface data converge on the same structural claim: love's inner depth is its relational reach. The deeper love is constitutionally (heart-inscrib…
findings.finding_value: The constitutional location data and the relational interface data converge on the same structural claim: love's inner depth is its relational reach. The deeper love is constitutionally (heart-inscribed, soul-constitutive, Spirit-sourced), the further its relational reach — from neighbour-love (soul-level reciprocal) to enemy-love (will-level against grain) to divine love (Spirit-level transcendent). The constitutional movement pattern (Spirit → heart → soul → body — Q&A-056) maps onto the relational directional pattern: divine love enters at the deepest constitutional level (Spirit, heart) and produces relational acts at the outermost level (community legibility, bodily expression). The GOD→HUMAN axis operates at the constitutional depth where love is received (heart-infusion — Rom 5:5); the HUMAN→GOD axis requires total constitutional mobilisation (Mat 22:37 — all heart, soul, mind); the HUMAN→HUMAN axis is the outward bodily expression of the internal constitutional reality. Constitutional and relational are thus not two separate dimensions of love but the inside and outside of the same movement.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-012: The faculty engagement pattern in T3 is produced by and oriented toward the relational interfaces in T4. Love's identity-faculty (T3.10) is constituted through the relational interface: being-loved by…
findings.finding_value: The faculty engagement pattern in T3 is produced by and oriented toward the relational interfaces in T4. Love's identity-faculty (T3.10) is constituted through the relational interface: being-loved by God (GOD→HUMAN axis) establishes the identity of agapētos; what-one-loves (active direction) establishes identity through the chosen object. The relational capacity faculty (T3.11) is the faculty through which the three relational axes are exercised: the GOD→HUMAN axis engages the relational capacity as receiver; the HUMAN→GOD axis engages it as giver; the HUMAN→HUMAN axis engages it in both directions simultaneously. Memory (T3.3) sustains the relational interface: love toward God is sustained through remembering his chesed (Jer 31:20); love in community is sustained through shared history. Moral sensitivity (T3.8) is calibrated by the relational interface structure: love-of-God calibrates the moral perception of what is evil (Psa 97:10); love-of-neighbour calibrates the perception of what is just. The deepest inter-tier finding: the faculty engagement pattern is not incidental — it is precisely the faculty configuration required by the relational architecture. The relational structure generates the faculty requirements.

The restraint of wrath (Psa 78:38 — OBS-111-038) shows that mercy is the active principle that holds back the alternative disposition — divine mercy is not passive but actively modulates the relationship. findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-004: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion…
findings.finding_value: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion on whom I have compassion"), covenantally grounded (chesed as the bond-loyalty that grounds the characteristic), and situationally responsive (splanchnizō — triggered by the specific sight of suffering). These three bases are not in tension but in integration: divine compassion is free, covenanted, and responsive simultaneously. The scope finding is among the most analytically significant in the registry: compassion explicitly and repeatedly crosses covenantal boundaries (Nineveh, the Samaritan/Jew axis, the power-asymmetric relationship). Scope is defined by perceived need, not moral standing or covenantal membership — this is formally confirmed in the data and distinguishes compassion from many other relational characteristics. The chesed/splanchnizō distinction maps onto distinct relational registers: chesed sustains within established bonds; splanchnizō extends across distance and difference. T4.4 (receiver's inner-being experience) is the most significant gap — four P-rated prompts, entirely absent from the data. T4.6 (spiritual beings interface) is entirely silent across all four prompts.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-010: T1's scope finding (compassion requires a suffering other; scope is determined by perceived need, not moral standing) is precisely confirmed in T4's relational analysis. The explicit crossing of coven…
findings.finding_value: T1's scope finding (compassion requires a suffering other; scope is determined by perceived need, not moral standing) is precisely confirmed in T4's relational analysis. The explicit crossing of covenantal boundaries (Nineveh, Samaritan/Jew) evidenced in T4 is the relational expression of T1's boundary-definition: compassion ends where the condition (pitiable need) is absent, not where covenantal membership ends. T1's four modes of operation (T1.4) — intra-covenantal, cross-boundary, anticipatory, Christological — map onto T4's chesed/splanchnizō distinction (within-bond sustaining vs across-distance extending) and the scope analysis (covenantal and transcovenantal registers). Definition and relational scope are structurally co-determining.

findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional origin analysis (somatic-relational-covenantal triple ground) and T4's relational direction analysis are structurally aligned. The somatic origin (womb, gut) grounds the cross-boundary relational direction in T4: splanchnizō's somatic immediacy is precisely what enables it to cross covenantal boundaries — the gut-movement toward the suffering other precedes any covenantal assessment of the relationship. The covenantal origin (chesed) grounds the within-bond sustaining direction in T4. The constitutional origin therefore predicts the relational direction: somatic = cross-boundary; covenantal = within-bond. T2's soul-body interface classification explains T4's scope-by-need finding: because compassion originates at the soul-body interface (before covenantal-rational assessment), its scope is determined by the pre-rational recognition of need rather than the post-rational assessment of covenantal standing.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-019: T3's perceptive-trigger finding (compassion is activated by sight — splanchnizō is perceptively dependent) and T4's scope-by-need finding (scope is determined by perceived need, not covenantal standin…
findings.finding_value: T3's perceptive-trigger finding (compassion is activated by sight — splanchnizō is perceptively dependent) and T4's scope-by-need finding (scope is determined by perceived need, not covenantal standing) are the same finding from two analytical perspectives. T3 names the faculty (perception) and its function (triggering compassion by seeing the pitiable condition); T4 names the relational consequence (scope defined by what is seen). The cross-boundary extension in T4 (Nineveh, Samaritan/Jew) is the relational expression of T3's merit-independence: compassion is perceptively dependent (it must see the need) but merit-independent (it does not assess the moral standing of the one seen). The three relational modes in T3.11 (building/sustaining, restoring/repairing, extending across difference) correspond precisely to T4's chesed/splanchnizō/cross-boundary structure.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-023: T4's finding that divine compassion operates on three simultaneous bases (sovereignly free, covenantally grounded, situationally responsive) and T5's three mechanisms of change (encounter/sudden, cove…
findings.finding_value: T4's finding that divine compassion operates on three simultaneous bases (sovereignly free, covenantally grounded, situationally responsive) and T5's three mechanisms of change (encounter/sudden, covenantal-sustaining/gradual, participatory-ontological) are structurally isomorphic. The sovereignly-free basis corresponds to the encounter/sudden mechanism: divine compassion operating freely produces the sudden compassion-event (splanchnizō). The covenantally-grounded basis corresponds to the covenantal-sustaining mechanism: chesed as the sustaining relational ground operates gradually and consistently. The situationally-responsive basis opens toward the participatory-ontological mechanism: formation at the deepest constitutional level produces a person who is dispositionally responsive to every situation of need. T4's relational architecture and T5's formation mechanisms are the same structural reality described from relational and developmental perspectives respectively.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-024: T4's scope-by-need finding (compassion crosses covenantal boundaries) and T6's co-occurrence landscape (the human-response cluster — peace, faith, will, surrender — co-occurring with compassion) revea…
findings.finding_value: T4's scope-by-need finding (compassion crosses covenantal boundaries) and T6's co-occurrence landscape (the human-response cluster — peace, faith, will, surrender — co-occurring with compassion) reveal a structural pattern: divine compassion reaching across boundaries generates a characteristic cluster of human inner-being responses regardless of the covenantal position of the recipient. The Nineveh response (repentance and turning) and the pattern of peace/faith/will/surrender co-occurring with compassion both confirm this: compassion-received generates a recognisable inner-being response cluster that is structurally consistent across relational positions. T6's mapping of the human-response cluster is the co-occurrence evidence for T4's structural finding about scope and response.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-025: T4's three bases of divine compassion (sovereignly free, covenantally grounded, situationally responsive) are each grounded in specific textual evidence from T7. The sovereignly-free basis is evidence…
findings.finding_value: T4's three bases of divine compassion (sovereignly free, covenantally grounded, situationally responsive) are each grounded in specific textual evidence from T7. The sovereignly-free basis is evidenced in Rom 9:15 (T7's argument structure analysis — divine compassion as sovereign determination). The covenantally-grounded basis is evidenced in Exod 34:6 (T7's most multiply-anchored verse — the divine self-declaration in the covenant context). The situationally-responsive basis is evidenced in the Synoptic splanchnizō pattern (T7.2 — the sight-event structure of the Gospels). T7's framework divergences (sovereignty vs automaticity) map directly onto T4's relational analysis: the framework correctly identifies that divine compassion's sovereign freedom (T4.1) is what exceeds the natural empathic automaticity that human science frameworks describe.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-004: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — a…
findings.finding_value: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — all God-as-subject). The basis of divine extension is the giver's character and prior knowing (Exo 33:17 — "I know you by name"), not the receiver's merit — neither merit-based nor arbitrary. The human-to-God direction is specifically supplication: tachanum (H8469) is the receiving side's corresponding vocabulary built into the same root family as the giving side (chen/chanan) — the vocabulary embeds the two-directional circuit in a single root. The human-giving direction extends grace horizontally through three modes: forgiving (charizō — Eph 4:32), gracious conduct (chen as character quality — 889-003), and gracious speech (SD022). The receiving direction is the most underexamined (T4.4 — P-rated throughout); the scope analysis (T4.5) reveals grace crossing covenantal and social boundaries (Ruth narrative — grace in the context of foreign status and vulnerability). T4.6 (spiritual beings) is evidenced at one point: Luk 1:28 (kecharitōmenē — the angel's announcement), which implies angelic ministry as a vehicle of grace rather than grace operating independently in the spiritual-beings register. T4 synthesis: the relational architecture of grace is unique in the programme — it is the only characteristic where the giving-side vocabulary and the receiving-side vocabulary are built from the same root (chen/tachanum), encoding the grace-circuit's two-sidedness at the lexical level.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-010: T1's four modes of operation map onto T4's four relational directions. The sovereign-bestowal mode corresponds to the God-to-human direction (T4.1 — primary and dominant). The covenantal-relational-su…
findings.finding_value: T1's four modes of operation map onto T4's four relational directions. The sovereign-bestowal mode corresponds to the God-to-human direction (T4.1 — primary and dominant). The covenantal-relational-sustaining mode corresponds to the relational scope (T4.5 — grace operating within and across covenantal boundaries). The capacity-conferring mode corresponds to the human-to-God direction in its supplication register (T4.2 — SD026: grace giving even the capacity to appeal). The character-forming mode corresponds to the human-giving direction (T4.3 — gracious conduct and speech as the horizontal expression of received grace-character). The vocabulary's structural insight (T4 synthesis: giving-side and receiving-side built from the same root, chen/tachanum) explains T1's finding that grace requires the receptor's inner engagement to complete its operation — the vocabulary encodes the two-sidedness because grace is constitutively a two-sided circuit.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-015: T2's origin analysis (grace does not originate in the human constitutional system — it arrives from God) and T4's directional analysis (God-to-human is primary and dominant) are the same finding from …
findings.finding_value: T2's origin analysis (grace does not originate in the human constitutional system — it arrives from God) and T4's directional analysis (God-to-human is primary and dominant) are the same finding from constitutional and relational perspectives respectively. The spirit level as reception point (T2.1) and the God-to-human direction as primary (T4.1) are mutually explanatory: because grace originates with God and is received at the spirit level, the primary relational direction is necessarily God-initiated toward the human spirit. The human-to-God direction (T4.2 — supplication) corresponds to T2.10's constitutional movement in reverse: the soul's recognition of need translates into the somatic enactment of supplication (prostration, fasting, sackcloth), which is T2.7's bidirectional body-soul finding. Constitutional location and relational direction are co-determining.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-023: T4's relational directions correspond to T5's formation mechanisms. The God-to-human direction (T4.1 — sovereign bestowal) corresponds to the encounter and spirit-outpouring mechanisms (T5.3 — sudden …
findings.finding_value: T4's relational directions correspond to T5's formation mechanisms. The God-to-human direction (T4.1 — sovereign bestowal) corresponds to the encounter and spirit-outpouring mechanisms (T5.3 — sudden specific relational event; Zec 12:10). The human-to-God direction (T4.2 — supplication) corresponds to the sustained-formation arc of T5.5: the person who habitually supplicates is being formed into the character that supplicates, which is itself the character-quality kind identified in T1. The human-giving direction (T4.3 — gracious forgiving, speech-grace) corresponds to T5.3's mediated-transformation mechanism (grace → tenderheartedness → forgiving → gracious speech — SD030, Eph 4:32). T4 describes the relational shape of each mechanism; T5 describes the inner formation process each mechanism produces.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-024: T4's relational architecture and T6's co-occurrence network express the same structural reality from relational and cross-registry perspectives. The seeking co-occurrence dominance (T6 — R140, 40 vers…
findings.finding_value: T4's relational architecture and T6's co-occurrence network express the same structural reality from relational and cross-registry perspectives. The seeking co-occurrence dominance (T6 — R140, 40 verses) is the co-occurrence expression of T4.2 (the human-to-God supplication direction): seeking is the relational posture, and R140 is the registry that names it. The sequential relationship confirmed in T6.2 (grace precedes and enables faith, repentance, supplication, mourning — SD003, SD006, SD026, SD038) is the causal expression of T4's architectural finding: grace is the enabling condition for every positive human-to-God relational posture. The boundary questions in T6.5 (grace-love, grace-mercy, grace-chesed) correspond to T4.5's scope analysis: the characteristics that share grace's scope (particularly love and mercy) are the same characteristics whose relational scope overlaps with grace's at T4.5.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-025: T4's most analytically distinctive finding (the vocabulary encodes the two-sided grace-circuit in a single root: chen/chanan for giving; tachanum/techinah for seeking) is T7's most significant root-le…
findings.finding_value: T4's most analytically distinctive finding (the vocabulary encodes the two-sided grace-circuit in a single root: chen/chanan for giving; tachanum/techinah for seeking) is T7's most significant root-level finding. T7.1 confirms: the chen root family embeds both the giving side (chen — favour, chanan — to be gracious) and the receiving-seeking side (tachanum, techinah — supplication) in a single etymological family. This is unique in the programme's vocabulary data: no other characteristic has the giving-side and receiving-side vocabulary built from the same root. T4's relational architecture and T7's lexical analysis are the relational and lexical descriptions of the same structural reality — that grace is constitutively a two-sided circuit whose two sides are inseparable at the root level.

findings.session_b_note: God's covenant-extension toward the human person reveals a relational disposition of initiating, self-binding, persistent, and ultimately self-giving love. (1) Initiating: God always acts first — no covenant in the data is human-initiated toward God. The initiative is exclusively divine. (2) Self-binding: God binds himself by oath (OBS-034-052), by the covenant sign (rainbow, Gen 9:15 context), and ultimately by the blood of his Son (Heb 13:20 — OBS-034-074). His commitment is not merely declared but enacted through self-binding mechanisms that make his faithfulness legally and sacrificially secured. (3) Persistent: God remembers his covenant even when humans break it (Gen 9:15; Lk 1:72 — OBS-034-073; Lev 26:44-45 in 765-001 context). His disposition is not conditional on continuous human faithfulness. (4) Self-giving: the new covenant is enacted through Christ's death (Heb 9:16 — OBS-034-069). God's covenant-extension ultimately costs him the life of his Son — the most extreme form of self-giving. This reveals that God's disposition toward the human person is one of total, self-giving, initiative-bearing love.
