findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-067-004: T4 as a whole reveals that goodness operates across all relational directions simultaneously — God-to-human, human-to-God, and human-to-human — but with a fundamental asymmetry: the God-to-human direc…
findings.finding_value: T4 as a whole reveals that goodness operates across all relational directions simultaneously — God-to-human, human-to-God, and human-to-human — but with a fundamental asymmetry: the God-to-human direction is prior, generative, and abundant in evidence; the human-to-God direction is responsive and derivative; the human-to-human direction is overflow from prior reception. This is not a simple tripartite scheme but a structured cascade: God's goodness initiates and flows toward the human person (Q&A-099-101); the human responds in trust, seeking, and worship (Q&A-103-105); the goodness received overflows toward others through instruction, justice, and kindness (Q&A-107-109). The most structurally significant T4 finding is the unconditional/conditional distinction (Q&A-100): God's goodness as a character attribute is unconditional; the human's ongoing experience of its relational benefits is conditional on continued trust. This distinction has direct implications for how goodness is taught, received, and sustained. The spiritual beings interface is largely silent — the relational architecture of goodness is thoroughly human-divine in orientation.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-067-015: T2 confirmed that goodness originates externally to the person — the origin is God's character, Spirit, and word; the person is the site of reception, not generation (Q&A-060-061). T4 maps the relatio…
findings.finding_value: T2 confirmed that goodness originates externally to the person — the origin is God's character, Spirit, and word; the person is the site of reception, not generation (Q&A-060-061). T4 maps the relational architecture of this origin: the God-to-human direction (T4.1) is the relational channel through which the external origin reaches the person; the human-to-God direction (T4.2) is the responsive movement that the received goodness enables; the human-to-human direction (T4.3) is the overflow once received. T2's single-origin/multiple-mechanism finding (Q&A-061) maps onto T4's three relational directions: the encounter mechanism corresponds to the human-to-God direction (seeking and tasting); the covenantal-word mechanism corresponds to the God-to-human covenantal direction; the Spirit-infusion mechanism is the Spirit's work in the human constitutional levels (T2.1-2.2). The constitutional and relational architectures are co-extensive — they describe the same reality from inside (constitutional) and outside (relational).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-067-019: T3 confirmed that goodness engages every inner faculty (except creativity), with particular depth in moral evaluation (goodness as the normative anchor — Q&A-089), conscience (goodness calibrates the …
findings.finding_value: T3 confirmed that goodness engages every inner faculty (except creativity), with particular depth in moral evaluation (goodness as the normative anchor — Q&A-089), conscience (goodness calibrates the standard — Q&A-092), and relational capacity (dual-directional overflow — Q&A-098). T4 confirmed that goodness operates across all three relational directions. The inter-tier connection: the faculty engagements of T3 are the inner mechanisms through which T4's relational directions operate. The God-to-human direction (T4.1) engages the perceptive faculty (tasting and seeing — Q&A-066) and the moral evaluation faculty (calibrating the conscience's standard — Q&A-092). The human-to-God direction (T4.2) engages the affective faculty (trust, praise) and the relational capacity faculty. The human-to-human direction (T4.3) engages agency (doing justice — Q&A-084) and relational capacity (overflow toward others — Q&A-098). T3's faculty map is the inner architecture; T4's relational directions are the external expressions of those faculties in lived relationship. They are not separate dimensions but the inside and outside of the same relational-characterological phenomenon.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-067-023: T4 identified that God's goodness as a character attribute is unconditional while the human's ongoing experience of its relational benefits is conditional (Q&A-100). T5 named the transformation arcs t…
findings.finding_value: T4 identified that God's goodness as a character attribute is unconditional while the human's ongoing experience of its relational benefits is conditional (Q&A-100). T5 named the transformation arcs through which the conditional dimension operates: the positive transformation arc (encounter → trust → reorientation → overflow) is the arc in which the conditional relational experience is deepened; the moral awareness arc (recognition → loathing → repentance) is the arc that recovers the relational experience when it has been lost through departure. T4's human-to-God enabling inner postures (waiting, seeking, trust — Q&A-104) correspond to T5's formation mechanisms: the posture of waiting corresponds to the encounter mechanism (sustained receptive openness); the moral awareness arc is the recovery mechanism for the person who has departed from the relational posture. Together: T5's formative processes are the mechanisms through which T4's relational conditions are entered, sustained, and restored. Transformation and relationship are inseparable in goodness.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-067-025: T4 confirmed that the God-to-human direction of goodness is initiatory, generous, and sustaining (Q&A-101). T7 confirms that the primary literary form carrying divine goodness (prophetic covenantal ad…
findings.finding_value: T4 confirmed that the God-to-human direction of goodness is initiatory, generous, and sustaining (Q&A-101). T7 confirms that the primary literary form carrying divine goodness (prophetic covenantal address at Mic 6:8, doxological Psalm declarations, Pauline epistolary) all use forms that emphasise divine initiative and human receptivity. T7's literary analysis (Q&A-178-179) reveals that the literary forms carrying goodness are theologically intentional: the covenant lawsuit form (Mic 6:8) establishes divine initiative in defining the good; the invitation form ("taste and see" — Psa 34:8) establishes divine initiative in the encounter; the indicative-imperative structure of Col 3:12 (God has made you chosen → therefore put on kindness) establishes divine prior action before human response. T7's literary analysis confirms T4's relational architecture through the literary forms that carry them: the literature itself models the God-initiates-human-responds structure.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-103-004: Love's relational architecture is structured by three directional axes — GOD → HUMAN, HUMAN → GOD, HUMAN → HUMAN — with divine love structurally prior and causally generative of all subsequent love. 1…
findings.finding_value: Love's relational architecture is structured by three directional axes — GOD → HUMAN, HUMAN → GOD, HUMAN → HUMAN — with divine love structurally prior and causally generative of all subsequent love. 1Jo 4:19 ('we love because he first loved us') is the axis-precedence statement: the first axis is not responsive to but constitutive of the second and third. The GOD → HUMAN direction moves through four mechanisms: covenantal declaration (naming the beloved — Jer 12:7, Mat 3:17), Spirit-infusion (Rom 5:5), redemptive acts (Joh 3:16), and covenantal covering (Eze 16:8). The HUMAN → GOD direction requires total inner mobilisation (Mat 22:37 — all heart, soul, mind) and the clearing of rival loves as its condition (1Jo 4:19, 1Ti 6:10). The HUMAN → HUMAN direction spans five structural types (neighbour, enemy, community, friendship, family) and creates the social architecture described in Q&A-088 (restructured kinship, public legibility, competitive generosity). The most significant finding in T4: the human-to-God direction is conditioned by prior reception of divine love — the capacity for human love toward God is itself a gift. The one structural gap: T4.6 (spiritual beings) is absent from the evidence.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-003: Love's definition as directed attachment reaches its relational specification in T4's three-axis architecture. The object-determination principle (Q&A-144) — that love's moral quality depends entirely…
findings.finding_value: Love's definition as directed attachment reaches its relational specification in T4's three-axis architecture. The object-determination principle (Q&A-144) — that love's moral quality depends entirely on its object — is enacted relationally when the proper objects are named: God (vertical-ascending), neighbour and enemy (horizontal), and the beloved community (horizontal-mutual). The definition's three registers map onto the relational axes: the dispositional register (stable inner orientation) grounds the covenantal-faithful love in the GOD→HUMAN axis (God's chesed never ceasing — Lam 3:22); the active register (commanded, exercised) grounds the love of neighbour and enemy (Lev 19:18, Mat 5:44); the condition register (being-loved as identity) is the GOD→HUMAN axis's effect in the person (agapētos — constituted as beloved). The relational interfaces reveal what the definition describes abstractly: love's mechanism in concrete directional operation. The most significant inter-tier finding: the definition's requirement that love be directed toward an object is fulfilled eschatologically when the object is perfectly and permanently God — Jer 31:34, 1Jo 4:18 (perfect love).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-008: The constitutional location data and the relational interface data converge on the same structural claim: love's inner depth is its relational reach. The deeper love is constitutionally (heart-inscrib…
findings.finding_value: The constitutional location data and the relational interface data converge on the same structural claim: love's inner depth is its relational reach. The deeper love is constitutionally (heart-inscribed, soul-constitutive, Spirit-sourced), the further its relational reach — from neighbour-love (soul-level reciprocal) to enemy-love (will-level against grain) to divine love (Spirit-level transcendent). The constitutional movement pattern (Spirit → heart → soul → body — Q&A-056) maps onto the relational directional pattern: divine love enters at the deepest constitutional level (Spirit, heart) and produces relational acts at the outermost level (community legibility, bodily expression). The GOD→HUMAN axis operates at the constitutional depth where love is received (heart-infusion — Rom 5:5); the HUMAN→GOD axis requires total constitutional mobilisation (Mat 22:37 — all heart, soul, mind); the HUMAN→HUMAN axis is the outward bodily expression of the internal constitutional reality. Constitutional and relational are thus not two separate dimensions of love but the inside and outside of the same movement.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-016: The relational interface structure and the formation process are interdependent: the formation process is directed toward equipping the person for love's three relational axes, and the relational axes…
findings.finding_value: The relational interface structure and the formation process are interdependent: the formation process is directed toward equipping the person for love's three relational axes, and the relational axes are the context in which formation occurs. GOD→HUMAN axis as formation ground: divine love received (1Jo 4:19) is the formative act that establishes the person's capacity for all subsequent love — receiving is formation's enabling event. HUMAN→GOD axis as formation goal: total inner mobilisation (Mat 22:37 — all heart, soul, mind) is the fully formed love toward God; partial mobilisation marks love still in formation. HUMAN→HUMAN axis as formation context: community (1Pe 1:22, Tit 2:4) is both the goal-state (mutual love as community identity — Joh 13:35) and the formation context (love formed through exercising love within community). The reversibility asymmetry (divine love irreversible; human love subject to redirection) maps onto the axis structure: the GOD→HUMAN axis is the stable ground; the HUMAN→GOD and HUMAN→HUMAN axes are the formation-dependent expressions. Formation deepens the second and third axes; the first axis does not depend on formation.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-018: The evidential foundation directly supports each of the three relational axes. GOD→HUMAN axis — most densely evidenced: Exo 34:6 (divine self-declaration of love as primary attribute), Jer 12:7 (belov…
findings.finding_value: The evidential foundation directly supports each of the three relational axes. GOD→HUMAN axis — most densely evidenced: Exo 34:6 (divine self-declaration of love as primary attribute), Jer 12:7 (beloved of God's soul), Mat 3:17 (beloved Son named), Joh 3:16 (God so loved the world), Rom 5:5 (love poured into hearts through Spirit). The lexical evidence for this axis runs from the OT's chesed-God group (169 active verses — largest single group in the registry, Q&A-038) through the NT's agapē-God group (35 relevant). HUMAN→GOD axis — Psa 63:3 (chesed above life), Mat 22:37 (total inner mobilisation), Joh 14:15 (love producing obedience); these are carried by the agapaō-love-of-God group (571-001) and the chesed-human group (536-002). HUMAN→HUMAN axis — Lev 19:18 (neighbour-love commandment), Mat 5:44 (enemy-love), Joh 13:34 (new commandment), Joh 13:35 (community identity); these span the rea-group (173 active), the agapaō-mutual group (571-004, 53 relevant), and the filadelfia group (558-001). The evidential foundation confirms that all three axes have strong lexical and verse-level grounding, with the GOD→HUMAN axis carrying the greatest evidential weight.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-111-004: Reading T4 as a whole reveals mercy's relational architecture as directional and asymmetric in all three interface directions (God→human, human→God, human→human), with a structural requirement that re…
findings.finding_value: Reading T4 as a whole reveals mercy's relational architecture as directional and asymmetric in all three interface directions (God→human, human→God, human→human), with a structural requirement that receiving precedes giving. The key synthesis across T4: (a) God-to-human direction is the most extensively evidenced and is the source of mercy in all other directions; (b) human-to-God direction is characterised by normative ongoing supplication — not exceptional crisis-response; (c) human-to-human direction requires prior receipt from God and solidarity-knowledge of the condition being addressed; (d) mercy operates characteristically across relational distance and rupture (Q&A-117), not within maintained relationships; (e) the scope is wide (crossing covenantal boundaries) but not unconditionally permanent (withdrawal is named possibility). The T4 synthesis: mercy's relational architecture is an asymmetric chain — divine mercy → received human mercy → extended human mercy — with the chain requiring the prior link at each stage.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-030-004: T4 as a whole reveals contrition's relational structure is strongly asymmetric: the God-to-human and human-to-God directions are richly evidenced; the human-to-human and spiritual-beings directions ar…
findings.finding_value: T4 as a whole reveals contrition's relational structure is strongly asymmetric: the God-to-human and human-to-God directions are richly evidenced; the human-to-human and spiritual-beings directions are thin or silent. The asymmetry is analytically significant — contrition is primarily a vertical characteristic. What the tier establishes collectively is that contrition constitutes the condition for divine-human relational proximity. The key T4 synthesis: the God-to-human direction (God draws near, dwells with, looks to the contrite) and the human-to-God direction (the contrite person approaches God in lowliness) together create the relational event that contrition is. Neither direction alone describes contrition — it is the convergence of the two movements: divine movement toward the contrite, and creaturely movement toward God through brokenness. The substitutionary group (Isa 53:5) is the only instance of contrition vocabulary operating horizontally — and it is unique to the Servant, not a general pattern.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-010: The definition tier (T1) establishes that contrition operates in three modes along different relational axes; the relational interface tier (T4) maps those axes to specific directional relationships. …
findings.finding_value: The definition tier (T1) establishes that contrition operates in three modes along different relational axes; the relational interface tier (T4) maps those axes to specific directional relationships. The mapping is precise: the penitential mode (T1) corresponds to the human-to-God direction (T4.2) and generates the divine-to-human response (T4.1). The substitutionary mode (T1) corresponds to the only evidence of contrition operating horizontally (T4.3 — Isa 53:5). T1's three-mode structure and T4's directional structure are the same phenomenon described from two perspectives: modes describe what kind of crushing; directions describe who is involved in the relational event. The convergence confirms that contrition is inherently a relational event — its definition cannot be separated from its directional structure.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-023: The relational tier (T4) establishes that contrition creates the condition for divine-human relational proximity; the formative tier (T5) shows that this relational positioning is the goal of contriti…
findings.finding_value: The relational tier (T4) establishes that contrition creates the condition for divine-human relational proximity; the formative tier (T5) shows that this relational positioning is the goal of contrition's formative work. Together T4 and T5 reveal that contrition's formation is relational formation — the character produced by repeated contrition is not moral character in the abstract but the specific relational disposition of creaturely proximity to God. The settled lowliness produced by T5 is precisely the inner posture that T4 names as the condition for divine dwelling and divine looking. Formation (T5) and relational positioning (T4) are therefore the same reality described longitudinally and synchronically: T5 shows the character being formed; T4 shows what that character makes possible.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-062-004: T4 reveals fellowship as the most relationally comprehensive characteristic in the registry: it operates in all four primary directions (God-to-human, human-to-God, human-giving, human-receiving) and …
findings.finding_value: T4 reveals fellowship as the most relationally comprehensive characteristic in the registry: it operates in all four primary directions (God-to-human, human-to-God, human-giving, human-receiving) and partially in the spiritual-beings direction. The key T4 synthesis: 1Jo 1:3's structural claim — horizontal fellowship is derived from and grounded in vertical fellowship — means the relational architecture of fellowship is hierarchical: the divine-human fellowship is primary; human-human fellowship is its extension and expression. The scope analysis (Q&A-119) reveals that fellowship scope narrows as its depth increases: all-the-living (widest) → God-fearers → covenant partner → ecclesial body → divine nature participants (deepest-narrowest). Depth and breadth are inversely proportional in fellowship's relational structure.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-010: T1's five modes correspond directly to T4's relational directions: existential mode = all-the-living (widest scope); companionship mode = human-to-human (giving and receiving); covenantal mode = coven…
findings.finding_value: T1's five modes correspond directly to T4's relational directions: existential mode = all-the-living (widest scope); companionship mode = human-to-human (giving and receiving); covenantal mode = covenant partner; ontological mode = human-to-God (deepest). The scope-narrows-as-depth-increases finding (T4, Q&A-119) is the relational expression of T1's definition: as the fellowship object becomes more specific (from all-the-living to divine nature), the depth increases while the scope narrows. T1's structural negative (misdirected fellowship) maps onto T4's receiving-direction analysis (Hos 4:17 — prior wrong fellowship blocks reception of right fellowship).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-015: T2's constitutional origin analysis (multiple origins — divine initiative, human volitional alignment, existential given) directly maps onto T4's relational directions: divine initiative (God-to-human…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional origin analysis (multiple origins — divine initiative, human volitional alignment, existential given) directly maps onto T4's relational directions: divine initiative (God-to-human direction — T4.1); human volitional alignment (human-to-God and human-giving — T4.2, T4.3); existential given (the condition of all-the-living — T4.5 scope analysis). The constitutional origin determines the relational direction: the mode of fellowship's origin determines who is the primary relational agent in that mode.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-019: T3's faculty engagements all run in the same relational direction that T4 identifies as primary (vertical — human toward God). Perception, volition, moral evaluation, conscientiousness, and relational…
findings.finding_value: T3's faculty engagements all run in the same relational direction that T4 identifies as primary (vertical — human toward God). Perception, volition, moral evaluation, conscientiousness, and relational capacity are all deepened when directed toward the right fellowship object (God and God-fearers). T3's bilateral finding (right fellowship deepens; wrong fellowship degrades) explains T4's structural negative (misdirected fellowship is more dangerous than absence — Hos 4:17, Mat 23:30): when every faculty is progressively shaped by the fellowship object, misdirected fellowship progressively degrades every faculty, not just the relational capacity.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-023: T4's relational architecture (vertical primary; horizontal derived) and T5's formation arc (habituation → constitutional character) are structurally connected through 1Jo 1:3: the horizontal fellowshi…
findings.finding_value: T4's relational architecture (vertical primary; horizontal derived) and T5's formation arc (habituation → constitutional character) are structurally connected through 1Jo 1:3: the horizontal fellowship is derived from and grounded in the vertical (T4), and the vertical fellowship is the source from which the horizontal formation extends (T5 — the person who has received divine fellowship can extend human fellowship that is grounded in that divine reality). T4's scope-narrows-as-depth-increases finding is T5's formation telos: the deepest fellowship (divine nature participation — 2Pe 1:4) is also the narrowest in scope and the furthest eschatological endpoint.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-025: T4's relational directions map directly onto T7's literary forms. The divine-to-human direction (T4.1) is primarily carried by the apostolic epistolary setting (2Pe 1:4, 2Cor 13:14, 1Jo 1:3). The huma…
findings.finding_value: T4's relational directions map directly onto T7's literary forms. The divine-to-human direction (T4.1) is primarily carried by the apostolic epistolary setting (2Pe 1:4, 2Cor 13:14, 1Jo 1:3). The human-to-God direction (T4.2) is primarily carried by wisdom poetry (Psa 119:63, Phili 3:10) and apostolic letter (Phili 3:10). The human-giving direction (T4.3) is carried by wisdom poetry (Ecc 4:10), apostolic letter (2Cor 1:7), and covenantal text (Mal 2:14). The literary form determines which relational direction is expressed: the apostolic letter form enables the most explicit vertical formulation; wisdom poetry enables the most explicit horizontal formulation.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-064-004: T4 establishes the most structurally developed relational architecture of any characteristic reviewed in this series. All four primary directions are fully evidenced: God-to-human (the dominant vertic…
findings.finding_value: T4 establishes the most structurally developed relational architecture of any characteristic reviewed in this series. All four primary directions are fully evidenced: God-to-human (the dominant vertical direction — exclusively divine in the OT salach domain), human-to-God (seeking-forgiveness — intercession and confession), human-giving (commanded horizontal), human-receiving (implied in the horizontal transaction). The spiritual-beings direction adds the Holy Spirit as the enabling mediator (Joh 20:22-23) and the unforgivable sin as the outer limit (Mar 3:29). The vertical-horizontal interdependence (Mat 18:35; Mat 6:14-15) is the most structurally developed relational feature: the human-giving direction is structurally conditioned on the human-receiving direction (one who genuinely received divine forgiveness can genuinely extend human forgiveness). The scope analysis shows: universal access through faith (Act 10:43) with an absolute outer limit (Mar 3:29). T4's synthesis: forgiveness has the fullest relational architecture of the characteristics reviewed — every direction is evidenced, and the vertical-horizontal interdependence is a structural claim unique to forgiveness.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-010: T1's four modes map directly onto T4's relational directions. Covenantal-objective mode = God-to-human (cultic ritual mediated); divine relational-personal = God-to-human (personal declaratory); inter…
findings.finding_value: T1's four modes map directly onto T4's relational directions. Covenantal-objective mode = God-to-human (cultic ritual mediated); divine relational-personal = God-to-human (personal declaratory); intercessory = human-to-God on behalf of others; human horizontal = human-giving and human-receiving. The vertical-horizontal interdependence (T4 — the structural claim that receiving divine forgiveness enables extending human forgiveness) is the relational expression of T1's layered modes (the horizontal mode assumes the divine relational-personal mode has operated). T1's structural negative (retained claim = inner torment) is T4's receiving-blocked condition (Hos 4:17 parallel — wrong prior alignment blocks reception of right offering; Mat 18:35 — unforgiveness calling into question whether divine forgiveness was genuinely received).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-015: T2's constitutional origin (divine character as the source — Psa 86:5, Psa 130:4) explains T4's God-to-human directional dominance. Because forgiveness originates exclusively in divine character at th…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional origin (divine character as the source — Psa 86:5, Psa 130:4) explains T4's God-to-human directional dominance. Because forgiveness originates exclusively in divine character at the deepest level, the primary relational direction is necessarily God-initiated toward the human. T2's heart-locus requirement (Mat 18:35) explains T4's giving-direction requirement: genuine horizontal forgiveness requires the same constitutional depth as the received vertical (heart-level in both cases). The somatic-compassion origin (T2.5) is the constitutional enabler of the horizontal-giving direction (T4.3): the person who genuinely gives forgiveness does so from a somatic-affective inner origin (splagchnizomai), not merely a verbal performance.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-019: T3's faculty engagements all point in the same relational directions that T4 identifies as primary. Conscience (T3.9) is engaged in both the seeking-forgiveness direction (human-to-God: confession as …
findings.finding_value: T3's faculty engagements all point in the same relational directions that T4 identifies as primary. Conscience (T3.9) is engaged in both the seeking-forgiveness direction (human-to-God: confession as conscience's public verdict) and the giving direction (human horizontal: the conscience that recognises the offence to be released). Memory (T3.3) is engaged in the God-to-human direction (divine "remember no more" — Jer 31:34) and the human-giving direction (releasing the memory's active use against the offender). Volition (T3.6) drives the giving direction (heart-level release is chosen). The vertical-horizontal interdependence (T4 structural claim) is the relational expression of T3's conscience-and-volition faculty account: the person whose conscience has accurately received the magnitude of divine forgiveness has the volitional capacity to extend horizontal forgiveness.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-025: T4's relational directions map onto T7's literary forms. The God-to-human direction (T4.1 — dominant) is carried by the cultic-legal corpus (H5545 Niphal — God forgives, people receive), the prophetic…
findings.finding_value: T4's relational directions map onto T7's literary forms. The God-to-human direction (T4.1 — dominant) is carried by the cultic-legal corpus (H5545 Niphal — God forgives, people receive), the prophetic corpus (Jer 31:34 — divine forgiveness promise), and the apostolic letter corpus (Eph 1:7 — through his blood). The human-to-God direction (T4.2 — seeking) is carried by the penitential psalm corpus (Psa 130, Dan 9) and the Synoptic narrative (1Jo 1:9). The horizontal-giving direction (T4.3) is carried by the Synoptic parable corpus (Mat 18:23-35) and the apostolic command corpus (Eph 4:32; Luk 17:3-4). T7's literary forms are the evidential vehicles for T4's relational directions — each direction has a primary literary home.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-004: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion…
findings.finding_value: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion on whom I have compassion"), covenantally grounded (chesed as the bond-loyalty that grounds the characteristic), and situationally responsive (splanchnizō — triggered by the specific sight of suffering). These three bases are not in tension but in integration: divine compassion is free, covenanted, and responsive simultaneously. The scope finding is among the most analytically significant in the registry: compassion explicitly and repeatedly crosses covenantal boundaries (Nineveh, the Samaritan/Jew axis, the power-asymmetric relationship). Scope is defined by perceived need, not moral standing or covenantal membership — this is formally confirmed in the data and distinguishes compassion from many other relational characteristics. The chesed/splanchnizō distinction maps onto distinct relational registers: chesed sustains within established bonds; splanchnizō extends across distance and difference. T4.4 (receiver's inner-being experience) is the most significant gap — four P-rated prompts, entirely absent from the data. T4.6 (spiritual beings interface) is entirely silent across all four prompts.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-004: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — a…
findings.finding_value: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — all God-as-subject). The basis of divine extension is the giver's character and prior knowing (Exo 33:17 — "I know you by name"), not the receiver's merit — neither merit-based nor arbitrary. The human-to-God direction is specifically supplication: tachanum (H8469) is the receiving side's corresponding vocabulary built into the same root family as the giving side (chen/chanan) — the vocabulary embeds the two-directional circuit in a single root. The human-giving direction extends grace horizontally through three modes: forgiving (charizō — Eph 4:32), gracious conduct (chen as character quality — 889-003), and gracious speech (SD022). The receiving direction is the most underexamined (T4.4 — P-rated throughout); the scope analysis (T4.5) reveals grace crossing covenantal and social boundaries (Ruth narrative — grace in the context of foreign status and vulnerability). T4.6 (spiritual beings) is evidenced at one point: Luk 1:28 (kecharitōmenē — the angel's announcement), which implies angelic ministry as a vehicle of grace rather than grace operating independently in the spiritual-beings register. T4 synthesis: the relational architecture of grace is unique in the programme — it is the only characteristic where the giving-side vocabulary and the receiving-side vocabulary are built from the same root (chen/tachanum), encoding the grace-circuit's two-sidedness at the lexical level.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-010: T1's four modes of operation map onto T4's four relational directions. The sovereign-bestowal mode corresponds to the God-to-human direction (T4.1 — primary and dominant). The covenantal-relational-su…
findings.finding_value: T1's four modes of operation map onto T4's four relational directions. The sovereign-bestowal mode corresponds to the God-to-human direction (T4.1 — primary and dominant). The covenantal-relational-sustaining mode corresponds to the relational scope (T4.5 — grace operating within and across covenantal boundaries). The capacity-conferring mode corresponds to the human-to-God direction in its supplication register (T4.2 — SD026: grace giving even the capacity to appeal). The character-forming mode corresponds to the human-giving direction (T4.3 — gracious conduct and speech as the horizontal expression of received grace-character). The vocabulary's structural insight (T4 synthesis: giving-side and receiving-side built from the same root, chen/tachanum) explains T1's finding that grace requires the receptor's inner engagement to complete its operation — the vocabulary encodes the two-sidedness because grace is constitutively a two-sided circuit.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-015: T2's origin analysis (grace does not originate in the human constitutional system — it arrives from God) and T4's directional analysis (God-to-human is primary and dominant) are the same finding from …
findings.finding_value: T2's origin analysis (grace does not originate in the human constitutional system — it arrives from God) and T4's directional analysis (God-to-human is primary and dominant) are the same finding from constitutional and relational perspectives respectively. The spirit level as reception point (T2.1) and the God-to-human direction as primary (T4.1) are mutually explanatory: because grace originates with God and is received at the spirit level, the primary relational direction is necessarily God-initiated toward the human spirit. The human-to-God direction (T4.2 — supplication) corresponds to T2.10's constitutional movement in reverse: the soul's recognition of need translates into the somatic enactment of supplication (prostration, fasting, sackcloth), which is T2.7's bidirectional body-soul finding. Constitutional location and relational direction are co-determining.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-019: T3's agency-constituting finding (grace constitutes rather than replaces agency — 1Cor 15:10) and T4's human-to-God direction (supplication as the human posture of appeal — requiring genuine human age…
findings.finding_value: T3's agency-constituting finding (grace constitutes rather than replaces agency — 1Cor 15:10) and T4's human-to-God direction (supplication as the human posture of appeal — requiring genuine human agency in the act of plea) are structurally aligned. The constituted agency (T3.7) is precisely the agency that supplication requires: the creature must genuinely appeal, not merely receive passively. T3's finding that grace and conscience are mutually necessary (T3.9) corresponds to T4's relational-access finding: grace transforms the threshold of human-to-God approach (prosagōgē — SD035) from impassable to open, which is the relational expression of T3.9's constitutional finding that grace creates the condition within which conscience can operate fully without destruction. T3 names the inner-being event; T4 names the relational consequence of the same event.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-023: T4's relational directions correspond to T5's formation mechanisms. The God-to-human direction (T4.1 — sovereign bestowal) corresponds to the encounter and spirit-outpouring mechanisms (T5.3 — sudden …
findings.finding_value: T4's relational directions correspond to T5's formation mechanisms. The God-to-human direction (T4.1 — sovereign bestowal) corresponds to the encounter and spirit-outpouring mechanisms (T5.3 — sudden specific relational event; Zec 12:10). The human-to-God direction (T4.2 — supplication) corresponds to the sustained-formation arc of T5.5: the person who habitually supplicates is being formed into the character that supplicates, which is itself the character-quality kind identified in T1. The human-giving direction (T4.3 — gracious forgiving, speech-grace) corresponds to T5.3's mediated-transformation mechanism (grace → tenderheartedness → forgiving → gracious speech — SD030, Eph 4:32). T4 describes the relational shape of each mechanism; T5 describes the inner formation process each mechanism produces.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-025: T4's most analytically distinctive finding (the vocabulary encodes the two-sided grace-circuit in a single root: chen/chanan for giving; tachanum/techinah for seeking) is T7's most significant root-le…
findings.finding_value: T4's most analytically distinctive finding (the vocabulary encodes the two-sided grace-circuit in a single root: chen/chanan for giving; tachanum/techinah for seeking) is T7's most significant root-level finding. T7.1 confirms: the chen root family embeds both the giving side (chen — favour, chanan — to be gracious) and the receiving-seeking side (tachanum, techinah — supplication) in a single etymological family. This is unique in the programme's vocabulary data: no other characteristic has the giving-side and receiving-side vocabulary built from the same root. T4's relational architecture and T7's lexical analysis are the relational and lexical descriptions of the same structural reality — that grace is constitutively a two-sided circuit whose two sides are inseparable at the root level.

findings.session_b_note: Yes — the human-toward-God direction is extensively evidenced as the responsive axis of the covenant relationship. (1) Covenant entry as movement toward God: Neh 10:29 — "enter into a curse and an oath to walk in God's Law" — the community moves toward God through formal covenantal commitment (OBS-034-035). 2Ki 23:3 — the king "made a covenant before the Lord, to walk after the Lord" — covenant-making is explicitly a movement toward God (OBS-034-047). (2) Covenant-keeping as sustained movement: Deu 7:9 — "those who love him and keep his commandments" — sustained love and commandment-keeping as the ongoing human posture toward God within the covenant (OBS-034-039). Psa 25:10 — "those who keep his covenant and his testimonies" — covenant-keeping as a description of the person who walks with God. (3) Confession of covenant breach as movement back toward God: Dan 9:11 (OBS-034-036) — Daniel's prayer is a movement of confessional return toward God after covenant failure — using covenantal language to re-engage the God whose covenant has been broken. (4) Swearing by God's name as allegiance (3308-003 — OBS-034-055): taking an oath in God's name as an act of inner allegiance directed toward God.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-034-004: T4 as a whole reveals that covenant's relational interface structure is asymmetric but genuinely bilateral. The God-to-human direction (T4.1) is the founding and sustaining axis — God initiates, commi…
findings.finding_value: T4 as a whole reveals that covenant's relational interface structure is asymmetric but genuinely bilateral. The God-to-human direction (T4.1) is the founding and sustaining axis — God initiates, commits, inscribes, and mediates. The human-to-God direction (T4.2) is the responsive axis — the whole person moves toward God through commitment, love, and faithfulness. The horizontal directions (T4.3 giving; T4.4 receiving) are genuine but secondary, and the evidence shows they are grounded in and enabled by the vertical. The relational scope expands progressively across the covenant trajectory — from particular (Abraham) to expanding (Israel) to universal (new covenant in Christ). The spiritual-beings interface (T4.6) is largely absent from the data — the only relevant material is the pagan deity named "lord of covenant" (H1286) and the inferred adversarial spiritual claim. T4 as a whole shows that covenant's relational architecture is constituted by God's prior initiative and realised through the whole person's responsive engagement.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-015: T2 reveals that covenant operates constitutionally in the heart, mind, soul, mouth, and body. T4 reveals that covenant operates relationally through God-to-human, human-to-God, and horizontal interfac…
findings.finding_value: T2 reveals that covenant operates constitutionally in the heart, mind, soul, mouth, and body. T4 reveals that covenant operates relationally through God-to-human, human-to-God, and horizontal interfaces. The T2 × T4 synthesis: the constitutional locations and the relational interfaces are not separate registers — they are the same inner reality viewed from different angles. The soul's engagement in covenant (T2 — "with all his heart and all his soul") is precisely the inner posture required for genuine human-to-God movement (T4.2 — Q&A-106). The mouth as constitutional location (T2 — Isa 59:21) is the organ through which the human-to-God relational direction is enacted (oath as speech act — Q&A-024, T1.4). The blood as somatic covenant-medium (T2 — Q&A-053) is the mediating substance through which the God-to-human interface is constituted (the blood of the covenant — Q&A-101). Constitutional location and relational interface are two views of the same inner-being dynamic.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-019: T3 reveals that the inner faculties covenant most deeply engages are Other-oriented (relational capacity, conscience, moral evaluation, memory). T4 reveals that covenant's relational interfaces are as…
findings.finding_value: T3 reveals that the inner faculties covenant most deeply engages are Other-oriented (relational capacity, conscience, moral evaluation, memory). T4 reveals that covenant's relational interfaces are asymmetric (God initiates; human responds; horizontal is grounded in vertical). The T3 × T4 synthesis: the Other-oriented faculty bias (T3) and the asymmetric relational structure (T4) are coherently related — the inner faculties that covenant engages are precisely those required for the kind of asymmetric responsive relationship that covenant constitutes. The relational capacity (T3.11) is the constitutional equipment for genuine connection; the covenant's relational interfaces (T4) are the actual connections that this capacity enables. The inner posture required for human-to-God covenant movement (T4.2 — Q&A-106: reverent fear, love, all-heart, hearing orientation) corresponds directly to the inner faculties that covenant engages: fear engages moral evaluation (T3.8), love engages affect and relational capacity (T3.4, T3.11), all-heart engages volition (T3.6), and hearing engages perception (T3.1). T3 and T4 are two analytical views of the same responsive inner-being structure.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-025: T4 establishes that covenant's relational interfaces are carried through specific acts — oath-taking, blood-shedding, covenant-meal participation, circumcision. T7 establishes that these acts are carr…
findings.finding_value: T4 establishes that covenant's relational interfaces are carried through specific acts — oath-taking, blood-shedding, covenant-meal participation, circumcision. T7 establishes that these acts are carried by specific literary forms — legal-narrative (covenant-making), prophetic oracle (new covenant promise), liturgical (Eucharist), and epistle-argument (Hebrews). The T4 × T7 synthesis: the relational acts of covenant (T4) are embedded in and shaped by their literary contexts (T7). The covenantal meal (T4 receiving — Q&A-113) is not merely a relational act but a liturgical-formular act (T7). The prophetic oracle of the new covenant (Jer 31:31-34) is not merely a T4 divine-to-human act of declaration but is embedded in the prophetic genre's authority structures (T7). The literary form analysis (T7) provides the interpretive framework within which the relational interface data (T4) must be read. Responsible interpretation of the covenantal acts requires attention to their literary embedding.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-099-004: T4 reveals that kindness operates across all four relational directions for which evidence exists — God-to-human (most extensively evidenced), human-to-God (appeal/chasid identity mode), human giving,…
findings.finding_value: T4 reveals that kindness operates across all four relational directions for which evidence exists — God-to-human (most extensively evidenced), human-to-God (appeal/chasid identity mode), human giving, human receiving, and communal — with spiritual beings being the only direction that is genuinely absent from the evidence. The structural finding: the four evidenced directions form a coherent circuit, not parallel independent operations. Divine kindness flows to the human → the human receives it and appeals to it (human-to-God) → the human, having received, is equipped and obligated to give it to others (human giving, grounded in Eph 4:32's "as God in Christ forgave you, be kind") → kindness given and received forms the communal relational fabric (chasidim assembly). The circuit is both moral and ontological: it is not merely that we ought to be kind because God is kind, but that the human person is constituted to be a bearer of the divine kindness in the relational world. T4's most significant intra-tier finding: the divine-to-human direction is the source and ground of all other directions — human giving of kindness is explicitly grounded in received divine kindness, making T4 a circuit with a single originating source.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-025: T4's finding that the divine-to-human direction is the most extensively evidenced direction in the registry is directly confirmed by T7's lexical finding: H2617A (chesed) group 536-001 (180 relevant v…
findings.finding_value: T4's finding that the divine-to-human direction is the most extensively evidenced direction in the registry is directly confirmed by T7's lexical finding: H2617A (chesed) group 536-001 (180 relevant verses, dominant subject GOD) is the largest single data group in the entire cross-registry material. The quantity of evidence for divine kindness toward humans is not an analytical artefact — it is a lexical and textual reality. T7's LXX finding (chesed → eleos/mercy) is relevant to T4's human-to-God direction: the LXX's emphasis on the mercy/compassion dimension over the faithfulness dimension may have shaped how the human-to-God movement was perceived in the Greek-speaking community — as appeal to divine mercy rather than appeal to divine faithfulness. The T7 primary anchor verse finding (Lam 3:22) is the definitive statement of the T4 divine-to-human direction in its fullest form: the anchor verse is chosen precisely because it asserts the T4 interface's stability (never ceasing, always available) under maximum relational pressure (Jerusalem destroyed, T4 interface apparently withdrawn). The two tiers together confirm that the divine-to-human relational interface is both the most evidenced and the most definitionally important direction for kindness.

findings.finding_value: T2 establishes the constitutional location of peace; T4 establishes the relational directions through which peace moves into and out of those locations. The synthesis: God gives peace (T4.1 → T2) by addressing the constitutional locations directly — the Aaronic blessing (Num 6:26) addresses the whole person; Joh 14:27 ("let not your hearts be troubled") addresses the heart specifically; Phili 4:7 ("peace will guard your hearts and minds") names both heart and mind as the guarded locations. The human receives peace (T4.4) through the same constitutional locations — the receptive soul (Psa 131:2, T2.2) and the directed mind (Isa 26:3, T2.4) are the reception points. The relational and constitutional analyses converge: peace moves through relational channels (T4) into constitutional locations (T2).

findings.finding_value: T4's God-to-human direction (peace given through covenant, word, cross, Spirit) maps onto T5's mechanisms (proclamation, covenant-ground, cross-accomplishment, Spirit-formation) and sequences (gift received → heart/mind guarded → somatic rest → expressed in community). The developing scope of T4 (covenant → universal) maps onto T5's eschatological trajectory: the expanding relational scope and the deepening eschatological fullness are the same movement outward from its source in God's identity as peace. The T4 finding that peace refused worsens peacelessness (Q&A-114) connects to T5's reversibility finding (T5.1.2) — the experiential peace is reversible in both directions: given and received, or offered and refused.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-060-004: T4 as a whole reveals that the relational architecture of this characteristic is directionally structured and asymmetrical. The dominant direction is God-to-human (6 of 7 groups, confirmed across T4.1…
findings.finding_value: T4 as a whole reveals that the relational architecture of this characteristic is directionally structured and asymmetrical. The dominant direction is God-to-human (6 of 7 groups, confirmed across T4.1); the human direction is responsive (T4.2: human gives back what was first given). The basis of divine giving is plural — covenantal, responsive, formative, moral-consequential, eschatological-grace (Q&A-102) — revealing that faithfulness is not a single relational mode but a relational orientation that differentiates itself across relational conditions while remaining unified in character. The human-to-God direction reveals responsive correspondence as the relational structure (Q&A-107): the proper relational form is one in which the human gives back to God what is his (glory, praise, self), having first received. The human-to-human direction is thinner in the data (Q&A-109) — reflecting the registry's God-subject dominance. T4.6 is substantially silent on spiritual beings. What T4 reveals as a whole: faithfulness-as-giving is constitutively a divine-initiative relational reality that the human enters through responsive participation. The human's giving is always downstream of divine giving; the correspondence is the proper form of the relationship.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-012: The faculty engagement pattern (T3 — perception, affect, volition, relational capacity all engaged) and the relational interface structure (T4 — God-to-human, human-to-God) reveal a faculty-interface …
findings.finding_value: The faculty engagement pattern (T3 — perception, affect, volition, relational capacity all engaged) and the relational interface structure (T4 — God-to-human, human-to-God) reveal a faculty-interface correspondence. In the God-to-human direction: divine hearing (T3.1 — perception) precedes compassionate giving (T4.1 — responsive basis); divine affect (T3.4 — rahamim, leb) determines the direction of giving (T4.1 — basis of extension); divine relational capacity (T3.11) is the prior orientation that makes the giving possible. In the human-to-God direction: human perception (Q2 — recognising divine sovereignty), human affect (blessing under loss), human volition (choosing to give glory), and human relational capacity (genuine correspondence) are all required for the giving to be genuine (T4.2 — inner posture). What this pair reveals: the relational interfaces are not external channels through which giving flows; they are relational events in which the inner faculties of both parties are engaged simultaneously and correspondingly. The correspondence is not mechanical but genuinely personal.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-018: The relational interface analysis (T4 — six of seven groups are God-to-human; the divine disposition ranges from covenantal to compassionate to formative to moral-consequential) and the primary anchor…
findings.finding_value: The relational interface analysis (T4 — six of seven groups are God-to-human; the divine disposition ranges from covenantal to compassionate to formative to moral-consequential) and the primary anchor identification (T7 — Hos 11:8 as the verse that uniquely reveals the divine inner-being decision structure) converge. Hos 11:8 is the primary anchor precisely because it holds the full complexity of T4 in a single verse: it shows the God-to-human relational direction (the giving is addressed at Ephraim/Israel), the multiple bases of divine giving (deserved-judgement vs. compassionate restraint), and the divine disposition (heart recoiling, compassion warming). The full vocabulary arc (T7.1.10 — enacted + constituted poles) maps onto the two directions of T4: the enacted pole (na.tan) is the God-to-human and human-to-God relational act; the constituted pole (emunah/hesed/pistis) is the dispositional quality that makes the relational giving faithful rather than merely generous. What this pair reveals: the relational architecture and the vocabulary architecture are the same structure described at two levels of abstraction.

Two directions. (1) Human hatred of God (group 3596 — 14 verses): "those who hate me" (Exo 20:5) — hating God is the defining inner orientation of those in covenant rupture. (2) Human hatred of evil as covenant alignment (group 550-NEW-02): Psa 97:10: "O you who love the Lord, hate evil!" — hating what God hates is an act of covenant participation. These are opposite expressions of the same relational orientation toward God.

The dominant movement is the human's contempt directed toward God: despising his name (Mal 1:6), treating his table as despicable (Mal 1:7, 12), spurning his counsel (Psa 107:11), saying in the heart "you will not call to account" (Psa 10:13). The inner posture required to sustain this is covenantal presumption — the assumption that God's claims are negotiable. Contempt toward God operates from within the covenantal relationship, making it a form of covenant betrayal from within.

The righteous abhorrence of evil as covenant alignment: Psa 119:163: "I hate and abhor falsehood, but I love your law" — the abhorrence of falsehood is the negative expression of what loving God's law means positively. In the inverted form: abhorring justice (Amo 5:10, Mic 3:9) is the inner movement away from God — those who abhor what God loves are moving against him in their inner constitution.

The ruthlessness of M06-D is the inner condition of those who have most comprehensively moved away from God — "they do not set God before themselves" (Psa 54:3). The ruthless person's inner movement is the maximum possible distance from God in the M06 cluster — not merely despising him or hating him but removing him from the inner governing framework entirely.

The dominant human-to-God movement in M06-E is appeal. Joel 2:17: "spare your people, O Lord, and make not your heritage a reproach." Psa 119:39: "turn away the reproach that I dread." Lam 5:1: "remember, O Lord, what has befallen us; look, and see our disgrace." The characteristic does not generate human contempt or hatred toward God — it generates the opposite: intense appeal from within the condition of being reproached.

Appeal is the dominant human-to-God movement. Psa 35:1: "contend, O Lord, with those who contend with me." Jer 18:19: "hear me, O Lord, and listen to the voice of my adversaries." The person facing an adversary turns to God and asks him to contend. The human-to-God movement in M06-F is the appeal-posture in the context of adversarial opposition.
No verse in M06-G shows malice operating in the human person's movement toward God. The malice of the nations is directed at Israel; God is named only as the judge of that malice. Silent.

The human-to-God direction for compassion is petitionary only: appealing to God's compassion, not showing it toward him. This is a structural asymmetry: compassion flows only downward (from greater to lesser), and the human is never the greater in relation to God.

**[A1 — God Righteousness]** Yes — the appeal to God's righteousness as the ground of petition is the primary human-to-God movement in A1. "In your righteousness deliver me" (Psa 31:1; 71:2; 143:1; 143:11, VSG M26-A1-004). The psalmist moves toward God through his righteousness — it becomes the ground of approach, of petition, of confident appeal. God's righteousness is not an obstacle to approach but the most secure ground of it.

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Yes — "everyone who practices righteousness has been born of him" (1Jo 2:29, VSG M26-A2-014) — practicing righteousness is itself an orientation toward God: it is the expression of the new birth. Walking with God (M26-A2-014) is the relational mode of human righteousness — righteousness as the orientation of the person toward God. Bringing offerings "in righteousness" (Mal 3:3, VSG M26-A2-014) — worship as the righteous person's movement toward God.

**[B — Moral Uprightness]** Yes — "whoever walks in uprightness fears the Lord" (Pro 14:2, VSG 1211-002). The walk in uprightness is simultaneously a walk toward the Lord — the two are inseparable. The preparation before God in prayer (a.rakh, Psa 5:3, VSG 6753-003 in the F-group): preparing oneself before God as an act of devotional orientation — the reckoning faculty in its devotional mode.

**[C — Justification]** Yes — receiving justification by faith is itself a movement toward God: the person who believes God (Rom 4:3–5) is turning toward him, accepting the basis he has provided for right standing. Justification creates the conditions for ongoing approach to God through the new standing it establishes.

**[D — Avenging Justice]** Yes — the cry for justice (Luk 18:3; Rev 6:10, VSG 944-001) is the primary human-to-God movement in D. The wronged person turns to God rather than to themselves — this is an act of faith and dependence: bringing the injustice to God and trusting him to respond.
**[E — Condemnation]** Freedom from condemnation enables movement toward God — but E itself does not primarily describe a human-to-God movement. Silence on direct human-to-God direction in E.

**[F — Moral Reckoning]** Yes — "count yourselves dead to sin and alive to God" (Rom 6:11) — the reckoning toward God is a movement of orientation: the person reckons themselves as belonging to and alive for God. The devotional preparation (a.rakh, Psa 5:3, VSG 6753-003): preparing oneself before God in prayer is the reckoning faculty directed toward God in worship.

**[CLUSTER — T4.2]** E. The human-to-God interface is present across the cluster: appeal on the basis of divine righteousness (A1), righteous living as movement toward God (A2), upright walk toward the Lord (B), receiving justification by faith (C), the cry for justice as dependent prayer (D), and the reckoning of oneself as alive to God (F). The cluster reveals that righteousness in all its modes orients the person toward God — it is constitutively God-ward.

findings.finding_value: M01-A extensively documents the human person moving toward God in reverential fear: (1) **worship** — Psa 5:7 (fear drawing the psalmist into the temple — "reverence for who God is motivates his approach to the temple and shapes his posture of bowing down"); Heb 12:28 (fear and awe as "the fitting inner disposition for approaching God in worship"); (2) **prayer** — Dan 9:4 (reverential fear of God as the inner disposition from which Daniel's prayer arises); Jer 26:19 (Hezekiah's fear producing active prayer that averted disaster); (3) **covenant** — Mal 2:5 (Levi's reverential fear as the covenant response to God's gift of life and peace — fear governing the covenant relationship); (4) **vow** — Jon 1:16 (the sailors' fear leading to sacrifice and vows — fear becoming the ground of devotion).

M01-E-VCG-02 shows the human person trembling before God's word as a specific mode of movement toward God: Isa 66:2 (trembling at God's word as the inner posture God looks for — the human person responsive before divine communication); Ezr 9:4; 10:3 (those who tremble at God's commandment gathering for covenant decision-making — trembling as the posture of covenant engagement).

M01-B shows movement toward God through the theophanic fear and subsequent worship: Jon 1:16 (storm-terror converting to reverential worship — "fear becomes the inner ground of devotion"); Mat 27:54 (centurion's fear producing confession — "Truly this was the Son of God"); Mat 9:8 (crowd's fear "moves inward immediately into glorifying God" — fear as gateway to worship).

The human-to-God movement across M01 is most extensively documented in M01-A (worship, prayer, covenant, vow) and M01-E-VCG-02 (trembling-at-word as the posture of receptive covenant engagement). M01-B shows fear functioning as a gateway to worship when the fear is triggered by encounter with divine power.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes — this is the dominant direction in the corpus. The vast majority of VCG-01's 58 verses show human exultation directed toward God: "my soul will rejoice in the Lord" (Psa 35:9); "I will greatly rejoice in the Lord; my soul shall exult in my God" (Isa 61:10); "yet I will rejoice in the Lord" (Hab 3:18); "exult in your name all the day" (Psa 89:16); "to God my exceeding joy" (Psa 43:4). The human-to-God direction is the primary mode of this characteristic.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes — this is the dominant direction in M04-B-VCG-05 (90 verses of God-directed psalmist and prophetic gladness) and throughout M04-C. The human-to-God direction includes: direct "rejoice in the Lord" commands (Psa 32:11; 97:12; Phili 4:4; 3:1); rejoicing in God's salvation as the psalmist's oriented movement (Psa 9:2; 14:7; 35:9; 53:6; 63:11; Isa 25:9; 61:10); the feast-joy before God at his sanctuary (Deu 12:7, 18; 16:11–15 — the spatial movement of Israel to the chosen place and the inner movement toward God); praise, thanksgiving, and prayer accompanying joy (Psa 100:2; Jer 33:11; Phili 4:4–6).

**[CHAR-7]** E — Yes: (1) **Worship and prayer** — Luk 10:21 (Jesus' agalliao immediately moves into addressed prayer: "I thank you, Father") — Suffering-Joy is the inner state that generates worshipful movement toward the Father; Luk 1:47 (Mary's spirit exults "in God my Savior" — the exultation is directed toward God as its object); Act 2:26 (tongue rejoicing → "my flesh also will dwell in hope" — the movement toward trust in God); (2) **Continued faithful mission** — Act 5:41 (apostles' rejoicing → continued teaching — the movement toward God through faithful mission-action); (3) **Joyful endurance** — Heb 12:2 (Christ's joy-grounded endurance of the cross — the cross as the climactic movement toward the Father's purpose).

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes. (1) **Doxological movement** — the ki-tov praise declarations (Psa 100:5; 106:1 — "give thanks to the Lord, for he is good") are the human person's movement toward God in recognition of his goodness; the formula frames thanksgiving and praise as the inner movement prompted by Gladness-recognition; (2) **Seeking** — Lam 3:25–26 ("the Lord is good to those who wait for him, to the soul who seeks him") — seeking God is the human movement that positions the person to experience his goodness; (3) **Gratitude** — Ezr 3:11 ("for he is good, for his steadfast love endures forever toward Israel" — responsive praise at the temple foundation); Deu 8:10 ("you shall bless the Lord your God for the good land") — receiving the good land occasions the movement of blessing toward God; (4) **Trust** — the entire M04-O-VCG-04 register shows the human person trusting in God's good promises as a movement of the inner being toward him.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes, in M04-G and M04-H's upward registers: (1) **Affective upward movement** — Psa 37:4 ("delight yourself in the Lord") — commanded upward orientation of the inner being toward God as its object; Isa 58:14 ("you shall take delight in the Lord") — Delight as the human person's movement toward God; Job 22:26 (future delight in the Almighty); Job 27:10 (the hypocrite who will not delight in the Almighty — exposing the expected upward movement as absent); (2) **Delight in God's word as movement toward God** — Psa 119 series (delight in statutes, testimonies, commandments, law — all as God's self-expression); Rom 7:22 ("I delight in the law of God, in my inner being") — the innermost self moving toward God through his word; (3) **Obedience-Delight** (M04-M) — Joh 8:29; 1Jo 3:22 — the soul's movement toward what pleases God as the sustaining orientation of the inner person's upward relationship; (4) **Seeking God's presence as Delight** — Psa 73:28 ("it is good to be near God") — the human person's inner experience of divine nearness as the supreme good, motivating continued movement toward it; (5) **Neh 1:11** — "who delight to fear your name" — the soul's reverential Delight in God's name as the form of upward movement.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes: (1) **Psa 27:4** — "one thing have I asked of the Lord, that will I seek after: that I may dwell in the house of the Lord… to gaze upon the beauty of the Lord" — the entire movement of the seeking person toward God is motivated by and culminates in Pleasure (gazing upon divine beauty); (2) **The ni.cho.ach worship acts** (M04-K-VCG-01) — the worshiper's act of offering correctly-prepared sacrifice is a movement toward God that produces the pleasing-aroma Pleasure relationship; human-to-God Pleasure operates through worship action; (3) **Psa 147:1** — "for it is good to sing praises to our God; for it is pleasant and a song of praise is fitting" — the pleasantness of praise as the experience of human worship-movement toward God; (4) **Psa 135:3** — "praise the Lord… for it is pleasant!" — pleasantness of worship as the felt quality of the human movement toward God in praise.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes: (1) **Wonder producing worship-movement** — the proclamatory corpus is consistently doxological: "sing to him, sing praises to him; tell of all his wondrous works" (1Ch 16:9) — Wonder moves the person toward God in praise; "I will give thanks to the Lord with my whole heart; I will recount all of your wonderful deeds" (Psa 9:1) — Wonder producing wholehearted Godward movement; (2) **Seeking to behold** — Psa 119:18 ("open my eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of your law") — Wonder-seeking in the law as movement toward God through his word; (3) **Contemplative movement** — Psa 119:27 ("make me understand the way of your precepts, and I will meditate on your wondrous works"); Psa 145:5 ("on your wondrous works, I will meditate") — sustained contemplative movement toward God through Wonder-meditation; (4) **Job's return** — Job 42:3 ("things too wonderful for me, which I did not know") — Job's Wonder-humility as the restored posture of a person returned to right relationship with God.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All seven evidence human-to-God operation, but with different relational profiles: (1) **Most dominantly human-to-God**: Exultation (Char 1) — the entire VCG-01 corpus is human exultation directed toward God (Psa 35:9; Isa 61:10; Hab 3:18); (2) **Extensively human-to-God**: Joy (Char 2) — M04-B-VCG-05 (90 verses of God-directed psalmist joy) and M04-C throughout; Wonder (Char 6) — the proclamatory corpus is consistently Godward (Psa 9:1; 1Ch 16:9); (3) **Devotionally human-to-God**: Delight (Char 4) — Psa 37:4 (delight yourself in the Lord), Psa 73:25 (nothing on earth I desire besides you), M04-G throughout; Gladness (Char 3) — ki-tov praise as Godward gladness-declaration; (4) **Worship-mediated human-to-God**: Pleasure (Char 5) — Psa 27:4 (seeking to gaze on God's beauty), ni.cho.ach worship-offering as human-to-God Pleasure-act; (5) **Paradox-grounded human-to-God**: Suffering-Joy (Char 7) — Luk 10:21 (Jesus' Spirit-rejoicing moving immediately into prayer to the Father); Luk 1:47 (Mary's spirit exulting in God my Savior). The cluster is primarily Godward: the seven characteristics are most fully realised when directed toward God as their object. Psa 43:4's "God my exceeding joy" names the characteristic's ultimate Godward orientation.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes, and the M07-C corpus (M07-C-VCG-01 and -03) is the primary evidence. The person in the M07-C mode moves toward God *through* shame: the penitential posture of lying down in shame (Jer 3:25, vc=37308/37470), the inability to lift the face to God that nonetheless constitutes a kind of prayer (Ezr 9:6), the conscience-driven shame that moves toward renewed service (2Ch 30:15). The M07-C-VCG-02 material shows the complementary movement: the person's movement toward God through trust simultaneously protects from shame — these are the two faces of the human-toward-God movement in shame's register (moving toward God through shame's guilt; moving toward God through trust and word). Both are movements toward God; they differ in what drives them (guilt-shame vs. confident trust).

**[CHAR-2]** E — Limited evidence. Eze 44:13 — Levites bearing shame as a restriction on their approach to God — shows CHAR-2 governing human-to-God access in the priestly context. CHAR-2 does not primarily operate as a human movement toward God; it is imposed on humans from God or from other humans.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Extensively evidenced in VCG-01. Joh 8:49 — "you dishonor me" (Jesus = God incarnate); Rom 2:23 — "you dishonor God by breaking the law"; Heb 6:6 — apostates "hold him up to contempt." The human-to-God direction of CHAR-3 is the active worth-denial of God's incarnate person and his moral authority. The inner posture required to avoid CHAR-3 toward God is described in its absence in Luk 18:2 — fearing God is the inner posture that prevents CHAR-3 toward God.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The idolatrous-shameful-objects register (VCG-01 — Jer 3:24; 11:13; Hos 9:10) is precisely about what the human conscience should assess as shameful in relation to God: the idol is "the shameful thing" (bo.shet — Jer 3:24) that has replaced God in the person's movement toward him. CHAR-4's proper functioning toward God means assessing idolatrous objects as shameful and recoiling from them toward God.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — Human-to-God CHAR-5 is evidenced in the mockery of Jesus (Luk 23:11 — Herod and his soldiers treating Jesus with contempt and mockery). The acts directed at Jesus in his passion are CHAR-5 in its most concentrated form: the world's contempt-verdict on God incarnate. Act 4:11 (the builders rejecting the cornerstone) shows the human rejection of God's sent-one as CHAR-5 directed toward God through the mediating agency of Jesus. The inner posture that prevents CHAR-5 toward God is the recognition of divine worth — receiving the despised as "an angel of God, as Christ Jesus" (Gal 4:14).

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — The primary human-to-God direction of CHAR-6 is worship and approach: Psa 26:6 — "I wash my hands in innocence and go around your altar, O Lord" — is the movement of the innocent person toward God in the cultic act of going around the altar. CHAR-6 is what enables this movement. The inner posture required is moral cleanness — the person who approaches God must have their inner moral condition aligned with the holiness they approach.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The human-to-God movement across M07 concentrates in three registers. (1) Shame-mediated approach — the guilt-shame of Char 1 (M07-C) and the innocence-enabled approach of Char 6 constitute the two poles of the human-to-God encounter: shame as recognition of moral inadequacy before holiness (Ezr 9:6); innocence as the condition enabling approach without guilt's barrier (Psa 26:6). These two poles are the cluster's most theologically significant human-to-God dimension. (2) Dishonour and contempt directed at God incarnate — Chars 3 and 5 evidence the human actively dishonouring God incarnate (Joh 8:49; Rom 2:23) and directing contempt toward Jesus (Luk 23:11). These are the most theologically acute forms of CHAR-3 and CHAR-5. (3) Shamefulness as covenant infidelity — Char 4's idolatrous-shameful-objects register (Jer 3:24; 11:13; Hos 9:10) shows the human movement toward God corrupted when idolatry produces the shameful object that displaces God.

Psa 10:4 (vc=34074, M08-A2-VCG-02): "the wicked does not seek him; all his thoughts are, 'there is no God'" — CHAR-1 displaces the act of seeking God entirely, substituting self-sufficient cognitive closure for the movement of seeking. Psa 86:14 (vc=34097, M08-B-VCG-02): "they do not set God before them" — CHAR-2 removes God from the directional horizon of the inner person's movement. Neh 9:16 (vc=34120, M08-B-VCG-01): "they did not obey your commandments" — the obedience that is the vehicle of human-to-God movement is specifically what CHAR-2 refuses. Jer 50:29 (vc=34127, M08-B-VCG-01): "she has defied the Lord, the Holy One of Israel" — CHAR-2 directed explicitly against the divine person, inverting the movement of human-to-God approach into direct opposition.

VCG-03 positive: Phili 3:3 (vc=33879, M08-C-VCG-03): "worship by the Spirit of God and glory in Christ Jesus and put no confidence in the flesh" — the VCG-03 glorying is genuine movement toward God; Rom 5:11 (vc=33876, M08-C-VCG-03): "we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ."

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes — as the characteristic that distorts the cognitive self-assessment foundational to accurate movement toward God. Rom 12:3 (vc=60866, M08-D-VCG-02): the commanded alternative (sober judgment within God-assigned measure) is the cognitive posture that enables proper human-to-God orientation — CHAR-4 removes this by inflating the self-picture beyond God's assigned measure. 1Ti 3:6 (vc=33924, M08-D-VCG-02): the movement CHAR-4 generates is toward the condemnation associated with the devil's paradigm — the inverse of movement toward God.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes — as the inner posture that replaces movement toward God with structural self-sufficiency. Isa 47:8 (vc=9563, M08-E-VCG-02): "you who say in your heart, 'I am, and there is no one besides me'" — the self-sufficient declaration specifically claims the ontological completeness that would make movement toward God unnecessary. 1Ti 6:17 (vc=60878, M08-E-VCG-02): "set their hopes on the uncertainty of riches" rather than on God — CHAR-5's wealth-pride re-directs hope from God to structural goods, inverting the human-to-God movement.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All five characteristics operate as barriers to or inversions of the human person's movement toward God. CHAR-1: closes perception of God and blocks seeking (Psa 10:4, M08-A2-VCG-02). CHAR-2: replaces movement toward God with defiant self-assertion against God's authority (Neh 9:16, M08-B-VCG-01: "did not obey your commandments"). CHAR-3 VCG-01: misdirects the glorying-impulse away from God toward the self; VCG-03 uniquely constitutes the redeemed form of movement toward God through boasting. CHAR-4: generates the self-sufficiency cognitive claim that makes movement toward God unnecessary (Rom 12:3, M08-D-VCG-02). CHAR-5: replaces hope in God with hope in riches (1Ti 6:17, M08-E-VCG-02). The cluster-synthesis: M08 characteristics are uniformly God-movement-blocking — all five obstruct or invert the human-to-God relational direction.

The contrite inner state is thus implicitly a Godward orientation: the person in genuine contrition is not turned away from God but broken before him, which constitutes a movement toward God in the most acute form. The lowly posture paired with contrition in Isa57:15 ("contrite and lowly spirit") confirms the Godward direction — the characteristic includes within it the lowly orientation that opens toward God.

The semnotēs is thus the characteristic that shapes how the person inhabits their God-directed life in the public sphere. The characteristic operates in the human-toward-God movement by providing the manner-quality with which the person inhabits their godly life — not as a movement toward God specifically but as the quality of how they live before God and others.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes — the characteristic is constitutively a human-toward-God movement. All five verses evidence this direction: Exo35:5 — "contribution to the Lord" (toward God); Exo35:22 — gold brought to God's tabernacle; 1Ch28:21 — service for the house of God; 2Ch29:31 — burnt offerings and thank offerings (toward God); Psa51:12 — joyfully, freely-offered devotion (toward God). The freely-moved heart's movement is consistently Godward — willing-heartedness is the human movement toward God in its most genuine and uncoerced form.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes; the human-toward-God direction is the dominant register of the M09-A voluntary corpus. 2Ch7:14 — humbling → prayer → seeking God's face → turning from wickedness: humbling is the first and foundational act of the person's movement toward God, preceding and enabling the further movements of prayer and seeking. 2Ch33:12 — Manasseh "entreated the favor of the Lord his God and humbled himself greatly": the supplication is integrated with and enabled by the humbling.
