**[CLUSTER]** E — The human-toward-God direction is the dominant relational direction of the cluster. All six characteristics evidence this direction; the cluster's primary movement is creature toward Creator. CHAR-1: 2Ch7:14 — humbling → prayer → seeking → turning — the most complete multi-step Godward sequence in the cluster. CHAR-2: the gospel-obedience cluster (Rom1:5; 16:26; Heb5:9) — submission toward God as the telos of gospel response. CHAR-3: constitutively Godward — the contrite spirit is before God and draws God's dwelling. CHAR-5: 1Ti2:2 — godliness-and-dignity pairing situates the characteristic within the believer's Godward life. Cluster-level: CHAR-4 is the only characteristic in M09 without direct evidence of the human-to-God directional operation — it is the most horizontally-oriented characteristic in the cluster. All others have extensive Godward evidence. This horizontal orientation of CHAR-4 is consistent with its role as the cluster's mediating-engagement characteristic: it equips the person to engage the erring other rather than primarily to orient toward God.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes. The human-to-God direction is the primary directional axis of VCG-01 (32 verses). Wilful sinning *directed against God* is the defining characteristic of VCG-01: Gen 39:9 ("sin against God"), Psa 51:4 ("against you, you only, have I sinned"), Eze 14:13 ("sins against me"), Jer 40:3/44:23 ("sinned against the Lord"). In each case the sinning act is the human will moving *against* God — a negative movement toward God in which the relational bond is violated rather than honoured. Conversely, VCG-03's deterrence register shows the human-to-God movement in its positive mode: Psa 119:11 ("stored up your word in my heart, that I might not sin against you") — the word-storage is a positive movement toward God that guards against the negative sinning movement.

**[CHAR-10]** E — All three mechanisms disrupt the human-to-God movement. (1) *Enticement*: Jam 1:14 — "lured and enticed by his own desire" — the enticement draws the person away from God toward the desire-object, disrupting the human-to-God movement. (2) *Hypocrisy*: Gal 2:13 — "led astray by their hypocrisy" — the authentic covenantal identity through which the person moves toward God is falsified; the performed identity cannot sustain genuine God-directed movement. (3) *Apostasy*: Act 21:21 — "forsake Moses" — the departure from the covenantal framework is a movement away from the God-given covenantal structure rather than toward God within it.

**[CHAR-11]** E — The condition *blocks and reverses* the human-to-God movement. Joh 8:21 — "where I am going, you cannot come" — the condition creates an absolute barrier to the human person's movement toward where Jesus goes; Act 26:18 — "from the power of Satan to God" — the condition places the person in the domain opposite to God; Eph 2:1 — "dead in trespasses and sins" — spiritual death prevents movement toward God. The condition is constitutively a relational barrier: the movement toward God requires addressing the condition first (repentance — Mar 1:4; forgiveness — Luk 1:77; the Spirit's conviction — Joh 16:8).

**[CHAR-12]** E — Sin's enslaving power *blocks* the human person's movement toward God. Gal 3:22 — "imprisoned everything under sin, so that the promise... might be given to those who believe" — the universal imprisonment under sin is what prevents human movement toward God through human effort; the imprisonment makes the movement possible only through faith (not through the imprisoned person's own power). Joh 8:34 — "a slave to sin" — the slave's will cannot freely move toward God; the enslaving power constrains the will's God-directed freedom. Rom 6:2 — "how can we who died to sin still live in it?" — living in sin is incompatible with the God-oriented life of the one who has died to sin.

**[CHAR-13]** E — The record *blocks and burdens* the human person's movement toward God. Isa 59:2 — "your iniquities have made a separation between you and your God, and your sins have hidden his face from you so that he does not hear" — the record severs both divine attention and divine response to prayer, blocking the human-to-God movement at the communication level. Exo 34:9 — Moses's prayer — "pardon our iniquity and our sin, and take us for your inheritance" — the movement toward God requires first naming and petitioning for the record's removal; the record is the obstacle that must be addressed before God-directed movement can succeed.

**[CHAR-14]** E — Yes — the seeking dimension is entirely human-toward-God. Exo 32:30 — "I will go up to the Lord; perhaps I can make atonement for your sin" — Moses's movement upward toward God is the seeking's directional metaphor; Act 2:38 — "repent and be baptized... for the forgiveness of your sins" — the commanded human movement toward God in repentance and baptism; Act 10:43 — "everyone who believes in him receives" — the believing is a movement of trust toward Christ; Lev 23:27 — "you shall afflict yourselves and present a food offering to the Lord" — the self-affliction and offering are Israel's collective movement toward God.

**[CHAR-15]** E — Yes — through the corporate confession and repentance movement. 1Ki 8:47 — "if they turn their heart... and repent and plead with you... saying, 'We have sinned and have acted perversely and wickedly'" — the movement toward God is explicit: turning, repenting, pleading, and confessing are all movements directed toward God from within the generational-sin condition. Jer 8:14 — "why do we sit still? Gather together; let us go into the fortified cities and perish there" — paradoxically, this text shows a movement away from seeking God (going to fortified cities) in hopeless acceptance of doom; the movement toward God is by contrast the preferred response named in 1Ki 8:47.

**[CHAR-16]** E — Yes — through two contrasting modes. (1) *Positive movement toward God*: Luk 5:8 — "Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, O Lord" — Peter's movement is paradoxically a confession that draws him toward the holy even as it registers his unworthiness; Luk 18:13 — "God, be merciful to me, a sinner" — the movement toward God is explicit: the tax collector addresses God directly with the sinner-identity as the basis of the plea; Psa 51:13 — "sinners will return to you" — the return movement is the sinner's God-directed restoration; (2) *Negative movement against God*: Gen 13:13 — "sinners against the Lord" — the sinner-identity's directional orientation is against God; Heb 12:3 — hostility from sinners directed against Christ.

**[CHAR-17]** E — Yes — through the acknowledgment-and-seeking movement. Hos 5:15 — "until they acknowledge their guilt and seek my face, and in their distress earnestly seek me" — the guilt-acknowledgment is paired with the face-seeking of God; acknowledging guilt is simultaneously a movement toward God; Ezr 9:6 — "I am ashamed and blush to lift my face to you, my God" — even the shame-posture of guilt is directed toward God; the face may not be lifted, but the address is toward God. Gen 44:16 — "God has found out the guilt of your servants; behold, we are my lord's servants" — the confession before Joseph is simultaneously a posture of submission that mirrors the guilt-before-God movement.

**[CHAR-18]** E — Yes — through the acknowledgment-confession-plea movement. Exo 34:9 — Moses pleads "pardon our iniquity and our sin, and take us for your inheritance" — the movement toward God is through honest naming and plea; Psa 38:18 — "I confess my iniquity; I am sorry for my sin" — the voluntary movement toward God through confession; Hos 14:2 — "take with you words and return to the Lord; say to him, 'Take away all iniquity'" — the commanded movement toward God with the iniquity explicitly named; Psa 25:11 — "for your name's sake, O Lord, pardon my guilt, for it is great" — the movement toward God specifically through the acknowledgment of iniquity's greatness as the basis for the plea.

**[CHAR-19]** E — Yes — through the acknowledgment-repentance-return movement. Psa 32:5 — "I will confess my transgressions to the Lord, and you forgave the iniquity of my sin" — the movement toward God is through verbal confession; Eze 18:30 — "repent and turn from all your transgressions, lest iniquity be your ruin" — the commanded movement is volitional repentance-turning; Isa 59:20 — "a Redeemer will come to Zion, to those in Jacob who turn from transgression" — the human turning is the condition for the divine coming; Hos 14:1 — "return, O Israel, to the Lord your God, for you have stumbled because of your iniquity."

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes. The remedy sequence in the VCG-01 corpus is fundamentally a human-toward-God movement. Lev 5:5 ("when he realizes his guilt... and confesses the sin he has committed") — confession is directed toward God, an acknowledgment before the divine of what the person did. Num 15:27 ("he shall offer a female goat a year old for a sin offering") — the offering is brought "to the Lord" (Num 15:27 context: "before the Lord") — the act of bringing the offering is a human movement toward God in the wake of inadvertent sinning. Num 22:34 (Balaam — "if it is evil in your sight, I will turn back") — "in your sight" addresses the angel of the Lord, orienting Balaam's will toward God's evaluation.

**[CHAR-20]** E — Yes — through the confession-and-return movement. Lev 26:40 — "if they confess their iniquity and the iniquity of their fathers in their treachery that they committed against me, and also in walking contrary to me" — the confession is the movement toward God; the treachery itself is named in the movement-toward; Ezr 10:2 — "we have broken faith with our God and have married foreign women from the peoples of the land, but even now there is hope for Israel" — the confession of faithlessness is simultaneously a movement toward God with hope; Ezr 10:10 — Ezra's declaration "you have broken faith and married foreign women" — the communal acknowledgment initiating the corporate return.

**[CHAR-21]** E — Yes — through the confession-movement. 1Ki 8:47 — "we have sinned and have acted perversely and wickedly" — the exile's confession of perversity is the movement toward God (followed in 1Ki 8:48 by "if they return to you with all their mind and with all their heart"); Dan 9:5 — "we have sinned and done wrong and acted wickedly" — Daniel's prayer naming perversity as part of the comprehensive movement toward God; Job 33:27 — "I sinned and perverted what was right" — the individual's confession before God.

**[CHAR-22]** E — Yes — through the confession-and-cessation movement. Job 34:32 — "teach me what I do not see; if I have done iniquity, I will do it no more" — the movement toward God is through acknowledgment and volitional commitment to cease; Eze 33:15 — "the wicked restores the pledge... not doing injustice, he shall surely live" — the movement toward God through restitution and conduct-change; 2Sa 3:34 — "as one falls before the wicked you have fallen" — the lament implies the expectation of justice from God for unjust death.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes — this is the dominant directional axis of CHAR-3. The overwhelming majority of confessions in the corpus are explicitly directed toward God: "I have sinned against the Lord" (1Sa 7:6), "we have sinned against you" (Judg 10:10; Dan 9:11), "I have sinned against him" (Mic 7:9), "Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you" (Luk 15:21). Confession is the human person's movement toward God after the movement away from God that sin constituted. Neh 1:6 — praying "day and night" with confession as the primary posture — shows sustained human movement toward God through the confessional posture. The direction is unambiguous: confession is the person moving back toward the God they sinned against.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Conscience suppression produces a *false or disrupted* human-to-God movement. Jer 2:35 — the person claims "surely his anger has turned from me" — they believe they are in good standing with God without the act of confession and turning that genuine standing requires. The movement toward God is simulated: the person acts as though the relationship is untroubled, but the simulation is based on a false self-assessment rather than genuine reconciliation. Jer 16:10 — the people ask "what sin have we committed?" in the context of a prophetic confrontation — their question may be an implicit appeal to God, but it is an appeal that does not acknowledge the relationship's actual state.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The human-to-God movement is disrupted by refusal to repent. The corpus describes the absence of the movement toward God that repentance would constitute: 2Ki 10:31 — "not careful to walk in the law of the Lord, the God of Israel" — the movement toward God through law-walking is precisely what is withheld. Neh 9:29 — "you warned them in order to turn them back to your law. Yet they acted presumptuously" — the movement toward God (turning back to his law) is available but the will moves in the opposite direction (presumptuousness). Refusal to repent is the blocking of the human-to-God movement: the will that could move toward God in turning chooses not to.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Habitual defection *blocks and reverses* the human-to-God movement. 2Ki 17:7 — "sinned against the Lord their God... and had feared other gods" — the direction of movement is explicitly away from the Lord and toward other gods; the human-to-God movement has been replaced by human-to-false-gods movement. 1Jo 3:6 — "no one who keeps on sinning has either seen him or known him" — the habitual sinner is not moving toward God; they are in a condition of fundamental non-encounter with God. The human-to-God movement that covenant life requires is absent: instead of approaching, the habitual sinner is persistently withdrawing.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Contagious sin *reverses* the human-to-God movement in the community. 2Ki 17:21 — "Jeroboam drove Israel from following the Lord" — the community's movement toward God (following the Lord) is explicitly reversed by the leader's contagious sin; the movement now runs away from God rather than toward him. 1Ki 14:22 — Judah "provoked him to jealousy with their sins" — the community's movement is not toward God in worship but toward provoking him in sinning. The human-to-God movement that covenant life requires has been inverted by the contagious sin transmission: the community moves toward idols and away from God.

**[CHAR-8]** E — Political revolt's relationship to the human-to-God movement is evidenced negatively in 2Ch 21:10: the movement toward political revolt is linked to the *prior withdrawal from God* — "he had forsaken the Lord." The forsaking of the Lord (a movement away from God) precedes and enables the political revolts. Political revolt thus operates in a context where the ruler's human-to-God movement has already been reversed (the Lord was forsaken). The political revolt is a downstream consequence of the broken human-to-God movement.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Sinful speech directed at God is the *anti-movement* of the human-to-God direction: Rev 13:6 — "It opened its mouth to utter blasphemies against God, blaspheming his name and his dwelling" — the creature's speech is directed against God rather than toward him. VCG-02's blasphemy-charge against Jesus (Mar 2:7; Joh 10:33) represents the religious authorities' speech moving against the one through whom the human-to-God movement is restored. Sinful speech against God is constitutively the reversal of human-to-God movement — it is the creature speaking in the opposite direction.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes, but in a negative register: wickedness-as-settled-person-identity is specifically the state in which the human person's movement is away from God rather than toward him. Psa 9:17 (VCG-02): "the wicked… all the nations that forget God" — the characteristic's defining relational posture toward God is forgetting (absence of movement toward). Mal 3:18 (VCG-02): "one who does not serve him" — non-service as the defining relational stance. Psa 10:13 (VCG-02): "renounce God and say in his heart 'You will not call to account'" — active inner renunciation rather than movement toward. Pro 15:8 (VCG-09): "the sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination" — even the wicked person's nominal religious approach is corrupted by the inner state; the movement toward God is structurally disabled. The one redemptive signal is Eze 18:21-27 and 33:11-19 (VCG-07): the wicked person can turn toward God — the movement is possible but requires a volitional reversal of the characteristic itself.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes, in a negative register: the characteristic specifically blocks the human person's movement toward God. Heb 10:22 (vc=14426 — VCG-06) is the most direct statement: the evil conscience makes approach to God impossible — "draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, with our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience" implies that the unsprinkled evil conscience prevents drawing near. Heb 3:12 (vc=14423 — VCG-06): the evil, unbelieving heart leads to "falling away from the living God" — movement is away from God rather than toward him. The one verse showing movement toward God in the context of this characteristic is Act 3:26 (vc=14410 — VCG-05): "turning every one of you from your wickedness" — the turn from the constitutional evil is the precondition for movement toward God.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes, in a negative register: the characteristic specifically describes what blocks or corrupts the human person's movement toward God. The worship evidence (VCG-03) is definitional: Pro 15:8 (vc=1678 — VCG-03): the wicked person's sacrifice — a movement toward God — is rendered an abomination by the abominable inner character of the one moving; Pro 28:9 (vc=65958 — VCG-03): turning the ear from the law renders even prayer an abomination. Pro 21:27 (vc=1693 — VCG-03): the sacrifice is abominable, and evil intent deepens the offense. Isa 1:13 (vc=1695 — VCG-03): "incense is an abomination to me. New moon and Sabbath…I cannot endure iniquity and solemn assembly." The human-to-God movement is structurally blocked at every point by the abominable inner condition: approach to God through prayer, sacrifice, or religious assembly is rendered repugnant when the inner person is abominable.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes, but exclusively in a negative register: idolatrous abomination specifically perverts and blocks the human person's movement toward God. Deu 17:1 (vc=1684 — VCG-02): offering a flawed animal is an abomination — the act of worship is corrupted by the inner failure to value God's worth rightly. Jer 7:10 (vc=65963 — VCG-04): "come and stand before me in this house… only to go on doing all these abominations?" — the human movement toward God (standing before him) is decoupled from inner transformation; outward religious presence is combined with continued inner idolatrous practice. This reveals that the characteristic produces a dissociated religious life: outward approach to God combined with inner idolatrous attachment — a form of double-allegiance worship that is itself abominable.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes, exclusively in the negative register: iniquity as active scheming specifically blocks the human person's movement toward God. Psa 66:18 (vc=38182 — VCG-04): "If I had cherished iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not have listened" — the iniquity-schemer's prayer channel is closed; the cherished iniquity breaks the prayer-relationship. Isa 1:13 (vc=38197 — VCG-04): "incense is an abomination to me. I cannot endure iniquity and solemn assembly" — religious worship performed while harbouring iniquity is intolerable to God; the characteristic corrupts the religious approach. Psa 14:4 (vc=38229 — VCG-03): evildoers "do not call upon the Lord" — the characteristic specifically excludes the act of calling on God; Psa 53:4 (VCG-03): same.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes, but entirely in the negative register: the characteristic is the inversion of movement toward God. Rev 16:9 (vc=14352 — VCG-01): "they did not repent and give him glory" — the withheld repentance and glory name exactly what genuine movement toward God would look like; the characteristic is the refusal of that movement even when under judgment. The characteristic thus defines the anti-movement-toward-God: instead of repentance, cursing; instead of glory-giving, name-cursing. Jude 8 (vc=14354 — VCG-01): "reject authority and blaspheme the glorious ones" — authority-rejection as the inner posture precludes the submission that genuine movement toward God requires.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All six characteristics show their respective evil-forms blocking or inverting the human person's movement toward God — confirming the cluster as comprehensively anti-worship and anti-prayer. Char 1 (Psa 9:17 — wicked forget God; Psa 5:4 — wicked cannot stand before God). Char 2 (Eph 4:18 — alienated from the life of God). Char 3 (Pro 3:32 — excluded from divine confidence; Pro 15:8 — wicked person's sacrifice an abomination; Isa 1:13 — incense and iniquity together intolerable). Char 4 (Deu 32:16 — idolatrous worship provokes God to jealousy). Char 5 (Psa 66:18 — cherished iniquity forecloses divine hearing; Isa 1:13 cross-reference — simultaneous worship and iniquity). Char 6 (Rev 16:9 — "they did not repent and give him glory" — the anti-worship response; Psa 14:4 — evildoers do not call on the Lord). The cluster's uniform finding: every M10b characteristic blocks the approach to God.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes. The characteristic's management is precisely oriented toward restoring access to God. The men at Num 9:7 (M10c-A-VCG-07) express the grief of blocked worship-movement: "Why are we kept from bringing the Lord's offering?" — the impulse toward God is blocked by the defilement-state, but the movement itself is active. Their approach to Moses to ask about provision for their defilement shows active seeking of a pathway to restored worship. Deu 26:14 (M10c-B-VCG-01) — the declaration of freedom from unclean state at sacred tithe-giving — is itself a movement toward God in which the person's defilement-state or its absence is a condition of integrity. The entire remedial system (washing, waiting, examination, water of impurity) is oriented toward restoring the person's access to the divine presence.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes — as a barrier. The moral-inner defilement-state operates precisely as what blocks the person's movement toward God. 2Cor 6:17 (VCG-03): "touch no unclean thing; then I will welcome you" — the barrier between the person and divine welcome is the contact with unclean things; separation is the condition for the movement toward God being restored. Eph 5:5 (VCG-04): "has no inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God" — the impure person's movement toward God's kingdom is blocked. The characteristic thus operates in the human-to-God direction as an obstacle, and the remedial actions (separation, cleansing — 2Cor 7:1, Isa 52:11) are the means by which the blocked movement is restored.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes — as the primary barrier. Eze 20:31 (VCG-02): "shall I be inquired of by you, O house of Israel? As I live, declares the Lord God, I will not be inquired of by you" — the persistent corporate self-defilement through idolatry closes the channel of divine inquiry; the characteristic blocks the primary movement of seeking God. Num 5:3 (VCG-05): defiling persons are removed from the camp "that they may not defile their camp, in the midst of which I dwell" — the defilement disqualifies the person from proximity to the divine presence. The entire ordeal law (Num 5:13-29, VCG-01) is structured as an access question: does the woman have integrity to remain in the covenant community (access to God's presence) or has she forfeited it through defilement?

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes — as a barrier, and as a context in which movement toward God is enabled through proxy. The characteristic bars the person's own direct movement toward God: speech and hearing suppressed (Mar 9:25) — the person cannot pray or receive divine word; they are driven into the desert (Luk 8:29) rather than toward the divine presence. Movement toward God is enabled through others: Mar 7:25 (VCG-01) — "a woman... came and fell down at his feet" — the mother's movement on behalf of her daughter. Act 5:16 — communities bringing their afflicted. The characteristic forces the movement toward God to be mediated through others.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All four characteristics show the defilement-state operating in the human-to-God direction, but the mode differs. Characteristic 1: the defilement-state blocks the movement (Num 9:7 — worship desire blocked) and the remedial system restores it; the entire system is oriented toward restored divine access. Characteristic 2: the characteristic operates as an active barrier to divine welcome (2Cor 6:17 — "then I will welcome you" — conditioned on separation from the unclean) and to eschatological inheritance (Eph 5:5 — "has no inheritance in the kingdom"); separation and cleansing restore access. Characteristic 3: the characteristic closes the channel of divine inquiry (Eze 20:31 — "I will not be inquired of by you") and severs divine proximity (Num 35:34 — defilement of the land in which God dwells); the eschatological cleansing restores the covenant formula ("they shall be my people, and I will be their God"). Characteristic 4: the characteristic bars the person's own movement toward God (speech and hearing suppressed — Mar 9:25; driven away from the community that embodies proximity to God) and forces the movement to be mediated through others (Mar 7:25 — the mother's seeking; Act 5:16 — communities bringing the afflicted). Cluster pattern: defilement in every register bars human movement toward God. The barrier is bodily-sacral (Char 1), moral-interior (Char 2), corporate-covenantal (Char 3), and spiritual-dominative (Char 4). In the fourth, uniquely, the movement must be carried by the community on behalf of the possessed person.

questions.question_text: What inner posture does this movement require, as the evidence shows?

findings.session_b_note:
The inner posture for the human-to-God movement is comprehensively named in the data:

**Radical dependence:** OBS-064-015 names Dan 9:19 as the paradigm of dependence — "not resting on any claim of merit." The inner posture is the creature before the Creator, with no leverage except the character and name of God himself. OBS-064-016: "the human's condition (sin, rebellion) is the reason forgiveness is needed; God's character is the basis on which forgiveness is expected."

**Grounding in God's character, not human merit:** The intercessory corpus consistently appeals to what God is (goodness, hesed, his name) rather than what the petitioner has done. Dan 9:19 — "for your own sake, O my God, because your city and your people are called by your name." The posture excludes self-justification.

**Urgency:** Dan 9:19 — "delay not." The inner posture of genuine intercession includes urgency — the person is not indifferent to whether forgiveness comes but presses toward it.

**Receptivity:** The access-postures (repentance, faith, confession) name receptivity as the inner stance — the person opens themselves to receive what God is disposed to give. Receptivity is distinct from passivity: it is an active inner orientation of openness.

findings.session_b_note:
Three inner postures emerge from the data as required for the human-to-God compassion-movement:

**Vulnerability and need-recognition:** The supplication vocabulary presupposes that the person knows they need what they are asking for. The act of earnest appeal (techinah, tahanun) is constitutively a posture of acknowledged insufficiency. The person who believes themselves self-sufficient (the Laodicean pattern — Rev 3:17) cannot make this movement. Vulnerability — the open awareness of one's own pitiable condition — is the enabling inner posture.

**Heart-openness (Joel 2:13 — heart-rending):** "Rend your hearts and not your garments." The inner posture required for the movement toward God's compassion is not ritual performance but heart-level openness — the tearing apart of inner defences and self-protection. This is a posture of radical inner availability: the person brings not a performance but an exposed inner life.

**Trust in divine chesed as the ground:** Psa 25:7 grounds the supplication in "your steadfast love" — the person approaches God not on the basis of their own worthiness but on the basis of God's established character. The inner posture required is trust in the divine compassion-character as the reliable ground of appeal. Without this trust, the appeal cannot be made with the confidence implied by the word techinah (earnest supplication, not tentative request).

findings.session_b_note: The required inner posture is the three-fold constellation of Isa 66:2: **humble + contrite in spirit + trembling at God's word**. These three together constitute the posture that enables genuine movement toward God. Additionally, from Q002: openness (non-resistance to divine assessment), honest self-knowledge (recognising the condition before God rather than defending against it), and absence of merit-claim (approaching with disclosed need, not performance). The anti-posture from Jer 44:10: unhumbled, unfearing, law-disregarding — three closures that block the movement.

findings.session_b_note:
Finding 062-GROUN-001 addresses this: the ground of genuine fellowship is *moral and spiritual alignment rather than preference or proximity*. The inner posture required for human-to-God fellowship movement includes:

- **Fear of God:** Psa 119:63 — companionship with the fear-of-God community presupposes a personal fear-of-God orientation.
- **Escape from corruption:** 2Pe 1:4 — entry into divine nature participation requires escape from the corruption of sinful desire.
- **Desire for knowing:** Phili 3:10 — *that I may know him* — the inner posture is a burning desire for participatory knowledge of Christ, including through suffering.
- **Moral-spiritual compatibility:** 2Cor 6:14 — the person moving toward righteous fellowship must be oriented toward righteousness, not lawlessness.

findings.session_b_note: Three inner postures are named for human-toward-God movement in goodness: (1) Waiting — Lam 3:25 ("the Lord is good to those who wait for him"). Waiting is the inner posture of active expectation without premature action — a stance of dependence and trust. (2) Seeking — Lam 3:25 ("the soul who seeks him"). Seeking is directional — the soul oriented actively toward God. findings.finding_value: T4 identified that God's goodness as a character attribute is unconditional while the human's ongoing experience of its relational benefits is conditional (Q&A-100). T5 named the transformation arcs through which the conditional dimension operates: the positive transformation arc (encounter → trust → reorientation → overflow) is the arc in which the conditional relational experience is deepened; the moral awareness arc (recognition → loathing → repentance) is the arc that recovers the relational experience when it has been lost through departure. T4's human-to-God enabling inner postures (waiting, seeking, trust — Q&A-104) correspond to T5's formation mechanisms: the posture of waiting corresponds to the encounter mechanism (sustained receptive openness); the moral awareness arc is the recovery mechanism for the person who has departed from the relational posture. Together: T5's formative processes are the mechanisms through which T4's relational conditions are entered, sustained, and restored. Transformation and relationship are inseparable in goodness.

findings.session_b_note: The condition for human love toward God is prior reception of divine love (1Jo 4:19 — 'we love because he first loved us'). Human love toward God is always responsive, not originating. The capacity required: soul-purification (1Pe 1:22, OBS-103-124) — the inner person must be cleared of the disordering loves that block genuine love toward God. The great commandment ('with all your soul') implies that the soul must be free from divided ultimate attachment to function as love-toward-God. Love of money (1Ti 6:10, OBS-103-132) and love of the world (2Ti 4:10, OBS-103-148) represent the prior conditions that prevent the human-to-God love-flow. The capacity for human love toward God is therefore: received divine love (enabling condition) + soul-purification from rival loves (clearing condition).

findings.finding_value: Love's relational architecture is structured by three directional axes — GOD → HUMAN, HUMAN → GOD, HUMAN → HUMAN — with divine love structurally prior and causally generative of all subsequent love. 1Jo 4:19 ('we love because he first loved us') is the axis-precedence statement: the first axis is not responsive to but constitutive of the second and third. The GOD → HUMAN direction moves through four mechanisms: covenantal declaration (naming the beloved — Jer 12:7, Mat 3:17), Spirit-infusion (Rom 5:5), redemptive acts (Joh 3:16), and covenantal covering (Eze 16:8). The HUMAN → GOD direction requires total inner mobilisation (Mat 22:37 — all heart, soul, mind) and the clearing of rival loves as its condition (1Jo 4:19, 1Ti 6:10). The HUMAN → HUMAN direction spans five structural types (neighbour, enemy, community, friendship, family) and creates the social architecture described in Q&A-088 (restructured kinship, public legibility, competitive generosity). The most significant finding in T4: the human-to-God direction is conditioned by prior reception of divine love — the capacity for human love toward God is itself a gift. The one structural gap: T4.6 (spiritual beings) is absent from the evidence.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-004: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion…
findings.finding_value: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion on whom I have compassion"), covenantally grounded (chesed as the bond-loyalty that grounds the characteristic), and situationally responsive (splanchnizō — triggered by the specific sight of suffering). These three bases are not in tension but in integration: divine compassion is free, covenanted, and responsive simultaneously. The scope finding is among the most analytically significant in the registry: compassion explicitly and repeatedly crosses covenantal boundaries (Nineveh, the Samaritan/Jew axis, the power-asymmetric relationship). Scope is defined by perceived need, not moral standing or covenantal membership — this is formally confirmed in the data and distinguishes compassion from many other relational characteristics. The chesed/splanchnizō distinction maps onto distinct relational registers: chesed sustains within established bonds; splanchnizō extends across distance and difference. T4.4 (receiver's inner-being experience) is the most significant gap — four P-rated prompts, entirely absent from the data. T4.6 (spiritual beings interface) is entirely silent across all four prompts.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-004: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — a…
findings.finding_value: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — all God-as-subject). The basis of divine extension is the giver's character and prior knowing (Exo 33:17 — "I know you by name"), not the receiver's merit — neither merit-based nor arbitrary. The human-to-God direction is specifically supplication: tachanum (H8469) is the receiving side's corresponding vocabulary built into the same root family as the giving side (chen/chanan) — the vocabulary embeds the two-directional circuit in a single root. The human-giving direction extends grace horizontally through three modes: forgiving (charizō — Eph 4:32), gracious conduct (chen as character quality — 889-003), and gracious speech (SD022). The receiving direction is the most underexamined (T4.4 — P-rated throughout); the scope analysis (T4.5) reveals grace crossing covenantal and social boundaries (Ruth narrative — grace in the context of foreign status and vulnerability). T4.6 (spiritual beings) is evidenced at one point: Luk 1:28 (kecharitōmenē — the angel's announcement), which implies angelic ministry as a vehicle of grace rather than grace operating independently in the spiritual-beings register. T4 synthesis: the relational architecture of grace is unique in the programme — it is the only characteristic where the giving-side vocabulary and the receiving-side vocabulary are built from the same root (chen/tachanum), encoding the grace-circuit's two-sidedness at the lexical level.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-010: T1's four modes of operation map onto T4's four relational directions. The sovereign-bestowal mode corresponds to the God-to-human direction (T4.1 — primary and dominant). The covenantal-relational-su…
findings.finding_value: T1's four modes of operation map onto T4's four relational directions. The sovereign-bestowal mode corresponds to the God-to-human direction (T4.1 — primary and dominant). The covenantal-relational-sustaining mode corresponds to the relational scope (T4.5 — grace operating within and across covenantal boundaries). The capacity-conferring mode corresponds to the human-to-God direction in its supplication register (T4.2 — SD026: grace giving even the capacity to appeal). The character-forming mode corresponds to the human-giving direction (T4.3 — gracious conduct and speech as the horizontal expression of received grace-character). The vocabulary's structural insight (T4 synthesis: giving-side and receiving-side built from the same root, chen/tachanum) explains T1's finding that grace requires the receptor's inner engagement to complete its operation — the vocabulary encodes the two-sidedness because grace is constitutively a two-sided circuit.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-015: T2's origin analysis (grace does not originate in the human constitutional system — it arrives from God) and T4's directional analysis (God-to-human is primary and dominant) are the same finding from …
findings.finding_value: T2's origin analysis (grace does not originate in the human constitutional system — it arrives from God) and T4's directional analysis (God-to-human is primary and dominant) are the same finding from constitutional and relational perspectives respectively. The spirit level as reception point (T2.1) and the God-to-human direction as primary (T4.1) are mutually explanatory: because grace originates with God and is received at the spirit level, the primary relational direction is necessarily God-initiated toward the human spirit. The human-to-God direction (T4.2 — supplication) corresponds to T2.10's constitutional movement in reverse: the soul's recognition of need translates into the somatic enactment of supplication (prostration, fasting, sackcloth), which is T2.7's bidirectional body-soul finding. Constitutional location and relational direction are co-determining.

findings.finding_value: T3's agency-constituting finding (grace constitutes rather than replaces agency — 1Cor 15:10) and T4's human-to-God direction (supplication as the human posture of appeal — requiring genuine human agency in the act of plea) are structurally aligned. The constituted agency (T3.7) is precisely the agency that supplication requires: the creature must genuinely appeal, not merely receive passively. T3's finding that grace and conscience are mutually necessary (T3.9) corresponds to T4's relational-access finding: grace transforms the threshold of human-to-God approach (prosagōgē — SD035) from impassable to open, which is the relational expression of T3.9's constitutional finding that grace creates the condition within which conscience can operate fully without destruction. T3 names the inner-being event; T4 names the relational consequence of the same event.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-023: T4's relational directions correspond to T5's formation mechanisms. The God-to-human direction (T4.1 — sovereign bestowal) corresponds to the encounter and spirit-outpouring mechanisms (T5.3 — sudden …
findings.finding_value: T4's relational directions correspond to T5's formation mechanisms. The God-to-human direction (T4.1 — sovereign bestowal) corresponds to the encounter and spirit-outpouring mechanisms (T5.3 — sudden specific relational event; Zec 12:10). The human-to-God direction (T4.2 — supplication) corresponds to the sustained-formation arc of T5.5: the person who habitually supplicates is being formed into the character that supplicates, which is itself the character-quality kind identified in T1. The human-giving direction (T4.3 — gracious forgiving, speech-grace) corresponds to T5.3's mediated-transformation mechanism (grace → tenderheartedness → forgiving → gracious speech — SD030, Eph 4:32). T4 describes the relational shape of each mechanism; T5 describes the inner formation process each mechanism produces.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-025: T4's most analytically distinctive finding (the vocabulary encodes the two-sided grace-circuit in a single root: chen/chanan for giving; tachanum/techinah for seeking) is T7's most significant root-le…
findings.finding_value: T4's most analytically distinctive finding (the vocabulary encodes the two-sided grace-circuit in a single root: chen/chanan for giving; tachanum/techinah for seeking) is T7's most significant root-level finding. T7.1 confirms: the chen root family embeds both the giving side (chen — favour, chanan — to be gracious) and the receiving-seeking side (tachanum, techinah — supplication) in a single etymological family. This is unique in the programme's vocabulary data: no other characteristic has the giving-side and receiving-side vocabulary built from the same root. T4's relational architecture and T7's lexical analysis are the relational and lexical descriptions of the same structural reality — that grace is constitutively a two-sided circuit whose two sides are inseparable at the root level.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-019: T3 reveals that the inner faculties covenant most deeply engages are Other-oriented (relational capacity, conscience, moral evaluation, memory). T4 reveals that covenant's relational interfaces are as…
findings.finding_value: T3 reveals that the inner faculties covenant most deeply engages are Other-oriented (relational capacity, conscience, moral evaluation, memory). T4 reveals that covenant's relational interfaces are asymmetric (God initiates; human responds; horizontal is grounded in vertical). The T3 × T4 synthesis: the Other-oriented faculty bias (T3) and the asymmetric relational structure (T4) are coherently related — the inner faculties that covenant engages are precisely those required for the kind of asymmetric responsive relationship that covenant constitutes. The relational capacity (T3.11) is the constitutional equipment for genuine connection; the covenant's relational interfaces (T4) are the actual connections that this capacity enables. The inner posture required for human-to-God covenant movement (T4.2 — Q&A-106: reverent fear, love, all-heart, hearing orientation) corresponds directly to the inner faculties that covenant engages: fear engages moral evaluation (T3.8), love engages affect and relational capacity (T3.4, T3.11), all-heart engages volition (T3.6), and hearing engages perception (T3.1). T3 and T4 are two analytical views of the same responsive inner-being structure.

The human must give glory before inner-being disorder sets in.

The human-to-God direction is the most structurally asymmetric dimension in M05. M05-B and M05-C are structurally silent — the directional asymmetry of compassion and mercy (flowing only from greater to lesser) means the human can never be the compassion-giver or mercy-giver toward God. M05-A (love toward God) and M05-E (humility before God) are the strongest human-to-God directions. M05-G (walking in the light, sharing sufferings) is present but constitutively responsive to divine initiative. The cluster teaches that the human's primary relational movement is not self-generated love toward God but a responsive, enabled participation in the love God has first shown.

findings.finding_value: The inner posture required for genuine movement toward God in M01-A includes: (1) **an undivided heart** (Psa 86:11: "fear of God requires inner integration; a divided heart is an obstacle"); (2) **humility** (Pro 15:33; 22:4: fear paired with humility); (3) **whole-heartedness** (1Sa 12:24: "all-heart devotion grounded in memory of God's great deeds"); (4) **the absence of competing fear-objects** (Isa 8:12-13: the prophet must not fear what the crowd fears in order to rightly fear God).

The inner posture required for trembling-at-God's-word (M01-E-VCG-02) includes: humility and a contrite spirit (Isa 66:2 anchor) — the posture that makes genuine responsiveness to God's word possible.

The inner posture required for movement toward God across M01 is: undivided heart, humility, whole-heartedness, and the absence of competing fear-objects. These are enabling conditions for the reverential posture that moves the person toward God.

M02-E-VCG-03 (Elijah, Phinehas, psalmists): the inner posture is consuming exclusive devotion — the person who moves toward God in zeal has entirely identified their own honor with God's honor (Psa 69:9: "others' reproach of God falls upon him personally"). The posture required is a self-giving identification with God's claim.

Gen 18:30/32 (M02-B-VCG-05): intercession toward God while navigating his anger requires boldness constrained by reverence — Abraham presses the petition but does not exceed what the anger-threshold allows. The posture is bold but not presumptuous.

The inner posture evidenced for effective human-to-God grief movement is primarily humility and genuine inner orientation. Josiah's weeping before God is effective because of his "tender, humbled heart" (2Ki 22:19 — M03-A-VCG-02 anchor). Deu 1:45 (M03-A-VCG-02) shows weeping that goes unanswered because it follows disobedience without genuine repentance — the posture is absent. The inner conditions required appear to be: genuine inner state (not performance), Godward orientation, and — in the penitential context — humility. Distress directed to God through prayer appears to require simply the genuine experience of distress itself — no prerequisite of spiritual worthiness is named; the groaning of slaves reaches God without qualification (Exo 2:24 — M03-E-VCG-01).
