**[CHAR-1]** E — Trust (Psa 13:5); uprightness of heart (Psa 32:11); seeking God (Psa 40:16; 70:4); waiting for God (Isa 25:9); love of God's salvation (Psa 40:16; 70:4); righteous living (Psa 68:3; 97:8). The characteristic's inner posture is not passive — it requires active orientation toward God through trust, seeking, and righteous alignment.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Inner postures that enable Joy toward God: (1) **Seeking** — Psa 40:16; 70:4 ("may all who seek you rejoice and be glad in you"); Psa 85:6 (revival → rejoicing "in you"); (2) **Trust** — Psa 33:21 ("our heart is glad in him, because we trust in his holy name"); (3) **Uprightness and righteousness** — Psa 32:11 ("rejoice, O righteous"); Psa 97:11 ("joy for the upright in heart"); (4) **Wholehearted devotion** — 2Ch 15:15 ("sworn with all their heart and had sought him with their whole desire"); (5) **Obedience** — 1Jo 3:22 paired with Gal 5:22 — the obedient life produces Spirit-joy; (6) **Faith in Christ** — Rom 15:13 ("joy and peace in believing"); Act 16:34 (joy because of faith in God).

**[CHAR-7]** E — (1) **Faith in the unseen** — 1Pe 1:8 ("though you do not now see him, you believe") — faith as the inner posture that opens toward God and enables Suffering-Joy; (2) **Eschatological orientation** — the cognitive holding of future glory as the ground for present exultation; (3) **Identification with Christ** — 1Pe 4:13 (sharing Christ's sufferings as the posture that produces Suffering-Joy in the movement toward him); (4) **Humility before the Father's will** — Luk 10:21's "yes, Father, for such was your gracious will" — receptive humility toward divine sovereignty as the posture that enables the Spirit's rejoicing.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The inner postures that enable human-to-God Gladness: (1) **Purity of heart** — Psa 73:1 ("those who are pure in heart" experience God's goodness toward them); (2) **Seeking and waiting** — Lam 3:25–26 (the soul who seeks, who waits quietly); (3) **Gratitude** — Deu 8:10 (eating and blessing God for the good land — gratitude as the posture); (4) **Trust in God's promise** — M04-O-VCG-04's covenantal gladness requires the inner act of trusting that God's good word will be fulfilled; (5) **Humility** — Deu 9:6 (receiving the good land as grace, not merit — the humble posture).

**[CHAR-4]** E — (1) **Wholeness / non-divided will** — Psa 37:4's "delight yourself in the Lord" presupposes an undivided orientation; Psa 73:25's exclusive desire ("nothing on earth I desire besides you") is the fullest form; (2) **Choosing what God chooses** — Isa 56:4 ("who choose the things that please me") — active volitional alignment; (3) **Fearing God** — Neh 1:11 ("delight to fear your name") — reverence as the inner posture that sustains Delight-in-God; (4) **Inward truthfulness** — Psa 51:6 ("you delight in truth in the inward being") — authentic interior honesty as the enabling condition for receiving God's Delight; (5) **Sabbath faithfulness** — Isa 58:13 (honoring the Sabbath → "you shall take delight in the Lord" — Isa 58:14) — Sabbath as the practised form of upward Delight.

**[CHAR-5]** E — (1) **Single-minded seeking** — Psa 27:4 ("one thing have I asked") — the one thing focused on God's beauty enables receiving his Pleasure; (2) **Covenant obedience** — the ni.cho.ach corpus: correct, prescribed worship is the enabling posture; (3) **Faithfulness** — Job 36:11 ("if they listen and serve him, they complete their years in pleasantness") — listening and serving as the inner posture that enables Pleasure to be the quality of one's years; (4) **Willingness to praise** — Psa 147:1; 135:3 — the posture of genuine praise enabling the felt pleasantness of worship.

**[CHAR-6]** E — (1) **Attending and considering** — Job 37:14 ("stop and consider the wondrous works of God") — deliberate attention as the prerequisite; (2) **Wholehearted engagement** — Psa 9:1 ("with my whole heart") — half-hearted Wonder-movement toward God is insufficient; (3) **Humility and non-overreach** — Psa 131:1 ("my heart is not lifted up… I do not occupy myself with things too great and too marvellous for me") — the humble not-overreaching posture as enabling genuine Wonder; (4) **Prior consecration** — Jos 3:5 ("consecrate yourselves, for tomorrow the Lord will do wonders") — moral preparedness enabling receptive Wonder; (5) **Memory-engagement** — Psa 77:11 (deliberate memory of the Lord's wonders as the inner strategy for Wonder-movement toward God through distress).

**[CLUSTER]** E — The enabling postures across the seven share three common features: (1) **Wholehearted orientation** — required consistently across Exultation (Char 1: uprightness; Psa 32:11), Joy (Char 2: 2Ch 15:15 — "with all their heart and whole desire"), Delight (Char 4: undivided will; Psa 73:25), and Wonder (Char 6: Psa 9:1 — "whole heart"); divided or self-referential orientation blocks all seven; (2) **Trust / faith** — named as enabling for Joy (Psa 33:21), Suffering-Joy (1Pe 1:8), and implied for Exultation (Psa 13:5 — "I have trusted in your steadfast love"); (3) **Covenant faithfulness / obedience** — enabling for Pleasure (ni.cho.ach conditioned on correct worship), Delight (Psa 51:6's inward truthfulness), and Wonder (Jos 3:5's consecration). The most distinctive enabling posture: Wonder (Char 6) requires **attending and considering** (Job 37:14) — deliberate perceptive openness; Gladness (Char 3) requires **humility** (Deu 9:6). The cluster's enabling postures reveal that the human-to-God movement is not passive but requires active inner orientation and moral preparation.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The inner posture required for the shame-mediated movement toward God is *moral honesty* — willingness to let shame be what it is, to "lie down in our shame" (Jer 3:25) without defensiveness or hardening. The M07-B seared-conscience material shows what happens when this posture is refused: no movement toward God is possible because the inner faculty that registers failure (conscience) is dead. The M07-C gateway passages show that where this posture is maintained, shame becomes the specific inner preparation for receiving God's self-disclosure (Eze 43:10-11).

**[CHAR-2]** E — Limited evidence. Eze 44:13 — Levites bearing shame as a restriction on their approach to God — shows CHAR-2 governing human-to-God access in the priestly context. CHAR-2 does not primarily operate as a human movement toward God; it is imposed on humans from God or from other humans.

---

**[CHAR-3]** E — Extensively evidenced in VCG-01. Joh 8:49 — "you dishonor me" (Jesus = God incarnate); Rom 2:23 — "you dishonor God by breaking the law"; Heb 6:6 — apostates "hold him up to contempt." The human-to-God direction of CHAR-3 is the active worth-denial of God's incarnate person and his moral authority. The inner posture required to avoid CHAR-3 toward God is described in its absence in Luk 18:2 — fearing God is the inner posture that prevents CHAR-3 toward God.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — The idolatrous-shameful-objects register (VCG-01 — Jer 3:24; 11:13; Hos 9:10) is precisely about what the human conscience should assess as shameful in relation to God: the idol is "the shameful thing" (bo.shet — Jer 3:24) that has replaced God in the person's movement toward him. CHAR-4's proper functioning toward God means assessing idolatrous objects as shameful and recoiling from them toward God.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — Human-to-God CHAR-5 is evidenced in the mockery of Jesus (Luk 23:11 — Herod and his soldiers treating Jesus with contempt and mockery). The acts directed at Jesus in his passion are CHAR-5 in its most concentrated form: the world's contempt-verdict on God incarnate. Act 4:11 (the builders rejecting the cornerstone) shows the human rejection of God's sent-one as CHAR-5 directed toward God through the mediating agency of Jesus. The inner posture that prevents CHAR-5 toward God is the recognition of divine worth — receiving the despised as "an angel of God, as Christ Jesus" (Gal 4:14).

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — The primary human-to-God direction of CHAR-6 is worship and approach: Psa 26:6 — "I wash my hands in innocence and go around your altar, O Lord" — is the movement of the innocent person toward God in the cultic act of going around the altar. CHAR-6 is what enables this movement. The inner posture required is moral cleanness — the person who approaches God must have their inner moral condition aligned with the holiness they approach.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — The human-to-God movement across M07 concentrates in three registers. (1) Shame-mediated approach — the guilt-shame of Char 1 (M07-C) and the innocence-enabled approach of Char 6 constitute the two poles of the human-to-God encounter: shame as recognition of moral inadequacy before holiness (Ezr 9:6); innocence as the condition enabling approach without guilt's barrier (Psa 26:6). These two poles are the cluster's most theologically significant human-to-God dimension. (2) Dishonour and contempt directed at God incarnate — Chars 3 and 5 evidence the human actively dishonouring God incarnate (Joh 8:49; Rom 2:23) and directing contempt toward Jesus (Luk 23:11). These are the most theologically acute forms of CHAR-3 and CHAR-5. (3) Shamefulness as covenant infidelity — Char 4's idolatrous-shameful-objects register (Jer 3:24; 11:13; Hos 9:10) shows the human movement toward God corrupted when idolatry produces the shameful object that displaces God.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — The evidence reveals the required posture negatively, through what CHAR-1 removes. Psa 131:1 (vc=34059, M08-A1-VCG-03; vc=34224, M08-A2-VCG-01): "my heart is not lifted up; my eyes are not raised too high; I do not occupy myself with things too great and too marvelous for me" — the deliberate inner lowering of the heart and eyes is the posture that enables the God-ward orientation CHAR-1 precludes. Dan 4:37 (vc=34094, M08-A4-VCG-04): after Nebuchadnezzar's CHAR-1 is humbled, he "praises and extols and honours the King of heaven, for all his works are right and his ways are just" — the posture of God-directed praise emerges as CHAR-1 is removed. The required posture for human-to-God movement is its direct opposite: the heart held at creaturely level, not lifted above it; the eyes not raised in prideful claim; the self positioned as receiver and respondent rather than as self-exalted agent.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Evidenced negatively through CHAR-2's precise inversal. Deu 17:13 (vc=34124, M08-B-VCG-01): "all the people shall hear and fear" — hearing and fearing (reverent submission) is the posture for human-to-God movement that CHAR-2 replaces with defiant self-assertion. Psa 19:13 (vc=34095, M08-B-VCG-02): the psalmist's posture of "keep back your servant from presumptuous sins" — the servant orientation that seeks divine restraint is the human-to-God posture that CHAR-2 inverts. 2Pe 2:10 (vc=42739, M08-B-VCG-03): "they do not tremble" — trembling reverence is the human-toward-divine posture; its absence marks CHAR-2.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Jer 9:23–24 (vc=33342 context, M08-C-VCG-01): the implied positive — "let him who boasts boast in this: that he understands and knows me" — the posture required is knowing God, not knowing about one's own attributes. 1Cor 1:31 (vc=33878, M08-C-VCG-03): "let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord" — the posture is Lord-directed exultation. Gal 6:14 (vc=33869, M08-C-VCG-02): "the world has been crucified to me" — the cross-mediated death to worldly boasting-grounds is the required inner posture for God-directed movement.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Rom 12:3 (vc=60866, M08-D-VCG-02) directly names the required posture: "think of yourself with sober judgment, each according to the measure of faith that God has assigned" — accurate, God-referenced cognitive self-assessment within divinely-assigned measure is the posture required for proper human-to-God orientation. CHAR-4 removes this posture by inflating the self-picture.

**[CHAR-5]** E — 1Ti 6:17 (vc=60878, M08-E-VCG-02) most directly evidences the required alternative posture: "set their hopes... on God, who richly provides everything to enjoy" — the posture required for human-to-God movement is the recognition of God as the source of all structural goods, displacing CHAR-5's self-sufficiency claim. Lev 26:19 (vc=33982, M08-E-VCG-01) implies the same: the proper posture toward God-given power is dependence on God rather than confidence in the power itself.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The five characteristics define the required posture negatively — by evidencing precisely what blocks it. Reading the five together: movement toward God requires a heart not lifted above its creaturely station (the inverse of CHAR-1); a will submitted to God's established authority (the inverse of CHAR-2); a glorying-capacity directed toward God rather than toward the self (the inverse of CHAR-3 VCG-01, actualised by VCG-03); a mind holding itself within God-assigned measure (the inverse of CHAR-4); and hope placed in God as the genuine provider rather than in structural goods (the inverse of CHAR-5). The cluster-synthesis: the required posture for human-to-God movement is the composite inverse of M08 — creaturely lowliness (M09), reverential submission (anti-CHAR-2), God-directed glorying (CHAR-3 VCG-03), sober-minded self-assessment (anti-CHAR-4), and God-trusting stewardship (anti-CHAR-5).

**[CHAR-2]** E — The inner posture required is evidenced across the M09-C corpus. *Faith-trust:* Heb11:8 — Abraham "obeyed by faith" — the trust-orientation that submits to God's word before comprehending its outcome. *Fear of God:* Phili2:12; Col3:22 — reverential awareness of God's authority rather than social-pressure compliance. *Sincere heart:* Eph6:5; Col3:22 — undivided inner genuineness rather than divided performance. *Self-denial of merit:* Luk17:10 — "we are unworthy servants; we have only done what was our duty" — the inner posture that does not claim credit for submission, precisely the posture required for the characteristic's genuineness before God.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The inner posture is the contrite and lowly spirit itself (Isa57:15). The characteristic does not require any additional posture beyond itself — genuine contrition is already the posture before God that draws his dwelling presence. The broken heart and crushed spirit (Psa34:18) constitute the Godward posture: they are an opening toward God created by the collapse of proud self-sufficiency that normally stands between the person and genuine divine encounter.

**[CHAR-4]** S — The evidence is silent on the inner posture required for the characteristic's Godward operation. The characteristic in this corpus operates primarily in the human-toward-others direction rather than the human-toward-God direction.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The inner posture required for semnotēs is established across all three verses: genuine inner character gravity (not performed), paired with godliness (1Ti2:2) and integrity (Tit2:7). The posture required is settled authentic inner-grounded seriousness rather than anxious external performance of gravity. This requires genuine inner formation rather than surface-level manner adoption.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The inner posture required for the human-toward-God movement evidenced by this characteristic is the *freely-moved, uncoerced inner orientation toward God*. Exo35:5 — "whoever is of a willing heart" — the posture is the heart genuinely moving from within rather than under external compulsion. Psa51:12 — the willing spirit as divine gift needed to sustain the movement toward God — implies that genuine posture requires divine upholding when the person's own orientation has been disrupted.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The inner posture required for genuine Godward humbling is evidenced across multiple verses. *Heart-tenderness:* 2Ch34:27 — "your heart was tender" — genuine receptivity of the inner person to being addressed and moved. *Genuine acknowledgment of God's rightness:* 2Ch12:6 — "the Lord is righteous" — the cognitive-moral act of affirming God's authority and one's own inadequacy. *Recognition of one's actual situation:* 2Ki22:19 — hearing God's words as personally claiming — the inner capacity to receive divine address as genuinely relevant to oneself. *Freedom from self-enclosure:* the contrast with 2Ch36:12 (refusal to humble before the prophet) identifies the blocking condition — self-closure against divine address — and its absence as the required posture.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The inner postures required for genuine Godward movement converge across the four characteristics with direct Godward evidence. Humility (CHAR-1): heart-tenderness (2Ch34:27), genuine acknowledgment of God's rightness (2Ch12:6 — "the Lord is righteous"), and receptivity to being addressed as if the word is personally claiming. Submission (CHAR-2): faith-trust (Heb11:8 — obeying by faith before comprehending the outcome), fear of God as the deepest motivator (Phili2:12; Col3:22), and sincere-heart genuineness rather than eye-service. Contrition (CHAR-3): the contrite state is itself the required posture — genuine contrition is already the Godward opening, created by the collapse of proud self-sufficiency. Willing-heartedness (CHAR-6): the freely-moved, uncoerced inner orientation toward God (VCG-01); or divine upholding when the person's own orientation has been disrupted by moral failure (VCG-02). Dignity (CHAR-5): genuine inner character gravity paired with godliness and integrity rather than performed gravity. Cluster-level convergence: all postures require genuine inner reality rather than managed external presentation — M09 characteristics directed toward God are incompatible with performed religious behaviour that bypasses the inner person.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — The sinning movement toward God requires an inner posture of deflection from God's moral claim — the will turning away from the covenantal obligation. 1Sa 15:24 shows this posture: Saul's fear of the people took priority over his fear of God — the inner posture was one of displaced allegiance. Jer 44:23 names the inner posture explicitly: "you did not obey the voice of the Lord or walk in his law and in his statutes" — non-listening and non-walking as the inner posture that constitutes sinning against God. The posture that prevents sinning (VCG-03) is named as its opposite: fear of God before you (Exo 20:20), word stored in heart (Psa 119:11).

**[CHAR-10]** E — The positive inner posture is revealed through the mechanisms' negation. (1) *Against enticement*: stable desire oriented toward God (the opposite of "his own desire" drawing toward sin — Jam 1:14); (2) *Against hypocrisy*: authentic covenantal identity — living truly rather than performing (the opposite of Gal 2:13's collective performance); (3) *Against apostasy*: covenantal faithfulness — remaining in the framework rather than departing (the opposite of Act 21:21's forsaking). The required posture is: desire oriented toward God, authentic identity, and covenantal perseverance.

**[CHAR-11]** E — VCG-02 establishes the required inner posture for movement toward God under the condition: (1) *Faith*: Mat 9:2; Mar 2:5 — "when Jesus saw their faith, he said... your sins are forgiven" — faith is the inner posture that enables the forgiveness-declaration to address the condition; Joh 8:24 — "unless you believe that I am he you will die in your sins" — belief in Jesus is the posture that breaks the condition's fatal hold; (2) *Repentance*: Mar 1:4; Luk 3:3; Act 3:19 — baptism of repentance for forgiveness — repentance is the inner turning required; (3) *Confession*: Mat 3:6; Mar 1:5 — "confessing their sins" — the inner act of acknowledging the condition is part of the required posture.

**[CHAR-12]** E — The inner posture required for human-to-God movement against sin's enslaving power is *faith receiving the promise*: Gal 3:22 — "the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe" — faith-reception is the only posture that can receive the promise the universal imprisonment points toward; no human effort (imprisoned under sin) can achieve the promise. Additionally, *the posture of the born-of-God non-sinner*: 1Jo 3:9 — "no one born of God makes a practice of sinning" — the born-of-God posture is the result of God's initiative (new birth) rather than human effort; the posture of non-sinning that enables God-movement is itself God-given.

**[CHAR-13]** E — Three required inner postures. (1) *Acknowledgment*: Psa 32:5 — "I acknowledged my sin to you, and I did not cover my iniquity; I said, 'I will confess my transgressions to the Lord'" — the posture of non-concealment and active acknowledgment is the first requirement; (2) *Turning*: Eze 18:21 — "turns away from all his sins that he has committed and keeps all my statutes and does what is just and right" — the volitional turning from sin is the required posture for the record to be addressed; (3) *Dependence on divine erasure*: Psa 51:2 — "wash me thoroughly from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin" — the posture of dependence on God's action rather than self-cleansing is the foundational human-to-God posture under the record.

**[CHAR-14]** E — Three required inner postures. (1) *Acknowledgment of the sin*: Exo 32:31 — Moses names it "a great sin" before God; Lev 4:14 — recognition when sin "becomes known"; (2) *Self-affliction*: Lev 23:27 — "you shall afflict yourselves" — the inner posture of humbling and penitential self-examination; (3) *Faith toward the forgiver*: Act 10:43 — "everyone who believes in him receives" — trust directed toward Christ; Act 2:38 — "repent" (metanoeō) — cognitive and volitional reorientation toward God. All three are required: mere recognition without self-affliction is incomplete; self-affliction without faith in the specific forgiver (Christ's name — Act 10:43) does not produce reception.

**[CHAR-15]** E — Three required inner postures. (1) *Heart-turning*: 1Ki 8:47 — "if they turn their heart" — the heart's volitional reorientation from the sinning-direction toward God is the primary required posture; (2) *Repentance*: 1Ki 8:47 — "repent" — the inner volitional act of changing direction within the inherited condition; (3) *Honest confession*: 1Ki 8:47 — "saying, 'We have sinned and have acted perversely and wickedly'" — the corporate speech-act of naming the condition accurately ("perversely and wickedly" — not minimising) is the verbal dimension of the required posture.

**[CHAR-16]** E — Three required inner postures. (1) *Honest self-naming*: Luk 5:8 — "I am a sinful man" — the movement toward God requires naming the identity accurately without minimisation; Luk 18:13 — "be merciful to me, a sinner" — the self-naming precedes and enables the appeal; (2) *Self-abasement*: Luk 18:13 — "standing far off, would not even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast" — the physical and inner posture of self-lowering is the required orientation; (3) *Appeal for mercy rather than justice*: Luk 18:13 — "be merciful to me" — the movement toward God with the sinner-identity requires appealing to grace rather than claiming entitlement.

**[CHAR-17]** E — Three required inner postures. (1) *Acknowledgment*: Hos 5:15 — "until they acknowledge their guilt" — the first movement is honest inner acknowledgment; Jer 3:13 — "only acknowledge your guilt" — acknowledgment is the sine qua non; (2) *Confession*: Lev 5:5 — "confesses the sin he has committed" — verbal naming of what conscience has registered; Num 5:7 — "he shall confess his sin" — the speech-act before God; (3) *Restitution*: Lev 6:4 — "will restore what he took" — the movement toward God under guilt is not merely verbal but restitutive; the wronged person must be made whole.

**[CHAR-18]** E — Three required inner postures. (1) *Humbled heart*: Lev 26:41 — "if then their uncircumcised heart is humbled and they make amends for their iniquity" — the uncircumcised (unreformed) heart must be humbled before movement toward God becomes possible; (2) *Honest verbal acknowledgment*: Lev 26:40 — "if they confess their iniquity and the iniquity of their fathers"; Hos 14:2 — "take with you words" — the movement requires spoken words; (3) *Non-concealment*: Psa 32:5 — "I did not cover my iniquity; I said, 'I will confess my transgressions to the Lord,' and you forgave the iniquity of my sin" — the movement toward God requires uncovering what was concealed.

**[CHAR-19]** E — Three required inner postures. (1) *Volitional turning*: Eze 18:28 — "he considered and turned away from all the transgressions that he had committed" — the turn is both cognitive (considered) and volitional (turned away); (2) *Honest verbal confession*: Psa 32:5 — "I said, 'I will confess my transgressions to the Lord'" — the non-concealment; Pro 28:13 — "he who confesses and forsakes them will obtain mercy"; (3) *Non-self-justification*: Lam 3:42 — "we have transgressed and rebelled, and you have not forgiven" — the honest acknowledgment without self-excuse, even while still bearing unforgiven guilt.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The inner posture required for the human-toward-God movement is *honest acknowledgment of the inadvertent sin*. Lev 5:5 — "confesses the sin he has committed" — the confession must name the sin as sin, even though it was unintentional. Num 22:34 — Balaam does not minimise ("it wasn't my fault, I didn't know") but takes full ownership ("I have sinned") — the inner posture is one of accountability without defensiveness. The posture does not require pre-existing awareness at the moment of sinning (since the characteristic is defined by its absence) but requires honest responsiveness once awareness arrives. The movement toward God is enabled by the conscience's retrospective engagement (T3.9) and blocked by its suppression.

**[CHAR-20]** E — Three required inner postures. (1) *Verbal acknowledgment of the specific treachery*: Lev 26:40 — "confess their iniquity and the iniquity of their fathers in their treachery" — the confession must name the faithlessness specifically, including generational dimensions; (2) *Humility (not pride)*: 2Ch 33:19 — Manasseh's prayer "and how God was moved by his entreaty" — the humbling (2Ch 33:12 — "he humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers") is the counterpoint to 2Ch 26:16's pride that generated the faithlessness; humility is the required inner posture; (3) *Hope-maintained movement*: Ezr 10:2 — "but even now there is hope for Israel in spite of this" — movement toward God under faithlessness requires hope that the relationship remains accessible.

**[CHAR-21]** E — Three required inner postures. (1) *Honest naming of the perversity*: 1Ki 8:47 — "acted perversely" — the confession must name the specific distortion, not generic sin; Dan 9:5 — the comprehensive self-indictment includes "done wrong" (a.vah) specifically; (2) *Putting off the old self*: Eph 4:22-24 — "put off your old self which... is corrupt" → "put on the new self, created after the likeness of God" — the movement requires deliberate interior action at the level of identity; (3) *Sowing to the Spirit rather than the flesh*: Gal 6:8 — the orientation-change from flesh-sowing to Spirit-sowing is the practical inner posture required.

**[CHAR-22]** E — Three required inner postures. (1) *Volitional commitment to cease*: Job 34:32 — "if I have done iniquity, I will do it no more" — the will's commitment to stop; (2) *Active restitution*: Eze 33:15 — "restores the pledge, gives back what he has taken by robbery" — the movement toward God under injustice requires concrete material restitution, not merely inner intention; (3) *Hand-withholding*: Eze 18:8 — "withholds his hand from injustice, executes true justice between man and man" — the active volitional restraint paired with positive just conduct.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The inner posture required for the human-toward-God confessional movement is *honesty without self-protection*. 1Ch 21:17 — "It is I who have sinned and done great evil. But these sheep, what have they done?" — the posture is complete ownership of the sin without deflection, combined with concern for the innocent. Luk 15:21 — "I am no longer worthy to be called your son" — the posture includes honest self-assessment of unworthiness without using that assessment as a bargaining position (the prodigal does not demand a position; he simply names the truth). Contrast: 1Sa 15:30 (Saul) — "I have sinned; yet honor me now before the elders" — the inner posture is compromised by self-protective concern. The required posture is honest self-naming without attached conditions.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Conscience suppression produces an *incorrect inner posture* for the human-to-God movement: Jer 2:35 — the posture of assumed innocence rather than the posture of acknowledged sin. The correct posture (confession — CHAR-3; fear of God — Ecc 8:12 contrast) is exactly what conscience suppression prevents. The inner posture of the conscience-suppressed person toward God is one of false confidence or genuine blindness — neither of which positions the person to receive what the relationship with God actually requires.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The corpus names the required inner posture for the human-to-God movement by its absence: 2Ki 10:31 — "with all his heart" — wholehearted commitment is the required posture; its absence ("not with all his heart") is what enables the refusal. Neh 9:29's "stubborn shoulder and stiffened their neck" describes the actual posture: bodily-metaphor resistance, the opposite of submissive receptivity. The inner posture required for movement toward God is willing surrender of the neck and shoulder to the yoke of God's law — the posture of humility and submission that refusal to repent explicitly withholds.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The inner posture required for the human-to-God movement is named by contrast in two verses. 1Ki 8:46 — Solomon's prayer presupposes that hearing in captivity and turning (repenting) is the required posture for restoration: the movement toward God requires the acknowledgment of sin and the turning from it. 1Jo 3:6 — "no one who abides in him keeps on sinning" — the abiding posture is the one that enables the sustained human-to-God orientation. The required inner posture is thus: the shuv-turn (repentance that 1Ki 8:46 envisions) and the abiding relationship (1Jo 3:6) — both of which habitual defection explicitly withholds.

**[CHAR-7]** E — The inner posture required for genuine human-to-God movement is named through contrast: 2Ki 23:15 — Josiah's demolition of the altar — the posture of a leader whose inner commitment to God drives the community back toward God through structural dismantling. Josiah's act is the implicit positive model: a leader whose inner God-orientation enables the community's movement back toward God rather than away from him. Exo 23:33's preventive command — not allowing the sinning influence to dwell in the land — names the required posture of maintaining the community's God-orientation by protecting it from contagious sin transmission before it begins.

**[CHAR-8]** E — 2Ch 21:10's causal structure implies the positive: the ruler whose inner posture is *faithful to the Lord* (not forsaking) maintains the covenantal ground that prevents political revolt. The required inner posture for the human-to-God movement — covenant fidelity, not forsaking the Lord — is what sustains the political order against revolt. When that posture is maintained, the revolts do not occur (or are resisted); when it is abandoned, the revolts follow.

**[CHAR-9]** E — The inner posture that enables genuine human-to-God movement is implied through contrast with sinful speech. Jude 9 — Michael's posture: "The Lord rebuke you" — deferring to God's authority rather than presuming to speak God's verdict. This creaturely deference is the inner posture for movement toward God: acknowledging God's authority and not presuming to speak what only God can speak. 1Ti 1:13's reversal — from blasphemer to apostle — shows that the inner posture of receiving mercy and knowing God restores the human-to-God movement disrupted by sinful speech.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The inner posture required for the wicked person to move toward God is the reversal of the characteristic's defining elements: the will must "turn from his way" (Eze 3:18; 33:11), the thoughts must be forsaken (Isa 55:7 — VCG-07 — "let the unrighteous man forsake his thoughts"), and the way must be abandoned ("let the wicked forsake his way"). The evidence shows that the required posture is one of active renunciation of the wicked orientation — not passive drift but deliberate departure from the settled inner direction. The one passage where the inner posture of movement toward God is evidenced in the wicked person is Jer 14:20 (re.sha — VCG-11): "we acknowledge our wickedness… for we have sinned against you" — a communal conscience-acknowledgment that opens the path toward God.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The posture required for the constitutionally evil person to move toward God is one of repentance and reception. Act 8:22 (vc=14361 — VCG-05): "Repent, therefore, of this wickedness of yours, and pray to the Lord that, if possible, the intent of your heart may be forgiven you" — the required posture is repentance (turning from the constitutional evil) combined with supplication (prayer for forgiveness of the heart's intent). Jam 1:21 (vc=14368 — VCG-05): "put away all filthiness and rampant wickedness and receive with meekness the implanted word" — the required posture is active stripping away of the constitutional evil combined with receptive meekness toward the word. The posture is not passive — it involves active renunciation and active reception.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The evidence reveals the inner posture required negatively: what must not be present for approach to God to be acceptable. The abominable inner condition must be absent or addressed. Pro 15:8 (vc=1678 — VCG-03): the prayer of the upright is acceptable — the upright inner person is the required posture. Pro 28:9 (vc=65958 — VCG-03): the ear must not be turned from the law — receptivity to divine instruction is required. The VCG-04 repentance evidence (Eze 14:6 — vc=65984) shows what the required posture of movement toward God looks like: turning the face from abominations, which requires active volitional redirection and a conscience that registers the abomination and responds with grief/loathing (Eze 9:4; 36:31). The required inner posture is: conscience functional, will oriented away from abominations, heart without crookedness or arrogance.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The inner posture required for genuine movement toward God is the active removal of idolatrous attachments before or as part of the approach. Jer 4:1 (vc=65903 — VCG-04): "If you return, O Israel… to me you should return. If you remove your detestable things from my presence, and do not waver" — the removal of detestable things is the precondition for genuine return. Eze 14:6 parallel (from CHAR-3 but structurally identical): "repent and turn away from your idols, and turn away your faces from all your abominations." The evidence shows that genuine movement toward God is only possible when the characteristic has been actively removed — the double-allegiance approach of Jer 7:10 (VCG-04) is rejected.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The evidence reveals the required inner posture through the prescribed departure conditions. Isa 55:7 (vc=38200 — VCG-02): "let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts; let him return to the Lord" — forsaking iniquitous way and thoughts is the required inner posture for genuine approach. Jer 4:14 (vc=38205 — VCG-02): "wash your heart from evil, that you may be saved" — the required inner posture is a cleansed heart. Job 11:14 (vc=38207 — VCG-04): "if iniquity is in your hand, put it far away, and let not injustice dwell in your tents" — removal of actively held iniquity and expelled injustice from the dwelling are both required. The inner posture required for movement toward God is: released iniquity, forsaken iniquitous thoughts, cleansed heart — the exact opposite of the characteristic's inner state.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The evidence reveals the required posture through its precise negation. Rev 16:9 (vc=14352 — VCG-01): "they did not repent and give him glory" — repentance and glory-giving are the two required postures for genuine movement toward God. The characteristic's persistent absence of repentance (Rev 16:9/11/21 — VCG-01) names what the movement requires by showing its refusal: a will that yields under judgment, repents of deeds, and redirects its speech from cursing to glorifying. 1Pe 2:12 (vc=14377 — VCG-03): "glorify God on the day of visitation" — the eventual glorifying of God is the movement-toward-God that honourable conduct enables even former accusers to make.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster defines the required posture for genuine movement toward God by naming what must be absent or addressed. All six characteristics identify the removal of their respective evil-form as the precondition for genuine approach: Char 1 (Isa 55:7 — forsake his way and return); Char 2 (Act 3:26 — turning from wickedness); Char 3 (Eze 14:6 — repent, turn from idols, turn faces from abominations); Char 4 (Jer 4:1 — remove detestable things from my presence); Char 5 (Jer 4:14 — wash your heart from evil; Isa 55:7 — forsake his thoughts); Char 6 (Rev 16:9 — repent and give him glory — the required but withheld posture). The cluster reveals: genuine movement toward God requires simultaneous inner-turning (away from the evil form) and directional-turning (toward God). The cluster's required posture is repentance in the fullest sense — a comprehensive re-orientation of the inner person from their M10b characteristic toward God.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Three inner postures are required for the movement toward God within this characteristic. First, recognition: the person must know they are in the defilement-state (Lev 5:2-3, M10c-A-VCG-01 — "when he comes to know it"). Second, integrity: the person must not attempt to move toward God while in the defilement-state without resolution — Lev 7:21 (M10c-A-VCG-08) shows the severest consequence for attempting sacred participation while unclean. Third, active pursuit of remedy: the prescribed remedial acts (washing, waiting, presenting for examination, applying the water of impurity) must be undertaken willingly — Num 19:20 shows that refusal of remedy blocks the movement toward God indefinitely.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Three elements of the required inner posture are evidenced. (1) Active separation from what defiles: 2Cor 6:17 (VCG-03) — "go out from their midst, and be separate from them... touch no unclean thing." The posture is active withdrawal from defiling associations. (2) Self-purification in both body and spirit: 2Cor 7:1 (VCG-03) — "let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of body and spirit." The posture is comprehensive, extending to both constitutional levels. (3) Fear of God as motivating principle: 2Cor 7:1 (VCG-03) — "bringing holiness to completion in the fear of God." The movement toward God is motivated and governed by the fear of God, not merely by self-improvement. The inner posture required is therefore: active-separating, self-purifying, God-fearing.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Two required inner postures are evidenced. (1) Corporate non-defilement through covenantal fidelity: Num 35:34 (VCG-04) — "you shall not defile the land in which you live, in the midst of which I dwell" — the inner posture required for sustained divine proximity is the ongoing maintenance of land, sanctuary, and covenantal integrity. (2) Future repentance through remembered defilement: Eze 20:43 (VCG-02) — the future posture of "loathing yourselves" for past defilement is the inner posture from which the restored approach to God proceeds. The movement toward God requires both the avoidance of defilement (prospective) and the genuine grief over past defilement (retrospective).

**[CHAR-4]** E — The inner posture evidenced is that of the proxies: Mar 7:25 (VCG-01) — prostrate urgency ("fell down at his feet") and persistent seeking. Act 5:16 (VCG-02) — communal care and purposeful gathering ("bringing the sick and those afflicted with unclean spirits"). For the person in the condition, the required posture cannot be named because the person cannot form or express it themselves — the posture is held by those who bring them.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The required inner postures reveal a spectrum from active self-engagement (Chars 1-3) to proxy-mediation (Char 4). Characteristic 1: recognition of the condition, integrity in not attempting access while defiled (Lev 7:21 — the severe consequence of sacred participation while unclean), and active pursuit of remedy (Num 19:19-20). Characteristic 2: active separation from defiling environments (2Cor 6:17 — "go out from their midst"), comprehensive self-purification in body and spirit (2Cor 7:1), and the fear of God as motivating principle (2Cor 7:1 — "bringing holiness to completion in the fear of God"). Characteristic 3: ongoing maintenance of covenantal integrity (Num 35:34) and future genuine self-loathing over past defilement (Eze 20:43) — the posture is both prospective (avoidance) and retrospective (genuine grief). Characteristic 4: the possessed person cannot form or express the required posture — the posture is held by proxies who seek on their behalf (Mar 7:25 — prostrate urgency; Act 5:16 — communal bringing). The cluster's inner posture spectrum: self-recognising-and-seeking (Char 1) → actively-separating-purifying-fearing (Char 2) → covenantally-maintaining-and-genuinely-grieving (Char 3) → proxy-mediated (Char 4). Movement toward God in the M10c cluster requires increasing levels of communal agency as the characteristic's depth and externality increase.

questions.question_text: What does the human-to-God direction of the characteristic show about the person's relationship with God?

findings.session_b_note:
The human-to-God direction reveals three things about the person's relationship with God:

1. **The relationship is asymmetrical in the person's favour:** The person can seek something from God that God alone can give — the forgiveness-capacity is entirely with God (salach-root exclusivity). The relationship is not between equals; the person approaches the one who holds what they need.

2. **The relationship is grounded in God's initiative and character:** Even the human-to-God movement (intercession) is grounded in the conviction that God is disposed to forgive — "there is forgiveness with you" (Psa 130:4). The human movement is a response to what is already known about God's character, not a blind hope.

3. **The relationship has a structural vulnerability:** The outer limit (Mar 3:29 — blasphemy against the Spirit) names the one condition in which the human-to-God movement toward forgiveness is permanently closed. The relationship has a permanent boundary that the human person can cross. This vulnerability is unique to the forgiveness interface: no other characteristic in the data names a permanent foreclosure of the human-to-God relational movement.

findings.session_b_note:
The creature's constitutional dependence: the person approaches God in supplication having recognised they have no basis other than grace for the approach. SD035 (Rom 5:2 prosagōgē — access, approach): grace is the relational condition that transforms the threshold from impassable to open. The human-to-God direction of grace is the creature entering through the door that grace has opened.

*Consistent with prior analysis. Adds T4 framing: prosagōgē as the relational access-concept is significant.*

findings.session_b_note:
The human-to-God direction of compassion reveals a relationship characterised by three structural features:

**Asymmetric but genuinely reciprocal:** The human person does not extend compassion to God in the same way God extends it to the human person — the human person's movement toward God is one of appeal, seeking, and return, not of mercy-giving. Yet the movement is genuinely relational: the person is not passive before a sovereign who dispenses; they actively seek, contemplate, and return. The relationship is asymmetric in power and in the direction of compassion's primary flow but genuinely reciprocal in its relational character.

**Grounded in divine character rather than human performance:** The human person's appeal is always addressed to what God is, not to what the person has done. Psa 25:7 — "according to your steadfast love" — is the recurring structural feature: the ground of appeal is divine character, not human merit. This reveals a relationship in which the human person's movement toward God is constitutively humble — it cannot be based on self-presentation.

**Enabled by the certainty of divine compassion:** The very existence of the supplication vocabulary — earnest, expectant, persistent appeal — reveals that the human person's relationship with God is characterised by the expectation that divine compassion will respond. Techinah is not a tentative request; it is earnest appeal grounded in the knowledge of who God is. The relationship is one in which the human person can approach with confidence — not in their own standing but in the divine compassion-character that is the ground of all approach.

findings.session_b_note:
The human-to-God direction of contrition reveals that the person's relationship with God is **asymmetric and honest**. The contrite person approaches God without pretence, without performance, and without merit-claim — bringing only what is actually present in their inner being: brokenness, lowliness, disclosed need. This is a fundamentally different mode of God-approach than self-presentation or merit-claim.

The asymmetry is honoured rather than resisted: the contrite person does not approach God as an equal or as a claimant but as a creature whose condition has been broken open. This transparency in the God-relationship — bringing what is actually true of oneself rather than a performed version — is what the verse evidence identifies as the mode of approach that draws divine response. The relationship is characterised by creaturely honesty before divine holiness.

*New finding: the human-to-God direction reveals that contrition is the inner-being condition that enables transparent, unperformed, asymmetric approach to God — bringing what is actually true rather than what is presentable. This is the mode of approach that matches the divine character (holy-and-near-to-the-low) evidenced at T0.*

findings.session_b_note:
The human-to-God fellowship direction reveals that the person's relationship with God is participatory rather than merely observational or obedient. The person does not merely obey God or acknowledge him — they *enter* him, share in him, are conformed to him. The language of 2Pe 1:4 (becoming partakers) and Phili 3:10 (sharing his sufferings, becoming like him in his death) is language of genuine entry into divine reality, not merely proximity to it.

This reveals that the human person is constitutionally capable of a genuine participatory relationship with God — not merely a contractual or observational one. Fellowship with God is the deepest expression of what human beings are constitutionally made for (imaging the divine nature in which they participate).

Fellowship with God is the deepest expression of what human beings are constitutionally made for (imaging the divine nature in which they participate).

findings.session_b_note: The human-to-God direction reveals that the relationship is one of responsive dependence grounded in prior divine initiative. The sequence is always: God's goodness is encountered or declared first → the human moves toward God in trust, praise, and seeking → God sustains and fulfils. The human's movement toward God in goodness is not autonomous spiritual achievement but a response enabled by prior encounter with divine goodness. Psa 119:68's "you are good... teach me" names the relationship structure directly: God's goodness is the basis; human receptive orientation follows. The relationship revealed is one of: initiated by God, received by the human, responded to in trust and worship, sustained in covenantal fidelity. The human's part is not passive but it is always derivative — the human's goodness-orientation toward God is itself produced by God's prior goodness toward the human. (OBS-067-OBS-026, OBS-067-OBS-025, OBS-067-OBS-001)

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-067-010: T1 named goodness as carrying directional, relational, and constitutional implications in its very name (Q&A-015). T4 maps those implications onto the relational architecture: the directional implicat…
findings.finding_value: T1 named goodness as carrying directional, relational, and constitutional implications in its very name (Q&A-015). T4 maps those implications onto the relational architecture: the directional implication (goodness flows from God and toward others) is precisely the God-to-human cascade confirmed in T4; the relational implication (goodness operates in relationship) is confirmed by the extensive T4 evidence across all three relational directions; the constitutional implication (goodness is a character depth, not a surface act) is confirmed by the T4 finding that human-to-human giving of goodness requires prior constitutional transformation (Q&A-109). T1's naming-level insight (Q&A-015) is validated by T4's relational-structure evidence: the name carries the architecture.

findings.session_b_note: The data gives several descriptions: (a) Psa 63:3 (OBS-103-087): the person who loves God so values chesed above life that praise becomes natural — the inner state is one of valuation so high it reorders the hierarchy of goods; (b) Joh 14:15 (OBS-103-140): the person who loves Christ keeps commandments — the inner state produces a habitual obedience-pattern; (c) 1Pe 2:17 (OBS-103-065): 'love the brotherhood, fear God' — love toward God and fear of God co-exist as the person's dual dispositional orientation toward the divine. Fear is not love's replacement but its companion. The inner state: reverent love, or loving reverence — the integration of love and fear that Hos 3:5 names ('come in fear to the Lord and to his goodness,' OBS-103-082). The person who loves God is also the person who properly fears God.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-103-004: Love's relational architecture is structured by three directional axes — GOD → HUMAN, HUMAN → GOD, HUMAN → HUMAN — with divine love structurally prior and causally generative of all subsequent love. 1…
findings.finding_value: Love's relational architecture is structured by three directional axes — GOD → HUMAN, HUMAN → GOD, HUMAN → HUMAN — with divine love structurally prior and causally generative of all subsequent love. 1Jo 4:19 ('we love because he first loved us') is the axis-precedence statement: the first axis is not responsive to but constitutive of the second and third. The GOD → HUMAN direction moves through four mechanisms: covenantal declaration (naming the beloved — Jer 12:7, Mat 3:17), Spirit-infusion (Rom 5:5), redemptive acts (Joh 3:16), and covenantal covering (Eze 16:8). The HUMAN → GOD direction requires total inner mobilisation (Mat 22:37 — all heart, soul, mind) and the clearing of rival loves as its condition (1Jo 4:19, 1Ti 6:10). The HUMAN → HUMAN direction spans five structural types (neighbour, enemy, community, friendship, family) and creates the social architecture described in Q&A-088 (restructured kinship, public legibility, competitive generosity). The most significant finding in T4: the human-to-God direction is conditioned by prior reception of divine love — the capacity for human love toward God is itself a gift. The one structural gap: T4.6 (spiritual beings) is absent from the evidence.

findings.session_b_note: The human-to-God mercy-direction reveals the person as constitutively dependent on divine mercy for survival, identity, and access to God. The supplication vocabulary (24 active *techinah* verses; 19 active *atar* verses) as a systematic category within R111 shows that mercy-seeking is not exceptional but normative — the human person's ongoing posture before God is mercy-seeking. *New finding: the volume and systematic nature of the supplication vocabulary in R111 reveals that mercy-seeking is the normative ongoing mode of the human person's relationship with God — not a crisis measure but a structural feature of the human-divine relationship.* OBS-111-010, OBS-111-057.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-111-004: Reading T4 as a whole reveals mercy's relational architecture as directional and asymmetric in all three interface directions (God→human, human→God, human→human), with a structural requirement that re…
findings.finding_value: Reading T4 as a whole reveals mercy's relational architecture as directional and asymmetric in all three interface directions (God→human, human→God, human→human), with a structural requirement that receiving precedes giving. The key synthesis across T4: (a) God-to-human direction is the most extensively evidenced and is the source of mercy in all other directions; (b) human-to-God direction is characterised by normative ongoing supplication — not exceptional crisis-response; (c) human-to-human direction requires prior receipt from God and solidarity-knowledge of the condition being addressed; (d) mercy operates characteristically across relational distance and rupture (Q&A-117), not within maintained relationships; (e) the scope is wide (crossing covenantal boundaries) but not unconditionally permanent (withdrawal is named possibility). The T4 synthesis: mercy's relational architecture is an asymmetric chain — divine mercy → received human mercy → extended human mercy — with the chain requiring the prior link at each stage.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-111-015: T2 establishes the receiving-before-generating constitutional principle (Q&A-062) and T4 establishes the asymmetric relational chain (God→received human→extended human mercy). These are the constituti…
findings.finding_value: T2 establishes the receiving-before-generating constitutional principle (Q&A-062) and T4 establishes the asymmetric relational chain (God→received human→extended human mercy). These are the constitutional and relational descriptions of the same structural requirement: mercy cannot be generated from within the person (T2) and mercy cannot be extended without prior receipt (T4). T2 explains why T4's relational chain is necessary: the constitutional principle of receiving-before-generating is what creates the structural necessity of the T4 relational chain. The body-soul interface through which mercy's mechanism operates (T2 — blood atonement on nephesh) is the constitutionally specific expression of the God→human directional mercy (T4.1).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-111-019: T3 shows mercy activating the full faculty system (perception, cognition, memory, affect, volition, agency, moral evaluation, conscience, conscientiousness, relational capacity) and T4 shows mercy ope…
findings.finding_value: T3 shows mercy activating the full faculty system (perception, cognition, memory, affect, volition, agency, moral evaluation, conscience, conscientiousness, relational capacity) and T4 shows mercy operating across three relational directions (God→human, human→God, human→human). Reading together: the faculty activations in T3 are the inner capacities that each T4 relational direction requires. God→human mercy (T4.1) engages mercy's receptive faculty complex — conscience, moral evaluation, affect, memory (asymmetric structure). Human→God mercy (T4.2 — mercy-seeking) engages volition, agency, affect, conscience, and perception (face-toward-God). Human→human mercy (T4.3) engages moral evaluation, agency, volition, and relational capacity. The three relational directions of T4 are served by the specific faculty subsets activated in T3.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-111-023: T4's relational chain (God→human→human mercy) and T5's formative arc (mercy received forms mercy-giving capacity) are structurally identical processes described at different levels. T4 describes the r…
findings.finding_value: T4's relational chain (God→human→human mercy) and T5's formative arc (mercy received forms mercy-giving capacity) are structurally identical processes described at different levels. T4 describes the relational structure (who gives, who receives, under what conditions); T5 describes the developmental process (what changes in the person as a result). Reading together: T4's relational chain is the structure within which T5's formative arc occurs. The transition from receiving mercy (T4, God→human direction) to giving mercy (T4, human→human direction) is not automatic but requires the formative arc T5 describes — specifically the character formation through suffering (T5.4) and the sustained effects of mercy-reception (T1, confirmed by T5). T4's normative mercy-seeking posture (Q&A-107) is the relational expression of T5's sustained developmental practice (Dan 6:11 daily prayer, Q&A-137).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-111-025: T7's vocabulary analysis shows supplication terms are a major category within R111 (H8467 techinah 24 active; H6279 atar 19 active; G2433 hilaskomai imperative in Luk 18:13). T4 shows the human-to-God…
findings.finding_value: T7's vocabulary analysis shows supplication terms are a major category within R111 (H8467 techinah 24 active; H6279 atar 19 active; G2433 hilaskomai imperative in Luk 18:13). T4 shows the human-to-God direction is characterised by normative ongoing supplication (Q&A-107). Reading T4 and T7 together: the large volume of supplication vocabulary in T7's lexical analysis is the lexical quantification of T4's finding that mercy-seeking is the normative ongoing mode of the human-divine relationship. The vocabulary scale confirms the relational claim: if supplication were exceptional, there would be fewer terms; the 43 active supplication-vocabulary verses confirm ongoing, structured, habitual mercy-seeking. T7's grammatical range analysis (petition as the speech-mode of mercy, T1.4.3) maps to T4's human-to-God direction as the primary speech-mode context.

findings.session_b_note: The human-to-God movement through contrition reveals that the human person's authentic relationship with God is one of creaturely dependence, not merit-based equality. The contrite approach is the most honest form of human-to-God relationship available to the fallen person: no pretension, no performance, no claim — only the broken inner being presented to the holy One who revives. *New finding: contrite approach to God is the paradigm of authentic human-to-God relationship — the form that corresponds most truthfully to the reality of creaturely dependence before divine holiness.* OBS-030-001, OBS-030-045, OBS-030-052.
findings.finding_value: The human-to-God movement through contrition reveals that the human person's authentic relationship with God is one of creaturely dependence, not merit-based equality. The contrite approach is the most honest form of human-to-God relationship available to the fallen person: no pretension, no performance, no claim — only the broken inner being presented to the holy One who revives. *New finding: contrite approach to God is the paradigm of authentic human-to-God relationship — the form that corresponds most truthfully to the reality of creaturely dependence before divine holiness.* OBS-030-001, OBS-030-045, OBS-030-052.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-030-004: T4 as a whole reveals contrition's relational structure is strongly asymmetric: the God-to-human and human-to-God directions are richly evidenced; the human-to-human and spiritual-beings directions ar…
findings.finding_value: T4 as a whole reveals contrition's relational structure is strongly asymmetric: the God-to-human and human-to-God directions are richly evidenced; the human-to-human and spiritual-beings directions are thin or silent. The asymmetry is analytically significant — contrition is primarily a vertical characteristic. What the tier establishes collectively is that contrition constitutes the condition for divine-human relational proximity. The key T4 synthesis: the God-to-human direction (God draws near, dwells with, looks to the contrite) and the human-to-God direction (the contrite person approaches God in lowliness) together create the relational event that contrition is. Neither direction alone describes contrition — it is the convergence of the two movements: divine movement toward the contrite, and creaturely movement toward God through brokenness. The substitutionary group (Isa 53:5) is the only instance of contrition vocabulary operating horizontally — and it is unique to the Servant, not a general pattern.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-010: The definition tier (T1) establishes that contrition operates in three modes along different relational axes; the relational interface tier (T4) maps those axes to specific directional relationships. …
findings.finding_value: The definition tier (T1) establishes that contrition operates in three modes along different relational axes; the relational interface tier (T4) maps those axes to specific directional relationships. The mapping is precise: the penitential mode (T1) corresponds to the human-to-God direction (T4.2) and generates the divine-to-human response (T4.1). The substitutionary mode (T1) corresponds to the only evidence of contrition operating horizontally (T4.3 — Isa 53:5). T1's three-mode structure and T4's directional structure are the same phenomenon described from two perspectives: modes describe what kind of crushing; directions describe who is involved in the relational event. The convergence confirms that contrition is inherently a relational event — its definition cannot be separated from its directional structure.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-015: The constitutional tier (T2) establishes that contrition originates in the encounter between divine holiness and human moral condition (T2.9) and moves constitutionally downward through the person; th…
findings.finding_value: The constitutional tier (T2) establishes that contrition originates in the encounter between divine holiness and human moral condition (T2.9) and moves constitutionally downward through the person; the relational tier (T4) establishes that the primary relational direction is vertical (human before God). The constitutional origin (external, from divine holiness) and the relational direction (vertical, toward God) are structurally aligned: contrition's constitutional ground explains its relational asymmetry. Because contrition originates from divine-human encounter, its primary relational interface is necessarily with God — the one whose holiness generated the encounter. The vertical asymmetry in T4 is not arbitrary but constitutionally determined by T2's origin analysis.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-019: The faculty tier (T3) establishes that contrition opens every engaged faculty toward God (perception deepened for divine address, volition redirected toward God, agency converted to God-seeking, relat…
findings.finding_value: The faculty tier (T3) establishes that contrition opens every engaged faculty toward God (perception deepened for divine address, volition redirected toward God, agency converted to God-seeking, relational capacity enabled for divine nearness); the relational tier (T4) shows that the primary relational direction is indeed toward God. T3 and T4 are aligned: the faculty effects all point in the same direction that T4's relational analysis names as the primary direction. The faculties do not pull in multiple directions — they converge on the vertical relational axis. This convergence is analytically significant: it means contrition is constitutively God-directed at the faculty level, not merely structurally positioned toward God.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-023: The relational tier (T4) establishes that contrition creates the condition for divine-human relational proximity; the formative tier (T5) shows that this relational positioning is the goal of contriti…
findings.finding_value: The relational tier (T4) establishes that contrition creates the condition for divine-human relational proximity; the formative tier (T5) shows that this relational positioning is the goal of contrition's formative work. Together T4 and T5 reveal that contrition's formation is relational formation — the character produced by repeated contrition is not moral character in the abstract but the specific relational disposition of creaturely proximity to God. The settled lowliness produced by T5 is precisely the inner posture that T4 names as the condition for divine dwelling and divine looking. Formation (T5) and relational positioning (T4) are therefore the same reality described longitudinally and synchronically: T5 shows the character being formed; T4 shows what that character makes possible.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-025: The relational tier (T4) shows the divine-to-human and human-to-God directions of contrition; the evidential tier (T7) identifies the primary literary contexts (penitential psalm = human-to-God; proph…
findings.finding_value: The relational tier (T4) shows the divine-to-human and human-to-God directions of contrition; the evidential tier (T7) identifies the primary literary contexts (penitential psalm = human-to-God; prophetic address = God-to-human). The literary forms in T7 directly correspond to the relational directions in T4: the psalm form is the human-to-God literary vehicle; the prophetic form is the God-to-human literary vehicle. The two primary anchor verses confirm this: Psa 51:17 (psalm — human addressing God in contrition) and Isa 57:15 (prophecy — God addressing the community with the promise of dwelling with the contrite). T7's literary analysis explains why T4 finds two distinct relational directions: they are embedded in two distinct literary genres.

findings.session_b_note: The human-to-God direction reveals that the human person is constitutively participatory — made for fellowship with God. 2Pe 1:4's divine nature participation is not a foreign addition but the fulfilment of the image-bearer's created participatory capacity. 1Jo 1:3 establishes horizontal fellowship as derived from and dependent on vertical fellowship. OBS-062-056, OBS-062-058.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-062-004: T4 reveals fellowship as the most relationally comprehensive characteristic in the registry: it operates in all four primary directions (God-to-human, human-to-God, human-giving, human-receiving) and …
findings.finding_value: T4 reveals fellowship as the most relationally comprehensive characteristic in the registry: it operates in all four primary directions (God-to-human, human-to-God, human-giving, human-receiving) and partially in the spiritual-beings direction. The key T4 synthesis: 1Jo 1:3's structural claim — horizontal fellowship is derived from and grounded in vertical fellowship — means the relational architecture of fellowship is hierarchical: the divine-human fellowship is primary; human-human fellowship is its extension and expression. The scope analysis (Q&A-119) reveals that fellowship scope narrows as its depth increases: all-the-living (widest) → God-fearers → covenant partner → ecclesial body → divine nature participants (deepest-narrowest). Depth and breadth are inversely proportional in fellowship's relational structure.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-010: T1's five modes correspond directly to T4's relational directions: existential mode = all-the-living (widest scope); companionship mode = human-to-human (giving and receiving); covenantal mode = coven…
findings.finding_value: T1's five modes correspond directly to T4's relational directions: existential mode = all-the-living (widest scope); companionship mode = human-to-human (giving and receiving); covenantal mode = covenant partner; ontological mode = human-to-God (deepest). The scope-narrows-as-depth-increases finding (T4, Q&A-119) is the relational expression of T1's definition: as the fellowship object becomes more specific (from all-the-living to divine nature), the depth increases while the scope narrows. T1's structural negative (misdirected fellowship) maps onto T4's receiving-direction analysis (Hos 4:17 — prior wrong fellowship blocks reception of right fellowship).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-023: T4's relational architecture (vertical primary; horizontal derived) and T5's formation arc (habituation → constitutional character) are structurally connected through 1Jo 1:3: the horizontal fellowshi…
findings.finding_value: T4's relational architecture (vertical primary; horizontal derived) and T5's formation arc (habituation → constitutional character) are structurally connected through 1Jo 1:3: the horizontal fellowship is derived from and grounded in the vertical (T4), and the vertical fellowship is the source from which the horizontal formation extends (T5 — the person who has received divine fellowship can extend human fellowship that is grounded in that divine reality). T4's scope-narrows-as-depth-increases finding is T5's formation telos: the deepest fellowship (divine nature participation — 2Pe 1:4) is also the narrowest in scope and the furthest eschatological endpoint.

findings.session_b_note: The human-to-God direction reveals the person as constitutively dependent on divine forgiveness for restored relational access. The act of seeking forgiveness names the person's honest position: one who owes a debt they cannot pay and appeals to the one who can cancel it. This is a specific form of the Dependence/Creatureliness dimension — not general creaturely dependence but specifically moral-debt dependence. OBS-064-022.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-064-004: T4 establishes the most structurally developed relational architecture of any characteristic reviewed in this series. All four primary directions are fully evidenced: God-to-human (the dominant vertic…
findings.finding_value: T4 establishes the most structurally developed relational architecture of any characteristic reviewed in this series. All four primary directions are fully evidenced: God-to-human (the dominant vertical direction — exclusively divine in the OT salach domain), human-to-God (seeking-forgiveness — intercession and confession), human-giving (commanded horizontal), human-receiving (implied in the horizontal transaction). The spiritual-beings direction adds the Holy Spirit as the enabling mediator (Joh 20:22-23) and the unforgivable sin as the outer limit (Mar 3:29). The vertical-horizontal interdependence (Mat 18:35; Mat 6:14-15) is the most structurally developed relational feature: the human-giving direction is structurally conditioned on the human-receiving direction (one who genuinely received divine forgiveness can genuinely extend human forgiveness). The scope analysis shows: universal access through faith (Act 10:43) with an absolute outer limit (Mar 3:29). T4's synthesis: forgiveness has the fullest relational architecture of the characteristics reviewed — every direction is evidenced, and the vertical-horizontal interdependence is a structural claim unique to forgiveness.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-023: T4's vertical-horizontal interdependence (the structural claim that receiving divine forgiveness enables extending human forgiveness) is T5's formation arc described at the relational level. The forma…
findings.finding_value: T4's vertical-horizontal interdependence (the structural claim that receiving divine forgiveness enables extending human forgiveness) is T5's formation arc described at the relational level. The formation sequence (T5 — forgiveness received → love generated → capacity to extend formed) is the inner development through which T4's structural interdependence is created: the person who genuinely receives divine forgiveness and generates the love-response (T5) is the person who has the genuine volitional capacity to extend horizontal forgiveness (T4). The eschatological telos (T5.6 — Jer 31:34) is also T4's permanent relational state: the guilt-barrier permanently removed produces permanently restored relational access to God.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-004: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion…
findings.finding_value: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion on whom I have compassion"), covenantally grounded (chesed as the bond-loyalty that grounds the characteristic), and situationally responsive (splanchnizō — triggered by the specific sight of suffering). These three bases are not in tension but in integration: divine compassion is free, covenanted, and responsive simultaneously. The scope finding is among the most analytically significant in the registry: compassion explicitly and repeatedly crosses covenantal boundaries (Nineveh, the Samaritan/Jew axis, the power-asymmetric relationship). Scope is defined by perceived need, not moral standing or covenantal membership — this is formally confirmed in the data and distinguishes compassion from many other relational characteristics. The chesed/splanchnizō distinction maps onto distinct relational registers: chesed sustains within established bonds; splanchnizō extends across distance and difference. T4.4 (receiver's inner-being experience) is the most significant gap — four P-rated prompts, entirely absent from the data. T4.6 (spiritual beings interface) is entirely silent across all four prompts.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-004: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — a…
findings.finding_value: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — all God-as-subject). The basis of divine extension is the giver's character and prior knowing (Exo 33:17 — "I know you by name"), not the receiver's merit — neither merit-based nor arbitrary. The human-to-God direction is specifically supplication: tachanum (H8469) is the receiving side's corresponding vocabulary built into the same root family as the giving side (chen/chanan) — the vocabulary embeds the two-directional circuit in a single root. The human-giving direction extends grace horizontally through three modes: forgiving (charizō — Eph 4:32), gracious conduct (chen as character quality — 889-003), and gracious speech (SD022). The receiving direction is the most underexamined (T4.4 — P-rated throughout); the scope analysis (T4.5) reveals grace crossing covenantal and social boundaries (Ruth narrative — grace in the context of foreign status and vulnerability). T4.6 (spiritual beings) is evidenced at one point: Luk 1:28 (kecharitōmenē — the angel's announcement), which implies angelic ministry as a vehicle of grace rather than grace operating independently in the spiritual-beings register. T4 synthesis: the relational architecture of grace is unique in the programme — it is the only characteristic where the giving-side vocabulary and the receiving-side vocabulary are built from the same root (chen/tachanum), encoding the grace-circuit's two-sidedness at the lexical level.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-010: T1's four modes of operation map onto T4's four relational directions. The sovereign-bestowal mode corresponds to the God-to-human direction (T4.1 — primary and dominant). The covenantal-relational-su…
findings.finding_value: T1's four modes of operation map onto T4's four relational directions. The sovereign-bestowal mode corresponds to the God-to-human direction (T4.1 — primary and dominant). The covenantal-relational-sustaining mode corresponds to the relational scope (T4.5 — grace operating within and across covenantal boundaries). The capacity-conferring mode corresponds to the human-to-God direction in its supplication register (T4.2 — SD026: grace giving even the capacity to appeal). The character-forming mode corresponds to the human-giving direction (T4.3 — gracious conduct and speech as the horizontal expression of received grace-character). The vocabulary's structural insight (T4 synthesis: giving-side and receiving-side built from the same root, chen/tachanum) explains T1's finding that grace requires the receptor's inner engagement to complete its operation — the vocabulary encodes the two-sidedness because grace is constitutively a two-sided circuit.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-015: T2's origin analysis (grace does not originate in the human constitutional system — it arrives from God) and T4's directional analysis (God-to-human is primary and dominant) are the same finding from …
findings.finding_value: T2's origin analysis (grace does not originate in the human constitutional system — it arrives from God) and T4's directional analysis (God-to-human is primary and dominant) are the same finding from constitutional and relational perspectives respectively. The spirit level as reception point (T2.1) and the God-to-human direction as primary (T4.1) are mutually explanatory: because grace originates with God and is received at the spirit level, the primary relational direction is necessarily God-initiated toward the human spirit. The human-to-God direction (T4.2 — supplication) corresponds to T2.10's constitutional movement in reverse: the soul's recognition of need translates into the somatic enactment of supplication (prostration, fasting, sackcloth), which is T2.7's bidirectional body-soul finding. Constitutional location and relational direction are co-determining.
