findings.finding_value: T3's agency-constituting finding (grace constitutes rather than replaces agency — 1Cor 15:10) and T4's human-to-God direction (supplication as the human posture of appeal — requiring genuine human agency in the act of plea) are structurally aligned. The constituted agency (T3.7) is precisely the agency that supplication requires: the creature must genuinely appeal, not merely receive passively. T3's finding that grace and conscience are mutually necessary (T3.9) corresponds to T4's relational-access finding: grace transforms the threshold of human-to-God approach (prosagōgē — SD035) from impassable to open, which is the relational expression of T3.9's constitutional finding that grace creates the condition within which conscience can operate fully without destruction. T3 names the inner-being event; T4 names the relational consequence of the same event.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-023: T4's relational directions correspond to T5's formation mechanisms. The God-to-human direction (T4.1 — sovereign bestowal) corresponds to the encounter and spirit-outpouring mechanisms (T5.3 — sudden …
findings.finding_value: T4's relational directions correspond to T5's formation mechanisms. The God-to-human direction (T4.1 — sovereign bestowal) corresponds to the encounter and spirit-outpouring mechanisms (T5.3 — sudden specific relational event; Zec 12:10). The human-to-God direction (T4.2 — supplication) corresponds to the sustained-formation arc of T5.5: the person who habitually supplicates is being formed into the character that supplicates, which is itself the character-quality kind identified in T1. The human-giving direction (T4.3 — gracious forgiving, speech-grace) corresponds to T5.3's mediated-transformation mechanism (grace → tenderheartedness → forgiving → gracious speech — SD030, Eph 4:32). T4 describes the relational shape of each mechanism; T5 describes the inner formation process each mechanism produces.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-025: T4's most analytically distinctive finding (the vocabulary encodes the two-sided grace-circuit in a single root: chen/chanan for giving; tachanum/techinah for seeking) is T7's most significant root-le…
findings.finding_value: T4's most analytically distinctive finding (the vocabulary encodes the two-sided grace-circuit in a single root: chen/chanan for giving; tachanum/techinah for seeking) is T7's most significant root-level finding. T7.1 confirms: the chen root family embeds both the giving side (chen — favour, chanan — to be gracious) and the receiving-seeking side (tachanum, techinah — supplication) in a single etymological family. This is unique in the programme's vocabulary data: no other characteristic has the giving-side and receiving-side vocabulary built from the same root. T4's relational architecture and T7's lexical analysis are the relational and lexical descriptions of the same structural reality — that grace is constitutively a two-sided circuit whose two sides are inseparable at the root level.

findings.session_b_note: The human-to-God direction of covenant reveals that the relationship with God is not passive receipt but active responsive engagement — the person is not merely a beneficiary of God's covenant but a participant who moves toward God through commitment, love, and sustained faithfulness. This reveals three things about the relationship: (1) It is asymmetric but genuinely mutual — God initiates, but the human's responsive movement is genuinely required and genuinely meaningful. The covenant is not a monologue but a dialogue with defined roles. (2) The whole person is engaged — "all your heart and all your soul" means the human-to-God movement requires the full inner person, not merely intellectual assent or ritual compliance. (3) The relationship is sustained through practice — not merely entered once but maintained through ongoing covenant-keeping, remembering, and love. The relationship with God is therefore constitutively covenantal in its structure: it has entry (joining), maintenance (keeping), failure (breach), and return (confession) — a full relational arc.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-010: T1 establishes that covenant has directional, relational, and constitutional implications that orient the entire enquiry (Q&A-015). T4 shows how these directional implications are realised: the God-to…
findings.finding_value: T1 establishes that covenant has directional, relational, and constitutional implications that orient the entire enquiry (Q&A-015). T4 shows how these directional implications are realised: the God-to-human direction is the primary axis (T4.1), the human-to-God direction is the responsive axis (T4.2), and the horizontal direction (T4.3/4.4) is grounded in the vertical. The T1 × T4 synthesis: the directional implication identified at the definitional level (T1) is fully realised in the relational interface structure (T4). The asymmetry of the definition (God initiates, human responds — Q&A-015) is the same asymmetry that governs all four relational directions in T4. Definition and relational interface are structurally consistent — covenant is asymmetric at every level of analysis.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-024: T4 reveals that God-to-human covenant operates through five modes (establishment, faithfulness, inscription, oath-binding, mediation — Q&A-101). T6 reveals that covenant is causally prior to other cha…
findings.finding_value: T4 reveals that God-to-human covenant operates through five modes (establishment, faithfulness, inscription, oath-binding, mediation — Q&A-101). T6 reveals that covenant is causally prior to other characteristics and produces love/hesed, hope, knowing, and faithfulness as its effects (Q&A-152). The T4 × T5 synthesis: the God-to-human directional modes (T4) are the relational mechanisms through which the causal productivity identified in T6 operates. God establishes covenant (T4.1) → covenant becomes the ground for hope (T6, Q&A-150, Q&A-152). God inscribes on the heart (T4.1 mode 3) → knowing is produced (T6, Q&A-152). God mediates through Christ (T4.1 mode 5) → sanctification is produced (T6, Q&A-152). The five God-to-human modes (T4) are the directional mechanisms that produce the T6 causal effects. T4 is the directional 'how'; T6 is the consequential 'what'.

findings.session_b_note: The human-to-God movement in peace reveals that the human person has the constitutional capacity to orient toward God and thereby receive peace — the movement is not coerced but voluntary, and it is genuinely possible. The refusal pattern (Isa 30:15 — "but you were unwilling") demonstrates that the movement can be declined — the human person retains the capacity to refuse peace. This reveals: the human's relational standing with God is not static but dynamically engaged by the direction of the inner person's orientation. When the human turns toward God in quiet trust, peace flows from God to the human; when the human turns away (stubbornness, false peace), the peace-channel is closed from the human side. God remains ready to give peace; the human's inner posture determines whether it is received.

findings.session_b_note: The human-to-God giving direction reveals that the relationship with God is one of responsive correspondence: the human gives back to God (glory, praise, self) in direct correspondence to what God has first given. Job's blessing mirrors divine giving-and-taking. The Servant's self-offering mirrors divine covenantal faithfulness. The glory-giving (Jer 13:16) returns to God what is already his. The relationship is not symmetrical — God gives primarily, the human gives responsively — but it is genuinely reciprocal in form. The inner postures required (recognition, trust, urgency) reveal that the relationship requires the full engagement of the human inner person — it is not a passive receiving relationship but an active responsive one. The DHC (Divine-Human Correspondence) dimension of group 872-006 (OBS-060-023) is the clearest expression: the correspondence is the relational structure constituted by the proper flow of giving in both directions.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-060-004: T4 as a whole reveals that the relational architecture of this characteristic is directionally structured and asymmetrical. The dominant direction is God-to-human (6 of 7 groups, confirmed across T4.1…
findings.finding_value: T4 as a whole reveals that the relational architecture of this characteristic is directionally structured and asymmetrical. The dominant direction is God-to-human (6 of 7 groups, confirmed across T4.1); the human direction is responsive (T4.2: human gives back what was first given). The basis of divine giving is plural — covenantal, responsive, formative, moral-consequential, eschatological-grace (Q&A-102) — revealing that faithfulness is not a single relational mode but a relational orientation that differentiates itself across relational conditions while remaining unified in character. The human-to-God direction reveals responsive correspondence as the relational structure (Q&A-107): the proper relational form is one in which the human gives back to God what is his (glory, praise, self), having first received. The human-to-human direction is thinner in the data (Q&A-109) — reflecting the registry's God-subject dominance. T4.6 is substantially silent on spiritual beings. What T4 reveals as a whole: faithfulness-as-giving is constitutively a divine-initiative relational reality that the human enters through responsive participation. The human's giving is always downstream of divine giving; the correspondence is the proper form of the relationship.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-003: The five operational modes of giving (T1.4) map onto the four relational interfaces (T4) in a specific structural way. Performative and covenantal giving (modes 1) operate through the God-to-human int…
findings.finding_value: The five operational modes of giving (T1.4) map onto the four relational interfaces (T4) in a specific structural way. Performative and covenantal giving (modes 1) operate through the God-to-human interface (T4.1) with a covenantal basis. Responsive giving (mode 2) operates through the God-to-human interface with a responsive basis. Endowing giving (mode 3) operates through God-to-human with a formative basis. Judicial giving (mode 4) operates through God-to-human with a moral-consequential basis. Relinquishing self-giving (human mode) operates through the human-to-God interface. Glory-giving operates through the human-to-God interface. The relational interface is not external to the definition — it is a structural element of each operational mode. What this pair reveals: the characteristic cannot be defined without specifying its relational direction. The same act-concept (giving) becomes a different operational mode depending on which interface it operates through.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-008: The constitutional locations where the characteristic operates (T2 — heart, soul/nephesh, spirit, body) and the relational interfaces through which it operates (T4 — God-to-human, human-to-God) reveal…
findings.finding_value: The constitutional locations where the characteristic operates (T2 — heart, soul/nephesh, spirit, body) and the relational interfaces through which it operates (T4 — God-to-human, human-to-God) reveal a mirroring structure. God's giving proceeds from his leb (heart, Hos 11:8) and his nafshi (soul, Jer 12:7) — the deepest divine inner-being locations are engaged in the God-to-human direction. The human's giving toward God is expressed through the body (back, cheeks, face — Isa 50:6) and from the deepest inner orientation (Job 1:21 — recognition of divine sovereignty). The constitutional depths engaged in both directions are commensurate: God gives from his heart and soul; the human gives from the whole self, expressed bodily. What this pair reveals: the divine-human relational correspondence (DHC dimension, group 872-006) has a constitutional depth structure — the correspondence is not merely behavioural but engages the deepest constitutional levels of both parties. The giving that constitutes the correspondence is heart-to-body deep.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-017: The relational interfaces (T4 — God-to-human primary, human-to-God responsive, covenantal scope) and the structural landscape (T6 — hub position, causal sequences, shared anchors) reveal that R060's h…
findings.finding_value: The relational interfaces (T4 — God-to-human primary, human-to-God responsive, covenantal scope) and the structural landscape (T6 — hub position, causal sequences, shared anchors) reveal that R060's hub position is constituted by its position at the centre of the divine-human relational network. The sequential patterns (T6.2 — giving→worship, suffering→giving, faithlessness→giving-over) are relational sequences: each involves God and the human in the roles described by T4. The shared anchors (T6.6) are high-density precisely because they are relational nodes — Hos 11:8 anchors five registries because it holds the divine inner-being and the human relational situation simultaneously. What this pair reveals: the structural hub position of R060 in the inner-being landscape is a direct consequence of its occupation of the divine-human relational centre. It is a hub because it is where the primary divine-human dynamic (God gives, human receives and responds) is most directly expressed and most extensively connected.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-018: The relational interface analysis (T4 — six of seven groups are God-to-human; the divine disposition ranges from covenantal to compassionate to formative to moral-consequential) and the primary anchor…
findings.finding_value: The relational interface analysis (T4 — six of seven groups are God-to-human; the divine disposition ranges from covenantal to compassionate to formative to moral-consequential) and the primary anchor identification (T7 — Hos 11:8 as the verse that uniquely reveals the divine inner-being decision structure) converge. Hos 11:8 is the primary anchor precisely because it holds the full complexity of T4 in a single verse: it shows the God-to-human relational direction (the giving is addressed at Ephraim/Israel), the multiple bases of divine giving (deserved-judgement vs. compassionate restraint), and the divine disposition (heart recoiling, compassion warming). The full vocabulary arc (T7.1.10 — enacted + constituted poles) maps onto the two directions of T4: the enacted pole (na.tan) is the God-to-human and human-to-God relational act; the constituted pole (emunah/hesed/pistis) is the dispositional quality that makes the relational giving faithful rather than merely generous. What this pair reveals: the relational architecture and the vocabulary architecture are the same structure described at two levels of abstraction.

**[CLUSTER]** E. The human-to-God direction of righteousness reveals that relationship with God is the constitutive context of righteousness in M26. Righteousness is not primarily a social virtue or a moral performance — it is the orientation of the person toward the God who is himself righteous. Every human-to-God movement in the cluster (appeal, worship, cry for justice, faith, upright walk) is an expression of righteousness as a relational disposition toward God.

The wisdom-orientation directed toward God (froneō Spirit, VCG04) reveals the human-divine relationship as one of orientation: the person's inner directional constitution is either aligned with God or against him. Wisdom-toward-God reveals that the relationship is constitutive of the person's deepest inner character — not a transactional posture but an orientation of the whole self.

findings.finding_value: The wealth domain is one of Scripture's primary tests of whether the human person's foundational relationship is with God or with material goods. M46-A shows what the relationship looks like when wealth has displaced God (trust redirected, self-sufficient self-assessment, no seeking). M46-C and M46-D show what the relationship looks like when God remains primary (wealth received as gift, honoured with firstfruits, wealth voluntarily released for the higher valuation of God's purposes). The person's relationship with God is revealed by their relationship with wealth.

findings.finding_value: The extensive documentation of human-to-God reverential fear in M01-A reveals that the relationship between the human person and God is fundamentally asymmetrical: God is the holy, incomparable sovereign; the human person is the created image-bearer whose appropriate posture before God is awe and reverence. But the evidence also reveals this as a *relationship* rather than mere subjection: Psa 25:14 (fear positioning for covenant friendship — intimacy, not servility), Psa 103:13 (God showing "fatherly compassion" to those who fear him — parental, not merely imperial relationship). The human-to-God direction of M01-A reveals a relationship of asymmetrical intimacy: the appropriate posture is reverential, and that very reverential posture opens the person to God's friendship and covenant love.

The human-to-God direction of M01 reveals that genuine relationship with God begins in and is sustained by reverential fear. The absence of this fear (Rom 3:18; Psa 36:1) is the diagnostic of a broken relationship. The presence of it is the ground of covenant intimacy (Psa 25:14), divine provision (Psa 34:9), and eschatological reward (Rev 11:18; 19:5). Rev 13:6 — blaspheming God's name, dwelling, and people — shows the full scope of the inversion: every dimension of the creature's proper God-orientation (acknowledging God's name, his presence, his people) is reversed into speech against them. The disrupted human-to-God direction in sinful speech is not merely broken but actively reversed — the creature speaks against God rather than merely failing to speak toward him.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The human-to-God direction of the characteristic reveals that wickedness is a relational orientation — it is constituted by the person's orientation away from God (Psa 10:4; 9:17; Mal 3:18) and can potentially be reversed by reorientation toward God (Eze 33:11; Isa 55:7). The characteristic is therefore not merely a moral-quality category but a relational-directional one: the wicked person is the person whose inner life is pointed away from God. This relational definition is consistent with the structural opposite: righteousness (tsaddiq) is the person who serves God (Mal 3:18), knows God's way (Psa 1:6), and walks not in the counsel of the wicked (Psa 1:1). The human-to-God relational direction defines the characteristic as fundamentally a God-relationship status.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The human-to-God direction reveals that evil as constitutional inner nature is specifically a God-approach blocker — its primary relational consequence at the vertical level is the foreclosing of the human's access to God. Heb 10:22 (VCG-06) names the evil conscience as the specific obstacle. Heb 3:12 (VCG-06) frames the evil heart as leading away from God. The characteristic therefore defines the human person as constitutionally at a relational distance from God — not primarily by external circumstance but by constitutional inner condition. The human-to-God direction reveals that the characteristic's address (Act 3:26 — turning from wickedness; Heb 10:22 — cleansed conscience) is the precondition for vertical relational restoration.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The human-to-God direction reveals that abomination operates as a specific corruption of the approach relationship — it is not merely that the abominable person is bad; their very attempts at religious approach become additional abominations. Pro 15:8 (vc=1678 — VCG-03) and Isa 1:13 (vc=1695 — VCG-03) show that the attempt to approach God without inner transformation compounds the offense: the abominable inner person's sacrifice and incense are themselves additional abominations. This reveals the characteristic as one that, in its unaddressed state, makes approach to God impossible and any attempted approach counterproductive — deepening the relational violation rather than reducing it.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The human-to-God direction reveals that idolatrous abomination specifically blocks and corrupts the vertical relational movement. Deu 32:16 (vc=65938 — VCG-02): what should be movement toward God (worship) is redirected to "strange gods" — idolatrous abomination is the worship-capacity directed wrongly. Jer 7:10 (vc=65963 — VCG-04): standing in God's house while continuing in abominations — even the physical act of temple-approach is made ineffectual by the characteristic. The characteristic reveals that the devotion-capacity is a single faculty: it can move toward God or toward idols, but not both simultaneously. Idolatrous abomination occupies the devotion-channel so completely that genuine movement toward God requires its prior removal.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The human-to-God direction reveals that iniquity as active scheming specifically blocks and nullifies the prayer-worship channel. Psa 66:18 (vc=38182 — VCG-04): cherished iniquity = closed divine ear. Isa 1:13 (vc=38197 — VCG-04): iniquity-accompanied religious assembly = divine intolerance. Psa 14:4 (VCG-03): evildoers do not call on God — they lack even the orientation toward the divine. This blocking is the deepest consequence of the characteristic at the individual level: not merely the harm done to others but the severing of the person's own access to God through prayer and worship. The characteristic reveals itself as not merely antisocial but fundamentally anti-covenantal, cutting off the person from the primary relational resource of covenant life.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The human-to-God direction reveals that the characteristic is specifically and completely anti-worship: it converts every divine approach (including judgment) into an occasion for further hostility. Rev 16:9/11/21 (VCG-01): scorching heat, pain, hailstones — each escalating divine contact produces not approach but increased hostility. The characteristic transforms the encounter with divine power from a grace-invitation into a defiance-occasion. This reveals a will so hardened that the divine-human encounter itself cannot penetrate it with corrective force — the very instruments of divine approach become the stimuli for greater defiance. The human-to-God direction of the characteristic is thus: every divine encounter deepens the anti-movement.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's human-to-God evidence reveals that M10b characteristics function as the primary obstacles to the divine-human relationship — each characteristic blocking access to God in its own distinctive way. Char 3 (corrupt worship as additional abomination — Pro 15:8), Char 4 (idolatrous worship converting worship into divine provocation — Deu 32:16), Char 5 (cherished iniquity closing the divine ear — Psa 66:18), Char 6 (the most extreme form — blasphemy converting divine encounter into defiance rather than approach — Rev 16:9/11/21). At cluster scope: the M10b cluster names the inner-being conditions that make every attempted human-to-God movement an additional violation — the corrupted inner state makes the approach itself abominable (Char 3 VCG-03 — Isa 1:13; Pro 15:8). The cluster reveals that the M10b-constituted person cannot genuinely approach God without first departing from the M10b characteristic — approach and inner evil are constitutively incompatible.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The human-to-God direction reveals the relationship as one of structured access — God's holiness creates the access boundary; the defilement-state is the condition that disrupts access; the remedial system restores it. The person's relationship to God is mediated through the clean/unclean boundary: this boundary is not arbitrary but reflects the incompatibility of the divine holiness with the creaturely defilement-state (Lev 15:31: "defiling my tabernacle that is in their midst"). The grief of exclusion at Num 9:7 and the drive to find a remedial pathway show that the person's relationship to God is one of genuine desire for access, which the defilement-state blocks and which the remedial system restores.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The human-to-God direction reveals the relationship as one in which the person's inner moral condition is constitutively relevant to their access to God. The characteristic is not merely a private inner state but one that structurally affects the God-human relational capacity: Eph 5:5 (VCG-04) — "has no inheritance" — the characteristic severs covenantal relational access. The positive-inverse at Rev 14:4 (VCG-05) — "they follow the Lamb wherever he goes" — shows that the absence of the characteristic is the condition for the most intimate possible relational following of God. The relationship to God is thus in direct proportion to the person's moral-inner cleanliness: the more defiled, the more the relation is severed; the more undefiled, the more intimate the following.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The characteristic reveals the covenantal relationship with God as one in which the community's corporate conduct directly affects its relational access to God. The community inhabits sacred space (land, sanctuary) in which God dwells — this means that the community's moral conduct has direct consequences for divine proximity. Eze 5:11 (VCG-03) — defilement of the sanctuary provokes divine withdrawal — and Eze 20:31 — persistent self-defilement closes divine accessibility — both show that the characteristic is not a private inner condition but one with direct relational consequences for divine access.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The characteristic reveals that the relationship between the person and God can be mediated by the faith and agency of others when the person's own capacity for movement toward God is suppressed. The community of care (mother — Mar 7:25; father — implied in Luk 9:42; crowds — Act 5:16) functions as the relational conduit. This reveals the characteristic as testing and employing the community's relational-mediatorial capacity: the community's faith-agency toward God substitutes for the person's suppressed faith-agency.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's human-to-God direction collectively reveals four distinct relational profiles, each shaped by the defilement's mechanism. Characteristic 1: structured access — the relationship is mediated through the clean/unclean boundary; the person's relationship to God is governed by a sacral status system that both limits and enables access. Characteristic 2: moral condition as constitutive of relational standing — the inner moral condition directly determines the person's access to divine welcome (2Cor 6:17) and eschatological inheritance (Eph 5:5); the most defiled person is furthest from God; the most undefiled follows the Lamb most intimately (Rev 14:4). Characteristic 3: corporate covenantal conduct as constitutive of divine proximity — the community's corporate moral conduct determines whether God dwells in their midst or withdraws; the relationship to God is mediated through the community's shared sacral stewardship. Characteristic 4: the relationship can be mediated by the community of care when the person's own access is suppressed — the most distinctive revelation of the four, showing that even when an individual cannot move toward God themselves, the community's faith-agency can carry that movement on their behalf. The cluster's unified insight: the relationship with God is always present and relevant — but its access path is differently structured in each register (sacral status, moral condition, corporate conduct, community mediation).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-004: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion…
findings.finding_value: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion on whom I have compassion"), covenantally grounded (chesed as the bond-loyalty that grounds the characteristic), and situationally responsive (splanchnizō — triggered by the specific sight of suffering). These three bases are not in tension but in integration: divine compassion is free, covenanted, and responsive simultaneously. The scope finding is among the most analytically significant in the registry: compassion explicitly and repeatedly crosses covenantal boundaries (Nineveh, the Samaritan/Jew axis, the power-asymmetric relationship). Scope is defined by perceived need, not moral standing or covenantal membership — this is formally confirmed in the data and distinguishes compassion from many other relational characteristics. The chesed/splanchnizō distinction maps onto distinct relational registers: chesed sustains within established bonds; splanchnizō extends across distance and difference. T4.4 (receiver's inner-being experience) is the most significant gap — four P-rated prompts, entirely absent from the data. T4.6 (spiritual beings interface) is entirely silent across all four prompts.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-004: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — a…
findings.finding_value: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — all God-as-subject). The basis of divine extension is the giver's character and prior knowing (Exo 33:17 — "I know you by name"), not the receiver's merit — neither merit-based nor arbitrary. The human-to-God direction is specifically supplication: tachanum (H8469) is the receiving side's corresponding vocabulary built into the same root family as the giving side (chen/chanan) — the vocabulary embeds the two-directional circuit in a single root. The human-giving direction extends grace horizontally through three modes: forgiving (charizō — Eph 4:32), gracious conduct (chen as character quality — 889-003), and gracious speech (SD022). The receiving direction is the most underexamined (T4.4 — P-rated throughout); the scope analysis (T4.5) reveals grace crossing covenantal and social boundaries (Ruth narrative — grace in the context of foreign status and vulnerability). T4.6 (spiritual beings) is evidenced at one point: Luk 1:28 (kecharitōmenē — the angel's announcement), which implies angelic ministry as a vehicle of grace rather than grace operating independently in the spiritual-beings register. T4 synthesis: the relational architecture of grace is unique in the programme — it is the only characteristic where the giving-side vocabulary and the receiving-side vocabulary are built from the same root (chen/tachanum), encoding the grace-circuit's two-sidedness at the lexical level.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-010: T1's four modes of operation map onto T4's four relational directions. The sovereign-bestowal mode corresponds to the God-to-human direction (T4.1 — primary and dominant). The covenantal-relational-su…
findings.finding_value: T1's four modes of operation map onto T4's four relational directions. The sovereign-bestowal mode corresponds to the God-to-human direction (T4.1 — primary and dominant). The covenantal-relational-sustaining mode corresponds to the relational scope (T4.5 — grace operating within and across covenantal boundaries). The capacity-conferring mode corresponds to the human-to-God direction in its supplication register (T4.2 — SD026: grace giving even the capacity to appeal). The character-forming mode corresponds to the human-giving direction (T4.3 — gracious conduct and speech as the horizontal expression of received grace-character). The vocabulary's structural insight (T4 synthesis: giving-side and receiving-side built from the same root, chen/tachanum) explains T1's finding that grace requires the receptor's inner engagement to complete its operation — the vocabulary encodes the two-sidedness because grace is constitutively a two-sided circuit.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-015: T2's origin analysis (grace does not originate in the human constitutional system — it arrives from God) and T4's directional analysis (God-to-human is primary and dominant) are the same finding from …
findings.finding_value: T2's origin analysis (grace does not originate in the human constitutional system — it arrives from God) and T4's directional analysis (God-to-human is primary and dominant) are the same finding from constitutional and relational perspectives respectively. The spirit level as reception point (T2.1) and the God-to-human direction as primary (T4.1) are mutually explanatory: because grace originates with God and is received at the spirit level, the primary relational direction is necessarily God-initiated toward the human spirit. The human-to-God direction (T4.2 — supplication) corresponds to T2.10's constitutional movement in reverse: the soul's recognition of need translates into the somatic enactment of supplication (prostration, fasting, sackcloth), which is T2.7's bidirectional body-soul finding. Constitutional location and relational direction are co-determining.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-019: T3's agency-constituting finding (grace constitutes rather than replaces agency — 1Cor 15:10) and T4's human-to-God direction (supplication as the human posture of appeal — requiring genuine human age…
findings.finding_value: T3's agency-constituting finding (grace constitutes rather than replaces agency — 1Cor 15:10) and T4's human-to-God direction (supplication as the human posture of appeal — requiring genuine human agency in the act of plea) are structurally aligned. The constituted agency (T3.7) is precisely the agency that supplication requires: the creature must genuinely appeal, not merely receive passively. T3's finding that grace and conscience are mutually necessary (T3.9) corresponds to T4's relational-access finding: grace transforms the threshold of human-to-God approach (prosagōgē — SD035) from impassable to open, which is the relational expression of T3.9's constitutional finding that grace creates the condition within which conscience can operate fully without destruction. T3 names the inner-being event; T4 names the relational consequence of the same event.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-023: T4's relational directions correspond to T5's formation mechanisms. The God-to-human direction (T4.1 — sovereign bestowal) corresponds to the encounter and spirit-outpouring mechanisms (T5.3 — sudden …
findings.finding_value: T4's relational directions correspond to T5's formation mechanisms. The God-to-human direction (T4.1 — sovereign bestowal) corresponds to the encounter and spirit-outpouring mechanisms (T5.3 — sudden specific relational event; Zec 12:10). The human-to-God direction (T4.2 — supplication) corresponds to the sustained-formation arc of T5.5: the person who habitually supplicates is being formed into the character that supplicates, which is itself the character-quality kind identified in T1. The human-giving direction (T4.3 — gracious forgiving, speech-grace) corresponds to T5.3's mediated-transformation mechanism (grace → tenderheartedness → forgiving → gracious speech — SD030, Eph 4:32). T4 describes the relational shape of each mechanism; T5 describes the inner formation process each mechanism produces.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-025: T4's most analytically distinctive finding (the vocabulary encodes the two-sided grace-circuit in a single root: chen/chanan for giving; tachanum/techinah for seeking) is T7's most significant root-le…
findings.finding_value: T4's most analytically distinctive finding (the vocabulary encodes the two-sided grace-circuit in a single root: chen/chanan for giving; tachanum/techinah for seeking) is T7's most significant root-level finding. T7.1 confirms: the chen root family embeds both the giving side (chen — favour, chanan — to be gracious) and the receiving-seeking side (tachanum, techinah — supplication) in a single etymological family. This is unique in the programme's vocabulary data: no other characteristic has the giving-side and receiving-side vocabulary built from the same root. T4's relational architecture and T7's lexical analysis are the relational and lexical descriptions of the same structural reality — that grace is constitutively a two-sided circuit whose two sides are inseparable at the root level.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Extensively evidenced in VCG-01. Joh 8:49 — "you dishonor me" (Jesus = God incarnate); Rom 2:23 — "you dishonor God by breaking the law"; Heb 6:6 — apostates "hold him up to contempt." The human-to-God direction of CHAR-3 is the active worth-denial of God's incarnate person and his moral authority. The inner posture required to avoid CHAR-3 toward God is described in its absence in Luk 18:2 — fearing God is the inner posture that prevents CHAR-3 toward God.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The idolatrous-shameful-objects register (VCG-01 — Jer 3:24; 11:13; Hos 9:10) is precisely about what the human conscience should assess as shameful in relation to God: the idol is "the shameful thing" (bo.shet — Jer 3:24) that has replaced God in the person's movement toward him. CHAR-4's proper functioning toward God means assessing idolatrous objects as shameful and recoiling from them toward God.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — Human-to-God CHAR-5 is evidenced in the mockery of Jesus (Luk 23:11 — Herod and his soldiers treating Jesus with contempt and mockery). The acts directed at Jesus in his passion are CHAR-5 in its most concentrated form: the world's contempt-verdict on God incarnate. Act 4:11 (the builders rejecting the cornerstone) shows the human rejection of God's sent-one as CHAR-5 directed toward God through the mediating agency of Jesus. The inner posture that prevents CHAR-5 toward God is the recognition of divine worth — receiving the despised as "an angel of God, as Christ Jesus" (Gal 4:14).

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — The primary human-to-God direction of CHAR-6 is worship and approach: Psa 26:6 — "I wash my hands in innocence and go around your altar, O Lord" — is the movement of the innocent person toward God in the cultic act of going around the altar. findings.session_b_note:
Yes — horizontal giving is the second major dimension of forgiveness in the NT corpus, named in group 5377-002 (11 verses) and across multiple commands:

**The commanded giving of forgiveness:**
- Mat 18:35 — "forgive your brother from your heart." The giving is commanded, heart-level, and addressed to a specific relational other ("your brother").
- Luk 17:3-4 — "if he repents, forgive him... seven times in the day... you must forgive him." The giving is repeated, responsive to verbal repentance, and without accumulating limit.
- Mar 11:25 — "whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone." The giving of forgiveness is embedded in the prayer-posture — the regular rhythmic context.
- Luk 11:4 — "forgive us our sins, for we ourselves forgive everyone who is indebted to us." The giving is described as the accompanying act that grounds the request for received forgiveness — the structural congruence (F-003).

**How the giving operates:** OBS-064-026 — "the inner-being act is a volitional release — choosing to no longer hold a legitimate claim." The giving operates as a deliberate inner decision to release what is legitimately held. The giving is not a natural impulse (like love or compassion) but a commanded volitional act with a cost.

findings.session_b_note:
Yes — the human-to-human giving direction is well-evidenced, primarily through the splanchnizō Gospels pattern (human subjects), the sumpatheō/sumpaschō vocabulary, and the eleēmosunē evidence.

**Luke 10:33 — the Good Samaritan:** The most explicit human-to-human compassion-giving in the data. The Samaritan is splanchnizō toward the wounded man and extends an extraordinary investment of care: binding wounds, providing transport, shelter, and ongoing financial provision. This is compassion-giving in its fullest and most complete form — extending across cultural distance, at personal cost, to a stranger.

**Luke 15:20 — the father of the prodigal:** Splanchnizō in a relational-moral context. The father's compassion-movement produces immediate, uninhibited action: running, embracing, kissing, restoring to full sonship. This is compassion-giving within a broken relational bond — the restoration of what was lost.

**Matt 18:27 — the king in the parable:** Splanchnizō producing release of debt. Compassion-giving in a judicial-moral context — mercy rather than judgment, at great personal financial cost to the king.

**Heb 10:34 — sumpatheō in the community:** The readers showing compassion (sumpatheō) to those in prison, expressed through the joyful acceptance of property plundering. This is participatory compassion-giving in the context of persecution — sharing in another's loss as an act of genuine solidarity.

**G1654 eleēmosunē:** Almsgiving as the normalised social form of compassion-giving. Matt 6:2-4 establishes the manner: privately, from inner purity, not for display. Luke 11:41 — "give as alms those things that are within" — grounds the outer act in the inner quality.

**Proclamatory giving:** 1Jo 1:3 — *that which we have seen and heard we proclaim also to you, so that you too may have fellowship with us* — the one who has received fellowship extends it to others through proclamation. The act of proclamation is the act of fellowship-extension.

findings.session_b_note: Human-to-human giving of goodness is evidenced in four forms: (1) Instruction and edification — Rom 15:14 ("full of goodness... able to instruct one another"): the goodness-filled person extends goodness toward others through teaching and building up. (2) Kindness as relational disposition — Col 3:12 (put on chrēstotēs as garment): the deliberate expression of generosity of spirit toward others in the community. (3) Justice and right action — Mic 6:8 ("to do justice"): goodness extended toward others as the active practice of just treatment. (4) Covenantal kindness — the tov vocabulary in its relational register covers loyalty and steadfast faithfulness in human relationships, paralleling the divine hesed-goodness pattern. Each of these is an extension of inner goodness toward another person. (OBS-067-OBS-025, OBS-067-OBS-027, OBS-067-OBS-039, SBF-067-Q039)

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-067-004: T4 as a whole reveals that goodness operates across all relational directions simultaneously — God-to-human, human-to-God, and human-to-human — but with a fundamental asymmetry: the God-to-human direc…
findings.finding_value: T4 as a whole reveals that goodness operates across all relational directions simultaneously — God-to-human, human-to-God, and human-to-human — but with a fundamental asymmetry: the God-to-human direction is prior, generative, and abundant in evidence; the human-to-God direction is responsive and derivative; the human-to-human direction is overflow from prior reception. This is not a simple tripartite scheme but a structured cascade: God's goodness initiates and flows toward the human person (Q&A-099-101); the human responds in trust, seeking, and worship (Q&A-103-105); the goodness received overflows toward others through instruction, justice, and kindness (Q&A-107-109). The most structurally significant T4 finding is the unconditional/conditional distinction (Q&A-100): God's goodness as a character attribute is unconditional; the human's ongoing experience of its relational benefits is conditional on continued trust. This distinction has direct implications for how goodness is taught, received, and sustained. The spiritual beings interface is largely silent — the relational architecture of goodness is thoroughly human-divine in orientation.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-067-024: T4 confirmed that goodness operates across all three relational directions (God-to-human, human-to-God, human-to-human). T6's structural relationships and shared anchors data confirms that the cross-r…
findings.finding_value: T4 confirmed that goodness operates across all three relational directions (God-to-human, human-to-God, human-to-human). T6's structural relationships and shared anchors data confirms that the cross-registry connections of goodness are organised along the same relational axes. The Mic 6:8 shared anchor (6 co-registries) is organized along the human-to-God and human-to-human axes: humility with God (vertical) and justice/kindness with others (horizontal). The Gal 5:22 shared anchor (5 co-registries) is organized along the human-community axis: Spirit-fruit characteristics that are all expressed in human relationship. The sequential finding (goodness → repentance, goodness → faith — Q&A-147-148) corresponds to the God-to-human relational direction: divine goodness producing these inner-being responses in the human. T6's cross-registry connections are the structural record of goodness's relational reach — the registries it is most connected to are the registries it most closely interacts with in its relational operation. Relational architecture (T4) and structural position (T6) are co-extensive.

findings.session_b_note: Love as given outward is the primary ethical direction of the commandment structure: love your neighbour (Lev 19:18), love your enemy (Mat 5:44), love one another (Joh 13:34). The giving of love reaches its maximum in Joh 15:13 (OBS-103-125) — 'greater love has no one than this: that someone lay down his life/soul for his friends.' The gift of the soul is love's outer limit. The giving-forms span: chesed as daily covenantal faithfulness given to the covenant-partner (OBS-103-089); agapē given to the enemy against natural preference (OBS-103-143); phileō given as warmth within the community (OBS-103-119); rachamim given as compassion toward the suffering (OBS-103-105). Love-as-given is the primary ethical form in which the inner orientation is concretely actualised.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-103-004: Love's relational architecture is structured by three directional axes — GOD → HUMAN, HUMAN → GOD, HUMAN → HUMAN — with divine love structurally prior and causally generative of all subsequent love. 1…
findings.finding_value: Love's relational architecture is structured by three directional axes — GOD → HUMAN, HUMAN → GOD, HUMAN → HUMAN — with divine love structurally prior and causally generative of all subsequent love. 1Jo 4:19 ('we love because he first loved us') is the axis-precedence statement: the first axis is not responsive to but constitutive of the second and third. The GOD → HUMAN direction moves through four mechanisms: covenantal declaration (naming the beloved — Jer 12:7, Mat 3:17), Spirit-infusion (Rom 5:5), redemptive acts (Joh 3:16), and covenantal covering (Eze 16:8). The HUMAN → GOD direction requires total inner mobilisation (Mat 22:37 — all heart, soul, mind) and the clearing of rival loves as its condition (1Jo 4:19, 1Ti 6:10). The HUMAN → HUMAN direction spans five structural types (neighbour, enemy, community, friendship, family) and creates the social architecture described in Q&A-088 (restructured kinship, public legibility, competitive generosity). The most significant finding in T4: the human-to-God direction is conditioned by prior reception of divine love — the capacity for human love toward God is itself a gift. The one structural gap: T4.6 (spiritual beings) is absent from the evidence.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-003: Love's definition as directed attachment reaches its relational specification in T4's three-axis architecture. The object-determination principle (Q&A-144) — that love's moral quality depends entirely…
findings.finding_value: Love's definition as directed attachment reaches its relational specification in T4's three-axis architecture. The object-determination principle (Q&A-144) — that love's moral quality depends entirely on its object — is enacted relationally when the proper objects are named: God (vertical-ascending), neighbour and enemy (horizontal), and the beloved community (horizontal-mutual). The definition's three registers map onto the relational axes: the dispositional register (stable inner orientation) grounds the covenantal-faithful love in the GOD→HUMAN axis (God's chesed never ceasing — Lam 3:22); the active register (commanded, exercised) grounds the love of neighbour and enemy (Lev 19:18, Mat 5:44); the condition register (being-loved as identity) is the GOD→HUMAN axis's effect in the person (agapētos — constituted as beloved). The relational interfaces reveal what the definition describes abstractly: love's mechanism in concrete directional operation. The most significant inter-tier finding: the definition's requirement that love be directed toward an object is fulfilled eschatologically when the object is perfectly and permanently God — Jer 31:34, 1Jo 4:18 (perfect love).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-111-004: Reading T4 as a whole reveals mercy's relational architecture as directional and asymmetric in all three interface directions (God→human, human→God, human→human), with a structural requirement that re…
findings.finding_value: Reading T4 as a whole reveals mercy's relational architecture as directional and asymmetric in all three interface directions (God→human, human→God, human→human), with a structural requirement that receiving precedes giving. The key synthesis across T4: (a) God-to-human direction is the most extensively evidenced and is the source of mercy in all other directions; (b) human-to-God direction is characterised by normative ongoing supplication — not exceptional crisis-response; (c) human-to-human direction requires prior receipt from God and solidarity-knowledge of the condition being addressed; (d) mercy operates characteristically across relational distance and rupture (Q&A-117), not within maintained relationships; (e) the scope is wide (crossing covenantal boundaries) but not unconditionally permanent (withdrawal is named possibility). The T4 synthesis: mercy's relational architecture is an asymmetric chain — divine mercy → received human mercy → extended human mercy — with the chain requiring the prior link at each stage.

findings.session_b_note: The substitutionary group (Isa 53:5) involves the Servant's crushing producing outcomes for others — the nearest instance of contrition-vocabulary being "extended" toward another. However, this is not interpersonal contrition (person A being contrite toward person B) but vicarious crushing (the Servant's crushing producing peace and healing in the community). Genuine interpersonal contrition — being contrite toward another human one has wronged — is implied in Psa 51's context (David's sin against Bathsheba and Uriah) but the verses in the registry focus on the vertical dimension. OBS-030-041, OBS-030-042.

findings.finding_value: T4 as a whole reveals contrition's relational structure is strongly asymmetric: the God-to-human and human-to-God directions are richly evidenced; the human-to-human and spiritual-beings directions are thin or silent. The asymmetry is analytically significant — contrition is primarily a vertical characteristic. What the tier establishes collectively is that contrition constitutes the condition for divine-human relational proximity. The key T4 synthesis: the God-to-human direction (God draws near, dwells with, looks to the contrite) and the human-to-God direction (the contrite person approaches God in lowliness) together create the relational event that contrition is. Neither direction alone describes contrition — it is the convergence of the two movements: divine movement toward the contrite, and creaturely movement toward God through brokenness. The substitutionary group (Isa 53:5) is the only instance of contrition vocabulary operating horizontally — and it is unique to the Servant, not a general pattern.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-015: T2's constitutional origin (divine character as the source — Psa 86:5, Psa 130:4) explains T4's God-to-human directional dominance. Because forgiveness originates exclusively in divine character at th…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional origin (divine character as the source — Psa 86:5, Psa 130:4) explains T4's God-to-human directional dominance. The somatic-compassion origin (T2.5) is the constitutional enabler of the horizontal-giving direction (T4.3): the person who genuinely gives forgiveness does so from a somatic-affective inner origin (splagchnizomai), not merely a verbal performance.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-025: T4's relational directions map onto T7's literary forms. The God-to-human direction (T4.1 — dominant) is carried by the cultic-legal corpus (H5545 Niphal — God forgives, people receive), the prophetic…
findings.finding_value: T4's relational directions map onto T7's literary forms. The God-to-human direction (T4.1 — dominant) is carried by the cultic-legal corpus (H5545 Niphal — God forgives, people receive), the prophetic corpus (Jer 31:34 — divine forgiveness promise), and the apostolic letter corpus (Eph 1:7 — through his blood). The human-to-God direction (T4.2 — seeking) is carried by the penitential psalm corpus (Psa 130, Dan 9) and the Synoptic narrative (1Jo 1:9). The horizontal-giving direction (T4.3) is carried by the Synoptic parable corpus (Mat 18:23-35) and the apostolic command corpus (Eph 4:32; Luk 17:3-4). T7's literary forms are the evidential vehicles for T4's relational directions — each direction has a primary literary home.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-004: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion…
findings.finding_value: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion on whom I have compassion"), covenantally grounded (chesed as the bond-loyalty that grounds the characteristic), and situationally responsive (splanchnizō — triggered by the specific sight of suffering). These three bases are not in tension but in integration: divine compassion is free, covenanted, and responsive simultaneously. The scope finding is among the most analytically significant in the registry: compassion explicitly and repeatedly crosses covenantal boundaries (Nineveh, the Samaritan/Jew axis, the power-asymmetric relationship). Scope is defined by perceived need, not moral standing or covenantal membership — this is formally confirmed in the data and distinguishes compassion from many other relational characteristics. The chesed/splanchnizō distinction maps onto distinct relational registers: chesed sustains within established bonds; splanchnizō extends across distance and difference. T4.4 (receiver's inner-being experience) is the most significant gap — four P-rated prompts, entirely absent from the data. T4.6 (spiritual beings interface) is entirely silent across all four prompts.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-004: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — a…
findings.finding_value: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — all God-as-subject). The basis of divine extension is the giver's character and prior knowing (Exo 33:17 — "I know you by name"), not the receiver's merit — neither merit-based nor arbitrary. The human-to-God direction is specifically supplication: tachanum (H8469) is the receiving side's corresponding vocabulary built into the same root family as the giving side (chen/chanan) — the vocabulary embeds the two-directional circuit in a single root. The human-giving direction extends grace horizontally through three modes: forgiving (charizō — Eph 4:32), gracious conduct (chen as character quality — 889-003), and gracious speech (SD022). The receiving direction is the most underexamined (T4.4 — P-rated throughout); the scope analysis (T4.5) reveals grace crossing covenantal and social boundaries (Ruth narrative — grace in the context of foreign status and vulnerability). T4.6 (spiritual beings) is evidenced at one point: Luk 1:28 (kecharitōmenē — the angel's announcement), which implies angelic ministry as a vehicle of grace rather than grace operating independently in the spiritual-beings register. T4 synthesis: the relational architecture of grace is unique in the programme — it is the only characteristic where the giving-side vocabulary and the receiving-side vocabulary are built from the same root (chen/tachanum), encoding the grace-circuit's two-sidedness at the lexical level.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-019: T3's agency-constituting finding (grace constitutes rather than replaces agency — 1Cor 15:10) and T4's human-to-God direction (supplication as the human posture of appeal — requiring genuine human age…
findings.finding_value: T3's agency-constituting finding (grace constitutes rather than replaces agency — 1Cor 15:10) and T4's human-to-God direction (supplication as the human posture of appeal — requiring genuine human agency in the act of plea) are structurally aligned. The constituted agency (T3.7) is precisely the agency that supplication requires: the creature must genuinely appeal, not merely receive passively. T3's finding that grace and conscience are mutually necessary (T3.9) corresponds to T4's relational-access finding: grace transforms the threshold of human-to-God approach (prosagōgē — SD035) from impassable to open, which is the relational expression of T3.9's constitutional finding that grace creates the condition within which conscience can operate fully without destruction. T3 names the inner-being event; T4 names the relational consequence of the same event.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-034-004: T4 as a whole reveals that covenant's relational interface structure is asymmetric but genuinely bilateral. The God-to-human direction (T4.1) is the founding and sustaining axis — God initiates, commi…
findings.finding_value: T4 as a whole reveals that covenant's relational interface structure is asymmetric but genuinely bilateral. The God-to-human direction (T4.1) is the founding and sustaining axis — God initiates, commits, inscribes, and mediates. The human-to-God direction (T4.2) is the responsive axis — the whole person moves toward God through commitment, love, and faithfulness. The horizontal directions (T4.3 giving; T4.4 receiving) are genuine but secondary, and the evidence shows they are grounded in and enabled by the vertical. The relational scope expands progressively across the covenant trajectory — from particular (Abraham) to expanding (Israel) to universal (new covenant in Christ). The spiritual-beings interface (T4.6) is largely absent from the data — the only relevant material is the pagan deity named "lord of covenant" (H1286) and the inferred adversarial spiritual claim. T4 as a whole shows that covenant's relational architecture is constituted by God's prior initiative and realised through the whole person's responsive engagement.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-019: T3 reveals that the inner faculties covenant most deeply engages are Other-oriented (relational capacity, conscience, moral evaluation, memory). T4 reveals that covenant's relational interfaces are as…
findings.finding_value: T3 reveals that the inner faculties covenant most deeply engages are Other-oriented (relational capacity, conscience, moral evaluation, memory). T4 reveals that covenant's relational interfaces are asymmetric (God initiates; human responds; horizontal is grounded in vertical). The T3 × T4 synthesis: the Other-oriented faculty bias (T3) and the asymmetric relational structure (T4) are coherently related — the inner faculties that covenant engages are precisely those required for the kind of asymmetric responsive relationship that covenant constitutes. The relational capacity (T3.11) is the constitutional equipment for genuine connection; the covenant's relational interfaces (T4) are the actual connections that this capacity enables. The inner posture required for human-to-God covenant movement (T4.2 — Q&A-106: reverent fear, love, all-heart, hearing orientation) corresponds directly to the inner faculties that covenant engages: fear engages moral evaluation (T3.8), love engages affect and relational capacity (T3.4, T3.11), all-heart engages volition (T3.6), and hearing engages perception (T3.1). T3 and T4 are two analytical views of the same responsive inner-being structure.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-099-004: T4 reveals that kindness operates across all four relational directions for which evidence exists — God-to-human (most extensively evidenced), human-to-God (appeal/chasid identity mode), human giving,…
findings.finding_value: T4 reveals that kindness operates across all four relational directions for which evidence exists — God-to-human (most extensively evidenced), human-to-God (appeal/chasid identity mode), human giving, human receiving, and communal — with spiritual beings being the only direction that is genuinely absent from the evidence. The structural finding: the four evidenced directions form a coherent circuit, not parallel independent operations. Divine kindness flows to the human → the human receives it and appeals to it (human-to-God) → the human, having received, is equipped and obligated to give it to others (human giving, grounded in Eph 4:32's "as God in Christ forgave you, be kind") → kindness given and received forms the communal relational fabric (chasidim assembly). The circuit is both moral and ontological: it is not merely that we ought to be kind because God is kind, but that the human person is constituted to be a bearer of the divine kindness in the relational world. T4's most significant intra-tier finding: the divine-to-human direction is the source and ground of all other directions — human giving of kindness is explicitly grounded in received divine kindness, making T4 a circuit with a single originating source.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-010: T1's definition of kindness as other-oriented loyal goodwill is perfectly reflected in T4's relational interface structure: kindness has no meaningful existence except in the relational directions T4 …
findings.finding_value: T1's definition of kindness as other-oriented loyal goodwill is perfectly reflected in T4's relational interface structure: kindness has no meaningful existence except in the relational directions T4 maps. The T4 finding that divine-to-human is the most extensively evidenced direction grounds T1's working definition — kindness in its primary form is God's stable outward-oriented goodwill toward the creature, and the human analogue is derived from and dependent on this. The T4 circuit (divine → human → reproduced in giving toward others → communal) maps onto T1's conditions of reception (Q&A-031): the person who has received divine kindness and responded with trust and covenant orientation is precisely the person positioned to extend it to others. T1's finding that kindness explicitly excludes self-serving motivation (Q&A-020) is structurally necessary for T4's circuit to function: if kindness at any point in the circuit becomes self-serving (chrēstologia), the transmission is severed — which is why Eph 4:32 grounds human giving not in the recipient's desert but in the received divine kindness.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-015: T2's constitutional location findings (heart as primary site; Spirit as origin) directly enable and ground T4's relational interface findings. The T4 circuit (divine → human → giving → communal) is no…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional location findings (heart as primary site; Spirit as origin) directly enable and ground T4's relational interface findings. The T4 circuit (divine → human → giving → communal) is not possible without a constitutional base that can receive, hold, and transmit kindness — which is exactly what T2's heart-level location provides. The T2 finding that kindness originates in God's own character (Exo 34:6), is Spirit-mediated into the believer (Gal 5:22), and is inscribed on the heart (Pro 3:3) describes the constitutional preparation of the relational equipment T4 maps. The T2 finding that kindness moves outward (soul → body expression) is the constitutional basis for T4's "giving" direction: the inner character disposition (T2) is what makes outward relational giving (T4) possible. Conversely, T4's relational circuit — and specifically the giving direction grounded in received divine kindness (Eph 4:32) — explains why the T2 constitutional movement runs in the direction it does: the constitutional movement is outward because the characteristic is constitutively relational.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-019: T3's faculty analysis and T4's relational interface analysis are structurally interdependent in a specific way: the faculties that kindness most strongly engages (volition, agency, relational capacity…
findings.finding_value: T3's faculty analysis and T4's relational interface analysis are structurally interdependent in a specific way: the faculties that kindness most strongly engages (volition, agency, relational capacity, conscientiousness) are precisely the faculties required for the T4 relational circuit to operate. Relational capacity (T3.11) is what makes the T4 interfaces possible at all — the person must have the constitutional equipment for genuine connection before kindness can flow in any direction. Agency (T3.7) is what makes the T4 giving direction concrete — not passive benevolence but enacted care. Conscientiousness (T3.10) is what makes the T4 circuit sustainable across time — the chasid who reliably keeps covenant. The T4 communal interface (Moses's intercession; the chasidim assembly) requires an intercessory capacity (T3 — memory + relational capacity) that knows how to appeal on behalf of others. The two tiers together describe a portrait of the whole inner person oriented outward: T3 names the inner equipment and T4 names the relational directions in which that equipment is deployed.

findings.finding_value: T4's relational circuit and T5's formation pathway are mutually reinforcing at a structural level. The T4 finding that human giving of kindness is grounded in received divine kindness (Eph 4:32 — Q&A-067) is also the primary T5 formation mechanism in its encounter mode: the encounter with divine chesed in the relational interface (T4 divine-to-human direction) is itself the formative encounter (T5 encounter mechanism) that produces the chasid. The T4 and T5 circuits are therefore not two separate processes but the same process described relationally (T4) and formationally (T5). The T5 finding that suffering does not impair kindness formation connects with T4's communal interface finding (Moses's intercession — Q&A-069): the most powerful intercessory kindness in the evidence (Moses at Num 14:19) occurs in the context of Israel's total failure — it is kindness formation under maximum covenant-crisis. The T5 eschatological trajectory finding (Eph 2:7; Psa 16:10) is the T4 divine-to-human direction extended beyond the present age: divine chesed toward the human person does not terminate at death but is eschatologically guaranteed — the T4 interface opens into eternity.

findings.finding_value: T4's relational circuit and T6's structural network overlap most clearly at the causal level. The T6 causal network (divine kindness → praise + repentance → reproduced human kindness → sustained covenant relationships) is a structural description of the T4 circuit in causal terms: T4 identifies the directions; T6 names the causal mechanism connecting them. The T6 finding that Mic 6:8 anchors eight registries is a cluster-level reflection of T4's circuit: Mic 6:8's triadic requirement (do justice / love kindness / walk humbly) is addressed to the covenant community's relational practice — it describes the T4 relational interface requirements in condensed form. The T6 finding that kindness is self-propagating through the causal chain (received kindness → reproduced kindness) is the structural guarantee that the T4 circuit is not a closed loop requiring constant external input but a self-sustaining relational ecosystem once kindness is received and given. The T4 finding that the spiritual beings interface is absent (Q&A-070) is consistent with T6's causal analysis: the causal chain operates within the human-divine-communal relational web, not across spiritual-ontological boundaries.

findings.finding_value: T1 names peace as integrative wholeness; T4 shows its relational structure is not incidental but constitutive. The peace-wholeness of T1 is not achievable in isolation — it is given by God (T4.1), oriented toward God (T4.2), extended toward others (T4.3), and contested cosmically (T4.6). The interiority (T1) and the relationality (T4) are co-constitutive (confirmed from T3.11.3): the person at peace is the person in right relation — with God, with others, and with themselves. T4's expanding scope (covenant → universal) maps onto T1's eschatological dimension (the peace that has no end, Isa 9:7): the scope expands toward the same fullness that the essence reaches toward.

findings.finding_value: T2 establishes the constitutional location of peace; T4 establishes the relational directions through which peace moves into and out of those locations. The synthesis: God gives peace (T4.1 → T2) by addressing the constitutional locations directly — the Aaronic blessing (Num 6:26) addresses the whole person; Joh 14:27 ("let not your hearts be troubled") addresses the heart specifically; Phili 4:7 ("peace will guard your hearts and minds") names both heart and mind as the guarded locations. The human receives peace (T4.4) through the same constitutional locations — the receptive soul (Psa 131:2, T2.2) and the directed mind (Isa 26:3, T2.4) are the reception points. The relational and constitutional analyses converge: peace moves through relational channels (T4) into constitutional locations (T2).

The conscience (T3.9 — gateway faculty for peace) connects directly to T4.2 (human to God): the human's movement toward God in confession (T4.2) is precisely the conscience-exercise that opens the peace-channel (T3.9). The volitional faculty (T3.6) connects to T4.3 (giving): genuine extension of peace requires authentic inner orientation (T4.3.2) — which is exactly the T3.6 finding that the giving of peace is a volitional act flowing from identity (Psa 120:7). Inner faculty and relational direction are structurally interconnected throughout.

findings.finding_value: T4's relational scope findings (peace given to Israel → expanding to nations → universal in Christ) are lexically grounded in T7's vocabulary arc. The greeting-blessing (H7965K, T4.3 — human giving of peace) has its person-type lexical ground in T7.1.6 (ish sha.lom — the man of peace as person-type). The absence of a dedicated antonym term (T7.1.5) confirms T4's finding that peace is primarily defined by its presence and relational giving, not by its absence — the vocabulary is positive-directional, matching the God-to-human direction of peace's primary flow (T4.1). The NT coinage eirēnopoieō (T7.1.9) names what T4.1.2 describes as the basis of God's peace-giving through Christ — the cross-accomplishment has its own unique verbal form precisely because it is a unique relational act.

**[A1 — God Righteousness]** God's righteousness is not given by one human to another — it is the divine standard. S.

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Yes — righteousness flows outward to others in multiple modes: guiding the neighbor (Pro 12:26), caring for animals (Pro 12:10), delivering from oppression (Jer 22:3), dealing fairly with workers (Mat 20:4), interceding for the community (Abraham's intercession for Sodom, Gen 18:23–28, VSG M26-A2-015). The righteous person's inner condition generates a giving movement toward others.

**[B — Moral Uprightness]** Yes — upright speech is given to others: "he who walks righteously and speaks uprightly" (Isa 33:15) — the uprightness of speech is expressed toward those who hear. "Whoever speaks the truth gives honest evidence" (Pro 12:17, VSG M26-A2-011) — truth-speaking is a giving act toward those who need honest testimony.

**[C — Justification]** Justification as such is not given by one human to another — it is God's exclusive act. However, the human judicial act of vindicating the innocent (947-002: Deu 25:1; 2Sa 15:4) is a human-to-human expression of the justification principle. The human judge who acquits the innocent is extending a form of the justification-act toward the person before them.

**[D — Avenging Justice]** Yes — the commissioned human avenger (Rom 13:4) extends justice toward wrongdoers on behalf of the wronged. This is a human-to-human giving of justice — the authority serves others by executing the retribution due to wrongdoers. Moses avenging the oppressed Israelite (Act 7:24, VSG 945-001) is a human giving of protective justice toward the vulnerable.

**[E — Condemnation]** Yes — the human judge extends condemnation toward the guilty (Mat 12:37; Luk 6:37). This can be legitimate (passing righteous judgment) or illegitimate (condemning the righteous, Pro 17:15). The human-to-human extension of condemnation is a reality in the cluster — and it requires careful scrutiny because it is susceptible to corruption.

**[F — Moral Reckoning]** Yes — the human judge who "reckons" the worth of a case and passes verdict (947-002: the judges who decide between persons, Deu 25:1) extends the reckoning act toward others. Paul's instruction to "consider" others (implied in the adiakritos material, G0087) — impartial assessment of others is a giving of honest moral reckoning toward them.

**[CLUSTER — T4.3]** E. The giving interface is present in A2 (outward-flowing righteousness), B (truth-speaking to others), C-adjacent (human judicial vindication), D (commissioned justice), E (human judgment), and F (impartial assessment of others). The cluster reveals that righteousness in the human person is inherently other-directed — it reaches toward others in giving modes across multiple forms.

findings.finding_value: M01-A's ethical dimension involves extending the effects of fear toward others: the God-fearer treats the vulnerable justly (Lev 19:14; 25:43) and extends generosity (Lev 25:36-37). But the fear itself is not "given" to another — it is the inner posture that governs the person's treatment of others. The one quasi-exception is the pedagogical dimension: the psalmist offers to "teach fear of the Lord" (Psa 34:11) — fear being transmitted through instruction and example.

M01-B's "do not fear" command shows one person extending release from fear toward another: David to Mephibosheth (2Sa 9:7), Elisha to his servant (2Ki 6:16), Jesus to the disciples (Mar 4:40; Mat 28:10). The characteristic being extended is not fear itself but the command and ground that releases fear.

M01-F-VCG-05 (pastoral anxiety) shows one person extending concern toward another: Paul's anticipatory dread for his churches (2Cor 12:20; Gal 4:11) flows from his care. The anxiety is in Paul, motivated by love for others — a one-directional giving of concerned attention.

Fear is not typically "given" as a gift from one person to another. The human-to-human dimension of M01 is primarily indirect: fear of God produces just treatment of others (M01-A), the command to release fear is extended from one to another (M01-B-VCG-06), and pastoral anxiety flows from loving concern (M01-F-VCG-05).
