**[CHAR-1]** E — The evidence identifies: righteous character in the one toward whom exultation is directed (Pro 23:24 — "the father of the righteous will greatly rejoice"; the son's righteousness is the condition for the father's joy); love of the other (Song 1:4; Isa 66:10 — "all who love her"). Exultation directed toward another person appears to require genuine relational attachment and recognition of real worth in the other.

**[CHAR-2]** E — (1) **Love for the other** — 1Cor 13:6 (love's joy rejoices with the truth; it is other-directed); 3Jo 4 ("no greater joy than to hear that my children are walking in the truth" — joy rooted in love for the other's flourishing); (2) **Genuine relational investment** — Phile 7 ("I have derived much joy and comfort from your love, my brother, because the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you") — the other's active love toward others produces joy in the observer; (3) **Generosity** — 2Cor 8:2 (the Macedonians' joy in poverty overflowing into generous giving — a joy that produces outward extension); (4) **Recognition of goodness in the other** — 2Cor 7:4 (joy overflowing in Paul's affliction because of the Corinthians' response); (5) **Solidarity in suffering** — Phili 2:17–18 (Paul and Philippians co-rejoicing across shared sacrifice).

**[CHAR-7]** E — (1) **Genuine Spirit-produced agalliao in the giver** — the jailer's extension to his household requires that the joy is real in him first; (2) **Shared faith context** — Act 5:41 (the apostles' shared joy in persecution is enabled by their shared faith-commitment); (3) **Love for those to whom it extends** — Act 16:34's household-encompassing joy requires relational investment; Luk 1:44's joy across Elizabeth and Mary requires the bond of kinship and shared vocation.

**[CHAR-3]** E — (1) **Moral integrity** — the good deeds that occasion relational Gladness (1Sa 25:15; 19:4) require prior inner goodness in the one who gives; (2) **Discernment** — Pro 15:23 ("apt answer") — the ability to say the right thing at the right time requires the evaluative-gladness faculty operating accurately; (3) **Truthfulness** — Pro 27:5 ("better is open rebuke than hidden love") — genuine extension of Gladness sometimes requires honest confrontation rather than comfortable flattery; (4) **Trust-witness** — Neh 2:18 (Nehemiah's testimony of God's good hand) — having personally experienced divine goodness enables genuine witness that extends Gladness to others.

**[CHAR-4]** E — (1) **Prior Delight in God** — Jer 31:20 as the divine model: God's Delight in Ephraim flows from his own character of steadfast love; the human extension of genuine Delight in others is analogously enabled by prior right orientation of the will; (2) **Genuine affection** — 1Sa 19:1 (Jonathan's "much delight" — the intensity of personal affection as the prerequisite for protective action); 1Th 2:8 (Paul's affectionate desire as the enabling condition for self-sharing); (3) **Honesty** — contrast with 1Sa 18:22 (Saul's false claimed Delight) — the genuine extension requires that the inner disposition actually exists; (4) **Relational stability** — Pro 27:10 (the nearby neighbour's value proven through crisis) — consistent presence as the form of relational Delight's extension.

**[CHAR-5]** E — (1) **Inner pleasantness of character** — the person who extends genuine pleasant speech (Pro 16:24) must have an inward purity (Pro 15:26 — "gracious words are pure") — the inner state of purity enables the extension of genuine Pleasure; (2) **Genuine appreciation of the other** — Song 1:16; 7:6 — the lover's genuine delight in the beloved's beauty enables the pleasantness to be authentically extended; (3) **Harmonious inner orientation** — Psa 133:1's brotherly unity requires each person to be inwardly harmoniously oriented toward the community; (4) **Wisdom** — Pro 3:17's wisdom-pleasantness — the wise person's life naturally extends pleasantness to those around them.

**[CHAR-6]** E — (1) **Prior personal Wonder** — the person who has genuinely experienced Wonder at God's acts can extend it to others; Psa 71:17's "from my youth you have taught me, and I still proclaim your wondrous deeds" shows sustained personal Wonder as the basis for sustained proclamatory extension; (2) **Generational faithfulness** — Psa 78:4's "we will not hide them from their children" implies an active decision not to interrupt the chain of Wonder-extension; (3) **Worship-community membership** — the Tell-Remember-Meditate tradition presupposes a worshipping community that sustains and transmits Wonder as a communal practice; (4) **Knowledge of God's acts** — 1Ch 16:12 ("remember the wondrous works") — knowing the wonders is the precondition for declaring them.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The enabling conditions across the seven converge on two shared requirements: (1) **Prior genuine reception** — the person who extends Joy (Char 2) toward another has received Joy themselves (sunchairo presupposes prior Joy); the person who extends Wonder (Char 6) has genuinely encountered divine wonders; the person who extends Gladness (Char 3) through good news has themselves been truthfully informed; (2) **Love for the other** — Joy (Char 2): 1Cor 13:6 (love's joy is other-directed); Delight (Char 4): 1Sa 19:1 (Jonathan's Delight in David enabling protective sacrifice); Suffering-Joy (Char 7): the jailer's household-inclusive rejoicing (Act 16:34) — the joy encompasses others through relational care. The characteristic most requiring the giver's prior formation: Wonder (Char 6) — the person can only transmit genuine wonder if they have been formed in it from youth (Psa 71:17). The characteristic most capable of immediate extension without prior formation: Joy (Char 2) — news-bearing Joy crosses relational distance even without prior relationship (Act 15:3 — bringing joy to brothers by news of Gentile conversions).

**[CHAR-1]** E — The corrective deployment evidence (Paul's letters; the community-discipline passages) shows that the giver of corrective shame must be acting from a position of genuine moral concern rather than hostility. Paul's distinction in 1Cor 4:14 (vc=34992) — "I do not write these things to *make you ashamed*, but to *admonish you as my beloved children*" — shows the fine line between legitimate corrective shame (motivated by affection and moral concern) and destructive shame-induction (motivated by hostility or self-elevation). The corrective giver must have their own standing grounded in what they appeal to — blameless conduct as the basis for causing opponents' shame (Tit 2:8; 1Pe 3:16).

**[CHAR-2]** E — VCG-01 involves humans extending CHAR-2 to other humans: Ammonites shaving David's envoys, tenants beating servants. In the unjust register, CHAR-2 is inflicted by malicious agents. In the corrective register, legitimate authority can impose CHAR-2 as a judicial act. The giving direction is morally ambiguous — it can be unjust infliction or just correction.

---

**[CHAR-3]** E — VCG-01 is primarily about humans extending dishonour toward other humans or toward God. The unjust judge (Luk 18:2/4) extends worth-denial to the widow. The rich receive honor while the poor man is dishonored (Jam 2:6). The head-covering symbolic acts extend disrespect toward divinely ordered authority structures.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4 can be extended interpersonally through the articulation of moral evaluations: Paul's renunciation of shameful ways (2Cor 4:2) is both his own functioning CHAR-4 and an implicit invitation to the community's conscience to recognise the same standard. 1Cor 14:35's articulated moral-evaluative judgment extends a community's shared CHAR-4 evaluation.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — The contempt-er extends CHAR-5 toward others through VCG-01's dismissive attitude, VCG-02's violent rejection, and VCG-03's verbal contempt. In every mode, the extending person must have a prior inner disposition of self-elevation or self-righteousness (Luk 18:9) to sustain the contemptuous dismissal of others. The person who gives CHAR-5 is one who has placed themselves above the person they despise — they must have an inflated inner self-assessment as the precondition for the contempt-extension.

---

**[CHAR-6]** S — The 8-verse corpus does not evidence CHAR-6 being extended by one person toward another in a direct relational-giving sense. CHAR-6 is an inner moral condition of the individual, not primarily a characteristic extended toward others. Silent on the giving direction as a direct relational-extension.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — The human giving of M07's characteristics spans a moral spectrum from unjust to legitimate. At the unjust pole: humans inflicting shame through military conquest (Char 2), extending worth-denial through favoritism and hypocrisy (Char 3), and directing contemptuous dismissal toward others (Char 5). At the legitimate-corrective pole: humans deploying corrective shame for moral formation (Char 1's entrepō passages — 2Th 3:14; 1Cor 6:5; Char 4's articulated moral evaluation). Cluster-level finding: the same characteristics that name the unjust forms also name their legitimate forms. The moral quality of the giving depends on whether the giver is aligned with God's own movement in the shame-field — God abases the proud justly; humans can enact the same correction legitimately (corrective community discipline) or unjustly (violence, contempt, worth-denial). The inner conditions enabling legitimate extension: genuine moral concern for the shamed person, not desire for their destruction; a grounded own moral position; recognition of the person's worth even in correction.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — The extension of CHAR-1 toward others is enabled by: settled elevated self-assessment relative to those toward whom it is directed — Psa 123:4 (vc=33953, M08-A4-VCG-03): "those who are at ease" whose contempt flows from their inner security in their own position; Psa 73:6 (vc=33959, M08-A2-VCG-02): "pride is their necklace" — pride as a displayed ornament worn from a settled inner state. Material or power advantage: the ga.on proud-might corpus (M08-E) establishes that structural power without accountability enables the outward extension of CHAR-1 as domination. Absence of relational accountability: Dan 11:36 (vc=34235, M08-A1-VCG-02) — "the king shall do as he wills" — unconstrained power enabling the fullest extension. The enabling conditions are internal (settled self-elevation) rather than external — CHAR-1 extends outward from an inner posture that has been established, not from a reactive impulse.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The enabling conditions for CHAR-2 directed toward others: (a) perceived power advantage — Mar 10:42 (vc=55588): "rulers who lord it over" — structural power position that enables domineering; Mat 24:49 (vc=55613): servant who assumes "my master is delayed" — perceived absence of accountability; (b) contempt for others' legitimate standing — Psa 119:69 (vc=34100): lying against the psalmist; Psa 119:85 (vc=34102): setting pitfalls; (c) the settled insolent identity — Pro 21:24 (vc=34096, M08-B-VCG-02): the scoffer as a stable person-type from whose inner posture CHAR-2 flows outward.

**[CHAR-3]** E — For VCG-01: alazoneia as the inner disposition (Jam 4:16, vc=33866) — the inner boasting-orientation generates the social claim. Trust in creaturely assets (Psa 49:6, vc=33355, M08-C-VCG-01): confidence in one's wealth enables the boast about one's wealth. For VCG-03: genuine love for the community (2Cor 7:4, vc=33917: "I have great pride in you; I am filled with comfort") — relational affection grounds the God-directed community boast.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The enabling conditions for CHAR-4 extended toward others: (a) perceived cognitive superiority (knowledge without love — 1Cor 8:1, vc=33935: knowing more than others generates inflation); (b) partisan tribal alignment (1Cor 4:6, vc=33937: loyalty to one leader over another creates us-vs-them cognitive inflation); (c) perceived absence of accountability (1Cor 4:18, vc=33938: the presumed absence of authority enables contemptuous confidence toward the absent authority figure).

**[CHAR-5]** E — The enabling conditions for CHAR-5 directed toward others: (a) structural power that makes the other's resistance or response ineffective (Eze 16:30: shal.le.tet — imperious, unrestrained self-will enabled by structural authority); (b) the self-sufficiency conviction that renders others as objects rather than subjects of genuine moral concern (Isa 47:8: "I am, and there is no one besides me" — the relational frame that excludes the other); (c) material ease that masks the other's need (Eze 16:49: prosperous ease enabling the neglect of the poor and needy).

**[CLUSTER]** E — The enabling conditions for M08 directed toward others are consistent across the five: structural power (CHAR-5), settled insolent identity (CHAR-2), alazoneia disposition (CHAR-3), perceived cognitive superiority (CHAR-4), and CHAR-1's elevated self-posture relative to those toward whom it is directed. The cluster-synthesis: M08 is extended toward others when the person perceives themselves as standing above others in some dimension — social, structural, intellectual, or spiritual. The characteristic that is most universally extensible toward others is CHAR-1 (the general dispositional elevation) precisely because it does not require a specific structural medium.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The enabling inner conditions in the giver (the one who submits) are: *Theological motivation:* Eph6:1 ("in the Lord, for this is right") and Col3:20 ("for this pleases the Lord") — the submission is enabled by the theologically grounded conviction that the authority is legitimate and the submission is right. *Sincere-heart genuineness:* Eph6:5; Col3:22 — undivided inner motive rather than divided performance. *Fear of God as deepest motivator:* Phili2:12 ("fear and trembling"); Col3:22 ("fearing the Lord") — the reverential affect that sustains submission beyond social pressure. *Self-assessment of unworthiness:* Luk17:10 — the inner posture of not claiming merit for having submitted — enabling the characteristic's genuine form without pride in submission.
**[CHAR-3]** S — The evidence is silent on horizontal extension of contrition (see T4.3.1). Prompt closed.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Heb5:2 directly evidences the enabling condition: genuine awareness of one's own shared creaturely weakness ("he himself is beset with weakness"). The giver of metriopatheō can only extend genuine gentleness from a ground of honest self-knowledge about their own limitation. Additionally, the Act9:38 context implies that the inner condition of genuine readiness (absence of self-protective hesitation) is what enables the extension of prompt responsiveness — the giver must have no internal friction that delays their response to genuine need.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Genuine inner formation rather than performed manner is the enabling condition: Tit2:7's pairing with integrity confirms that the dignity must be genuine (backed by moral integrity) rather than performed (mere gravity without inner-grounded worth). The person who extends genuine semnotēs must have it as a real character quality, not as a social performance — the difference between the two is evidenced by whether the characteristic produces ordered response (1Ti3:4 — genuine semnotēs produces compliance) or merely performance-that-the-children-see-through.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The enabling condition evidenced throughout the corpus is the *genuine freedom of the inner movement*: Exo35:5 — "whoever is of a willing heart" — the heart's own genuine free movement is the enabling condition. The person who gives from willing-heartedness gives because the heart is genuinely moved, not because external conditions require it. Psa51:12 adds the condition of *divine upholding* when the person's own inner freedom has been disrupted — genuine extension of the characteristic after failure requires divine restoration.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The conditions for genuine horizontal extension follow from the M09-A voluntary register. First, *genuine other-regard*: Phili2:3 requires the cognitive reordering of counting others more significant — the giver must genuinely arrive at an other-centred evaluation, not a performed one. Second, *freedom from conceit and selfish ambition*: Phili2:3 frames humility as the direct counter to "selfish ambition and conceit" — the giver must be free from the self-asserting drives that reverse the other-direction. Third, *the character-disposition*: Col3:12 — humility as a character-garment — suggests the giver must have the settled inner disposition, not merely the momentary act; Eph4:2 names it as "all humility" — the whole, not partial, disposition. Fourth, *the Christological pattern* (Phili2:5–8) suggests that genuine horizontal extension requires the same volitional self-giving that characterises Christ's own humbling.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The enabling inner conditions for horizontal extension form a convergent pattern across the six characteristics. Humility (CHAR-1): genuine other-regard (Phili2:3 — counting others more significant); freedom from selfish ambition and conceit; the settled character-disposition of tapeinofrosunē rather than a momentary act. The Christological grounding (Phili2:5–8) suggests the giver must have received the security of divine acceptance (Col3:12 — God's chosen, holy, and beloved) before they can genuinely extend the lower-place posture. Submission (CHAR-2): theological motivation (Eph6:1 — "in the Lord, for this is right"); sincere-heart genuineness (Eph6:5; Col3:22); fear of God as deepest sustainer (Phili2:12). Meekness and Gentleness (CHAR-4): genuine awareness of one's own shared creaturely weakness (Heb5:2 — the enabling condition that grounds metriopatheō); absence of self-protective hesitation (okneō — Act9:38). Dignity (CHAR-5): genuine inner formation rather than performed manner — integrity backing the dignity (Tit2:7). Willing-heartedness (CHAR-6): the genuinely free inner movement toward God and service (VCG-01); or divine restoration of the willing spirit after failure (VCG-02 — Psa51:12). Cluster-level: all enabling conditions for horizontal extension require genuine inner reality — the characteristics cannot be genuinely extended toward others if not genuinely held at the inner-being level.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — The inner conditions that enable interpersonal sinning are evidenced as: (1) *Deception / self-protective fear*: Gen 20:9 — Abraham's fear-driven deception produced sinning against Abimelech's household. (2) *Hostile intent*: 1Sa 19:5 — sinning against innocent blood by killing David without cause — the hostile will as enabling condition. (3) *Contempt for the neighbour*: Pro 14:21 ("whoever despises his neighbor is a sinner") — the inner attitude of contempt enables and constitutes the sinning. (4) *Impulsive action*: Pro 19:2 — haste without knowledge misses the way — the impulsive will bypassing discernment enables sinning. (5) *Wounding disregard for another's conscience*: 1Cor 8:12 — acting without regard for the weak brother's conscience enables sinning against him.

**[CHAR-10]** E — (1) *Enticement*: 2Pe 2:14 — "hearts trained in greed" — the enticing person's own formed inner character is the enabling condition; they can only extend what their hearts have been trained toward. "Eyes full of adultery, insatiable for sin" — the full formation of the desire-apparatus enables and drives the extending of the mechanism toward others. (2) *Hypocrisy*: Gal 2:13 — Peter's initial hypocrisy (the prominent person's action) creates the social-pressure enabling condition for others to extend the same performance; (3) *Apostasy*: Act 21:21 — the accusation implies that teaching-authority is the enabling condition for extending apostasy to others.

**[CHAR-11]** E — Three enabling conditions. (1) *Representative position*: Rom 5:12 — Adam's extension of the condition to all humanity was possible through his representative position as head of humanity; (2) *Shared vulnerability*: 1Ti 5:22 — hasty endorsement makes one share in the other's sin-condition — the shared human vulnerability under the condition enables extension through complicity; (3) *Predatory exploitation*: 2Ti 3:6 — those who target the condition-burdened exploit the weakness the condition creates; the enticers' own formed character (burdened with sin, led by passions) enables them to extend the condition's reach.

**[CHAR-12]** E — 1Jo 3:8 — "whoever makes a practice of sinning is of the devil" — the inner condition enabling the extension is the person's own habitual sinning practice that aligns them with the devil's domain; the extending mechanism is not willed transmission to others but the person's own enrollment in the devil's sinning-identity. The practice (habitual sinning) is what enables the extension of the enslaving power's reach through the individual's own constitution.

**[CHAR-13]** E — Two enabling conditions. (1) *Representative authority*: VCG-04 — the Jeroboam-pattern extension operates through royal representational authority; the king's record-generating acts extend to the people through his role as their covenantal leader. Exo 32:21 — Aaron's priestly-leadership role is what enabled his sin's extension to the people; (2) *Relational proximity and dependence*: Gen 20:9 — Abraham's deception affected Abimelech because Abimelech had received Abraham in relational trust; the extending person's record impacts those who depend on or are relationally bound to them.

**[CHAR-14]** E — Two enabling conditions. (1) *Priestly appointment and authority*: Lev 10:17 — the sin offering is "given to you" — the priest's authority to bear the congregation's iniquity is divinely granted, not self-assumed; the mediatorial role is received, not created; (2) *Proper inner disposition*: Lev 10:19 — Aaron's question about whether his grief would make the sin-offering unacceptable implies that the mediator's inner state matters; the priest must be in an appropriate inner condition to extend the seeking effectively on behalf of others.

**[CHAR-15]** E — Two enabling conditions. (1) *Representative position*: Isa 43:27 — the first father's position as the ancestral head and the mediators' positions as covenant-leaders are what makes their sinning generationally transmissible; ordinary community members do not extend the condition in the same way; (2) *The sinning acts themselves*: the extension requires actual sinning ("sinned... transgressed") — the representative position plus the sinning acts together create the transmissible condition.

**[CHAR-16]** E — Two enabling conditions. (1) *Authority or representative position*: Rom 5:19 — Adam's representative headship makes his sinning identity-constituting for all; Joh 9:24 — the Pharisees' authoritative social position makes their label-declaration socially operative; (2) *Moral certainty*: Joh 9:24 — "we know" — the Pharisees extend the label with claimed certainty; Luk 7:39 — the Pharisee's internal certainty about the woman's sinner-status enables the label's extension. The honest alternative (Joh 9:25 — "I do not know") refuses the extension without sufficient grounds.

**[CHAR-17]** E — Two enabling conditions. (1) *Representative position*: Lev 4:3 — the anointed priest's position as representative of the community is what makes his sin guilt-propagating to all; 1Ch 21:3 — the king's position makes his census decision guilt-generating for Israel; (2) *Voluntary assumption*: 1Sa 25:24 — Abigail's "on me alone, my lord, be the guilt" — the voluntary self-insertion into the guilt-bearing position; 2Sa 14:9 — the woman's "on me be the guilt" — the willing assumption of another's liability. The conditions are distinct: representative-position guilt-propagation is structural; voluntary-assumption is agentive.

**[CHAR-18]** E — Two enabling conditions. (1) *Representative position*: Lev 10:17 — "that you may bear the iniquity of the congregation" — the priests' position as representatives enables them to bear the community's iniquity; Lev 16:21 — Aaron's high-priestly office enables the transferral; 1Sa 3:13 — Eli's position as father and priest makes his iniquity community-affecting; (2) *Ancestral headship*: Exo 20:5 — "the fathers" whose idolatrous hatred of God generates the iniquity that is transmitted; the generational transmission operates through the ancestral position, not merely biological descent.

**[CHAR-19]** E — Two enabling conditions. (1) *Authority or representative position*: Isa 43:27 — "mediators" and "first father" — the representative position makes one's transgression community-affecting; Jer 2:8 — "shepherds" whose transgression affects the flock; (2) *Volitional invitation*: Amos 4:4 — "come to Bethel and transgress; to Gilgal, and multiply transgression" — the intentional invitation of others into transgressive practice; the extending person's will is engaged in actively recruiting others.

**[CHAR-2]** E — For the interpersonal sinning in VCG-01 (Lev 6:2/3 — deception, robbery, oppression), the enabling inner conditions are the same as the personal-moral register: acting without recognising the full moral weight of what is being done. However, Lev 6:2/3's Pass A meanings note elements of deliberateness ("deliberate lying," "willful act of inner deception"), which places these verses at the border with CHAR-1 rather than squarely in CHAR-2. The clearer CHAR-2 interpersonal extension is Lev 4:3 (priestly inadvertent sinning bringing communal guilt) — the enabling condition is simply that the priest acted in his representative capacity without full moral awareness, and the community is affected because of his representative role.

**[CHAR-20]** E — Two enabling conditions. (1) *Prior position of trust*: Mal 2:14 — "your companion and your wife by covenant" — the treachery is enabled by the prior intimate covenant that created the trust-position; Jer 12:6 — brothers and family-members — the betrayal is possible because of the prior bond; Jos 7:1 — Achan's position within Israel as a covenant-member; (2) *Internal desire-orientation toward false objects*: 1Ch 5:25 — "whored after the gods of the peoples" — the will's desire transferred to false objects is the enabling condition that makes the covenant-faithlessness an act of inner betrayal rather than mere preference-change.

**[CHAR-21]** E — Two enabling conditions. (1) *Relational or positional access*: 1Cor 15:33 — "bad company" — the company-relationship is the access-point; 2Cor 11:3 — the false teacher's preaching relationship with the congregation; Rev 19:2 — Babylon's position in the world-system; (2) *Active deception*: 2Cor 11:3 — "as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning" — cunning deception is the mechanism; the extension of perversion requires active misrepresentation rather than transparent wrongdoing.

**[CHAR-22]** E — Three enabling conditions. (1) *Authority or positional access*: Psa 82:2 — judges who have positional authority to determine others' outcomes; Lev 19:35 — the seller who controls the weights and measures; Mic 3:10 — leaders who direct civic construction; (2) *Appetitive internalization*: Job 15:16 — "drinks injustice like water" — the thoroughly internalized appetite enables effortless extension to others; (3) *God-ignorance*: Job 18:21 — "him who knows not God" — the absence of divine accountability in the inner life removes the restraint that would prevent extending injustice to others.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The enabling conditions for interpersonal confession parallel those for God-directed confession: (1) *Active conscience*: 2Sa 19:20 — "your servant knows that I have sinned" — the interpersonal confession is grounded in inner knowledge. (2) *Absence of self-protective calculation*: the person-directed confessions that are most genuine (2Sa 19:20 — Shimei, who comes first) show the confessor approaching without knowing the outcome — a posture of moral honesty. The compromised forms (Mat 27:4 — Judas, who immediately acts on the priests' indifference by returning the silver and hanging himself) show conscience driving the confession but the relational outcome being rejected.

**[CHAR-4]** S — The corpus does not evidence the mechanism by which one person extends conscience suppression to another. Tit 3:11's divisive person may influence others through modelled behaviour, but the inner conditions for this transmission are not specified. The corpus is insufficient to characterise this mechanism.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The enabling conditions for transmitting refusal to repent: (1) *Authority and representative position*: every king in the corpus holds the authority through which the sinful pattern is transmitted — "he made Israel to sin" — the enabling condition is positional authority that gives the leader's inner disposition communal scope. (2) *Modelled non-departure*: 2Ki 15:9 — "as his fathers had done" — the next generation's refusal is enabled by the prior generation's modelled refusal; the enabling condition is the observable pattern of the predecessor. (3) *The sinful course presented as normative*: when the king walks in Jeroboam's sins without departing, the community receives an implicit signal that this is the normative path — the community's refusal is enabled by the leader's presentation of the sinful course as acceptable.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The enabling conditions for transmitting habitual defection to others: (1) *Positional authority*: 1Sa 2:25 — Eli's sons are priests, giving their habitual defection communal scope through their representative role; (2) *Institutionalised sinning*: Hos 8:11 — the multiplication of altars creates a communal infrastructure that transmits the sinning orientation to all participants; (3) *Destructive influence at scale*: Ecc 9:18 — "one sinner destroys much good" — the sinner's settled orientation has disproportionate destructive reach. The enabling condition in each case is a pre-existing relationship of influence (priestly authority, institutional membership, communal proximity) through which the inner sinning orientation flows outward.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Three enabling conditions in the leader. (1) *Personal inner commitment to the sinning course*: 1Ki 16:26 — "walked in all the way of Jeroboam" — the leader's own sinning direction is the source; without it there is nothing to transmit. (2) *Occupation of and active exercise of authority*: 1Ki 16:2 — "I made you leader over my people" — the authority position is both the enabler and the medium of transmission; the authority must be actively exercised toward the sinning direction. (3) *The will to extend the sinning direction to others*: Jer 32:35 — the deliberate building of sinning structures with the purpose of causing others to sin — the intentional causative aspect is part of the enabling condition.

**[CHAR-8]** E — Two evidenced enabling conditions. (1) *Perceived political opportunity*: 2Ki 1:1 / 3:5 — "after the death of Ahab" — the governing authority's perceived weakness at a moment of leadership transition enables the revolt. (2) *Spiritual-authority vacuum in the governing authority*: 2Ch 21:10 — "because he had forsaken the Lord" — the governing authority's inner spiritual condition (forsaking God) creates a vacuum of legitimate covenantal authority that enables the revolts of Edom and Libnah. In both cases the enabling condition is a perceived weakening or delegitimisation of the governing authority.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Three enabling conditions. (1) *Corrupted heart*: Mat 15:19 — "out of the heart come... slander" — the corrupted inner moral centre is the primary enabler; (2) *Bitterness, wrath, and anger toward the target*: Eph 4:31 — the affective cluster of bitterness/wrath/anger is the emotional enabling condition for slander; (3) *Conceit and diseased craving*: 1Ti 6:4 — pride inflated by self-regard and the appetite for controversy enables the targeting of others with slanderous speech.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The inner conditions enabling the wicked person to extend their characteristic toward others are: (1) deliberate intent to recruit or harm — Exo 23:1 (VCG-04 — joining the wicked in malicious witness); Jer 5:26 (VCG-03 — deliberate predatory intent to trap); (2) social boldness — Pro 21:29 (VCG-08 — "a wicked man puts on a bold face" — the absence of inner check enables the bold outward extension); (3) the suppression of relational moral awareness — Psa 28:3 (VCG-08 — "speak peace while evil is in their hearts" — the deceptive extension is enabled by the suppression of transparent conscience). The enabling conditions are all internal suppressions of the moral-relational checks that would otherwise restrain the person from extending harm outward.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The enabling inner conditions for extending the characteristic are: (1) the absence of repentance — the characteristic that has not been addressed through repentance (Act 8:22 — VCG-05) remains available to be projected outward; (2) the presence of unchecked social power or authority — 3Jo 10 (vc=14454 — VCG-04) shows Diotrephes using his social position to extend his constitutional malice; (3) the rationalising inner condition — Rom 2:8 (vc=14338 — VCG-05): self-seeking combined with obedience to unrighteousness enables the person to present their constitutional evil as justified self-assertion; (4) Mat 22:18 (vc=14408 — VCG-05): the ponēria of the Pharisees is "calculated" — the deliberate, planned nature of the inner malice is what enables its outward extension.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The enabling conditions for extending abomination toward others are: (1) the settled inner disposition of contemptuous derision (the scoffer's character — Pro 24:9 — VCG-01); (2) the inverted moral-evaluative capacity that produces perverted judgment (Pro 17:15 — VCG-01 — the inner inversion enables the outer perversion of justice directed at others); (3) the concealed multiple abominations in the heart (Pro 26:25 — VCG-02) — the inner reservoir of corrupt motivations enables the outward extension of abomination through gracious-seeming social performance; (4) the faithless will that betrays covenant loyalty (Mal 2:11 — VCG-04 — an inward infidelity extending outward as betrayal).

**[CHAR-4]** E — The enabling inner conditions for extending idolatrous abomination toward others: (1) established inner attachment — a person extends the characteristic only when they are already deeply attached to the idolatrous objects (Solomon's attachments driven by his many wives — 1Ki 11:5-7 — VCG-03 — which enabled his building of high places for their gods); (2) institutional or royal authority — the power to shape communal practice (2Ki 21:11 — VCG-03: Manasseh's authority enables the communal extension of his personal abominations); (3) the covenantal community's failure to maintain separation (Ezr 9:1 — vc=65949 — VCG-03: failure to separate from abomination-practicing peoples enables extension through communal integration).

**[CHAR-5]** E — The enabling inner conditions for extending iniquity toward others: (1) the established inner habit of scheming — Mic 2:1 (vc=38217 — VCG-02): the person who has habitually devised extends their schemes outward at dawn; (2) the predatory inner appetite — Pro 19:28 (vc=38220 — VCG-03): "the mouth of the wicked devours iniquity" — the inner craving drives extension; (3) institutional authority — Isa 10:1 (vc=38191 — VCG-02): the lawmaker and writer have the power to extend iniquity institutionally; (4) anger and sustained grudge — Psa 55:3 (vc=38188 — VCG-01): "in anger they bear a grudge against me" — the affective state of sustained anger fuels the relational extension of harm.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Enabling conditions for extending evil speech toward another: (1) the hardened will that refuses to yield — Rev 16:9/11/21 (VCG-01): the will hardened against repentance enables continued defiant speech; (2) authority-rejection — Jude 8 (vc=14354 — VCG-01): rejecting authority enables blasphemy of the glorious ones; (3) hostile malicious evaluation of another — Joh 18:30 (vc=14378 — VCG-03): the accusers' inner evaluation produces the false verbal charge; (4) moral failure creating the occasion for social defamation — Rom 2:24 (vc=14357 — VCG-02): the moral failure of those who represent God creates the occasion for the Gentiles' blasphemous speech; (5) sensory self-indulgence combined with spiritual independence — Jude 8 (VCG-01): "relying on their dreams, defile the flesh" — the self-centred sensory orientation enables the contemptuous speech directed at authority.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster reveals a composite enabling profile for social extension of M10b evil. Shared enabling conditions across characteristics: (a) established inner evil-form (the person must first be constituted by the characteristic before extending it); (b) authority or power (Char 4 VCG-03 — royal authority; Char 5 — Isa 10:1 legislative authority); (c) relational proximity enabling exploitation (Char 5 — Psa 28:3 — speaking peace to neighbours while evil is in the heart; Char 6 — 1Pe 2:12 — opponents within social space); (d) the suppressed conscience that would otherwise restrain social harm. Char 4 adds the unique cultural-educational extension mechanism (Deu 20:18 — nations teaching abominable practices); Char 6 adds institutional-legal extension (Joh 18:30 — formal legal process as extension mechanism).

**[CHAR-1]** E — In the case of disease/defilement transmission, the question is reversed: what inner conditions prevent the person from transmitting their condition against others' will? The answer from the evidence is conscientious awareness — the person must know they are defiled and take the prescribed precautions (washing, self-declaration, maintaining distance). The "giving" is prevented by conscientiousness; it occurs through negligence or willful disregard.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The enabling conditions for morally defiling another are evidenced as: (1) sustained communal exposure — the formative power of a defilingly-oriented community (1Cor 8:7 — "former association with idols"); (2) the explicit or implicit normalization of impurity within a relational context — Eph 4:19 (VCG-02) describes a community that has collectively given itself up to impurity, which creates an environment in which the standard of conscience is collectively lowered. The inner condition of the extending person is the willing normalization of the defilement-state as a community practice.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The enabling conditions for extending the characteristic toward another are: (1) volitional violation of another's covenantal boundary — the violator in Gen 34 acts from desire without regard for the covenantal person of the other; (2) lust-driven alliance-seeking that draws another into idolatrous defilement — Eze 23:17 shows the Babylonians' "whoring lust" as the inner condition enabling the extension; (3) the sustained corporate pattern that becomes a shared moral environment — 1Cor 8:7's formative-association principle applies here too: the community's shared idolatrous practice creates an environment that defiles those within it.
**[CHAR-4]** S — Not applicable; see T4.3.1. The characteristic is not extended by a human person to another.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The enabling conditions for transmission/extension differ by characteristic. Characteristic 1: the defiling person's failure of conscientiousness — what enables transmission is the person's not washing their hands before contact (Lev 15:11 — the prevention is the hand-washing; the enabling is the absence of that precaution). Characteristic 2: the community's normalisation of impurity — the defiling formative environment is constituted by a community that has collectively silenced its conscience and normalized defilement (Eph 4:19 — "given themselves up to impurity"), which then shapes others who enter it. Characteristic 3: volitional violation (desire without regard for the covenantal person of the other — Gen 34), lust-driven alliance-seeking (Eze 23:17 — "whoring lust" of the Babylonians), and sustained corporate moral environment (the shared community of idolatrous practice). Characteristic 4: no human enabling conditions — the extending agent is the spirit, not the human person. The cluster's unified insight: in the three human-transmission characteristics, the enabling condition is always some form of failure — of conscientiousness (Char 1), of conscience and moral community formation (Char 2), of volitional self-governance and covenantal boundary (Char 3).

questions.question_text: What does the evidence show a person must have received or become before they extend the characteristic?

findings.session_b_note:
The data is unusually clear on this question — it is one of the most developed aspects of the forgiveness analysis:

**Must have received:** Divine forgiveness, at the heart level. F-003: "the received state enables and obligates the extended state." The parable of Mat 18 is constructed precisely to show that receipt of forgiveness is the necessary inner ground for giving it. The servant who received but did not let the receipt transform him inwardly was incapable of giving genuinely.

**Must have become:** A person in whom the love-orientation has been established (Luk 7:47 — "forgiven much → loved much"). The inner transformation from guilt-state to release-state, from self-preoccupation to relational generosity, is the becoming that enables genuine giving.

**The negative case confirms the positive:** OBS-064-001 — "the absence of forgiveness poisons the inner life of the withholder." The person who has not received (or not received at the heart level) cannot give genuinely because their inner life is constrained by the retained grievance. Receipt and genuine giving are constitutively linked.

They must have received grace (foundational reception); become tenderhearted (the mediating inner transformation — eusplanchnos); and passed through recognition of their own need (conscience-awareness, mourning) that makes giving genuine rather than condescending. The giver must be also a receiver who knows they are a receiver.

*Adds precision: the three conditions (received grace, tenderheartedness, recognition of own need) as a named sequence for the human giving-direction — not previously stated in these terms.*

findings.session_b_note:
**What the evidence suggests:** The mirroring principle (2 Sam 22:26) implies that prior reception of divine compassion is constitutively connected to the capacity for human compassion-giving. The devout person (chasid — H2623 XREF) is the one whose inner life embodies chesed — a quality formed through the sustained experience of divine chesed. The Exod 34:6 formula grounds human compassion in the divine character: to give chesed to others, one must first have been sustained by divine chesed.

The sumpatheō Christological grounding (Heb 4:15 — Christ sympathising because he has been tempted) establishes the participatory principle: genuine compassion-giving requires having been in the inner experience one is responding to. Christ can sympathise with human weakness because he has shared it. By implication, the human person who has suffered, been in need, and received compassion in that need has the inner ground to give compassion genuinely to those in a similar condition.

**What is missing (P):** The data does not directly state that prior reception of compassion is a necessary condition for genuine compassion-giving — it implies it through the structural logic of the vocabulary. Whether compassion-giving is possible without prior reception (e.g., through formation rather than experience) is not addressed. This is a gap; no SD pointer covers it directly.

findings.session_b_note:
The proclamatory mode of 1Jo 1:3 gives the clearest answer: the person must have *seen and heard* — that is, they must have been genuine witnesses of what they proclaim. They must have received the fellowship chain from those before them. Fellowship can only be genuinely extended by one who already participates in it. This is structurally different from some characteristics (like kindness or mercy) which can be extended by anyone regardless of prior reception.

**New finding:** Fellowship is structurally chain-dependent — it can only be extended by those who are already in it. The non-participant cannot create genuine fellowship; they can only be invited into an existing fellowship. This is implicit in the 1Jo 1:3 logic (*our fellowship is with the Father and his Son Jesus Christ*) — the extending party's fellowship with God is the precondition for extending it horizontally to others.

findings.session_b_note: The evidence requires that the giver must have: (1) Received Spirit-transformation — Rom 3:12 names the unregenerate condition as one of total goodness-absence. The implication is that genuine goodness-giving requires a prior Spirit-regeneration that creates the goodness-capacity. (2) Undergone moral reorientation — Psa 73:28's Asaph has moved from crisis to repositioned inner orientation before he can overflow goodness toward others. The person who has not undergone inner reorientation cannot genuinely give what they do not possess. (3) Been recognised as God's chosen and beloved — Col 3:12 explicitly grounds the "put on kindness" instruction in the prior identity declaration ("God's chosen ones, holy and beloved"). Giving genuine goodness requires the identity transformation that comes from being received by God in grace. This is the structural parallel: human goodness-giving to others requires the same prior divine-goodness-giving to the human that divine goodness-giving to creation requires nothing from creation (Gen 1:31 is unconditional). The human's giving is conditional on having first received. (OBS-067-OBS-039, OBS-067-OBS-046, OBS-067-OBS-029)

findings.session_b_note: The data consistently requires prior reception before genuine extension. Mat 18:33 makes this explicit — the failure to extend mercy is inexcusable specifically because of what was received. The Heb 2:17 principle extends this: the capacity to show mercy requires solidarity-knowledge of the condition mercy addresses. The person who can genuinely give mercy is one who knows themselves to be under mercy (Luk 18:13 — self-knowledge as sinner), has received mercy (Mat 18:28 — the sequence in the parable), and has had inner orientation reshaped (the expectation of Mat 18:33). findings.finding_value: Reading T4 as a whole reveals mercy's relational architecture as directional and asymmetric in all three interface directions (God→human, human→God, human→human), with a structural requirement that receiving precedes giving. The key synthesis across T4: (a) God-to-human direction is the most extensively evidenced and is the source of mercy in all other directions; (b) human-to-God direction is characterised by normative ongoing supplication — not exceptional crisis-response; (c) human-to-human direction requires prior receipt from God and solidarity-knowledge of the condition being addressed; (d) mercy operates characteristically across relational distance and rupture (Q&A-117), not within maintained relationships; (e) the scope is wide (crossing covenantal boundaries) but not unconditionally permanent (withdrawal is named possibility). The T4 synthesis: mercy's relational architecture is an asymmetric chain — divine mercy → received human mercy → extended human mercy — with the chain requiring the prior link at each stage.

Gap remains. OBS-030-041.

findings.finding_value: T3's faculty engagements all point in the same relational directions that T4 identifies as primary. Conscience (T3.9) is engaged in both the seeking-forgiveness direction (human-to-God: confession as conscience's public verdict) and the giving direction (human horizontal: the conscience that recognises the offence to be released). Memory (T3.3) is engaged in the God-to-human direction (divine "remember no more" — Jer 31:34) and the human-giving direction (releasing the memory's active use against the offender). Volition (T3.6) drives the giving direction (heart-level release is chosen). The vertical-horizontal interdependence (T4 structural claim) is the relational expression of T3's conscience-and-volition faculty account: the person whose conscience has accurately received the magnitude of divine forgiveness has the volitional capacity to extend horizontal forgiveness.

findings.finding_value: T4's vertical-horizontal interdependence (the structural claim that receiving divine forgiveness enables extending human forgiveness) is T5's formation arc described at the relational level. The formation sequence (T5 — forgiveness received → love generated → capacity to extend formed) is the inner development through which T4's structural interdependence is created: the person who genuinely receives divine forgiveness and generates the love-response (T5) is the person who has the genuine volitional capacity to extend horizontal forgiveness (T4). The eschatological telos (T5.6 — Jer 31:34) is also T4's permanent relational state: the guilt-barrier permanently removed produces permanently restored relational access to God.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-004: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion…
findings.finding_value: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion on whom I have compassion"), covenantally grounded (chesed as the bond-loyalty that grounds the characteristic), and situationally responsive (splanchnizō — triggered by the specific sight of suffering). These three bases are not in tension but in integration: divine compassion is free, covenanted, and responsive simultaneously. The scope finding is among the most analytically significant in the registry: compassion explicitly and repeatedly crosses covenantal boundaries (Nineveh, the Samaritan/Jew axis, the power-asymmetric relationship). Scope is defined by perceived need, not moral standing or covenantal membership — this is formally confirmed in the data and distinguishes compassion from many other relational characteristics. The chesed/splanchnizō distinction maps onto distinct relational registers: chesed sustains within established bonds; splanchnizō extends across distance and difference. T4.4 (receiver's inner-being experience) is the most significant gap — four P-rated prompts, entirely absent from the data. T4.6 (spiritual beings interface) is entirely silent across all four prompts.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-004: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — a…
findings.finding_value: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — all God-as-subject). The basis of divine extension is the giver's character and prior knowing (Exo 33:17 — "I know you by name"), not the receiver's merit — neither merit-based nor arbitrary. The human-to-God direction is specifically supplication: tachanum (H8469) is the receiving side's corresponding vocabulary built into the same root family as the giving side (chen/chanan) — the vocabulary embeds the two-directional circuit in a single root. The human-giving direction extends grace horizontally through three modes: forgiving (charizō — Eph 4:32), gracious conduct (chen as character quality — 889-003), and gracious speech (SD022). The receiving direction is the most underexamined (T4.4 — P-rated throughout); the scope analysis (T4.5) reveals grace crossing covenantal and social boundaries (Ruth narrative — grace in the context of foreign status and vulnerability). T4.6 (spiritual beings) is evidenced at one point: Luk 1:28 (kecharitōmenē — the angel's announcement), which implies angelic ministry as a vehicle of grace rather than grace operating independently in the spiritual-beings register. T4 synthesis: the relational architecture of grace is unique in the programme — it is the only characteristic where the giving-side vocabulary and the receiving-side vocabulary are built from the same root (chen/tachanum), encoding the grace-circuit's two-sidedness at the lexical level.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-019: T3's agency-constituting finding (grace constitutes rather than replaces agency — 1Cor 15:10) and T4's human-to-God direction (supplication as the human posture of appeal — requiring genuine human age…
findings.finding_value: T3's agency-constituting finding (grace constitutes rather than replaces agency — 1Cor 15:10) and T4's human-to-God direction (supplication as the human posture of appeal — requiring genuine human agency in the act of plea) are structurally aligned. The constituted agency (T3.7) is precisely the agency that supplication requires: the creature must genuinely appeal, not merely receive passively. T3's finding that grace and conscience are mutually necessary (T3.9) corresponds to T4's relational-access finding: grace transforms the threshold of human-to-God approach (prosagōgē — SD035) from impassable to open, which is the relational expression of T3.9's constitutional finding that grace creates the condition within which conscience can operate fully without destruction. T3 names the inner-being event; T4 names the relational consequence of the same event.

findings.session_b_note: The evidence suggests that genuine covenant-giving (horizontal) requires the person to have first received and been formed by covenant (vertical). The logic: a person who has not entered God's covenant and been formed by it — whose inner character has not been shaped by covenantal faithfulness (amanah-root — OBS-034-008) — lacks the inner moral quality that makes covenant-giving to another person genuine and sustainable. Specifically: (1) The person must have developed the moral character of oath-keeping (3308-002 — OBS-034-053) — one cannot give reliable covenant-commitment if one's inner character is that of an asunthetos (covenant-breaker — OBS-034-057). (2) Under the new covenant: the person who has received God's law on the heart (Heb 8:10) and the Spirit's transformation (2 Cor 3:6) is equipped to give covenant-loyalty from an inner nature that has been constituted for it. The new covenant provides the inner constitution from which genuine covenant-giving to others flows. In this sense, receiving the vertical covenant is the condition of possibility for giving genuine horizontal covenant.

findings.session_b_note: The data implies that genuine peace-extension requires prior reception and formation: (1) Prior reception: the person who has not received peace cannot authentically give it — the greeting-blessing (1Sa 25:6) is an invocation of God's peace upon another, not a self-generated gift; the extension is mediated from the divine source; (2) Character formation: G1516 eirēnikos — peaceableness as quality of heavenly wisdom and of discipline (Heb 12:11 — "the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it") — the person who extends peace has been trained; (3) Identity-level commitment: Psa 120:7 ("I am for peace") — the giver of peace is a person whose identity is peace; the extension flows from being, not merely from choosing. The data does not require perfect peace in the giver — Jer 29:7 (exiles seeking the welfare of their captor city) shows peace-extension is possible even from a position of suffering — but it requires genuine orientation.

findings.session_b_note: The data implies a prior-reception structure for genuine human giving. Job 1:21 establishes it most clearly: "the Lord gave" precedes and grounds the blessing. The human giver must have first received — must know themselves as recipient of divine giving — before their own giving is grounded in this characteristic rather than in self-generated generosity. The Servant's self-giving (Isa 50:6) is grounded in received covenantal identity and received promise of vindication (Isa 50:7-9). The person must have received: (a) covenantal identity (participation in the narrative of divine faithfulness), (b) inner-being formation through Spirit/wisdom endowment, and (c) the capacity to recognise divine sovereignty over all possessions. Without these prior receptions, giving remains transactional. This is consistent with the image-bearing structure (Q&A-008): the human gives responsively, and responsive giving requires prior reception.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-060-004: T4 as a whole reveals that the relational architecture of this characteristic is directionally structured and asymmetrical. The dominant direction is God-to-human (6 of 7 groups, confirmed across T4.1…
findings.finding_value: T4 as a whole reveals that the relational architecture of this characteristic is directionally structured and asymmetrical. The dominant direction is God-to-human (6 of 7 groups, confirmed across T4.1); the human direction is responsive (T4.2: human gives back what was first given). The basis of divine giving is plural — covenantal, responsive, formative, moral-consequential, eschatological-grace (Q&A-102) — revealing that faithfulness is not a single relational mode but a relational orientation that differentiates itself across relational conditions while remaining unified in character. The human-to-God direction reveals responsive correspondence as the relational structure (Q&A-107): the proper relational form is one in which the human gives back to God what is his (glory, praise, self), having first received. The human-to-human direction is thinner in the data (Q&A-109) — reflecting the registry's God-subject dominance. T4.6 is substantially silent on spiritual beings. What T4 reveals as a whole: faithfulness-as-giving is constitutively a divine-initiative relational reality that the human enters through responsive participation. The human's giving is always downstream of divine giving; the correspondence is the proper form of the relationship.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-003: The five operational modes of giving (T1.4) map onto the four relational interfaces (T4) in a specific structural way. Performative and covenantal giving (modes 1) operate through the God-to-human int…
findings.finding_value: The five operational modes of giving (T1.4) map onto the four relational interfaces (T4) in a specific structural way. Performative and covenantal giving (modes 1) operate through the God-to-human interface (T4.1) with a covenantal basis. Responsive giving (mode 2) operates through the God-to-human interface with a responsive basis. Endowing giving (mode 3) operates through God-to-human with a formative basis. Judicial giving (mode 4) operates through God-to-human with a moral-consequential basis. Relinquishing self-giving (human mode) operates through the human-to-God interface. Glory-giving operates through the human-to-God interface. The relational interface is not external to the definition — it is a structural element of each operational mode. What this pair reveals: the characteristic cannot be defined without specifying its relational direction. The same act-concept (giving) becomes a different operational mode depending on which interface it operates through.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-016: The relational interfaces (T4 — divine-initiative, human-responsive, covenantal scope) and the formation arc (T5 — constitutive endowment, sustained narrative, eschatological orientation) reveal that …
findings.finding_value: The relational interfaces (T4 — divine-initiative, human-responsive, covenantal scope) and the formation arc (T5 — constitutive endowment, sustained narrative, eschatological orientation) reveal that formation happens through relational interfaces. The God-to-human interface is the channel through which constitutive formation occurs (Spirit given, wisdom deposited — T5.5). The human-to-God interface is both the goal of formation (glory-giving as the proper orientation of the formed person) and a constituent of the formation process (practising glory-giving forms the person who gives glory). What this pair reveals: formation is not an individual inner process — it is a relational event. The person is not formed in isolation from God and others; they are formed through the giving and receiving that constitutes the relational interfaces. The formation arc (T5) is the temporal dimension of the relational structure (T4): what the interfaces do over time is formation.

The person must have received (or perceived) an injury that they have not released. In the righteous register: the person must have received the instruction that enables accurate moral evaluation (Psa 119:104).

The divine prior act specific to each characteristic: love received from God (M05-A); compassion from God's own compassion-character (M05-B); mercy received before mercy can be shown (M05-C); Spirit-produced goodness before good-doing (M05-D); Christological model of gentleness and Spirit-production (M05-E); comfort from God before comforting others (M05-F); divine calling into fellowship before extending fellowship to others (M05-G). The pattern is invariant: reception precedes genuine giving across all seven.

**[CLUSTER]** E. The pattern across the cluster is clear: before the person can give righteousness to others, they must have received it from God. The righteous person who guides their neighbor (A2-012) is first themselves righteous. The human judge who acquits the innocent (C-adjacent, 947-002) exercises a delegated judicial authority that comes from God. The commissioned avenger (D: Rom 13:4) acts on the basis of divine commission, not personal authority. The prerequisite is reception: the person must first stand in right relationship with God (received righteousness, C) before they can credibly extend righteous orientation toward others.
VCG03 (wisdom constituted as character): the giver must first be wise — character enables transmission. Wisdom cannot be transmitted from an empty vessel.

This is the propagating structure confirmed by Eph 4:32; Col 3:13; Luk 7:42–43 (the one with the larger cancelled debt loves more). A person cannot genuinely extend grace who has not received and recognised grace.
