findings.finding_value: To transmit reverential fear through instruction (Psa 34:11), the instructor must themselves have received and been formed by the fear. Deu 31:12-13 implies a multi-generational formation chain: each generation hearing and forming the fear, then transmitting it to the next. The person cannot give what they have not received and been formed by.

The general principle confirmed by M01: genuine giving of the characteristic's effects requires genuine possession of the characteristic. The God-fearer who treats others justly does so from the interior ground of their own reverential fear. The person who releases another from fear does so from the ground of their own courageous trust. The person whose pastoral anxiety flows from love does so from the ground of genuine relational investment.

For righteous anger to be genuinely extended, the person must have received or developed moral perception calibrated to genuine wrongdoing rather than self-interest. Moses' anger at the golden calf (Exo 32:19) is possible because Moses had been in God's presence receiving the law — he knows what has been violated. Nehemiah's anger at oppression is possible because Nehemiah is himself a person of covenant integrity whose anger is aligned with God's own standards.

For the jealous-zeal anger to be genuinely extended toward God's honor: Phinehas's jealousy (Num 25:11) was recognised as matching God's own jealousy — the person must have received enough of God's own jealous devotion to mirror it. The condition is a prior alignment with God's own inner life.

The evidence suggests that the ability to grieve on behalf of another requires having genuinely experienced grief oneself — or having the relational capacity to perceive another's loss as real and weighty. The corpus does not make this explicit, but the pattern of prophetic compassion-grief shows that the prophet who most authentically weeps for his people is the one most deeply aware of what they are losing. Grief for another therefore appears to require genuine inner capacity for grief — a person who has not experienced or does not feel the weight of loss will not be capable of genuine empathic grief.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The evidence does not directly address this. The implication of VCG-03 is that the parent who exults in their righteous child has themselves cultivated the capacity for exultation — the father's joy at righteousness suggests he values righteousness, which requires his own moral formation. But the evidence does not make this explicit.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The evidence implies: (1) **First received God's Joy** — the feast-joy (M04-B-VCG-01) must first be produced by divine blessing before it can overflow into communal sharing; Jer 32:41 (God's Joy over Israel precedes and enables Israel's Joy); (2) **Rightly-oriented inner life** — 1Cor 13:6 (love as the precondition of rightly-directed Joy extension — the person who rejoices with the truth must first love the truth); (3) **Spirit-filled** — Act 13:52 (filled with joy and the Holy Spirit — the Spirit's filling enables the joy that then radiates); (4) **Wholehearted** — 2Ch 15:15 (wholehearted seeking as the precondition for the joy that then unites the community). The person cannot genuinely give Joy toward others without first having received it in right relationship with God.

**[CHAR-7]** E — The evidence implies: (1) **Prior Spirit-filling** — the agalliao form requires being filled with or led by the Spirit; (2) **Prior coming-to-faith** — Act 16:34's jailer can only extend the joy to his household after he himself has believed; (3) **Prior experience of the suffering-paradox** — the apostles (Act 5:41) can extend the characteristic because they have themselves navigated the paradox of suffering-in-mission. One cannot genuinely give what one has not genuinely received.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The evidence implies: (1) **Moral formation** — the person who gives good evaluative judgment (Jethro in Exo 18:17; Naomi in Rut 2:22) must have the formed evaluative faculty; (2) **Experience of God's goodness** — Nehemiah's testimony (Neh 2:18) presupposes his own experience of God's good hand; (3) **Character goodness** — 1Sa 25:3 (Abigail's discernment enabling her relational goodness) — inner character is the prerequisite for extended relational Gladness; (4) **Wisdom** — the wisdom-comparative evaluations (M04-L-VCG-03) presuppose a formed wisdom that can correctly value wisdom above gold.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The evidence implies: (1) **Genuine Delight in God first** — Psa 37:4 (delight in the Lord producing aligned desires) — the person rightly ordered toward God can extend genuine relational Delight; (2) **Known parental/divine cherishing** — Jer 31:20 (God's cherishing as the model for the human parental Delight in children); the one who has been genuinely delighted in (by God, by a parent) has the inner pattern from which to give Delight genuinely to others; (3) **Law internalized** — Psa 40:8 (law within the heart) — the person formed by law-Delight has the moral orientation enabling them to rightly identify and extend Delight appropriately.

**[CHAR-5]** E — (1) **Wisdom dwelling in the heart** — Pro 2:10's "wisdom will come into your heart" enables the Pleasure in knowledge that can then be extended to others in wise speech (Pro 16:24); (2) **Prior experience of divine Pleasure** — Psa 27:4's one who gazes on God's beauty has received the deepest Pleasure and can then extend pleasantness in praise (Psa 45:1's overflow); (3) **Genuine appreciation of beauty** — the lover in Song of Songs who genuinely experiences the beloved as pleasant (Song 7:6) can extend genuine appreciative Pleasure.

**[CHAR-6]** E — (1) **A genuine encounter with divine Wonder** — Psa 107:24 ("they saw the deeds of the Lord, his wondrous works in the deep") — direct perceptive encounter with divine wonders; (2) **Formed memory** — 1Ch 16:12; Psa 77:11; 105:5 — the Wonder-tradition must be internalised in memory before it can be extended to others; (3) **Epistemological humility** — Job 42:3's "things too wonderful for me" — the person who has recognised the limits of their own knowledge can genuinely give Wonder without distorting it with false comprehension; (4) **Consecrated inner life** — Jos 3:5 — the morally prepared person can both receive and extend Wonder.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The comparative evidence reveals a consistent principle: **genuine giving requires prior genuine receiving**. Each characteristic's giving direction presupposes something in the giver: (1) **Exultation (Char 1)**: prior encounter with God's reality (Exo 18:9 — Jethro heard, then rejoiced); (2) **Joy (Char 2)**: genuine Joy in their own inner being (the sunchairo requires inner co-joy, not performed solidarity); (3) **Gladness (Char 3)**: prior accurate recognition of what is genuinely good (the apt-word speaker knows what is fitting — Pro 15:23); (4) **Delight (Char 4)**: prior Delight rightly directed (God's sha.a.shu.im in Ephraim persisting through rebuke models the prior-love that enables sacrificial giving); (5) **Pleasure (Char 5)**: inner pleasantness of character (Pro 16:24's gracious words require Pro 15:26's internal purity); (6) **Wonder (Char 6)**: formed personal Wonder from youth (Psa 71:17 — the person who still proclaims wondrous deeds in old age was taught from youth); (7) **Suffering-Joy (Char 7)**: Spirit-enabled Spirit-joy (the jailer's Suffering-Joy encompasses his household because his is genuine, not performed).

**[CHAR-1]** E — The evidence from the corrective-shame passages implies that the person who can legitimately invoke shame in another must themselves have received the corrective-shame signal and responded to it. Paul's own apostolic authority (2Cor 10:8) is the basis for his freedom from shame — his authority is genuinely from God. The person who invokes corrective shame without having themselves experienced and received shame's corrective function is working from a position of moral inconsistency that undermines the legitimacy of the invitation.

**[CHAR-2]** E — VCG-01 involves humans extending CHAR-2 to other humans: Ammonites shaving David's envoys, tenants beating servants. In the unjust register, CHAR-2 is inflicted by malicious agents. In the corrective register, legitimate authority can impose CHAR-2 as a judicial act. The giving direction is morally ambiguous — it can be unjust infliction or just correction.

---

**[CHAR-3]** E — VCG-01 is primarily about humans extending dishonour toward other humans or toward God. The unjust judge (Luk 18:2/4) extends worth-denial to the widow. The rich receive honor while the poor man is dishonored (Jam 2:6). The head-covering symbolic acts extend disrespect toward divinely ordered authority structures.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4 can be extended interpersonally through the articulation of moral evaluations: Paul's renunciation of shameful ways (2Cor 4:2) is both his own functioning CHAR-4 and an implicit invitation to the community's conscience to recognise the same standard. 1Cor 14:35's articulated moral-evaluative judgment extends a community's shared CHAR-4 evaluation.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — The contempt-er extends CHAR-5 toward others through VCG-01's dismissive attitude, VCG-02's violent rejection, and VCG-03's verbal contempt. In every mode, the extending person must have a prior inner disposition of self-elevation or self-righteousness (Luk 18:9) to sustain the contemptuous dismissal of others. The person who gives CHAR-5 is one who has placed themselves above the person they despise — they must have an inflated inner self-assessment as the precondition for the contempt-extension.

---

**[CHAR-6]** S — The 8-verse corpus does not evidence CHAR-6 being extended by one person toward another in a direct relational-giving sense. CHAR-6 is an inner moral condition of the individual, not primarily a characteristic extended toward others. Silent on the giving direction as a direct relational-extension.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — The human giving of M07's characteristics spans a moral spectrum from unjust to legitimate. At the unjust pole: humans inflicting shame through military conquest (Char 2), extending worth-denial through favoritism and hypocrisy (Char 3), and directing contemptuous dismissal toward others (Char 5). At the legitimate-corrective pole: humans deploying corrective shame for moral formation (Char 1's entrepō passages — 2Th 3:14; 1Cor 6:5; Char 4's articulated moral evaluation). Cluster-level finding: the same characteristics that name the unjust forms also name their legitimate forms. The moral quality of the giving depends on whether the giver is aligned with God's own movement in the shame-field — God abases the proud justly; humans can enact the same correction legitimately (corrective community discipline) or unjustly (violence, contempt, worth-denial). The inner conditions enabling legitimate extension: genuine moral concern for the shamed person, not desire for their destruction; a grounded own moral position; recognition of the person's worth even in correction.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — The evidence indicates that CHAR-1 is generated internally rather than received from outside and passed on. Mar 7:22 (vc=33928, M08-A4-VCG-01): pride among "the evil things that flow out of a person" — the generative direction is outward from within. 2Ti 3:2 (vc=1899, M08-A4-VCG-01): filautos (self-love) as the root from which pride, boasting, and arrogance all flow — the person must have developed the self-love root orientation before CHAR-1 can be extended outward. The occasion-triggers (prosperity — Deu 8:14, vc=34223; power — 2Ch 26:16, vc=34044; beauty — Eze 28:17, vc=34047) confirm that CHAR-1's extension begins when the person has received goods from God and then misattributed them as self-generated, activating the self-love root into the CHAR-1 posture that then extends outward toward others as contempt and domination.

**[CHAR-2]** E — CHAR-2 extended toward others requires: the settled inner posture of za.don/zed insolence as a dispositional state (Pro 21:24, vc=34096, M08-B-VCG-02), the cognitive self-deception that overestimates one's own authority (Obd 3, vc=34108; Jer 49:16, vc=34115, M08-B-VCG-02), and the removal of God-fear from the inner horizon (Psa 86:14, vc=34097). These are not received from outside but generated internally from the self-authorising will.

**[CHAR-3]** E — For VCG-01: the self-origination illusion (1Cor 4:7, vc=33871 — the inner cognitive state of treating received goods as self-generated) and the alazoneia inner orientation. For VCG-03: receiving grace, reconciliation, and community relationship — 2Cor 7:4 (vc=33917): Paul's overflowing comfort and joy are the received conditions from which the community boast emerges; Rom 5:11 (vc=33876): receiving reconciliation through Christ is what grounds the God-directed boasting.

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4 requires the receipt of some cognitive content (knowledge — 1Cor 8:1; partisan allegiance — 1Cor 4:6; spiritual experience — Col 2:18, vc=33941) which is then misprocessed into self-inflation. The characteristic requires received content to inflate — unlike CHAR-1 which generates from the self-love root without external stimulus. CHAR-4 is specifically triggered by received cognitive goods (knowledge, experience, allegiance) that generate the false self-picture through misattribution.

**[CHAR-5]** E — CHAR-5 requires the receipt of genuine structural goods: military power (Eze 30:6 — Egypt's actual military might), material wealth (Eze 28:5 — Tyre's actual wealth), physical height/fortification (Jer 49:16 — Edom's actual mountain fortress), or ease (Eze 16:49 — Sodom's actual material abundance). Unlike CHAR-1 (which arises from the self-love root without structural prerequisites), CHAR-5 specifically requires the prior receipt of genuine structural power or position as its enabling condition. The characteristic is the misuse of genuine goods, not a delusion about goods one does not have.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster comparison reveals a significant pattern: for CHAR-2, CHAR-3, CHAR-4, and CHAR-5, the giving of the characteristic toward others requires the prior receipt of something that generates an elevated self-position. CHAR-3 requires received goods misattributed as self-generated. CHAR-4 requires received knowledge or spiritual experience that generates the inflated self-picture. CHAR-5 requires genuine structural power or wealth. CHAR-1 alone generates from the self-love root without requiring a specific received occasion. The cluster-synthesis: CHAR-1 is the most "self-generating" M08 characteristic — it arises from the inner self without requiring external received goods. CHAR-2, CHAR-3, CHAR-4, and CHAR-5 all require received goods as their activating occasion.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The corpus evidences two foundational prerequisites. First, *reception of the gospel and obedience of faith:* 2Cor9:13 — submission "flows directly from confession of the gospel" — the person must have genuinely received the gospel and made the primary submission of faith before they can genuinely extend submission in other relationships. The primary Godward submission is the enabling condition for horizontal submission. Second, *formation through experience:* Heb5:8 — Christ's learning of obedience through suffering — the capacity for genuine submission in hard circumstances requires prior formation through costly engagement. Phili2:12's sustained obedience implies a sustained formation that precedes the sustained expression.
**[CHAR-3]** S — The evidence is silent on the horizontal giving direction (see T4.3.1). Prompt closed.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Heb5:2 provides the answer: the high priest must have genuinely experienced and accepted his own creaturely weakness before he can extend genuine gentleness toward the erring. The characteristic requires having genuinely reckoned with one's own limitation rather than suppressed or denied it. The person who can give metriopatheō is one who has received (or accepted) their own creaturely condition honestly — not transcended it, but genuinely inhabited it without self-deception.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The person must have genuinely formed the inner character quality — 1Ti3:4's "with all dignity" and Tit2:7's "show integrity, dignity" are standards for persons who have already formed the characteristic rather than descriptions of its acquisition. The person giving semnotēs must have genuinely inhabited the character gravity through formation in godliness (1Ti2:2 — pairing) and moral integrity (Tit2:7 — pairing) before it can be genuinely extended.

**[CHAR-6]** E — In VCG-01, the person must have a genuinely free inner orientation toward God — the willing heart is a given of their inner life rather than something requiring prior reception. In VCG-02 (Psa51:12), the person must have received the divine restoration of the willing spirit through God's upholding — after failure, the restoration precedes the renewed expression. The most profound answer the corpus gives: the person must have received (or had restored) the divine gift of the willing spirit (Psa51:12) before they can genuinely give from that spirit rather than from compelled compliance.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The Phili2 passage provides the clearest answer: the human call to humility (v.3 — "count others more significant") is grounded in Christ's prior self-humbling (v.8) and in the Trinitarian life of self-giving that the Incarnation expresses. This suggests the giver must have *received* the pattern and spirit of Christ's self-lowering before they can genuinely give it — the characteristic flows from an inner alignment with the kenotic movement of the Son. Col3:12 ("put on… humility, as God's chosen ones, holy and beloved") links the capacity for the character-disposition to the status of being known and loved by God — the person who has received divine acceptance does not need to assert themselves, and from that security can genuinely lower themselves for others. The security of being received by God enables the person to give the posture of lowering toward others.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The prerequisites for genuine horizontal extension vary by characteristic but share a structural feature: the person must have genuinely received or inhabited the characteristic at the inner-being level before they can extend it. Humility (CHAR-1): Phili2:3–8 and Col3:12 indicate the person must have received the security of divine acceptance and the kenotic pattern of the Son before they can genuinely count others more significant. Submission (CHAR-2): the primary Godward submission of faith (2Cor9:13 — submission flowing from confession of the gospel) is the enabling condition for horizontal submission; costly formation through experience (Heb5:8 — learning through suffering) precedes deep submission capacity. Meekness and Gentleness (CHAR-4): the person must have genuinely experienced and accepted their own creaturely weakness — not transcended it but honestly inhabited it (Heb5:2 — "since he himself is beset with weakness"). Dignity (CHAR-5): genuine formation in godliness and integrity must precede the extension of semnotēs — the person who extends genuine character gravity must have the inner quality rather than performing its manner. Willing-heartedness (CHAR-6): in VCG-02, the person must have received divine restoration of the willing spirit (Psa51:12) before they can give from that spirit rather than from compelled compliance. Cluster-level: CHAR-3 Contrition is the sole characteristic for which the prerequisite question does not apply — its horizontal giving direction is not evidenced.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — Wilful sinning is not received before being given — it is generated by the sinner's own will in the moment of decision. However, the corpus identifies enabling conditions that precede interpersonal sinning: (1) Gen 20:9 shows that Abraham first held the inner posture of fear-driven deception before extending sinning to Abimelech; (2) Pro 14:21 shows that contempt of the neighbour precedes and constitutes the sinning; (3) 1Sa 15:24 shows that fear of people precedes the sinning act against God. The "received" condition is not sinning-from-another but the inner dispositions (fear, contempt, deception) that make the sinning act possible.

**[CHAR-10]** E — (1) *Enticement*: 2Pe 2:14 — the enticers must have become people "with hearts trained in greed" — the mechanism can only be extended by those who have themselves been formed by it; the enticement-extension capacity is a product of the enticers' own formation. (2) *Hypocrisy*: Gal 2:13 — the extending persons must themselves have adopted the hypocritical identity performance (they "acted hypocritically along with him" — they are performing the identity before extending it to others through contagion). (3) *Apostasy*: Act 21:21 — the extending person must themselves have departed from or rejected the covenantal framework in order to teach its abandonment.

**[CHAR-11]** E — For the Adamic transmission (Rom 5:12), Adam's position as head of humanity was the prerequisite — the extension was made possible through representative identity, not merely personal sinning. For the complicity dimension (1Ti 5:22), the person must have made a hasty endorsement that aligns them with another's sin-condition. For the predatory exploitation (2Ti 3:6), the person must themselves be operating from within the condition's own corruption. In all cases: participation in the condition is the ground from which extension to others operates.

**[CHAR-12]** E — 1Jo 3:8 — "makes a practice of sinning... is of the devil" — the extending person must have become a habitual sinner, enrolled by their practice into the devil's domain of originary sinning. The practice-to-slavery mechanism (Joh 8:34) must have operated: the person must have practiced sinning to the point of constitutional enslavement before their condition reflects the devil's enslaving domain. The devil's originary sinning (1Jo 3:8 — "from the beginning") is what they are now aligned with through their formed habit.

**[CHAR-13]** E — The extending person must hold a position of influence, authority, or relational access that makes their sin-record transferable. VCG-04 — the kings who extended the Jeroboam-sin to Israel had first received the royal role (exalted "out of the dust" — 1Ki 16:2 — "since I exalted you out of the dust and made you leader over my people Israel"). The extension-capacity is grounded in the authority-position received: having been made leader, their record-generating acts become the nation's burden. Aaron likewise (Exo 32:21) had received the priestly-leadership role whose authority made his failure extend to all.

**[CHAR-14]** E — The extending person must have received the mediatorial appointment: Lev 10:17 — "given to you that you may bear the iniquity of the congregation" — the priestly appointment is the prerequisite for bearing others' iniquity. Exo 32:30 — Moses's authority to seek atonement for the people is grounded in his unique standing before God as Israel's covenant-mediator. In the NT: Mat 26:28 — Christ's blood is poured out "for many" — Christ's unique position as the covenant-establisher is what enables his extending of forgiveness to the many.

**[CHAR-15]** E — Isa 43:27 — the first father must have occupied the foundational ancestral position before his sinning could become generationally transmissible; the mediators must have been appointed to their leadership roles before their transgressions could be transmitted to those under their care. The extension requires both the representative position (received through appointment or birth-order) and the sinning act. Without the representative position, individual sinning does not generate the same generational transmission.

**[CHAR-16]** E — For label-assignment: the authority or knowledge-claim to render moral verdicts on others (Joh 9:24 — "we know"). For Adam's constitutive extension (Rom 5:19): his position as the covenant-representational head of humanity. For enticement (Pro 1:10): the established sinner-identity that makes the extending person an active recruiter. The extension capacity is grounded either in positional authority (Adam, the Pharisees) or in the fully formed sinner-identity (Pro 1:10's enticing sinners who have become the identity they extend).

**[CHAR-17]** E — For representative-propagation: the person must hold the representative position (Lev 4:3 — the anointed priest; 1Ch 21:3 — the king) before their sin propagates to others. For priestly-bearing: Exo 28:38 — Aaron must be vested in the high-priestly garments with the plate "on Aaron's forehead" — the office and its vestments are prerequisites for the guilt-bearing function. For voluntary-assumption: 1Sa 25:24 — Abigail must have relational access and standing before David to make the guilt-transfer offer effective.

**[CHAR-18]** E — For priestly-ritual extension (Lev 16:21): Aaron must be fully vested in the high-priestly office and garments before the iniquity-transfer through confession is valid — the office is the prerequisite; Exo 28:38 — "it shall regularly be on his forehead" — the gold plate inscription is prerequisite for bearing iniquity. For generational extension (Exo 20:5): the fathers must have committed the originating idolatrous iniquity — "those who hate me" — the hatred of God is the prerequisite moral condition that generates the transmissible iniquity.

**[CHAR-19]** E — For leadership-propagation (Isa 43:27; Jer 2:8): the person must hold the representative office (mediator, shepherd) whose transgression carries community-weight. For anger-contagion (Pro 29:22): the person must have allowed anger to become their constitutive inner disposition — "one given to anger" — before that disposition generates multiple transgressions in the social environment. For communal invitation (Amos 4:4): the person must be already established in transgressive practice before they can credibly invite others to "come and transgress."

**[CHAR-2]** S — Unintentional sinning is not a characteristic that the person intentionally "gives" to another — it is an inadvertent act that may affect others (Lev 4:3). The question of what must be received or become before extending this characteristic does not apply in the same way as for volitionally given characteristics. The corpus is silent on this framing.

**[CHAR-20]** E — The person must have been party to the covenant whose breaking constitutes the faithlessness. Mal 2:14 — "though she is your companion and your wife by covenant" — the prior covenant-membership is the prerequisite that makes the departure faithlessness rather than mere leaving. Jos 22:22 — "if it was in rebellion or in breach of faith against the Lord" — the eastern tribes were already covenant-members whose actions would constitute faithlessness; the covenant-membership precedes any faithlessness.

**[CHAR-21]** E — The person must have become constitutionally perverted before they can extend it. 2Pe 2:19 — "they themselves are slaves of corruption" — the false teachers who promise freedom are already enslaved to corruption before they extend it to others; the extending of perversion to others follows the consolidation of the perversion within the person. The vine-degeneracy pattern (Jer 2:21) applies: the vine must first turn wild from within before it produces wild fruit that corrupts the vineyard.

**[CHAR-22]** E — The extending person must have developed the unjust character-trait (Luk 16:10 — dishonest across all scales) and suppressed the shame-response (Zep 3:5 — knows no shame) before they can consistently extend injustice to others. For the judicial context (Psa 82:2), they must also have received a bribe or partiality-inducement (2Ch 19:7 — "partiality or taking bribes") that has corrupted the inner judgment-faculty before extending unjust judgments to those before them.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The person must first have had the conscience activated — the inner recognition must precede the interpersonal naming. 2Sa 19:20 — Shimei comes "the first" because his conscience is already active about his past wrong; the interpersonal confession flows from the prior inner recognition. The person must also have accepted that they have sinned — not merely that they might have. The equivocation present in Saul's confession (1Sa 15:30 — "I have sinned; yet honor me") shows that incomplete inner acceptance of the sin-verdict produces compromised interpersonal confession.

**[CHAR-4]** S — The corpus does not address the preconditions for extending conscience suppression to another. This is not a characteristic that is intentionally given — it is a condition that may be transmitted through influence or example, but the corpus does not evidence the transmission mechanism directly.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The transmitting person must have: (1) *received the inherited sinful orientation and accepted it* — 2Ki 15:9 "as his fathers had done" — they themselves did not depart, making the transmission a continuation of their own inner condition; (2) *held leadership authority* that gives their inner condition communal scope — the kings who transmit the refusal hold the authority through which their personal non-departure becomes the community's non-departure; (3) *established the sinful pattern as the operative norm* — by walking in it, by treating it as light (1Ki 16:31), by not publicly marking the path as wrong.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The transmitting person must themselves have become the sinner-type — Ecc 9:18 names "one sinner" as the agent of destruction, presupposing a settled sinner-identity. 1Sa 2:25 — Eli's sons are characterized by persistent sinning against the Lord; their extension to others follows from their own habituated condition. The person extends what they are, not merely what they do: habitual defection is transmitted from a settled inner character, not from isolated acts. The precondition for transmission is the formation of the habitual-defection character in the transmitter.

**[CHAR-7]** E — The transmitting leader must have: (1) *Received the sinning orientation themselves*: 1Ki 22:52 — Ahaziah followed the way of his father, mother, and Jeroboam — the leader first receives the sinning direction from prior authorities before they can transmit it; (2) *Internalised the sinning course as their own committed direction*: 1Ki 16:19 — "walking in the way of Jeroboam, and for his sin which he committed" — the personal commitment is a prerequisite; (3) *Occupied the leadership position that gives their inner commitment communal reach*: without the authority, the same inner sinful commitment produces only personal sinning (CHAR-1/5/6) rather than communal transmission.

**[CHAR-8]** E — The revolting community must have formed a collective will for independence that outweighs the political cost of revolt. 2Ki 8:20 — "set up a king of their own" — implies that the community had developed sufficient internal cohesion to establish alternative governance; revolt without this internal capacity would be premature. The community must have assessed both the governing authority's vulnerability (2Ki 1:1 — Ahab's death as opportunity) and their own capacity for self-governance (2Ki 8:20 — they can set up their own king).

**[CHAR-1]** E — The wicked person can extend their characteristic to others once they have themselves settled into it — once the internal God-exclusion (Psa 10:4), the suppression of conscience (Psa 36:1), and the volitional alignment with wickedness (Pro 4:14 — entering the path) have consolidated into a stable inner orientation. 1Sa 24:13 (VCG-04): "out of the wicked comes wickedness" — the wicked person must first be constituted as a wicked inner source before they can extend wickedness outward. The evidence suggests no external bestowal that enables this; it is an internally generated and consolidated state that then overflows outward as social harm and moral contagion.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Unlike a gift characteristic (wisdom, love, grace), evil as constitutional inner nature does not require the person to receive something from outside before extending it — it is the baseline constitutional condition from which extension flows. 1Sa 24:13 / CHAR-1's pattern of "out of the wicked comes wickedness" parallels the CHAR-2 pattern: the evil treasury (Mat 12:35 — VCG-03) is already full by constitutional default. The person extends the characteristic from their own constitutional inner store — they do not need to receive it first. The extension is the natural output of the constitutional condition already present. This makes CHAR-2 distinct from positive characteristics (like grace or wisdom) that require reception before giving.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Like CHAR-2, the characteristic is not received from another before being extended — it develops from within the inner moral character. The scoffer's contemptuous derision (Pro 24:9 — VCG-01), the dishonest dealer's habitual practice (Deu 25:16 — VCG-01), and the Pharisees' self-justifying pride (Luk 16:15 — VCG-02) are all inner conditions that developed from within the person's inner moral formation and are then expressed outward toward others. The person extends abomination toward others from the reservoir of their own abominable inner character — 1Sa 24:13's "out of the wicked comes wickedness" is structurally parallel here. The abominable condition is the inner generative source from which abominable acts directed at others flow.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The person extends idolatrous abomination toward others from their own established inner attachment: Hos 9:10 (vc=1632 — VCG-04): "they became detestable like the thing they loved" — the person who extends the characteristic has already been transformed by idolatrous attachment into someone who is themselves detestable. 1Ki 11:5 (vc=65898 — VCG-03): Solomon "went after Ashtoreth… and after Milcom" — he had already committed himself to these idols before building their high places. The person must first have settled into idolatrous inner attachment before they can extend it — the extension is the overflow of an established inner condition.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The evidence consistently presents iniquity as self-generated from within rather than received from another before extension (T2.9.1). The extending person extends what their own inner life has generated: Psa 7:14 (vc=38245 — VCG-02): "conceives evil… gives birth to lies" — the iniquity is conceived internally before being extended outward. Isa 32:6 (vc=38181 — VCG-02): "his heart is busy with iniquity" — the heart's own production is what flows outward. However, chosen association with evildoers (Job 34:8 — VCG-04) can shape the inner person toward iniquity; in this sense, what must be "received or become" before extension is the inner character of the evildoer-type (VCG-03), developed through volitional choice and associative formation.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The characteristic is generated from within the person's own inner moral state rather than received from another before extension. Jude 8 (vc=14354 — VCG-01): the dreamers' inner posture (sensory self-indulgence + authority-rejection) is what produces the blasphemous extension — they extend what their own inner condition generates. Rev 13:6 (VCG-01): the beast's sustained defiant contempt is what its mouth utters — inner contempt is expressed outward. Joh 18:30 (VCG-03): the accusers' malicious evaluation is their own — they have become people whose inner moral posture produces false accusatory speech. What must be received or become: a hardened will (VCG-01), a hostile evaluative posture (VCG-03), or a moral-failure condition (VCG-02).

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster consistently shows that M10b characteristics are extended from within the person's own settled inner-evil condition — not received from another and then passed on. Char 1 (the wicked person extends what their inner orientation generates), Char 2 (the evil treasury extends what the constitutional inner nature stores — Mat 12:35), Char 4 (the person extends the idolatrous attachment that has already constituted them — Hos 9:10 — becoming detestable before extending the pattern to others), Char 5 (the heart that is busy with iniquity extends its schemes outward), Char 6 (the will hardened against God generates the blasphemous speech from within). The cluster reveals that social extension of M10b evil requires the inner-evil-form to be established and deepened first — extension is the overflow of a settled inner condition.

**[CHAR-1]** S — The characteristic is not given in the positive sense; it is transmitted involuntarily through contact mechanisms. The prompt frame of "giving" does not apply to this characteristic's primary mode of operation. The relevant question is how transmission is prevented (through conscience-awareness and prescribed precautions), not how it is enabled.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The person who extends the moral-inner defilement-state through environmental-formative influence is someone whose own inner defilement has become so normalized and community-embedded that it functions as a formative context for others. Eph 4:19 (VCG-02) — the community that has collectively given itself up to impurity has become that formative context. The person extending the characteristic is one whose own conscience has been sufficiently silenced that the defilement is no longer perceived as defilement within their community.

**[CHAR-3]** S — The evidence does not frame the extending of corporate/covenantal defilement as requiring something the person has "received" in the positive sense. The extending is generated by desire, lust, volitional betrayal, and corporate unfaithfulness — conditions of the defiled inner life rather than received gifts. The characteristic is extended by what the person or community has become through moral defection, not by what they have received.
**[CHAR-4]** S — Not applicable; see T4.3.1.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's "giver" profiles reveal different forms of inner condition. Characteristic 1: transmission requires the person to be in the defilement-state themselves (one cannot transmit what one does not have) — what is transmitted is the condition itself through contact. Characteristic 2: the person who extends the characteristic through formative-environmental influence is someone whose own defilement has become normalized and community-embedded (Eph 4:19 — the community has collectively given itself up; the individual conscience has been silenced). Characteristic 3: the extending person is one whose desire or will has been oriented toward violation or idolatrous attachment (Eze 23:17 — the Babylonians' "whoring lust" as the inner condition enabling extension). Characteristic 4: no human "giver" profile is evidenced. The cluster's insight: in Characteristics 1-3, the extension of defilement requires the person to have already internalized or embodied the condition — defilement extends outward from an inner center.

findings.session_b_note: The evidence is silent on contrition as something extended from one person to another. Contrition is a condition of the inner being before God, not a characteristic extended toward other humans. The absence of a giving direction is structurally consistent with contrition's nature: it is intrinsically the posture of the self before God, not a relational commodity extended outward. This silence is complete and informative — it distinguishes contrition from characteristics like forgiveness, mercy, and compassion that have a constitutive giving direction.

findings.finding_value: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion on whom I have compassion"), covenantally grounded (chesed as the bond-loyalty that grounds the characteristic), and situationally responsive (splanchnizō — triggered by the specific sight of suffering). These three bases are not in tension but in integration: divine compassion is free, covenanted, and responsive simultaneously. The scope finding is among the most analytically significant in the registry: compassion explicitly and repeatedly crosses covenantal boundaries (Nineveh, the Samaritan/Jew axis, the power-asymmetric relationship). Scope is defined by perceived need, not moral standing or covenantal membership — this is formally confirmed in the data and distinguishes compassion from many other relational characteristics. The chesed/splanchnizō distinction maps onto distinct relational registers: chesed sustains within established bonds; splanchnizō extends across distance and difference. T4.4 (receiver's inner-being experience) is the most significant gap — four P-rated prompts, entirely absent from the data. T4.6 (spiritual beings interface) is entirely silent across all four prompts.

findings.finding_value: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — all God-as-subject). The basis of divine extension is the giver's character and prior knowing (Exo 33:17 — "I know you by name"), not the receiver's merit — neither merit-based nor arbitrary. The human-to-God direction is specifically supplication: tachanum (H8469) is the receiving side's corresponding vocabulary built into the same root family as the giving side (chen/chanan) — the vocabulary embeds the two-directional circuit in a single root. The human-giving direction extends grace horizontally through three modes: forgiving (charizō — Eph 4:32), gracious conduct (chen as character quality — 889-003), and gracious speech (SD022). The receiving direction is the most underexamined (T4.4 — P-rated throughout); the scope analysis (T4.5) reveals grace crossing covenantal and social boundaries (Ruth narrative — grace in the context of foreign status and vulnerability). T4.6 (spiritual beings) is evidenced at one point: Luk 1:28 (kecharitōmenē — the angel's announcement), which implies angelic ministry as a vehicle of grace rather than grace operating independently in the spiritual-beings register. findings.session_b_note:
Yes — receiving forgiveness from another person is evidenced, though less extensively than receiving from God. Two distinct contexts appear:

**Receiving divine forgiveness (primary):** The entire afesis corpus (group 879-001, 13 verses) and the H5545 corpus name the human person as the recipient of divine forgiveness. The reception operates through the access-postures (repentance, faith, confession) and produces the condition of release (afesis state). Eph 1:7 — "we have... the forgiveness of our trespasses." The reception is stated as an accomplished state.

**Receiving horizontal forgiveness from another person:** Less evidenced as a distinct reception-event. Luk 17:3-4 — the one who sins and repents ("I repent") is to receive forgiveness from the offended party. The reception in this context is the relational resolution — the claim is released by the other, and the offender receives the release. The inner-being experience of receiving horizontal forgiveness is not extensively named in the data.

**How reception operates:** The clearest account is Luk 7:47 — the woman who has received forgiveness demonstrates its reception through bodily acts (weeping, anointing) and through the love-orientation produced. The reception is inner and transformative — it generates a new orientation rather than merely relieving a pressure.

findings.session_b_note:
The data addresses reception of compassion from God toward the human person extensively (covered at T4.1), but reception of compassion from one human person to another is partially evidenced and the inner-being dynamics of reception are largely unaddressed.

**What is evidenced:** Gen 19:16 — Lot receives divine compassion (chem.lah) when the angels physically take him and his family by the hand and lead them out. The reception is enacted bodily — the compassion-act reaches him physically and produces rescue. Isa 57:18 — the straying person receives divine comfort (ni.chum) — "I will heal him; I will lead him and restore comfort to him." The reception produces healing and restoration.

In the Synoptic pattern, the recipients of Jesus's splanchnizō-movements receive healing (Matt 20:34 — "their eyes were opened"), restoration (Luke 7:14-15 — the widow's son raised), and feeding (Matt 15:32ff). The reception of compassion in these contexts produces material change in the recipient's condition.

**What is missing (P):** The inner-being dynamics of receiving compassion — what happens inside the person at the moment of reception — are almost entirely absent from the data. The focus of the vocabulary is on the giver's inner movement and the outer act of compassion, not on the receiver's inner experience. The gap identified at T1.5 P1 (receiver's immediate inner response) is reproduced and deepened here.

findings.session_b_note: Love as received is constitutive of identity (agapētos, OBS-103-040), productive of rest (Zep 3:17, OBS-103-094), and the enabling condition for giving love (1Jo 4:19, OBS-103-146). findings.finding_value: Love's relational architecture is structured by three directional axes — GOD → HUMAN, HUMAN → GOD, HUMAN → HUMAN — with divine love structurally prior and causally generative of all subsequent love. 1Jo 4:19 ('we love because he first loved us') is the axis-precedence statement: the first axis is not responsive to but constitutive of the second and third. The GOD → HUMAN direction moves through four mechanisms: covenantal declaration (naming the beloved — Jer 12:7, Mat 3:17), Spirit-infusion (Rom 5:5), redemptive acts (Joh 3:16), and covenantal covering (Eze 16:8). The HUMAN → GOD direction requires total inner mobilisation (Mat 22:37 — all heart, soul, mind) and the clearing of rival loves as its condition (1Jo 4:19, 1Ti 6:10). The HUMAN → HUMAN direction spans five structural types (neighbour, enemy, community, friendship, family) and creates the social architecture described in Q&A-088 (restructured kinship, public legibility, competitive generosity). The most significant finding in T4: the human-to-God direction is conditioned by prior reception of divine love — the capacity for human love toward God is itself a gift. The one structural gap: T4.6 (spiritual beings) is absent from the evidence.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-062-004: T4 reveals fellowship as the most relationally comprehensive characteristic in the registry: it operates in all four primary directions (God-to-human, human-to-God, human-giving, human-receiving) and …
findings.finding_value: T4 reveals fellowship as the most relationally comprehensive characteristic in the registry: it operates in all four primary directions (God-to-human, human-to-God, human-giving, human-receiving) and partially in the spiritual-beings direction. The key T4 synthesis: 1Jo 1:3's structural claim — horizontal fellowship is derived from and grounded in vertical fellowship — means the relational architecture of fellowship is hierarchical: the divine-human fellowship is primary; human-human fellowship is its extension and expression. The scope analysis (Q&A-119) reveals that fellowship scope narrows as its depth increases: all-the-living (widest) → God-fearers → covenant partner → ecclesial body → divine nature participants (deepest-narrowest). Depth and breadth are inversely proportional in fellowship's relational structure.

findings.finding_value: T3's faculty engagements all run in the same relational direction that T4 identifies as primary (vertical — human toward God). Perception, volition, moral evaluation, conscientiousness, and relational capacity are all deepened when directed toward the right fellowship object (God and God-fearers). T3's bilateral finding (right fellowship deepens; wrong fellowship degrades) explains T4's structural negative (misdirected fellowship is more dangerous than absence — Hos 4:17, Mat 23:30): when every faculty is progressively shaped by the fellowship object, misdirected fellowship progressively degrades every faculty, not just the relational capacity.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-064-004: T4 establishes the most structurally developed relational architecture of any characteristic reviewed in this series. All four primary directions are fully evidenced: God-to-human (the dominant vertic…
findings.finding_value: T4 establishes the most structurally developed relational architecture of any characteristic reviewed in this series. All four primary directions are fully evidenced: God-to-human (the dominant vertical direction — exclusively divine in the OT salach domain), human-to-God (seeking-forgiveness — intercession and confession), human-giving (commanded horizontal), human-receiving (implied in the horizontal transaction). The spiritual-beings direction adds the Holy Spirit as the enabling mediator (Joh 20:22-23) and the unforgivable sin as the outer limit (Mar 3:29). The vertical-horizontal interdependence (Mat 18:35; Mat 6:14-15) is the most structurally developed relational feature: the human-giving direction is structurally conditioned on the human-receiving direction (one who genuinely received divine forgiveness can genuinely extend human forgiveness). The scope analysis shows: universal access through faith (Act 10:43) with an absolute outer limit (Mar 3:29). T4's synthesis: forgiveness has the fullest relational architecture of the characteristics reviewed — every direction is evidenced, and the vertical-horizontal interdependence is a structural claim unique to forgiveness.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-004: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion…
findings.finding_value: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion on whom I have compassion"), covenantally grounded (chesed as the bond-loyalty that grounds the characteristic), and situationally responsive (splanchnizō — triggered by the specific sight of suffering). These three bases are not in tension but in integration: divine compassion is free, covenanted, and responsive simultaneously. The scope finding is among the most analytically significant in the registry: compassion explicitly and repeatedly crosses covenantal boundaries (Nineveh, the Samaritan/Jew axis, the power-asymmetric relationship). Scope is defined by perceived need, not moral standing or covenantal membership — this is formally confirmed in the data and distinguishes compassion from many other relational characteristics. The chesed/splanchnizō distinction maps onto distinct relational registers: chesed sustains within established bonds; splanchnizō extends across distance and difference. T4.4 (receiver's inner-being experience) is the most significant gap — four P-rated prompts, entirely absent from the data. T4.6 (spiritual beings interface) is entirely silent across all four prompts.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-004: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — a…
findings.finding_value: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — all God-as-subject). The basis of divine extension is the giver's character and prior knowing (Exo 33:17 — "I know you by name"), not the receiver's merit — neither merit-based nor arbitrary. The human-to-God direction is specifically supplication: tachanum (H8469) is the receiving side's corresponding vocabulary built into the same root family as the giving side (chen/chanan) — the vocabulary embeds the two-directional circuit in a single root. The human-giving direction extends grace horizontally through three modes: forgiving (charizō — Eph 4:32), gracious conduct (chen as character quality — 889-003), and gracious speech (SD022). The receiving direction is the most underexamined (T4.4 — P-rated throughout); the scope analysis (T4.5) reveals grace crossing covenantal and social boundaries (Ruth narrative — grace in the context of foreign status and vulnerability). T4.6 (spiritual beings) is evidenced at one point: Luk 1:28 (kecharitōmenē — the angel's announcement), which implies angelic ministry as a vehicle of grace rather than grace operating independently in the spiritual-beings register. T4 synthesis: the relational architecture of grace is unique in the programme — it is the only characteristic where the giving-side vocabulary and the receiving-side vocabulary are built from the same root (chen/tachanum), encoding the grace-circuit's two-sidedness at the lexical level.

Constitutional location and relational interface are two views of the same inner-being dynamic.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-099-004: T4 reveals that kindness operates across all four relational directions for which evidence exists — God-to-human (most extensively evidenced), human-to-God (appeal/chasid identity mode), human giving,…
findings.finding_value: T4 reveals that kindness operates across all four relational directions for which evidence exists — God-to-human (most extensively evidenced), human-to-God (appeal/chasid identity mode), human giving, human receiving, and communal — with spiritual beings being the only direction that is genuinely absent from the evidence. The structural finding: the four evidenced directions form a coherent circuit, not parallel independent operations. Divine kindness flows to the human → the human receives it and appeals to it (human-to-God) → the human, having received, is equipped and obligated to give it to others (human giving, grounded in Eph 4:32's "as God in Christ forgave you, be kind") → kindness given and received forms the communal relational fabric (chasidim assembly). The circuit is both moral and ontological: it is not merely that we ought to be kind because God is kind, but that the human person is constituted to be a bearer of the divine kindness in the relational world. T4's most significant intra-tier finding: the divine-to-human direction is the source and ground of all other directions — human giving of kindness is explicitly grounded in received divine kindness, making T4 a circuit with a single originating source.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-060-004: T4 as a whole reveals that the relational architecture of this characteristic is directionally structured and asymmetrical. The dominant direction is God-to-human (6 of 7 groups, confirmed across T4.1…
findings.finding_value: T4 as a whole reveals that the relational architecture of this characteristic is directionally structured and asymmetrical. The dominant direction is God-to-human (6 of 7 groups, confirmed across T4.1); the human direction is responsive (T4.2: human gives back what was first given). The basis of divine giving is plural — covenantal, responsive, formative, moral-consequential, eschatological-grace (Q&A-102) — revealing that faithfulness is not a single relational mode but a relational orientation that differentiates itself across relational conditions while remaining unified in character. The human-to-God direction reveals responsive correspondence as the relational structure (Q&A-107): the proper relational form is one in which the human gives back to God what is his (glory, praise, self), having first received. The human-to-human direction is thinner in the data (Q&A-109) — reflecting the registry's God-subject dominance. T4.6 is substantially silent on spiritual beings. What T4 reveals as a whole: faithfulness-as-giving is constitutively a divine-initiative relational reality that the human enters through responsive participation. The human's giving is always downstream of divine giving; the correspondence is the proper form of the relationship.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-017: The relational interfaces (T4 — God-to-human primary, human-to-God responsive, covenantal scope) and the structural landscape (T6 — hub position, causal sequences, shared anchors) reveal that R060's h…
findings.finding_value: The relational interfaces (T4 — God-to-human primary, human-to-God responsive, covenantal scope) and the structural landscape (T6 — hub position, causal sequences, shared anchors) reveal that R060's hub position is constituted by its position at the centre of the divine-human relational network. The sequential patterns (T6.2 — giving→worship, suffering→giving, faithlessness→giving-over) are relational sequences: each involves God and the human in the roles described by T4. The shared anchors (T6.6) are high-density precisely because they are relational nodes — Hos 11:8 anchors five registries because it holds the divine inner-being and the human relational situation simultaneously. What this pair reveals: the structural hub position of R060 in the inner-being landscape is a direct consequence of its occupation of the divine-human relational centre. It is a hub because it is where the primary divine-human dynamic (God gives, human receives and responds) is most directly expressed and most extensively connected.

The receiving direction is evidenced across all sub-groups but is unevenly documented. M05-A (love received), M05-B (compassion received — the cry for divine compassion), M05-C (mercy cry — Group 1629 — is the most vivid and extensive receiving evidencing in M05), M05-F (comfort received — extensively evidenced in both OT grief contexts and NT apostolic contexts) are the most receiver-prominent sub-groups. M05-D and M05-E are the most giver-oriented in their verse evidence — the receiver's immediate inner experience is underspecified. M05-G documents receiving reconciliation (Rom 5:11 — Group 2069) and being called into fellowship (1Cor 1:9 — Group 1055) as the primary receiving events.

**Conditions enabling reception** are consistent across sub-groups: humility, need, seeking, honest mourning, walking in the light — the posture of the person who acknowledges their need and opens themselves to receive.

**Non-receiving inner states** are also consistent: hardness (M05-A, D), refusal (M05-F), self-deception (M05-G), mercilessness (M05-C), disordered love priority (M05-A).

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Yes — indirectly: the person who receives instruction in righteousness is receiving from another. "I have taught you the way of wisdom; I have led you in the paths of uprightness" (Pro 4:11, VSG 1211-002). The righteousness that comes through teaching and formation is received from the teacher/parent/community.

**[C — Justification]** Yes — justification is received: "being justified by his grace" (Tit 3:7) is a reception event. The mode of reception is through faith — the person receives what God has declared through the act of believing.

**[D — Avenging Justice]** Yes — the wronged person receives justice from God through the mediating act of the commissioned human avenger (Rom 13:4) or through God's direct response to the cry (Luk 18:7–8). The reception of justice is the resolution of the wronged person's situation.

**[E — Condemnation]** Yes — the person receives the verdict of condemnation (external, from judge), the relief of freedom from condemnation (from God through Christ), or the self-condemnation of the conscience (from within, through autokatakritos). All three forms of condemnation-verdict are received.

**[CLUSTER — T4.4]** E. Reception of righteousness from others operates through teaching/formation (A2, B: instruction in right paths), through the declared verdict of justification received by faith (C), through received justice from God or commissioned agents (D), and through received verdict of condemnation or freedom (E). The cluster reveals that righteousness in all its modes is ultimately received — even the human righteousness of A2 is first received through formation and ultimately through God's credit.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Reception is evidenced for all seven. The most analytically significant comparative finding: the receiving direction reveals different primary mediums for each characteristic: (1) **Joy (Char 2)**: received primarily through news, report, and visible returning persons (Act 12:14; Phili 2:28; Act 15:3); (2) **Gladness (Char 3)**: received primarily through spoken words — the apt word, good news, testimony (Pro 12:25; Neh 2:18); (3) **Delight (Char 4)**: received primarily from divine action — rescue, exaltation, naming (Psa 18:19; Isa 62:4); (4) **Pleasure (Char 5)**: received from persons, their pleasantness, and their speech (2Sa 1:26; Pro 16:24); (5) **Wonder (Char 6)**: received from the community's witness-tradition and from direct encounter with God's wondrous acts (Psa 78:4; Psa 107:24); (6) **Suffering-Joy (Char 7)**: received within community through shared faith-crisis (Act 16:34's household) and Spirit-transmission (Luk 1:44's in-utero response); (7) **Exultation (Char 1)**: received from God's exultation over the person (Zep 3:17) as the primary instance — human-to-human receiving is less documented. The mediums confirm the characteristics' different relational modes: Joy through news; Gladness through speech; Pleasure through persons; Wonder through tradition and encounter; Suffering-Joy through Spirit-in-community.

**[CHAR-3]** S — The two-verse corpus does not evidence contrition being received horizontally from another person. The characteristic is a state the person is in before God; its reception in the sense of one person receiving contrition from another is not evidenced.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Heb5:2 evidences reception: the "ignorant and wayward" receive the high priest's metriopatheō — they are the recipients of his measured gentle dealing. The erring persons receive a form of engagement that is calibrated and compassionate rather than severe. The receiving of this characteristic is the experience of being dealt with gently rather than harshly when one has erred.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes. 1Ti3:4 — the overseer's children receive the effects of his semnotēs in the form of orderly, respectful compliance — they receive the character-quality's relational ordering. Tit2:7 — the hearers receive teaching that is authenticated by the teacher's semnotēs — they receive instruction whose credibility is established by the teacher's dignity. The reception is not the characteristic itself but its effects: orderly response and authentic teaching-reception.

**[CHAR-6]** E — 1Ch28:21 — Solomon and the temple-building project receive the willing-hearted service of the craftsmen — their service is received as a gift of willing engagement rather than compelled labour. God receives the willing-hearted offerings (Exo35:5/22; 2Ch29:31) — the willing-hearted person extends free offering; God receives it. The receiving direction is most clearly evidenced in God's reception of the free offerings and in Solomon's reception of the willing skilled service.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The receiving direction is less directly evidenced than the giving direction, but it is present. In Luk1:48, Mary receives the divine acknowledgement of her humble estate — God looks upon her humility and she receives his favour as a consequence. In the horizontal direction, the community that encounters Paul's humility (Act20:19; 2Cor11:7) receives the benefit of his self-lowering — the Corinthians' exaltation (2Cor11:7) is the received effect of Paul's self-humbling. In Eph4:2 and Phili2:3, the posture of humility toward one another creates a relational environment that the other person receives as genuine regard. The receiving of humility from another is evidenced as the reception of the other's genuine regard and self-lowering on one's behalf.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The receiving direction is evidenced across the cluster, but with different recipient profiles. CHAR-1: others receive the humble person's genuine regard; Mary receives divine acknowledgment of her humble estate (Luk1:48). CHAR-2: the authority receives submission from the one yielding; 2Cor7:15 — Titus receives the Corinthians' obedient welcome. CHAR-3: not directly evidenced in horizontal receiving — the characteristic is not received from another person; it is a state the person is in before God. CHAR-4: the erring receive the high priest's metriopatheō (Heb5:2). CHAR-5: the overseer's children receive orderly compliance-evoked-by-dignity (1Ti3:4); the hearers receive teaching authenticated by the teacher's semnotēs. CHAR-6: God receives the freely-offered worship; Solomon receives the willing service of craftsmen. Cluster-level: the pattern of who receives what from whom varies by characteristic's relational structure — CHAR-1 and CHAR-5 produce ordered responses in others; CHAR-2, CHAR-4, and CHAR-6 produce structured giving and receiving relationships. CHAR-3 remains the cluster's exclusively-before-God characteristic throughout the relational interface analysis.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes. The recipient of sinning is extensively evidenced in VCG-02. Gen 20:9 — Abimelech receives sinning from Abraham: "you have brought on me and my kingdom a great sin." Gen 42:22 — Joseph received sinning from his brothers: "Do not sin against the boy." 1Sa 19:4/5 — David as the would-be recipient of Saul's sinning: "Let not the king sin against his servant David." Mat 18:15 — the brother who has been sinned against and must decide whether to confront. 1Cor 8:12 — the weak brother whose conscience is wounded by another's sinning. The reception operates as a *harm received* — moral, relational, and sometimes physical damage inflicted on the recipient by the sinner's act.

**[CHAR-10]** E — Yes. (1) *Enticement received*: 2Pe 2:18 — "those who are barely escaping from those who live in error" receive the enticement directed at them by the false teachers; the mechanism is received by those at the vulnerable threshold between error and escape. (2) *Hypocrisy received*: Gal 2:13 — "even Barnabas was led astray by their hypocrisy" — Barnabas receives the collective hypocrisy and is drawn into it; the reception is described as "being led astray" — passive in form, showing the mechanism's power over the receiver.

**[CHAR-11]** E — Yes — the reception dimension is the condition's defining feature. (1) *Universal reception through Adam*: Rom 5:12 — "death spread to all men because all sinned" — the universal condition is received by all humanity through the Adamic representative structure; Joh 9:34 — "born in utter sin" — the condition is received at birth; (2) *Reception of forgiveness as the reversal*: VCG-02 throughout — "your sins are forgiven" (Mat 9:2) — the forgiveness is received by the person from Jesus; (3) *Reception of the Spirit's conviction*: Joh 16:8 — the Spirit convicts the world — the condition's recognition is received from the Spirit's external work.

**[CHAR-12]** E — Yes — the reception is the enslaving mechanism's primary operation. Joh 8:34 — "everyone who practices sin is a slave to sin" — the slavery is received through the practice: the person receives the enslaved state as the constitutional consequence of sustained sinning practice. Gal 3:22 — "imprisoned everything under sin" — the universal imprisonment is the structural condition received by all persons under the declaration of Scripture; the reception is universal and not individually chosen but corporately received.

**[CHAR-13]** E — Yes — through multiple reception modes. (1) *Inherited birth-condition*: Psa 51:5 — "in sin did my mother conceive me" (VCG-01) — the record-bearing condition is received at conception, prior to any individual act; (2) *Corporate inheritance through leaders*: VCG-04 — Israel received Jeroboam's sin-record as national inheritance through 46 verses of royal succession; (3) *Priestly loading*: Lev 16:21 — "he shall put them on the head of the goat" — the people's sins are loaded onto the scapegoat in the Day of Atonement ritual; (4) *Unexpected reception*: Gen 20:9 — Abimelech received Abraham's sin-record through deception; he was "about to have sinned" without knowledge.

**[CHAR-14]** E — Yes — the receiving dimension is the characteristic's completing act. Lev 16:30 — "you shall be clean before the Lord from all your sins" — the community receives the cleanliness that atonement confers; Luk 7:47/48 — the woman receives the forgiveness Jesus declares; Col 2:13 — "having forgiven us all our trespasses" — the "us" receives the comprehensive forgiveness; Act 2:38 — "you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit" — forgiveness enables receipt of the Spirit.

**[CHAR-15]** E — Yes — the present generation receives the accumulated condition from the ancestors. Isa 43:27 — "your first father sinned" — the "your" addresses the present community as the receivers of the ancestral condition; the present generation is characterised by the first father's sin without having personally committed it. Isa 64:5 — "in our sins we have been a long time" — the prolonged condition encompasses more than the present generation's own acts; the "long time" implies receipt of a condition that predates the present generation's own sinning.

**[CHAR-16]** E — Yes — through three reception modes. (1) *Constituted imputation*: Rom 5:19 — "the many were made sinners" — the sinner-identity is received through Adam's representative act, prior to any individual's personal sinning; (2) *Social reception*: Luk 7:37 — "a woman of the city, who was a sinner" — the city's label has been received as her public identity; Luk 18:13 — "be merciful to me, a sinner" — the tax collector has internalised the label as self-description; (3) *Authentic self-recognition*: Luk 5:8 — "I am a sinful man" — Peter receives the sinner-identity as an accurate inner self-description prompted by conscience.

**[CHAR-17]** E — Yes — through three reception modes. (1) *Individual incurrence*: Lev 5:19 — "he has indeed incurred guilt before the Lord" — the individual receives guilt through their own act; Lev 22:16 — "cause them to bear iniquity and guilt, by eating their holy things" — guilt is incurred through improper action; (2) *Communal inheritance*: Ezr 9:7 — "from the days of our fathers to this day we have been in great guilt" — the community receives inherited guilt across generations; Jer 32:18 — "you repay the guilt of fathers to their children after them" — intergenerational guilt-reception; (3) *Voluntary assumption*: Exo 28:38 — Aaron receives Israel's guilt for bearing; 1Sa 25:24 — Abigail proposes to receive David/Nabal's guilt.

**[CHAR-18]** E — Yes — through four reception modes. (1) *Personal incurrence*: Num 15:31 — "his iniquity shall be on him" — iniquity is received through one's own act and attaches to the person; Lev 5:17 — "he shall bear his iniquity" — the individual receives and carries the iniquity arising from their own violation; (2) *Generational inheritance*: Lam 5:7 — "our fathers sinned, and are no more; and we bear their iniquities" — the present generation receives the iniquity-burden of deceased ancestors; Jer 32:18 — "you repay the guilt of fathers to their children after them"; (3) *Priestly representative receiving*: Lev 10:17 — the priests receive the congregation's iniquity through the sin-offering; Num 18:1 — "you and your sons and your father's house with you shall bear iniquity connected with the sanctuary"; (4) *Servant's vicarious receiving*: Isa 53:6 — "the Lord has laid on him the iniquity of us all" — the servant receives the iniquity of all through divine appointment.

**[CHAR-19]** E — Yes — through three reception modes. (1) *Personal commission*: Psa 51:3 — "I know my transgressions" — personally owned; Rom 2:23 — "you who boast in the law dishonor God by breaking the law" — personally incurred; (2) *Generational inheritance*: Isa 57:4 — "children of transgression, offspring of deceit" — inheriting a transgression-identity from the parental generation; Isa 48:8 — "from before birth you were called a rebel" — the rebel-label received before personal choice; (3) *Adamic universal*: Rom 5:15/16/17/18 — "one man's trespass" producing "condemnation for all men" — the transgression received through the Adamic representative.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The receiving direction is present in Lev 4:3: the community receives the guilt consequence of the anointed priest's inadvertent sinning — "the anointed priest who sins, thus bringing guilt on the people." The people receive a moral liability they did not personally incur through any act of their own. Lev 9:15 (Aaron's communal sin offering "for the people") addresses this received communal guilt. The receiving is involuntary and inadvertent on both sides — the priest did not deliberately sin against the community, and the community did not knowingly receive the guilt.

**[CHAR-20]** E — Yes — through three reception modes. (1) *Personal commission*: Lev 26:40 — "treachery that they committed against me" — personally owned; 1Ch 10:13 — "Saul died for his breach of faith. He broke faith with the Lord" — named personal receipt of faithlessness as self-committed; (2) *Generational inheritance*: 2Ch 30:7 — "do not be like your fathers and your brothers, who were faithless" — the generational pattern received; Lev 26:40 — "the iniquity of their fathers in their treachery" — the fathers' faithlessness inherited as a pattern; (3) *Communal attribution*: Jos 7:1 — "the people of Israel broke faith" — individual faithlessness attributed to the whole community; Ezr 9:2 — "in this faithlessness the hand of the officials and chief men has been foremost" — communal reception of the faithlessness-charge.

**[CHAR-21]** E — Yes — through three reception modes. (1) *Personal inner generation*: Pro 6:14 — "with perverted heart devises evil" — the perversity is generated from within; Eph 4:22 — "corrupt through deceitful desires" — the old self receiving corruption through its own deceitful desires; (2) *External social reception*: 1Cor 15:33 — "bad company ruins good morals" — good morals received from without initially are ruined by external corrupting company; 2Cor 11:3 — "your thoughts will be led astray" — the congregants receive corrupted thinking from the false teacher; (3) *Generational inheritance*: Deu 32:20 — "perverse generation" — the perversity characterises the generation inherited as a communal condition.

**[CHAR-22]** E — Yes — extensively as victim-experience. (1) *Personal receipt*: Job 6:29 — "let no injustice be done" — Job as the intended recipient; Psa 43:1 — "from the deceitful and unjust man deliver me" — the psalmist as the one receiving unjust oppression; (2) *Communal receipt*: 2Sa 7:10 — "violent men shall afflict them" — Israel as collective recipient; Psa 125:3 — "the scepter of wickedness shall not rest on the land allotted to the righteous, lest the righteous stretch out their hands to do wrong" — the righteous as recipients of the pressure of injustice's rule; (3) *Cosmic receipt*: Rev 18:5 — the whole earth as the recipient of Babylon's accumulated injustice.
