Mat 27:4 — the chief priests receive Judas's confession: "I have sinned by betraying innocent blood" — their response: "What is that to us? See to it yourself." This is the paradigm of rejected reception: the confession is heard but the recipient disengages. 1Sa 26:21 — Saul's confession received by David in the field — David's response confirms he received it: "Return, my son David" (Saul's words) implies a relational response to the confession. 2Sa 19:20 — Shimei's confession received by King David — the outcome is that David's response is affected by the confession (the king grants mercy).

**[CHAR-4]** E — The communal dimension of Jer 16:10 provides the clearest evidence of received/transmitted conscience suppression: "And when you tell this people all these words, and they *say* to you, 'Why has the Lord pronounced all this great evil against us? What is our iniquity?'" — the people's collective conscience suppression is a communally held condition, not merely individual. This suggests that conscience suppression can be received through communal formation: the entire community fails to recognise its sin together, implying a shared moral blindness that was formed across generations (Jer 16:11–13 context — "your fathers forsook me").

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes — the communal reception of the refusal pattern is evidenced. 2Ki 13:6 — "Israel did not depart from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, which he made Israel to sin, but walked in them" — the whole people receive and enact the refusal as a communal pattern. 2Ki 15:9 — "as his fathers had done" — each king receives the refusal-pattern from his fathers and adopts it as his own. The reception is not forced but constituted by the community's own walk: "walked in them" — they received the pattern and actively sustained it.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes. The communal reception of the habitual defection pattern is evidenced. 2Ki 17:7 — Israel's communal habitual sinning — the whole people receive and sustain the defection pattern as a community. Hos 10:9 — "from the days of Gibeah, you have sinned, O Israel; there they have *continued*" — the Gibeah-origin sinning has been received and continued across generations. Hos 8:11 — altars for sinning — the institutional sinning structures that the community has received and participated in. The reception is not necessarily conscious adoption but occurs through inhabiting the sinning institutions and patterns that prior generations have established.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Yes. The receiving dimension is present throughout the Kings corpus but described from the giving side. The community's reception is evidenced by the communal outcomes: 1Ki 14:22 — "Judah did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, and they provoked him to jealousy with their sins" — Judah has received and enacted the transmitted sinning direction. 1Ki 22:52 — Ahaziah received the sinning direction from his father, mother, and Jeroboam — the most explicit multi-source reception in the corpus. 2Ki 17:21 — "made them commit great sin" — the community has received and committed the transmitted sin. Exo 23:33 — the anticipated reception through the snare mechanism — the community will receive the foreign nations' sinning direction if the boundary is not maintained.

**[CHAR-8]** E — Yes — the governing authority receives the revolt as a relational rupture. Israel receives Moab's revolt (2Ki 1:1; 3:5/7 — Jehoram receives the revolt as the named occasion for military response). Judah receives Edom's revolt (2Ki 8:20/22; 2Ch 21:8/10). The house of David receives Israel's revolt (1Ki 12:19; 2Ch 10:19). The receiving party is the governing authority that suffers the breaking of submission.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Yes. The receiving dimension is evidenced through the targets of sinful speech. Act 6:11 — Stephen receives the false blasphemous witness — the sinful speech is directed at him as its target. Rev 2:9 — the community of Smyrna receives the slander of those who falsely claim to be Jews — they are named as the recipients of the sinful speech against them ("the slander of those who say..."). Mat 26:65 / Mar 14:64 — Jesus receives the blasphemy-charge as the accused — he is the named recipient of the religious authorities' sinful speech verdict.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes. The evidence shows the characteristic being received through alliance and counsel. Psa 1:1 (VCG-04): walking in the counsel of the wicked, standing in the way of sinners, sitting in the seat of scoffers — three progressively deeper stages of receiving the wicked orientation through social alignment. Exo 23:1 (VCG-04): "join hands with a wicked man to be a malicious witness" — active voluntary reception through alliance. Num 16:26 (VCG-04): the community warned against proximity that would result in being "swept away with all their sins" — passive reception through dangerous proximity. 2Ch 19:2 (VCG-03): Jehoshaphat "helped the wicked" and thereby drew divine wrath — receiving a relational alignment with wickedness brings consequences even without fully adopting the characteristic.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes. The characteristic is received through: (1) association — 2Jo 11 (vc=14453 — VCG-04): merely greeting the wicked person makes one "a participant in his wicked works" — the characteristic is received through voluntary relational association; (2) false teaching — 2Ti 3:13 (vc=14451 — VCG-06): "deceiving and being deceived" — the characteristic's influence spreads through the deception of false teaching; (3) social alignment — Mat 12:45 (vc=65879 — VCG-06): the evil generation mirrors the spirit-filling pattern, showing collective reception of increasing evil; (4) community saturation — 1Cor 5:6-8 context (vc=14363/14412 — VCG-05): the old leaven's spread through the community shows the characteristic being received by those around the constitutionally evil person through communal contagion.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The characteristic is received primarily through: (1) communal saturation — Ezr 9:11 (vc=66005 — VCG-04): "the land that you are entering… is a land impure with the impurity of the peoples of the lands, with their abominations that have filled it" — the abominations of surrounding peoples are received communally through environmental saturation; (2) Eze 44:6-7 (vc=66001-66002 — VCG-04): Israel is addressed as a community that has received and accumulated abominations through its rebellious inner orientation and through admitting the uncircumcised in heart; (3) the Babylon figure (Rev 17:5 — vc=65878 — VCG-05): as "mother of earth's abominations" — abomination is actively generated and communicated to others through her influence. The primary reception mode is communal-environmental rather than individual-relational.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes. Reception occurs primarily through social-relational channels. (1) Cultural-educational reception: Deu 20:18 (vc=65932 — VCG-02): abominable practices received through being "taught" by idolatrous nations; Deu 18:9 (vc=65931 — VCG-02): the warning against "learning to follow the abominable practices of those nations" implies that learning is the primary reception mechanism. (2) Relational-marital reception: 1Ki 11:5 (vc=65898 — VCG-03): Solomon's wives drew him after their gods — idolatrous attachment received through intimate relational influence. (3) Social-environmental reception: Ezr 9:1 (vc=65949 — VCG-03): the community's failure to separate from peoples with abominations results in the characteristic permeating their communal life.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes. Reception occurs through social channels. Associational: Job 34:8 (vc=38214 — VCG-04): "who travels in company with evildoers and walks with wicked men" — chosen proximity to evildoers is the reception channel; the inner person is shaped by sustained companionship with those who work iniquity. Appetitive: Pro 17:4 (vc=38219 — VCG-03): "an evildoer listens to wicked lips" — the inner reception of harmful speech as a preferred input. Communal-embedded: Psa 55:10 (vc=38239 — VCG-01): "iniquity and trouble are within it" (the city) — iniquity is embedded in communal structures from which individual persons receive it through inhabiting the community. Psa 141:4 (vc=38230 — VCG-04): "do not let my heart incline to any evil, to busy myself with wicked deeds in company with men who work iniquity" — the prayer shows the reception risk through associational influence.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes. The reception of evil speech is directly documented in VCG-02 and VCG-03. 1Cor 4:13 (vc=14351 — VCG-02): "when slandered, we entreat" — the apostle receives slander from others; the slandering speech comes to him. 1Pe 2:12 (vc=14377 — VCG-03): believers receive false accusation as evildoers from opponents. 1Pe 3:16 (vc=14380 — VCG-03): "when you are slandered, those who revile your good behavior in Christ may be put to shame" — the slander is received. 1Pe 4:15 (vc=14381 — VCG-03): the instruction not to suffer as an evildoer implies some are suffering from accusations. The reception of the characteristic is the experience of the falsely accused target.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All six characteristics evidence reception mechanisms. The most extensively documented reception mechanisms across the cluster: (a) cultural-educational transmission (Chars 4 and 1 — Deu 20:18 nations teaching abominable practices; Psa 1:1 walking in the counsel of the wicked); (b) relational-associational formation (Chars 1 and 5 — Job 34:8 traveling with evildoers shapes inner character); (c) environmental saturation (Char 4 — Ezr 9:1 — peoples with abominations defiling shared social space; Char 5 — Psa 55:10 — iniquity and trouble within the city); (d) institutional authority imposing evil patterns (Char 4 VCG-03; Char 5 — Isa 10:1 iniquitous decrees). Char 6's reception mechanism is unique: the false accusation received by the innocent (1Pe 2:12; 3:16) is not self-chosen but imposed — VCG-03 is the only register where the characteristic is received without the recipient's choice.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes — secondary defilement reception is extensively documented. The contact-chain in M10c-A-VCG-06 (Lev 15:5-11) shows a person receiving defilement from contact with the discharge-person's bed, objects, body. Num 19:22 (M10c-A-VCG-07) — "whatever the unclean person touches shall be unclean, and anyone who touches it shall be unclean until evening" — shows cascading reception through a contact chain. The receiving person typically does not choose to receive the condition; it arrives through the contact event. The reception is bodily-mechanical: the contact creates the condition in the receiving person regardless of their intention.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes, through the conscience-formative pathway. 1Cor 8:7 (VCG-03): "through former association with idols, eat food as really offered to an idol, and their conscience, being weak, is defiled" — the defiled conscience results from prior association with a defiling community. The person received a moral-conscience formation through the association, producing the vulnerability that enables the conscience to be defiled. This is reception of the characteristic through formative immersion in a defiling context.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes. Gen 34:5 (VCG-01): Dinah receives defilement through Shechem's violent sexual act — the defilement is imposed on her through another's will. Eze 23:17 (VCG-02): "they defiled her with their whoring lust" — the community receives defilement through corrupting external relational engagement. Num 5:13/14 (VCG-01): the wife potentially receives the defilement through another man's act — the ordeal law assumes that a third party's act can produce the defilement-state in the woman.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes — from a spiritual agent. The unclean spirit enters and inhabits the person: Mar 1:23 (VCG-01) — "a man with an unclean spirit" — the spirit is present in the person as an inhabiting agent. Mar 5:2 (VCG-01) — the possession is the man's condition prior to the encounter with Jesus. The characteristic is received from the external spiritual agent rather than from a human person.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All four characteristics show reception, but from different sources. Characteristic 1: secondary defilement reception through the contact chain — the person receives defilement from contact with the defiling person's bed, objects, or body (Lev 15:5-11 VCG-06; Num 19:22 VCG-07 — cascading reception). The mechanism is bodily-mechanical; the receiving person does not choose to receive it. Characteristic 2: received through formative immersion — "former association with idols" (1Cor 8:7 VCG-03) shapes the conscience toward susceptibility; the receiving is through sustained environmental formation rather than direct contact. Characteristic 3: received through violation (Gen 34 — Dinah receives defilement through Shechem's act; Eze 23:17 — the community receives through corrupting external alliance) and through the mechanism of being drawn into a defiling corporate moral environment. Characteristic 4: received exclusively from a spiritual agent — the unclean spirit enters and inhabits the person; the reception is from an external spiritual being rather than from a human person. The cluster pattern: three characteristics show human-source reception (bodily, formative, violative); Characteristic 4 shows spiritual-agent reception alone.

questions.question_text: What inner conditions accompany or block uptake of the characteristic from another person?

findings.session_b_note:
The data addresses this primarily in the context of divine forgiveness, less so horizontal reception:

**Enabling conditions (divine forgiveness):** The access-postures already named (T1.7 Prompt 1): repentance, faith, confession, calling upon God. These enable reception by orienting the inner person toward the source.

**Blocking conditions (divine forgiveness):** T1.7 Prompt 2 — religious misunderstanding (scribes, Mar 2:7), volitional refusal, structural incoherence (receiving formally without inner transformation), the outer limit (Spirit-rejection, Mar 3:29).

**Enabling/blocking conditions (horizontal):** The data is partial here. Luk 17:3-4 names repentance as the condition the offender must meet — the offended party is commanded to forgive *if* the offender repents. Whether the inner condition of the *receiver* (the one who has wronged and is being forgiven) is addressed in the data is not clear. The inner-being state of the person receiving horizontal forgiveness is not named explicitly.

*Gap noted:* The inner-being experience and conditions of the person receiving horizontal forgiveness from another person is a genuine gap in the data. The data is rich on giving and on receiving from God; it is less attentive to the phenomenology of receiving forgiveness from a fellow human.

findings.session_b_note:
**Enabling conditions (partial):** The eleeinos evidence (Rev 3:17) establishes that the capacity to recognise one's own pitiable condition is necessary for reception. Without this recognition, compassion cannot reach the person who needs it. Need-recognition is therefore the primary enabling condition for reception — the inner openness that comes from knowing one is in need.

The supplication posture — earnest appeal (techinah, tahanun) — implies that active seeking of compassion is an enabling inner condition. The person who cries out positions themselves to receive.

**Blocking conditions:** Self-sufficiency and prosperity-blindness (the Laodicean pattern) block reception by preventing need-recognition. The person who believes they need nothing cannot open to what is being extended toward them.

**What is missing (P):** Reception of compassion specifically from another human person (rather than from God) is not addressed in terms of its enabling and blocking conditions. The human-to-human reception dynamics are entirely silent in the data. This is a significant gap; no SD pointer addresses it.

- **Openness to proclamation:** The person who hears the proclamation of 1Jo 1:3 must be inwardly open to receive it — though the data does not specify what enables this openness precisely.
- **Fear of God:** Psa 119:63 — the fear-of-God orientation makes the person receptive to righteous fellowship from those who share it.
- **Humility to receive support:** Ecc 4:10 — the ability to be lifted up presupposes not claiming self-sufficiency. The fallen companion receives precisely because they are genuinely fallen and unable to lift themselves.

**Blocking conditions:**
- **Moral incompatibility:** 2Cor 6:14 — the person oriented toward lawlessness cannot receive righteous fellowship without a fundamental orientation change.
- **Idolatrous bonding:** Hos 4:17 — the person already joined to idols is in a condition that blocks genuine vertical fellowship reception.

**Gap:** The data does not specifically address what happens when the person is offered fellowship and refuses it — the conditions of active refusal rather than incapacity.

findings.session_b_note: The data provides a distinction. True reception: 1Jo 4:19 — responsive love flows; the person who receives divine love loves in return. Psa 127:2 (OBS-103-084) — the beloved sleeps — reception produces rest and effortlessness. Jer 31:14 (OBS-103-081) — the soul is satisfied. Non-reception: Joh 3:19 (OBS-103-147) — those who encounter light-love do not receive it because their inner love-commitment runs the other way. The distinguishing feature: genuine reception of love produces love in return (1Jo 4:19) and produces rest/satisfaction (Psa 127:2). Non-reception while encountering: the person continues in the disordered love that blocked reception, unchanged and satisfied with it. The test of reception is: does love-received produce love-outward and rest-inward? If so, reception is genuine. If the person encounters the love-offer but remains oriented toward a rival love-object, reception has not occurred.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-103-004: Love's relational architecture is structured by three directional axes — GOD → HUMAN, HUMAN → GOD, HUMAN → HUMAN — with divine love structurally prior and causally generative of all subsequent love. 1…
findings.finding_value: Love's relational architecture is structured by three directional axes — GOD → HUMAN, HUMAN → GOD, HUMAN → HUMAN — with divine love structurally prior and causally generative of all subsequent love. 1Jo 4:19 ('we love because he first loved us') is the axis-precedence statement: the first axis is not responsive to but constitutive of the second and third. The GOD → HUMAN direction moves through four mechanisms: covenantal declaration (naming the beloved — Jer 12:7, Mat 3:17), Spirit-infusion (Rom 5:5), redemptive acts (Joh 3:16), and covenantal covering (Eze 16:8). The HUMAN → GOD direction requires total inner mobilisation (Mat 22:37 — all heart, soul, mind) and the clearing of rival loves as its condition (1Jo 4:19, 1Ti 6:10). The HUMAN → HUMAN direction spans five structural types (neighbour, enemy, community, friendship, family) and creates the social architecture described in Q&A-088 (restructured kinship, public legibility, competitive generosity). The most significant finding in T4: the human-to-God direction is conditioned by prior reception of divine love — the capacity for human love toward God is itself a gift. The one structural gap: T4.6 (spiritual beings) is absent from the evidence.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-012: The faculty engagement pattern in T3 is produced by and oriented toward the relational interfaces in T4. Love's identity-faculty (T3.10) is constituted through the relational interface: being-loved by…
findings.finding_value: The faculty engagement pattern in T3 is produced by and oriented toward the relational interfaces in T4. Love's identity-faculty (T3.10) is constituted through the relational interface: being-loved by God (GOD→HUMAN axis) establishes the identity of agapētos; what-one-loves (active direction) establishes identity through the chosen object. The relational capacity faculty (T3.11) is the faculty through which the three relational axes are exercised: the GOD→HUMAN axis engages the relational capacity as receiver; the HUMAN→GOD axis engages it as giver; the HUMAN→HUMAN axis engages it in both directions simultaneously. Memory (T3.3) sustains the relational interface: love toward God is sustained through remembering his chesed (Jer 31:20); love in community is sustained through shared history. Moral sensitivity (T3.8) is calibrated by the relational interface structure: love-of-God calibrates the moral perception of what is evil (Psa 97:10); love-of-neighbour calibrates the perception of what is just. The deepest inter-tier finding: the faculty engagement pattern is not incidental — it is precisely the faculty configuration required by the relational architecture. The relational structure generates the faculty requirements.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-004: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion…
findings.finding_value: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion on whom I have compassion"), covenantally grounded (chesed as the bond-loyalty that grounds the characteristic), and situationally responsive (splanchnizō — triggered by the specific sight of suffering). These three bases are not in tension but in integration: divine compassion is free, covenanted, and responsive simultaneously. The scope finding is among the most analytically significant in the registry: compassion explicitly and repeatedly crosses covenantal boundaries (Nineveh, the Samaritan/Jew axis, the power-asymmetric relationship). Scope is defined by perceived need, not moral standing or covenantal membership — this is formally confirmed in the data and distinguishes compassion from many other relational characteristics. The chesed/splanchnizō distinction maps onto distinct relational registers: chesed sustains within established bonds; splanchnizō extends across distance and difference. T4.4 (receiver's inner-being experience) is the most significant gap — four P-rated prompts, entirely absent from the data. T4.6 (spiritual beings interface) is entirely silent across all four prompts.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-004: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — a…
findings.finding_value: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — all God-as-subject). The basis of divine extension is the giver's character and prior knowing (Exo 33:17 — "I know you by name"), not the receiver's merit — neither merit-based nor arbitrary. The human-to-God direction is specifically supplication: tachanum (H8469) is the receiving side's corresponding vocabulary built into the same root family as the giving side (chen/chanan) — the vocabulary embeds the two-directional circuit in a single root. The human-giving direction extends grace horizontally through three modes: forgiving (charizō — Eph 4:32), gracious conduct (chen as character quality — 889-003), and gracious speech (SD022). The receiving direction is the most underexamined (T4.4 — P-rated throughout); the scope analysis (T4.5) reveals grace crossing covenantal and social boundaries (Ruth narrative — grace in the context of foreign status and vulnerability). T4.6 (spiritual beings) is evidenced at one point: Luk 1:28 (kecharitōmenē — the angel's announcement), which implies angelic ministry as a vehicle of grace rather than grace operating independently in the spiritual-beings register. T4 synthesis: the relational architecture of grace is unique in the programme — it is the only characteristic where the giving-side vocabulary and the receiving-side vocabulary are built from the same root (chen/tachanum), encoding the grace-circuit's two-sidedness at the lexical level.

findings.session_b_note: Enabling conditions for reception (drawn from Q&A-031 and the anchor verse pattern): (1) Covenant participation: being within the relational structure that God's giving constitutes. The land-giving texts presuppose covenant membership as the reception condition. (2) Presented inner need: compassionate giving is triggered by visible inner suffering (Leah's condition, Gen 29:33) — the authentic expression of need enables responsive reception. (3) Posture of mourning/depletion: the eschatological giving is addressed to "those who mourn in Zion" (Isa 61:3) — the state of acknowledged need and depleted inner life. Blocking conditions: (1) Idolatrous misattribution — receiving the gift but attributing it to Baal (Hos 2:8, Q&A-032) blocks genuine reception even when the material gift arrives. (2) Covenant violation — faithlessness inverts giving-to into giving-over (Q&A-032), removing the receptive condition. (3) Refusal to give ear — Neh 9:30 — the rejection of prophetic warning closes the channel of Spirit-mediated reception.

findings.finding_value: Reception of reverential fear through instruction is enabled by: openness of will (Deu 31:12-13 implies that gathering and hearing are necessary — the person must present themselves); not yet having competing allegiances (2Ki 17 corpus shows that syncretistic prior allegiances block genuine reception of fear-of-God). Reception is blocked by: divided heart (Psa 86:11), hardened heart (Isa 63:17), and prior commitment to other fear-objects (2Ki 17:33 — fearing the Lord and serving other gods simultaneously, which prevents genuine reception).

**[CHAR-1]** E — Enabling reception: (1) volitional openness to the wicked person's counsel — Psa 1:1 implies a sequence of increasing receptivity ("walks," "stands," "sits") that can be blocked at each stage; (2) the weakening of God-fear that would otherwise constitute resistance; (3) the attraction of the wicked person's apparent prosperity (Job 21:7 — VCG-10 — why do the wicked thrive? — this appearance of success is a reception-enabling attraction). Blocking reception: (1) active moral separation — Psa 26:5 (VCG-03): "I hate the assembly of evildoers and will not sit with the wicked" — deliberate relational separation; (2) maintained fear of God (the God-fear that is absent in the wicked person — Psa 36:1 — blocks reception of their orientation when present); (3) physical distancing — Num 16:26 (VCG-04): "depart from the tents of these wicked men."

**[CHAR-2]** E — Enabling reception: (1) voluntary relational alignment — 2Jo 11 (vc=14453 — VCG-04): greeting (choosing relationship with) the evil person; (2) unoccupied inner space — Mat 12:45 (vc=65879 — VCG-06): the swept and empty inner space invites reoccupation by more evil; (3) absence of the word of God abiding — 1Jo 2:14 (vc=14430 — VCG-01): the word abiding in a person is the primary blocking condition. Blocking reception: (1) the word of God abiding within (1Jo 2:14 — VCG-01), (2) faith as a shield (Eph 6:16 — vc=14428 — VCG-01: faith extinguishing the evil one's darts), (3) active moral separation — 1Cor 5:13 (vc=14465 — VCG-04): the community expels the evil person to prevent further spread.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Enabling conditions for receiving abomination: (1) the absence of conscience-based resistance — when the conscience is silenced (Jer 6:15; 8:12 — VCG-04), there is no inner faculty to resist incoming abominable influences; (2) the absence of discernment — Isa 44:19 (vc=65961 — VCG-05): no consideration, knowledge, or discernment enables reception of abomination without recognition; (3) the uncircumcised heart — Eze 44:7 (vc=66002 — VCG-04): admitting those uncircumcised in heart to sacred space shows that inner uncircumcision (non-responsiveness to God) enables the reception and embedding of abomination in communal space. Blocking conditions: a functional conscience (Eze 9:4 — VCG-04: those who sigh and groan — their conscience is the inner shield that prevents reception of the abomination).

**[CHAR-4]** E — Enabling reception: (1) coveting what is on the idols (Deu 7:25 — vc=1682 — VCG-02: "lest you be ensnared by it") — the inner covetousness is the vulnerability that enables reception; (2) failure of active separation (Deu 18:9 — VCG-02: learning rather than refusing); (3) intimate relational entanglement (1Ki 11:5 — VCG-03: wives drawing the heart). Blocking reception: (1) the immediate destruction of idol-objects (Deu 7:25 — VCG-02: "burn with fire") — removing the attractive object prevents the eye-feast-loop from starting; (2) maintained covenant separation (Ezr 9:1/14 — VCG-03 — the failure to do this enabled reception); (3) not coveting — the volitional act of not desiring what is on the idols is the primary inner blocking condition.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Enabling reception: (1) the heart's susceptibility to incline — Psa 141:4 (vc=38230 — VCG-04): the heart's capacity for inclination toward evil is the vulnerability that enables associational reception; (2) inner appetite for harmful input — Pro 17:4 (VCG-03): the evildoer listens to wicked lips — an already-present appetite that receives iniquity eagerly; (3) absence of the divine hearing — Job 36:10 (VCG-04): the closed ear to instruction leaves the person receptive to the wrong influencing voices. Blocking reception: (1) steady steps according to divine promise — Psa 119:133 (VCG-04): the blocking condition for iniquity's dominion; (2) active volitional distancing — Job 11:14 (VCG-04): "put it far away" — removing the characteristic from the hand blocks further accumulation; (3) maintained covenant loyalty — Deu 28:20 (VCG-05): the evil of deeds flows from forsaking God; sustained covenant attachment blocks reception.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The characteristic as received (false accusation, slander) is not blocked by inner conditions in the sense of preventing the speech from being directed at the person — it can be directed regardless of the recipient's inner state. What the evidence addresses is the response-conditions: 1Pe 3:16 (vc=14380 — VCG-03): "having a good conscience" — the inner condition of good conscience enables the person to receive the slander without being undone by it; 1Cor 4:13 (vc=14351 — VCG-02): the apostle's inner posture of non-retaliation (entreat rather than counter-blast) is what enables dignified reception. The inner condition that blocks the characteristic from damaging the recipient is good conscience combined with honourable conduct (1Pe 2:12 — VCG-03) — not blocking the speech itself but blocking its power to destroy.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster reveals a consistent blocking profile across all six characteristics: (a) functioning conscience as the primary internal block against receiving M10b evil (all six); (b) maintained covenant fidelity and active separation from evil-practitioners (Chars 1 and 4 — Deu 18:9 — "not learning to follow abominable practices"; Psa 1:1 — "not walking in the counsel of the wicked"); (c) instructed openness to divine word (Char 5 — Job 36:10 — open ear to instruction blocks return to iniquity); (d) good conscience maintained under pressure (Char 6 — 1Pe 3:16). Enabling reception: suppressed conscience, chosen proximity to evil-practitioners, and the characteristic's specific visual/auditory/relational entry mechanisms (Char 4 — eye-feasting; Char 5 — ear attuned to wicked lips — Pro 17:4; Char 6 — authority-rejection).

**[CHAR-1]** E — Reception is primarily mechanistic, not inner-condition-dependent: touching a defiling surface defiles regardless of the person's inner orientation. However, two inner conditions affect the outcome: (1) knowledge and vigilance: a person who knows which surfaces and persons are defiling and who maintains appropriate watchfulness can prevent reception through avoidance (Lev 11:43-44 principle, M10c-A-VCG-04); (2) hand-washing: Lev 15:11 (M10c-A-VCG-06) shows that the discharge-person could have washed their hands before touching the clean person, preventing transmission — the clean person's reception is blocked by the defiling person's prior action, not by the clean person's own inner state.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Enabling reception: a weakened or unformed conscience (1Cor 8:7 — "weak" conscience); long-term immersion in a defiling community; absence of the blocking posture of active separation (2Cor 6:17). Blocking reception: the strong/formed conscience that holds to genuine moral conviction without being overridden (1Cor 8:7 — those with "knowledge" eat without defiling their conscience); active separation from defiling environments (2Cor 6:17 — "go out from their midst"); purification practice (2Cor 7:1 — "let us cleanse ourselves").

**[CHAR-3]** E — Enabling reception: willingness to be drawn into corrupting alliances (Eze 23:17 — the community's turning toward the Babylonians); absence of the inner boundaries of covenantal commitment. Blocking reception: Nazirite consecration (Num 6:7 VCG-05 — the will's commitment to God overrides even natural kinship bonds, preventing defilement even from proximity to family death); priestly purity commitment (Eze 44:25 VCG-03 — priests guard against corpse-contact defilement); maintained covenantal fidelity (Eze 18:6/15 VCG-01 — the righteous man consistently "does not defile his neighbor's wife" across generations).

**[CHAR-4]** S — The 21-verse corpus does not evidence specific inner conditions that enable or block reception. The characteristic appears to be imposed regardless of the person's inner condition — a child is possessed (Mar 7:25/Luk 9:42), suggesting the condition does not depend on the person's volitional or moral state.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's reception-enabling and blocking conditions reveal the structural division between self-generated and externally-imposed characteristics. Characteristics 1, 2, and 3 each have inner conditions that enable or block reception; Characteristic 4 does not. Characteristic 1: reception blocked by knowledge and vigilance (Lev 11:43-44 — avoidance discipline) and by the defiling person's prior hand-washing (Lev 15:11); enabled by ignorance and negligence. Characteristic 2: reception blocked by strong/formed conscience (1Cor 8:7 — those with genuine conviction eat without defiling) and active separation (2Cor 6:17); enabled by weak conscience, long-term immersion, and absence of the blocking posture. Characteristic 3: reception blocked by Nazirite consecration (Num 6:7 — dedication overriding natural kinship impulse), active covenantal fidelity (Eze 18:6/15), and priestly discernment guardianship (Eze 44:25); enabled by willingness to be drawn into corrupting alliances and absence of covenantal commitment. Characteristic 4: the 21-verse corpus does not evidence specific inner conditions enabling or blocking reception — a child is possessed (Mar 7:25), suggesting the condition does not depend on the person's volitional or moral state. The cluster's insight: inner conditions govern reception in the three person-generated characteristics; the externally-imposed characteristic has no inner-condition-dependence.

questions.question_text: What is the inner-being state of the person who meets the characteristic from another but does not take it up?

findings.session_b_note:
The data addresses one case directly (already named at T1.7 P3) and implies others:

**The self-deceived (Rev 3:17):** The Laodiceans encounter the implicit compassion of the divine warning (Rev 3:17-20 — Jesus standing at the door, knocking) but cannot receive it because they cannot perceive their own pitiable condition. Their inner-being state is one of self-enclosed sufficiency — the door is closed from the inside (v.20 — "I will come in to him... if anyone hears my voice and opens the door"). The person who does not receive compassion in this mode remains in their actual condition of destitution while believing themselves rich.

**The hardened (implied by judicial non-pity):** The person whose inner orientation has been set toward judgment — whose eye has been trained not to pity — may encounter compassion from another and be unable to receive it because their inner constitution is oriented against it. This is speculative from the data and should be flagged as interpretation.

**What is missing (P):** The data does not describe the inner state of a person who encounters human compassion but cannot or will not receive it — who is in genuine need but closed against the compassion being extended. The inner experience of that closure is entirely absent from the data. This is a significant gap; no SD pointer addresses it.

findings.session_b_note: The verse evidence addresses non-reception primarily in the divine-to-human direction. Jer 6:16 ("we will not walk in it") is the clearest picture: the inner state is one of offered-and-refused goodness — active resistance of what is genuinely good. The will has been engaged and has chosen refusal. The person's inner state is: morally informed (they have encountered the good way), volitionally closed (they have refused it), and unaware of the full consequence of their refusal. For the human-to-human non-reception context specifically: the data is silent on the inner state of a person who encounters human goodness and refuses it. The Haman narrative (Est 5:9) names the inner state of the person who misidentifies goodness — but this is self-deception rather than active refusal of another's goodness. This is a partial gap. (OBS-067-OBS-040, OBS-067-OBS-043)

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-004: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion…
findings.finding_value: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion on whom I have compassion"), covenantally grounded (chesed as the bond-loyalty that grounds the characteristic), and situationally responsive (splanchnizō — triggered by the specific sight of suffering). These three bases are not in tension but in integration: divine compassion is free, covenanted, and responsive simultaneously. The scope finding is among the most analytically significant in the registry: compassion explicitly and repeatedly crosses covenantal boundaries (Nineveh, the Samaritan/Jew axis, the power-asymmetric relationship). Scope is defined by perceived need, not moral standing or covenantal membership — this is formally confirmed in the data and distinguishes compassion from many other relational characteristics. The chesed/splanchnizō distinction maps onto distinct relational registers: chesed sustains within established bonds; splanchnizō extends across distance and difference. T4.4 (receiver's inner-being experience) is the most significant gap — four P-rated prompts, entirely absent from the data. T4.6 (spiritual beings interface) is entirely silent across all four prompts.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-004: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — a…
findings.finding_value: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — all God-as-subject). The basis of divine extension is the giver's character and prior knowing (Exo 33:17 — "I know you by name"), not the receiver's merit — neither merit-based nor arbitrary. The human-to-God direction is specifically supplication: tachanum (H8469) is the receiving side's corresponding vocabulary built into the same root family as the giving side (chen/chanan) — the vocabulary embeds the two-directional circuit in a single root. The human-giving direction extends grace horizontally through three modes: forgiving (charizō — Eph 4:32), gracious conduct (chen as character quality — 889-003), and gracious speech (SD022). The receiving direction is the most underexamined (T4.4 — P-rated throughout); the scope analysis (T4.5) reveals grace crossing covenantal and social boundaries (Ruth narrative — grace in the context of foreign status and vulnerability). T4.6 (spiritual beings) is evidenced at one point: Luk 1:28 (kecharitōmenē — the angel's announcement), which implies angelic ministry as a vehicle of grace rather than grace operating independently in the spiritual-beings register. T4 synthesis: the relational architecture of grace is unique in the programme — it is the only characteristic where the giving-side vocabulary and the receiving-side vocabulary are built from the same root (chen/tachanum), encoding the grace-circuit's two-sidedness at the lexical level.

findings.session_b_note: The person who encounters peace and does not receive it is in the refusal pattern documented at Isa 30:15 and Jer 6:16. Their inner state: (1) Continuing inner restlessness — they do not find the rest they were offered; (2) Moral hardness — stubbornness persists as the inner posture (Isa 30:15 — "but you were unwilling"); (3) Compounding peacelessness — the refusal of offered peace does not leave the person where they were; the sword reaches their life (Jer 4:10) even after the prophetic promise of peace was extended. The inner-being consequence of refusing offered peace: the condition deteriorates rather than remaining static. This is theologically significant — peace refused is not neutral; it worsens the peaceless condition. The person who encounters peace from another and rejects it is not unaffected by the encounter.

findings.session_b_note: Two instances are evidenced. (1) Idolatrous misattribution (Hos 2:8): Israel receives God's grain, wine, and oil but attributes them to Baal. The inner-being state is one of deceived giving-orientation — the person gives to wrong objects (Baal) while receiving from the right source (God). The misattribution creates a split inner-being state: receiving God's gifts while refusing God as their giver. (2) Refusal to give ear (Neh 9:30): the prophetic warning-giving is addressed but not received. The inner-being state is one of closed reception — the faculty of hearing is present but the volitional-moral integration required for genuine reception is absent. (3) Jer 13:16 (Q&A-033): the person who encounters the command to give glory but does not give it experiences darkness, stumbling, gloom — inner-being disorder as the consequence of non-reception.
