Eze 9:4 (vc=1698 — VCG-04) involves the angel instructed by the Lord to mark the grieving — angelic agency is present in the marking of those whose conscience recoils from abomination, but the angelic role is responsive to the divine-human moral situation rather than directly constituting the characteristic. The evidence does not show this characteristic as specifically mediated through or operating within angelic or adversarial spiritual agency in the same way VCG-01 in CHAR-2 evidenced the evil one.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes. The characteristic is fundamentally about allegiance to spiritual powers other than God. 1Ki 11:5 (vc=65898 — VCG-03): "Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians" and "Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites" — foreign deities are the specific spiritual powers to whom the devotion-capacity is attached. Deu 32:16 (vc=65938 — VCG-02): "strange gods" — the characteristic involves allegiance to spiritual powers explicitly named as alien to the covenant relationship. Eze 8:5-17 (VCG-05): the Ezekiel vision shows idolatrous worship of specific figures (a creeping idol — Eze 8:10 context, women weeping for Tammuz — Eze 8:14 context, sun-worship — Eze 8:16 context) — these are specific spiritual beings/powers receiving the misdirected devotion.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Zec 10:2 (vc=38251 — VCG-01) provides the clearest spiritual-beings evidence: "household gods utter nonsense, and the diviners see lies; they tell false dreams and give empty consolation" — the iniquity of false spiritual guidance (household gods, diviners) operates in the context of spiritual beings whose deceptive counsel generates trouble and wandering. The a.ven vocabulary here names the emptiness-and-trouble produced by these spiritual-being-mediated deceptions. 1Sa 15:23 (vc=38185 — VCG-02): "rebellion is as the sin of divination" — the comparison of presumptuous self-will to divination links the characteristic's inner dynamics (the will asserting itself above God) to the adversarial spiritual realm of divination.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes. Jude 8 (vc=14354 — VCG-01): "blaspheme the glorious ones" — the "glorious ones" (doxas) are likely angelic or heavenly beings; the blasphemy is directed at these spiritual beings. This shows the characteristic operating directly in relation to angelic/heavenly beings as its targets. Rev 13:6 (vc=14356 — VCG-01): "blaspheming his name and his dwelling, that is, those who dwell in heaven" — the heavenly inhabitants are included in the target of the beast's blasphemy; the characteristic extends to the entire heavenly community. Jude 10 (vc=14355 — VCG-01): "blaspheme all that they do not understand" — including things that are heavenly/spiritual, beyond rational comprehension.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Three characteristics show direct engagement with spiritual beings. Char 2 (VCG-01 — the "evil one" as the cosmic adversarial figure — Mat 13:19; 1Jo 5:19 — "the whole world lies in the power of the evil one"; Eph 6:12 — spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly places). Char 4 (the foreign deities as the objects of misdirected devotion — 1Ki 11:5 — Ashtoreth and Milcom named as abominations; the idol-objects and spiritual powers behind them). Char 6 (Jude 8 — blasphemy directed at "the glorious ones" — angelic or heavenly beings; Rev 13:6 — beast's blasphemy against those who dwell in heaven). Chars 1, 3, and 5 do not directly address spiritual beings as active participants in their characteristics (though Char 5's Zec 10:2 — household gods uttering nonsense — touches the adversarial spiritual framing).

**[CHAR-1]** S — The 133-verse corpus does not show the ritual defilement-state operating in relation to angelic or adversarial spiritual beings. The characteristic operates within the human-God-community triangle; spiritual beings are not actors within this characteristic's evidence base. The unclean-spirit register is Characteristic 4 (M10c-E sub-group), outside the 133-verse scope of Characteristic 1.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes, in the Revelation apocalyptic register. Rev 16:13 (VCG-04): "three unclean spirits like frogs" emerging from the dragon, the beast, and the false prophet — the moral-inner defilement-state is named as a property of spiritual beings sourced in cosmic evil. Rev 17:4 (VCG-04): the cup held by the woman "full of abominations and the impurities of her sexual immorality" — impurity as the defining inner-moral character of total cosmic corruption. Rev 18:2 (VCG-04): "a haunt for every unclean spirit" — the fallen city's defining character is the habitation of unclean spirits, beings whose inner character is moral-inner defilement. The characteristic is operative in adversarial spiritual beings as their defining inner-moral condition.

**[CHAR-3]** S — The 83-verse corpus does not explicitly name angelic or adversarial spiritual beings in relation to the corporate/covenantal defilement-state. The characteristic operates within the God-Israel-land-sanctuary triangle without naming other spiritual beings as actors.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes — constitutively. The characteristic is produced by the action of unclean spirits as spiritual beings. The spirits recognise the divine spiritual identity (Mar 3:11 — "You are the Son of God"), resist expulsion (Act 8:7 — crying out), seek re-entry (Mat 12:43/Luk 11:24 — "I will return to my house"), and are subject to divine authority (Mar 1:27 — "they obey him"). The spiritual beings interface is the defining feature of this characteristic.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster shows a 2 E : 2 S pattern on spiritual beings engagement. Characteristics 2 and 4 evidence spiritual beings engagement; Characteristics 1 and 3 do not. Characteristic 2 (E): the Revelation apocalyptic register (VCG-04) shows spiritual beings as bearers of the characteristic — Rev 16:13 ("three unclean spirits like frogs"), Rev 17:4 ("full of abominations and the impurities"), Rev 18:2 ("a haunt for every unclean spirit") — adversarial spiritual beings are defined by moral-inner defilement as their essential character. Characteristic 4 (E): the entire characteristic is constituted by the action of unclean spirits — they recognise divine identity (Mar 3:11), resist expulsion (Act 8:7), seek re-entry (Mat 12:43/Luk 11:24), and are subject to divine authority (Mar 1:27 — "they obey him"). The spiritual beings interface is the defining feature of Characteristic 4. Characteristics 1 and 3 are silent on spiritual beings — they operate in the human-God-community triangle without spiritual beings as actors.

questions.question_text: Is the characteristic a site of adversarial activity — something that can be attacked, distorted, or weaponised by adversarial powers — as the evidence shows?

findings.session_b_note:
The evidence implies adversarial weaponisation of the fellowship-joining capacity, though the data does not state this explicitly.

The idolatrous joining mode (Hos 4:17 — *Ephraim is joined to idols*) and the occult-charming mode (groups 7565-002, 7569-001, 7569-002) together suggest that the joining/fellowship capacity can be captured and misdirected: the person's constitutional joining-capacity is engaged, but directed toward wrong spiritual objects (idols, occult powers) rather than toward God.

**New finding:** Fellowship's joining capacity may be structurally the most vulnerable faculty to adversarial misdirection, precisely because it is the constitutional capacity through which the human person connects most deeply to any reality. The same faculty that enables participation in divine nature (2Pe 1:4) can be engaged to produce joining to idols (Hos 4:17) and spiritual bondage. This vulnerability is implicit in the data but not assembled as a finding.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-004: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion…
findings.finding_value: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion on whom I have compassion"), covenantally grounded (chesed as the bond-loyalty that grounds the characteristic), and situationally responsive (splanchnizō — triggered by the specific sight of suffering). These three bases are not in tension but in integration: divine compassion is free, covenanted, and responsive simultaneously. The scope finding is among the most analytically significant in the registry: compassion explicitly and repeatedly crosses covenantal boundaries (Nineveh, the Samaritan/Jew axis, the power-asymmetric relationship). Scope is defined by perceived need, not moral standing or covenantal membership — this is formally confirmed in the data and distinguishes compassion from many other relational characteristics. The chesed/splanchnizō distinction maps onto distinct relational registers: chesed sustains within established bonds; splanchnizō extends across distance and difference. T4.4 (receiver's inner-being experience) is the most significant gap — four P-rated prompts, entirely absent from the data. T4.6 (spiritual beings interface) is entirely silent across all four prompts.

findings.finding_value: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — all God-as-subject). The basis of divine extension is the giver's character and prior knowing (Exo 33:17 — "I know you by name"), not the receiver's merit — neither merit-based nor arbitrary. The human-to-God direction is specifically supplication: tachanum (H8469) is the receiving side's corresponding vocabulary built into the same root family as the giving side (chen/chanan) — the vocabulary embeds the two-directional circuit in a single root. The human-giving direction extends grace horizontally through three modes: forgiving (charizō — Eph 4:32), gracious conduct (chen as character quality — 889-003), and gracious speech (SD022). The receiving direction is the most underexamined (T4.4 — P-rated throughout); the scope analysis (T4.5) reveals grace crossing covenantal and social boundaries (Ruth narrative — grace in the context of foreign status and vulnerability). T4.6 (spiritual beings) is evidenced at one point: Luk 1:28 (kecharitōmenē — the angel's announcement), which implies angelic ministry as a vehicle of grace rather than grace operating independently in the spiritual-beings register. T4 synthesis: the relational architecture of grace is unique in the programme — it is the only characteristic where the giving-side vocabulary and the receiving-side vocabulary are built from the same root (chen/tachanum), encoding the grace-circuit's two-sidedness at the lexical level.

Submission (CHAR-2): 2Cor10:5 — "arguments and every lofty opinion raised against the knowledge of God" — framed in battle-language (destroying strongholds, taking thoughts captive), suggesting a warfare dimension around the cognitive-volitional site of submission. The four remaining characteristics (CHAR-3, CHAR-4, CHAR-5, CHAR-6) are silent on adversarial activity in their verse corpora. Cluster-level: the cluster's primary adversarial vulnerability is at CHAR-1 (the characteristic most susceptible to performance-distortion incorporating spiritual false elements) and CHAR-2 (most susceptible to cognitive-intellectual resistance). The cluster is not primarily a spiritual-warfare cluster — its spiritual engagement is through conscience, will, and divine-human relation rather than through named adversarial powers.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes. The corpus evidences adversarial activity in the temptation/trap structure. Neh 6:13 — enemies construct a scenario specifically designed to cause Nehemiah to sin: "for this purpose he was hired, that I should be afraid and act in this way and sin." The trap is externally constructed adversarial pressure aimed at producing sinning. Gen 20:6 — God's restraint of Abimelech from sinning implies that without divine intervention the sinning would have occurred — adversarial conditions are assumed as the default. The temptation that Joseph resists (Gen 39:9) is presented as a persistent assault ("she spoke to Joseph day after day" — context). The characteristic is a site where adversarial forces seek to provoke and produce sinning.

**[CHAR-10]** E — Implied for enticement. Jam 1:14 is set in a broader context (Jam 1:13 — "God cannot be tempted with evil, and he himself tempts no one") that excludes God from the temptation-source role, leaving the human desire as the internal mechanism. The broader NT context (though not in the 5-verse corpus) associates temptation with adversarial spiritual dynamics, but within this corpus the adversarial dimension is not named. 2Pe 2:14's false teachers as "accursed children" may imply their alignment with adversarial powers, but this is not explicit.

**[CHAR-11]** E — Yes. Act 26:18 — "from the power of Satan to God" — the condition positions the person within Satan's power-domain; the condition is not merely a neutral moral deficit but is situated within an adversarial spiritual power structure. Gal 1:4 — "deliver us from the present evil age" — the evil age has spiritual-adversarial dimensions that the condition is embedded in. The remedy (forgiveness and liberation) is framed as deliverance from this adversarial domain, confirming the condition's location within it.

**[CHAR-12]** E — Yes — most explicitly in CHAR-12 of all M10 characteristics so far. 1Jo 3:8 — "the devil has been sinning from the beginning. The reason the Son of God appeared was to destroy the works of the devil" — the enslaving power is grounded in the devil's originary sinning works; the Son of God's appearance is specifically to destroy those works. 1Jo 5:18 — "the evil one does not touch him" — the evil one is the agent seeking to re-establish the enslaving grip on the born-of-God person; Christ's protection specifically bars this adversarial touch. Sin's enslaving power is a primary site of adversarial spiritual activity.

**[CHAR-13]** S — The 205-verse corpus does not explicitly identify sin as divine record as a site of adversarial activity in the sense of the devil or evil one operating through or against the record. VCG-03's Job-surveillance passages (Job 10:6; 13:23; 14:16) address God's scrutiny of Job but do not name adversarial activity as a factor. The accusation function (Isa 59:12 — "our sins testify against us") is the record's own testimony, not named as adversarial mediation.

**[CHAR-14]** E — Implicitly, through Mar 3:29. The "blasphemy against the Holy Spirit" that constitutes the eternal sin blocking all forgiveness implies an adversarial spiritual orientation: the one who blasphemes the Spirit has aligned against the divine agent of conviction and renewal in a way that forecloses the forgiveness-seeking. The adversarial dimension is implied by the Spirit being the agent of conviction (Joh 16:8/9 in CHAR-11's corpus) whose work is resisted in the eternal sin; but the adversarial agency is not explicitly named in this corpus.

**[CHAR-15]** S — The corpus is silent on adversarial spiritual activity in connection with generational sin. The idolatry named in Eze 37:23 ("their idols and their detestable things") implies an adversarial spiritual dimension (idolatry involves false spiritual powers) but this is not explicitly named in the corpus.

**[CHAR-16]** S — The 64-verse corpus does not explicitly name adversarial spiritual agency in connection with the sinner-identity. Pro 1:10 — sinners entice — the enticing is human; no adversarial spiritual power is named. The characteristic is constitutively a human moral identity, not explicitly mediated by adversarial spiritual beings in this corpus.

**[CHAR-17]** S — The corpus is silent on adversarial spiritual agency in connection with guilt as inner-being state. The guilt-state operates within the human-God covenant relationship without named adversarial involvement.

**[CHAR-18]** S — The corpus is silent on adversarial spiritual agency in connection with iniquity-as-accumulated-crime. The iniquity originates in human moral choices (Eze 14:3 — heart-seated idolatry; Isa 5:18 — drawn with cords of falsehood) and is maintained in God's record (Hos 13:12) without named adversarial involvement. The adversarial dimension is entirely human-to-God, not mediated by named spiritual adversaries in this corpus.

**[CHAR-19]** S — The 147-verse corpus does not explicitly name adversarial spiritual beings (Satan/demons) in connection with transgression-as-deliberate-boundary-crossing. The transgression originates in human will (Psa 36:1 — speaks from the heart; Isa 1:2 — "they have rebelled") without named adversarial instigation in this corpus.

**[CHAR-2]** S — The corpus does not evidence adversarial spiritual activity in connection with unintentional sinning. The angel in Num 22:34 is not adversarial in intent — the angel's standing against Balaam was protective (preventing a wrong course). No adversarial spiritual pressure producing inadvertent sinning is evidenced in the CHAR-2 corpus.

**[CHAR-20]** E — Partially — through the Judg 9:23 divine-instigation of treachery. "God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem, and the leaders of Shechem dealt treacherously with Abimelech" — a divine spirit is named as the instigating force behind the treachery; the treachery is divinely orchestrated as retribution. This is the only instance in the corpus where a spiritual agent is connected to the characteristic's operation, and it is divine rather than adversarial in nature.

**[CHAR-21]** E — Yes — through the serpent-archetype (2Cor 11:3). The false teachers operate with serpentine cunning to corrupt the congregation's thoughts — the adversarial activity is represented through the teacher-as-serpent-type. Rev 19:2's "great prostitute" operates as the cosmic adversarial corruption-agent who has corrupted the whole earth. Both figures function as adversarial agents whose perversion-activity is actively directed against the covenant community.

**[CHAR-22]** E — Partially — through Eze 28:15/18's cherub passage. "You were blameless in your ways from the day you were created, till unrighteousness was found in you... by the multitude of your iniquities, in the unrighteousness of your trade you profaned your sanctuaries" — the cherub's injustice (unrighteousness found within a created being) is the closest the corpus comes to naming a spiritual being engaged in CHAR-22. The injustice emerges from within the cherub rather than from an external adversarial agent.
**[CHAR-3]** S — No evidence in the corpus of adversarial spiritual activity targeting confession. The corpus is silent on this dimension.
**[CHAR-4]** S — No direct evidence in the corpus. The corpus is silent on adversarial spiritual involvement in conscience suppression. This is a gap the evidence does not address.

**[CHAR-5]** S — No direct evidence in the corpus of adversarial spiritual involvement in refusal to repent. The corpus presents refusal to repent as a self-sustaining human volitional condition — the will's own non-departure — without attributing it to adversarial spiritual pressure.

**[CHAR-6]** S — No direct evidence in the corpus of adversarial spiritual involvement in habitual defection. Ecc 7:26's "snare" (woman as trap) is a metaphor for temptation, but the trap is described in human-relational terms without explicit adversarial spiritual agency named. The corpus is silent on the spiritual-being adversarial dimension.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Limited evidence. Exo 23:33 — "it will surely be a snare to you" — the snare metaphor implies an adversarial dimension: the foreign gods and their worship practices function as a trap, suggesting adversarial spiritual interest in entrapping Israel through the contagious sin mechanism. The gods served through contagious sin (Baal — Jer 32:35; idols — 1Ki 16:13; Molech — Jer 32:35) represent adversarial spiritual realities to which the contagious sin's transmitted worship is directed. However, the corpus does not name adversarial spiritual beings as active agents in the transmission — the human leader remains the named agent.
**[CHAR-8]** S — No direct evidence in the corpus. The corpus is silent on adversarial spiritual involvement in political revolt.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Yes. VCG-03's beast (Rev 13:1/5/6) — the creature associated with the dragon/adversarial power — practises constitutive blasphemy. Rev 13:5 — "a mouth uttering haughty and blasphemous words" — the beast's blasphemous speech is the adversarial power's primary mode of God-defiance. The beast's mouth is the site through which the adversarial power directs its constitutive hostility against God. Jude 9's confrontation with the devil (where Michael withholds blasphemous judgment) also situates sinful speech at the adversarial boundary.

**[CHAR-1]** S — The 190-verse corpus does not directly evidence adversarial spiritual engagement with wickedness-as-settled-person-identity. The wicked person's characteristic is framed as generated from within (T2.9.1 — "out of the wicked comes wickedness") and sustained by the person's own volitional commitment. The corpus is silent on demonic instigation or adversarial amplification of this characteristic. Note: the broader M10b cluster includes cosmic-evil content (M10b-B-VCG-01 — the evil one, which belongs to Characteristic 2), but that is outside Characteristic 1's evidence scope.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes. VCG-01 (13V) documents this directly. Eph 6:16 (vc=14428 — VCG-01): "the flaming darts of the evil one" target the inner person — the constitutionally vulnerable inner person is the target of adversarial attack. Mat 13:19 (vc=14435 — VCG-01): the evil one snatches away the word sown in the heart — the heart's inner state of insufficient understanding makes it a site of adversarial attack. 1Jo 5:18 (vc=14432 — VCG-01): the one born of God is shielded from the evil one's touch — implying that the unprotected inner person is accessible to the evil one. The constitutionally evil inner state creates a vulnerability that adversarial powers exploit.

**[CHAR-3]** S — The evidence does not directly address adversarial spiritual powers in relation to abomination-as-moral-character-failure. The characteristic is framed as arising from within human inner moral character (the crooked heart, the arrogant heart, the dishonest practice) — not as the result of adversarial spiritual attack or exploitation. The adversarial dimension that appeared in CHAR-2 (VCG-01 — the evil one targeting the heart) is absent from CHAR-3's 40-verse corpus. This silence is noted explicitly.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes. The idolatrous objects and the spiritual powers behind them (the foreign deities) function as adversarial influences drawing the heart away from God. Deu 7:25-26 (vc=1682/65927 — VCG-02): the idol ensnares and makes the person "devoted to destruction" — the idol-object as a spiritually dangerous entrapment. Deu 12:31 (vc=1683 — VCG-02): "every abominable thing that the Lord hates they have done for their gods" — the foreign gods are the beneficiaries of the misdirected devotion; they function as adversarial powers competing with the covenant God. The characteristic is therefore inherently a site of adversarial spiritual activity — the idol-objects and the spiritual powers they represent are drawing the human devotion-capacity away from God.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes, partially. Zec 10:2 (VCG-01) shows the spiritual-being dimension: household gods and diviners produce the a.ven (nonsense, empty consolation, false dreams) that leaves the community wandering without a shepherd — this is adversarial spiritual activity generating iniquity-as-trouble in the community. 1Sa 15:23 (VCG-02): rebellion/presumption compared to divination — the self-assertion of the human will against God's word is analogised to divination (an adversarial spiritual practice). The characteristic is not primarily framed as a site of adversarial attack in this corpus, but the VCG-01 evidence shows adversarial spiritual guidance (false prophets, household gods) as one channel through which a.ven trouble is generated in the community.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes. Rev 13:6 (vc=14356 — VCG-01) is the primary adversarial evidence: the beast (an adversarial figure) is the agent of sustained blasphemy against God, his name, his dwelling, and heaven's inhabitants. The beast represents the concentration of adversarial spiritual opposition to God expressed through speech. The characteristic is thus not merely a human moral failure but finds its most intense expression in the adversarial cosmic-eschatological figure of the beast whose primary weapon is blasphemous speech. The characteristic is constitutively adversarial in its VCG-01 dimension.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Chars 2 and 4 are explicitly sites of adversarial activity. Char 2 (VCG-01 — the cosmic-evil-agent sub-corpus: 1Jo 5:19 — the whole world in the evil one's power; Mat 13:19 — the evil one snatching away the word from the heart). Char 4 (Deu 7:25-26 — the idol-objects as spiritually ensnaring; 1Ki 11:5 — foreign deities as active objects of misdirected devotion). Char 6 (Rev 13:6 — the beast as the adversarial figure whose primary mode of operation is blasphemous speech). The cluster reveals that adversarial spiritual activity specifically targets the three characteristics involving devotion-misdirection (Char 4), constitutional inner constitution (Char 2), and speech-expression of defiance (Char 6).

**[CHAR-1]** S — Not evidenced within Characteristic 1's 133-verse corpus. The characteristic operates as a condition of creaturely embodied vulnerability in relation to the divine holiness, not as a site of adversarial spiritual conflict.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes, at the formative-environmental level evidenced in the corpus. 1Cor 8:7 (VCG-03) — the former association with idols that shapes the conscience toward defilement — the adversarial spiritual influence behind idol-worship is the source of the defiling formative context. The "unclean spirits" of Rev 16:13 (VCG-04) function as "agents of deception sourced in darkness" — their operation produces defilement in the human environment they inhabit. The characteristic is thus not only a self-generated human condition but one that is fostered and deepened by adversarial spiritual activity. However, this adversarial involvement is contextual-environmental rather than direct individual attack as evidenced in Characteristic 4.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Indirectly yes. The idolatrous attachment that generates the characteristic (VCG-02) involves the worship of false gods — Molech (2Ki 23:10), Ashtoreth (2Ki 23:13), Chemosh, Milcom — which in the biblical framework are spiritual powers opposed to God. The child sacrifice to Molech (2Ki 23:10, Eze 20:26/31) is the most extreme expression: the community's idolatrous defilement is directed toward spiritual powers whose worship requires the most extreme form of self-defilement. However, the corpus does not frame the characteristic as a site of active adversarial attack; rather, the community actively pursues the idols through its own desire — the adversarial dimension is in the objects of idolatrous attachment, not in an attacking spiritual force.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes — it is the defining adversarial site among the M10c characteristics. The unclean spirits are adversarial spiritual powers that attack the human person's constitutional integrity — overriding will, suppressing faculties, severing communal access, afflicting the body. The characteristic is not merely a context where adversarial activity might occur; it is constituted by adversarial spiritual agency. Mar 5:8 (VCG-01): Jesus commands the spirit out — the command is directed at a spiritual adversary whose presence constitutes the defilement.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster reveals a spectrum from non-adversarial (Char 1) through contextual-adversarial (Chars 2, 3) to constitutively adversarial (Char 4). Characteristic 1: not a site of adversarial activity — the characteristic operates as a condition of creaturely embodied vulnerability in relation to divine holiness, not as a site of adversarial spiritual conflict. Characteristic 2: adversarial at the formative-environmental level — "former association with idols" (1Cor 8:7 VCG-03) implicates the adversarial spiritual influence behind idol-worship; the "unclean spirits" of Rev 16:13 (VCG-04) function as agents of deception that produce defilement in the human moral environment. The adversarial involvement is contextual-environmental rather than direct individual attack. Characteristic 3: indirectly adversarial through the idolatrous objects — the worship of Molech (2Ki 23:10), Ashtoreth (2Ki 23:13), and other named powers involves spiritual powers opposed to God; but the corpus frames the community as the active agent of its own defilement through desire, not as a passive victim of adversarial attack. Characteristic 4: constitutively adversarial — the characteristic is defilement-by-adversarial-agent; it is the defining adversarial site in the cluster; the unclean spirits attack the human person's constitutional integrity directly (overriding will, suppressing faculties, severing communal access). The cluster's adversarial gradient confirms M10c's internal structure: Characteristics 1 and 3 are primarily self-generated and non-adversarial; Characteristics 2 and 4 explicitly involve adversarial spiritual powers as environmental or direct agents.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-004: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion…
findings.finding_value: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion on whom I have compassion"), covenantally grounded (chesed as the bond-loyalty that grounds the characteristic), and situationally responsive (splanchnizō — triggered by the specific sight of suffering). These three bases are not in tension but in integration: divine compassion is free, covenanted, and responsive simultaneously. The scope finding is among the most analytically significant in the registry: compassion explicitly and repeatedly crosses covenantal boundaries (Nineveh, the Samaritan/Jew axis, the power-asymmetric relationship). Scope is defined by perceived need, not moral standing or covenantal membership — this is formally confirmed in the data and distinguishes compassion from many other relational characteristics. The chesed/splanchnizō distinction maps onto distinct relational registers: chesed sustains within established bonds; splanchnizō extends across distance and difference. T4.4 (receiver's inner-being experience) is the most significant gap — four P-rated prompts, entirely absent from the data. T4.6 (spiritual beings interface) is entirely silent across all four prompts.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-004: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — a…
findings.finding_value: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — all God-as-subject). The basis of divine extension is the giver's character and prior knowing (Exo 33:17 — "I know you by name"), not the receiver's merit — neither merit-based nor arbitrary. The human-to-God direction is specifically supplication: tachanum (H8469) is the receiving side's corresponding vocabulary built into the same root family as the giving side (chen/chanan) — the vocabulary embeds the two-directional circuit in a single root. The human-giving direction extends grace horizontally through three modes: forgiving (charizō — Eph 4:32), gracious conduct (chen as character quality — 889-003), and gracious speech (SD022). The receiving direction is the most underexamined (T4.4 — P-rated throughout); the scope analysis (T4.5) reveals grace crossing covenantal and social boundaries (Ruth narrative — grace in the context of foreign status and vulnerability). T4.6 (spiritual beings) is evidenced at one point: Luk 1:28 (kecharitōmenē — the angel's announcement), which implies angelic ministry as a vehicle of grace rather than grace operating independently in the spiritual-beings register. T4 synthesis: the relational architecture of grace is unique in the programme — it is the only characteristic where the giving-side vocabulary and the receiving-side vocabulary are built from the same root (chen/tachanum), encoding the grace-circuit's two-sidedness at the lexical level.

findings.session_b_note: Yes — Dan 10:19 establishes angelic mediation of peace directly: "peace be with you; be strong and of good courage" — the angelic being speaks peace to Daniel as a constitutive part of strengthening him for the vision. The mediation is: divine peace → angelic proclamation → human inner-being reception → strengthening. This establishes angels as genuine mediators of peace in the biblical data, not merely observers. The Christmas announcement (Luk 2:14) follows the same pattern: angelic chorus → peace proclaimed to earth → the incarnate peace-person arrives. The angelic mediation of peace is not merely formal (announcing) but apparently effective (Daniel's fear is addressed and he is strengthened).

The angelic role is to mediate divine presence (producing appropriate fear) and divine reassurance (releasing inappropriate fear). Angels function as the two-directional interface between divine holiness and human inner life in the fear register.
The theophanic trembling at Sinai (Exo 19:16 anchor, E-VCG-01) is mediated through divine presence itself rather than specifically through angels.

Angelic ministry is the primary mediation structure for M01-B's theophanic fear (producing it) and for the commanded release of that fear (commanding it away). Angels are the agents through which divine holiness crosses the threshold between the divine and the human, producing both fear and its commanded release.

No angelic mediation of anger is evidenced in the corpus. The destroying angels of Psa 78:49 (M02-B-VCG-06) are agents of God's anger but are not described as mediators of the anger to the human inner person — they are instruments of its enacted consequence. Silence noted: angelic mediation of anger is not evidenced.

The verse evidence is silent on angelic ministry in relation to M03's grief characteristic. Angels do not appear in the M03 corpus as mediators of grief, as comforters of the grieving, or as agents of the grief-producing experiences. This silence is notable given angels' active presence in some other clusters.
**[CHAR-1]** S — The evidence does not show angelic ministry in the mediation or strengthening of exultation in this corpus. Silent.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Partially evidenced. Luk 2:10 — the angel announces "good news of great joy" to the shepherds; the angelic announcement is the vehicle through which the gospel Joy is first communicated to humanity. Luk 1:14 — the angel (Gabriel) announces the Joy that Zechariah will have. These are the clearest instances of angelic mediation of Joy's announcement.
**[CHAR-7]** S — Not directly evidenced in this corpus. The Spirit is the mediating agent; angels are not named as mediators of Suffering-Joy in the M04-E-VCG-02 or M04-F evidence.
**[CHAR-3]** S — Not evidenced in this corpus. Silent.

**[CHAR-4]** S — Not evidenced in this corpus. The voice at baptism/transfiguration (Mat 3:17; 17:5) declaring divine Delight operates through divine speech, not angelic mediation. The ni.cho.ach aroma operates through the cultic-ritual mechanism, not angels. Angelic mediation of Delight is not evidenced.
**[CHAR-5]** S — Not evidenced in this corpus. Silent.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes, in the Rev 17:7 instance: the angel mediates a corrective response to John's Wonder — "why do you marvel? I will tell you the mystery" — the angel redirects and explicates John's Wonder, offering interpretive mediation of what was initially an overwhelming and disorienting inner response. The angel does not destroy John's Wonder but channels it toward proper understanding.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Angelic mediation is narrowly evidenced: (1) **Joy (Char 2)**: the clearest angelic mediation — Luk 2:10 (angel announces good news of great joy); Luk 1:14 (Gabriel announces Joy); (2) **Wonder (Char 6)**: Rev 17:7's angel redirecting and explicating John's misapplied Wonder — angelic interpretive mediation; (3) **Silent**: Exultation (Char 1), Gladness (Char 3), Delight (Char 4), Pleasure (Char 5), Suffering-Joy (Char 7) — no angelic mediation evidenced in these corpora. The narrowness of angelic mediation across the cluster is itself significant: the primary divine-to-human mediation of the cluster's characteristics is through the Word, the Spirit, and covenant relationship — not primarily through angelic beings. The exceptions (Joy's angelic announcement; Wonder's angelic redirection) are specific and instrumental rather than constitutive.
**[CHAR-1]** S — Not evidenced in the corpus.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Limited but present. Mar 1:25 (vc=30400) — Jesus silencing the demon — is CHAR-2 applied to an adversarial spiritual being: the demon's voice and presence are forcibly suppressed. Mar 4:39 (vc=30401) — the storm muzzled — applies the same authority to natural forces. These confirm the enforced-abasement mechanism applies beyond human persons when divine authority acts against them.

**[CHAR-3]** S — The 15-verse CHAR-3 corpus does not evidence worth-denial operating in relation to spiritual beings. Silent.

---

**[CHAR-4]** S — The 16-verse CHAR-4 corpus does not evidence shamefulness-as-moral-evaluation operating in relation to spiritual beings. Silent.

**[CHAR-5]** S — The 24-verse CHAR-5 corpus does not directly evidence contempt-produced shame operating in relation to angelic or adversarial spiritual beings in an explicit way. The world's contempt structures may be demonically energised (the parable of the tenants who reject the son could carry this dimension), but the text does not name this explicitly. Silent.

**[CHAR-6]** S — The 8-verse CHAR-6 corpus does not evidence innocence-as-counter-to-shame operating in relation to angelic or adversarial spiritual beings. Silent.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Limited but present. Char 2 provides the primary evidence: Jesus silencing the demon (Mar 1:25) and the storm (Mar 4:39) as applications of the enforced-abasement mechanism to spiritual and natural forces. Beyond this, the cluster is substantially silent on the spiritual beings interface — M07's primary field is the human-to-human and human-to-God relational space. The one significant interpretive observation: the enemy-language of Char 1's M07-A unjust-wound register (Psa 25:2-3; 35:4-5; 129:5) acknowledges enemies as the agents of unjust shame; whether these enemies carry an adversarial spiritual dimension is not named explicitly in the corpus, though the lament psalms' enemy-language could carry this dimension. Classified as silent on the specific spiritual beings interface pending further investigation.

**[CHAR-1]** S — The verse evidence is silent on angelic ministry in relation to CHAR-1. No verse in §3 evidences angelic involvement in the generation, expression, strengthening, or reversal of CHAR-1. The 149-verse corpus contains no angelic-ministry content pertaining to this characteristic.
**[CHAR-2]** S — The verse evidence is silent on angelic ministry in relation to CHAR-2 in §3.A.
**[CHAR-3]** S — The verse evidence is silent on angelic ministry in relation to CHAR-3 in §3.B.
**[CHAR-4]** S — The verse evidence is silent on angelic ministry in relation to CHAR-4 in §3.C.
**[CHAR-5]** S — The verse evidence is silent on angelic ministry in relation to CHAR-5 in §3.D.
**[CLUSTER]** S — All five characteristics are silent on angelic ministry in relation to M08. Confirmed.

**[CHAR-3]** S — The corpus does not evidence angelic mediation of the characteristic.

The cluster's mediation is through the human high priestly representative (CHAR-4 — Heb5:2), through apostolic instruction (CHAR-2, CHAR-5), through community formation (CHAR-1 — Eph4:2; Col3:12), and through direct divine action (CHAR-3 — God draws near; CHAR-6 — God upholds). Angelic ministry is not evidenced as a mechanism for any M09 characteristic.

**[CHAR-1]** S — The corpus contains no evidence of angelic ministry mediating or strengthening the *resistance to* wilful sinning, nor of angelic ministry facilitating sinning. The adversarial spiritual beings (2Pe 2:4, Eze 28:16) are themselves sinners, not agents preventing sinning. Ecc 5:6 mentions "the messenger" before whom rash speech constitutes sinning — this may be an angelic messenger (as in the LXX reading), in which case the angel functions as a witness who records the sinning rather than a mediator preventing it. No direct angelic ministry in strengthening the characteristic is evidenced.
**[CHAR-10]** S — No evidence. The corpus is silent on angelic mediation in connection with any of the three mechanisms.

**[CHAR-11]** S — The 112-verse corpus does not evidence angelic ministry as a medium for communicating, strengthening, or mediating the universal sin-condition. The condition's transmission is through the Adamic representative structure (Rom 5:12) and the person's own sinning (Rom 3:23); angelic agents are not named as mediators of the condition.

**[CHAR-12]** S — The 9-verse corpus does not evidence angelic (holy angels) ministry as a medium for communicating or mediating sin's enslaving power. The adversarial dimension (devil, evil one — 1Jo 3:8; 1Jo 5:18) names the opposing spiritual agent but not holy angelic mediation.

**[CHAR-13]** S — The 205-verse corpus does not evidence angelic ministry as a mediator of the divine record. The record is maintained by God directly and disclosed through prophetic speech (Isa 58:1; Mic 3:8) rather than through angelic agency.

**[CHAR-14]** S — The 34-verse corpus does not evidence angelic ministry as a mediator of forgiveness sought and received. The mediation is priestly (Lev 10:17 — priest bears iniquity) and Christological (Mat 26:28 — Christ's blood), not angelic.

**[CHAR-15]** S — The 8-verse corpus does not evidence angelic ministry in connection with generational sin. The characteristic operates through ancestral-lineage transmission and covenant-community belonging rather than through angelic agency.

**[CHAR-16]** E — Partly — through the angelic witness dimension. Luk 15:10 — "joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents" — the angels bear witness to the repentance event; their joy is the spiritual-beings' response to what occurs in the human moral realm. The angelic ministry here is not mediating the sinner-identity itself but witnessing and celebrating its reversal through repentance.

**[CHAR-17]** E — Partially — through the seraph in Isa 6:7. "He touched my mouth and said: 'Behold, this has touched your lips; your guilt is taken away, and your sin atoned for'" — the seraph is the agent of guilt-removal; the angelic ministry mediates the guilt's taking-away. This is the sole angelic-mediation instance in the corpus, and it is for guilt-removal rather than guilt-communication.

**[CHAR-18]** E — Partly — through the Zec 3:4 removal instance. Zec 3:4 — "the angel said to those who were standing before him, 'Remove the filthy garments from him.' And to him he said, 'Behold, I have taken your iniquity away from you'" — the angelic mediator pronounces and effects Joshua's iniquity-removal. This is the sole angelic-mediation instance in the corpus, and it is for iniquity-removal (VCG-06) rather than iniquity-communication or accumulation.

**[CHAR-19]** E — Yes — in two instances. (1) *Law mediated by angels* (Heb 2:2): the law against which transgression is committed was "declared by angels" — angelic ministry is the delivery mechanism for the divine law that defines transgression's boundaries; (2) *Intercession for transgressors* (Isa 53:12): the servant "makes intercession for the transgressors" — the mediatorial intercession moves on behalf of transgressors toward God. Both instances place angelic/servant-mediatorial ministry in the framework of transgression's legal definition (Heb 2:2) and resolution (Isa 53:12).

**[CHAR-2]** E — Num 22:34 evidences angelic ministry as a *disclosure mechanism* for inadvertent sinning: the angel's appearance disclosed the morally relevant fact that Balaam had not perceived, activating Balaam's confession. The angel did not prevent the inadvertent sinning (Balaam had already been proceeding) but mediated the disclosure that enabled conscience to engage. This is a form of angelic ministry: mediating the truth that surfaces the inadvertent sin to the sinner's awareness and enables the move toward confession and remedy.

**[CHAR-20]** S — No angelic ministry is named in connection with faithlessness as covenant-breaking sin in the 101-verse corpus. The characteristic operates as a direct human-God and human-human covenantal transaction without angelic mediation.

**[CHAR-21]** S — No angelic ministry is named in connection with perversion as inner inversion in the 64-verse corpus. The serpent (2Cor 11:3) is adversarial rather than angelic. No beneficial angelic mediation of CHAR-21's content or resolution is evidenced.
**[CHAR-22]** S — No angelic ministry is named in connection with injustice in the 72-verse corpus. The characteristic operates as a direct human moral-conduct failure without angelic mediation.
**[CHAR-3]** S — No evidence. The corpus is silent on angelic mediation of confession.
**[CHAR-4]** S — No evidence. The corpus is silent on angelic mediation in connection with conscience suppression.
**[CHAR-5]** S — No evidence. The corpus is silent on angelic mediation in connection with refusal to repent.
**[CHAR-6]** S — No evidence. The corpus is silent on angelic mediation in connection with habitual defection.
**[CHAR-7]** S — No evidence of angelic mediation in connection with contagious sin. The transmission mechanism is entirely human-authority-based in the corpus.
**[CHAR-8]** S — No evidence. The corpus is silent on angelic mediation in connection with political revolt.

**[CHAR-9]** S — No evidence of angelic ministry strengthening or mediating sinful speech. Jude 9 and 2Pe 2:11 present angelic beings as restraining blasphemous speech rather than mediating it. The angelic interface in this corpus is on the side of restraint, not facilitation.

**[CHAR-1]** S — The evidence is silent on angelic ministry in relation to wickedness-as-settled-person-identity. No verse in the 190-verse corpus addresses angelic communication, strengthening, or mediation of this characteristic in either direction (angelic support for righteousness against wickedness, or angelic involvement in the characteristic's operation). This is explicitly noted as silence.

**[CHAR-2]** S — The 90-verse corpus does not evidence angelic ministry as a communicator, strengthener, or mediator of evil as constitutional inner nature. The adversarial dimension (VCG-01) addresses the evil one / spiritual forces of evil, not angelic ministry in the positive sense. No verse in the corpus shows angelic ministry in relation to this characteristic in either direction. This is explicitly noted.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The only angelic presence in the corpus is in Eze 9:4 (vc=1698 — VCG-04): the angel instructed to mark those who grieve over abominations. The angelic ministry here is protective toward those whose conscience recoils from abomination — not a mediation or strengthening of the characteristic itself but a divine response to it through angelic agency. The angelic role is the divine identification of those who do not share the abominable character. This is the sole evidence of angelic ministry in relation to this characteristic.

**[CHAR-4]** S — The 99-verse corpus does not evidence angelic ministry in relation to the characteristic (Eze 9:4 from CHAR-3's corpus — the angelic marking of the grieving — does not appear in CHAR-4's evidence set). The characteristic is not evidenced as communicated, strengthened, or mediated through angelic ministry within this corpus. This silence is noted.

**[CHAR-5]** S — The 79-verse corpus does not evidence angelic ministry in relation to iniquity as active scheming. No verse shows the characteristic as communicated, strengthened, or mediated through angelic activity. This silence is noted.

**[CHAR-6]** S — The 17-verse corpus does not evidence angelic ministry in relation to evil expressed through speech. The plagues in Rev 16 are administered by angels (Rev 16:2 etc. in the broader context), but the characteristic itself (blasphemy in response to the plagues) is not communicated, strengthened, or mediated through angelic ministry. The characteristic is generated entirely from within human or adversarial-cosmic volitional sources.

**[CLUSTER]** S — None of the six characteristics is evidenced as communicated, strengthened, or mediated through angelic ministry. Char 3's Eze 9:4 (the angel marking those who grieve over abominations) shows angelic ministry in relation to the characteristic's targets and opponents, not in relation to the characteristic itself. The cluster's unanimous silence on angelic mediation of its evil-forms is consistent with the exclusively creaturely origin of M10b characteristics (T0.3.2).
**[CHAR-1]** S — Not evidenced within the 133-verse corpus.

**[CHAR-2]** S — The 26-verse corpus does not evidence the moral-inner defilement-state being mediated or opposed through angelic ministry. No verse in §3 names angelic agents in relation to the characteristic's operation or opposition.
**[CHAR-3]** S — Not evidenced within the 83-verse corpus.

**[CLUSTER]** S — All four characteristics are silent on angelic ministry. Across the entire 263-verse corpus, no verse names angelic beings as actors in relation to the defilement-state's operation, transmission, or resolution. The cluster's angelic-ministry profile is uniformly silent. The resolution of defilement in all four characteristics is directly divine (Chars 1-4 — God provides the remedy, God commands the spirit, God promises the cleansing) and in Characteristic 4 also delegated to human disciples (Mat 10:1, Mar 6:7) — but not mediated through angelic agents.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-004: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion…
findings.finding_value: T4 reveals the most structurally developed relational architecture for compassion's scope. God's compassion operates simultaneously on three bases: sovereignly free (Rom 9:15 — "I will have compassion on whom I have compassion"), covenantally grounded (chesed as the bond-loyalty that grounds the characteristic), and situationally responsive (splanchnizō — triggered by the specific sight of suffering). These three bases are not in tension but in integration: divine compassion is free, covenanted, and responsive simultaneously. The scope finding is among the most analytically significant in the registry: compassion explicitly and repeatedly crosses covenantal boundaries (Nineveh, the Samaritan/Jew axis, the power-asymmetric relationship). Scope is defined by perceived need, not moral standing or covenantal membership — this is formally confirmed in the data and distinguishes compassion from many other relational characteristics. The chesed/splanchnizō distinction maps onto distinct relational registers: chesed sustains within established bonds; splanchnizō extends across distance and difference. T4.4 (receiver's inner-being experience) is the most significant gap — four P-rated prompts, entirely absent from the data. T4.6 (spiritual beings interface) is entirely silent across all four prompts.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-004: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — a…
findings.finding_value: T4 establishes the most precisely articulated relational architecture of any characteristic in the review set. The God-to-human direction is primary and dominant (groups 888-001, 889-001, 5471-001 — all God-as-subject). The basis of divine extension is the giver's character and prior knowing (Exo 33:17 — "I know you by name"), not the receiver's merit — neither merit-based nor arbitrary. The human-to-God direction is specifically supplication: tachanum (H8469) is the receiving side's corresponding vocabulary built into the same root family as the giving side (chen/chanan) — the vocabulary embeds the two-directional circuit in a single root. The human-giving direction extends grace horizontally through three modes: forgiving (charizō — Eph 4:32), gracious conduct (chen as character quality — 889-003), and gracious speech (SD022). The receiving direction is the most underexamined (T4.4 — P-rated throughout); the scope analysis (T4.5) reveals grace crossing covenantal and social boundaries (Ruth narrative — grace in the context of foreign status and vulnerability). T4.6 (spiritual beings) is evidenced at one point: Luk 1:28 (kecharitōmenē — the angel's announcement), which implies angelic ministry as a vehicle of grace rather than grace operating independently in the spiritual-beings register. T4 synthesis: the relational architecture of grace is unique in the programme — it is the only characteristic where the giving-side vocabulary and the receiving-side vocabulary are built from the same root (chen/tachanum), encoding the grace-circuit's two-sidedness at the lexical level.
